A sweep over all positive boundary values at one fixed, possibly unknown, unequal weight ratio gives global identification through a Schröder-Koenigs iteration. We extend this result to a three-vertex chain with two observed free vertices under a sweep condition. For variable-ratio control, we prove finite-target recovery, local Lipschitz stability, and noisy-bisection bounds. Fixed-ratio stability and nonparametric estimation under uncertain controls remain open. In the reciprocal family $J_p$, an exact Gaussian model-selection probability benchmarks synthetic experiments under observation noise and errors in variables. These are identifiability results under controls; no measured data or physical system is analyzed.

papers.title: On Lorentzian torse-forming structure manifolds
papers.abstract: In this paper we introduce a class of non-flat Lorentzian manifolds, called Lorentzian torse-forming structure manifolds (briefly, LTFSMs). This class contains Lorentzian concircular structure manifolds (briefly, LCSMs), LSP-Sasakian manifolds, LP-Sasakian manifolds with coefficient $α$, LP-$α$-Sasakian manifolds, LP-Sasakian manifolds, and LP-$α$-Kenmotsu manifolds. The interrelations among these various classes of manifolds are illustrated in Figures 1 and 2. We investigate several geometric properties of LTFSMs. In particular, we show that the expansion scalar, given by the divergence of $ξ$, is nonzero and nonconstant, and that the flow of $ξ$ is irrotational. In an LCSM, the Ricci operator commutes with the structure tensor $φ$ [12]. However, it is shown that, in an LTFSM, the Ricci operator does not generally commute with $φ$. If the gradient of the torse-forming scalar $α$ is collinear with the torse-forming vector field $ξ$, then the Ricci operator commutes with $φ$, and the manifold reduces to an LCSM. It is known that a conformally flat LCSM is quasi-Einstein and hence is a manifold of quasi-constant curvature. We show that a conformally flat LTFSM is a generalized quasi-Einstein manifold in the sense of Chaki [1] and is also a manifold of generalized quasi-constant curvature. Several curvature-related properties of LTFSMs are established, and their sectional curvature is determined. The existence of LTFSMs is demonstrated through several proper nontrivial examples. We also present examples that are simultaneously LCSMs and LTFSMs, examples of LTFMs characterizing twisted cubic spacetimes, and generalized Robertson-Walker (GRW) spacetimes characterizing LCSMs. Finally, we provide examples of LTFSMs in which the vector field $ξ$ is a unit timelike torse-forming vector field but is not concircular; see Examples 5.6--5.8.

papers.title: A sharp bound on the binding number of $K_k$-free graphs and the Brandt conjecture
papers.abstract: The binding number of a graph is the smallest ratio $|N(S)|/|S|$ among all nonempty vertex sets $S$ whose neighborhood $N(S)$ is not the whole vertex set. We prove that every finite nonempty $K_k$-free graph has binding number at most $k-2$ for every $k\ge6$, confirming Brandt's conjecture; the bound is sharp for complete $(k-1)$-partite graphs with equal nonempty parts. We first prove the case $k=6$ and then extend it to all $k\ge6$ by induction.

papers.title: Existence of Ulrich bundles on polarized surfaces and weakly Ulrich bundles on polarized varieties in positive characteristic
papers.abstract: In their seminal paper \cite{eisenbud2003resultants}, Eisenbud and Schreyer asked whether every smooth projective variety admits an Ulrich bundle with respect to each very ample polarization. This question has stimulated extensive research for more than two decades. Recently, Anghel \cite{anghel2026smooth} constructed counterexamples over $\mathbb C$ in dimension two, and Lopez \cite{lopez2026existence} extended this nonexistence result to higher dimensions. In this article, we study the existence problem for sufficiently large multiples of a fixed polarization and derive applications in positive characteristic. Over an algebraically closed field of positive characteristic, we prove that every polarized smooth surface admits an Ulrich bundle and every polarized smooth variety admits a weakly Ulrich bundle. Consequently, the Chow forms of surfaces (resp. varieties) admit linear determinantal (resp. determinantal) representations. Moreover, for every such polarized surface, the cone of cohomology tables of coherent sheaves coincides with that on $(\mathbb{P}^2, \mathcal{O}_{\mathbb{P}^2}(1))$.

papers.title: Quasirandomness from balanced and repeated subgraph counts
papers.abstract: Let $F$ be a graph on $m$ vertices with at least one edge, and let $0<p\le1$. We study when prescribed subgraph counts across disjoint vertex classes characterize $p$-quasirandom graph sequences. For positive multiplicities $\bm=(m_1,\ldots,m_r)$ summing to $m$ and positive class proportions $\balpha=(α_1,\ldots,α_r)$ with total at most one, we first classify symmetrized repeated-class counts for $r\ge3$: when $0<p<1$, they are forcing precisely if $e(F)>1$ or $\balpha\ne\bm/m$. We also obtain a complete classification of labelled transversal counts: for \rev{$0<p<1$, the only nonforcing profile is $F=K_2$ with class proportions $(1/2,1/2)$.} Together, these results settle conjectures of Janson and Sós [European J. Combin. 46 (2015)], Hatami, Hatami and Li [European J. Combin. 56 (2016)], and Janson [arXiv:2606.20186v1 (2026)]. The common ingredient is a balanced-count theorem for every graph with more than one edge, proved through a degree-sequence inequality, and its consequence of additive rigidity. Our arguments also determine the bad indices of the associated functional nullspaces and isolate the exceptional single-edge profiles. In particular, a non-divisibility theorem for grouped elementary symmetric polynomials excludes the higher-order obstructions in the repeated-class setting. In contrast, for two repeated classes and every $p\in(0,1)$, we construct nonquasirandom graph sequences satisfying the crossing-triangle counts at proportions $(1/3,2/3)$, with limiting edge density strictly below $p$. These counterexamples answer the crossing-triangle question negatively and show why the three-class assumption cannot be omitted.

papers.title: Isolated zeros of the Riemann zeta function and zeros of linear combinations of Dirichlet $L$-functions
papers.abstract: Let $0<γ_1\leq γ_2\leq \cdots$ be the ordinates of the non-trivial zeros of the Riemann zeta function in the upper half-plane, counted with multiplicity, and fix $c>0$. We say that a non-trivial zero $ρ_n=β_n+iγ_n$ is $c$-isolated if $\min(γ_{n+1}-γ_n, γ_n-γ_{n-1})>2πc/\log γ_n$. Note that any isolated zero is necessarily simple and on the critical line. We prove unconditionally that there exists a positive constant $c>0$ such that at least $13/20$ of the zeta zeros are $c$-isolated. Moreover, we can show that this proportion is more than $1/2$ when $c=1/6$. Previously, it was not known unconditionally that there are infinitely many isolated zeros. We also show that there are positive proportions of $k$ consecutive ``moderate'' gaps (gaps larger than a constant times the average local gap) between the ordinates of the zeta zeros, for $k=3, 4, 5$. As an application we combine our work on isolated zeros (which we extend to Dirichlet $L$-functions) with an unconditional refinement of the Bombieri--Hejhal method to show unconditionally that at least $31\%$ of the zeros of a linear combination of two distinct primitive Dirichlet $L$-functions with the same conductor and parity lie on the critical line and have odd multiplicity. The previous unconditional record for this proportion was $7.38\times 10^{-9}$, which was obtained by Dousselin who refined and made explicit a result of Selberg.

papers.title: The sum-product conjecture holds for fixed-field lattice product constructions
papers.abstract: We study fixed-field analogues of the lattice product construction recently used by Bloom, Sawin, Schildkraut, and Zhelezov to disprove the sum-product conjecture over the real numbers. These sets are of the form $A_n = P_nG_n \subset F$, where $F$ is a fixed number field, $P_n$ can be rescaled to a set of algebraic integers whose conjugates are polynomially bounded in $|P_n \setminus \{0\}|$, and $G_n$ occupies a positive proportion of a bounded box of scale $Y_n$ in a fixed positive-rank multiplicative lattice. We prove that these fixed-field constructions satisfy the sum-product conjecture, $\max\{|A_n+A_n|, |A_nA_n|\} \ge |A_n|^{2-o(1)}$ as $|A_n| \to \infty$, with no restriction on the relative growth of the two factors. More strongly, any fixed power saving in the product set forces an asymptotically maximal sumset: there exists $C > 0$ such that, for each fixed $δ\in (0,1]$, if $|A_nA_n| \le |A_n|^{2-δ}$ for all sufficiently large $n$, then $Y_n \to \infty$ and $|A_n+A_n|/|A_n|^2 = 1/2 + O_δ((\log Y_n)^C/Y_n)$. In particular, the additive-box times unit-box construction of Bloom, Sawin, Schildkraut, and Zhelezov cannot produce sum-product counterexamples in any fixed totally real number field, at any relative scales. The proof combines a bound for factorizations of algebraic integers with a more general maximal-sumset theorem for coefficient sets whose nonzero-element ratios have small Weil height. The latter controls multiplication fibers and combines a lattice strip estimate with logarithmic separation derived from the theorems of Yu and Matveev.

papers.title: A fast Laguerre--Fourier spectral method for the polyatomic Boltzmann collision operator with continuous internal energy
papers.abstract: The polyatomic Boltzmann equation extends the classical kinetic description to gases whose molecules possess internal energy in addition to their translational motion. The distribution function then has one more variable than in the monatomic case, and the collision operator becomes an eight-fold integral whose evaluation dominates the cost of solving the equation. In this work, we propose a fast Laguerre--Fourier spectral method for the polyatomic Boltzmann equation with continuous internal energy, which evaluates the collision operator in $O(K^2MN^4\log N + K^3MN^4)$ online operations after a solution-independent precomputation, where $N$ is the number of Fourier modes in each velocity direction, $K$ is the number of Laguerre modes and $M$ is the number of quadrature points on the sphere. Specifically, the distribution function is expanded in generalized Laguerre functions in the internal energy and in Fourier modes in velocity. A sequence of changes of variables then separates the internal-energy integrals from the velocity convolutions, so that the former no longer involve the distribution function and are computed once and stored. Numerical experiments are presented for both the spatially homogeneous and the spatially inhomogeneous Boltzmann equation. They confirm the spectral accuracy of the proposed method and its agreement with the direct simulation Monte Carlo method.

papers.title: Optimal Priors for Betting Tests with Bounded Payoffs: An Exact Expected-Time Characterization
papers.abstract: Testing by betting is a powerful framework that recasts hypothesis testing as a betting game. A popular approach spreads the initial wealth over fixed bets according to a prior distribution, using a universal portfolio algorithm. For suitable priors, this approach achieves the optimal expected rejection time as the error probability goes to zero at a fixed alternative. Yet, priors with this guarantee can behave quite differently near the null. This motivates the question: Which prior should we use in testing-by-betting algorithms? We study bounded scalar payoffs and, under technical conditions, prove a sharp formula for expected rejection time, uniform over all bounded alternatives as the error probability tends to zero. The formula shows how the prior's mass around the zero bet determines the cost of adapting to an unknown alternative. We characterize the priors that attain the best possible leading constant when the error probability and alternative vary together. We also show that no valid test can uniformly improve on this cost across ranges of alternatives near the null. In particular, the uniform prior can require arbitrarily more observations than suitable priors that concentrate around the zero bet. A general inversion argument converts our results into sharp expected times to reach a prescribed confidence-sequence width. We also give a concrete prior choice and an FFT-based algorithm with almost linear computational complexity.

papers.title: Free boundary regularity for the porous medium equation
papers.abstract: In this paper, we resolve the local cone conjecture proposed by Kienzler, Koch, and Vázquez concerning the free-boundary regularity of the porous medium equation. We prove that the local cone condition guarantees the smoothness of the free boundary lying outside the initial support. The proof relies on new gradient estimates obtained through maximum principle arguments and comparison principles. As an application, we establish the global-in-time smoothness of the free boundary for solutions with convex initial support under standard assumptions on the initial data.

papers.title: Structural stability of cylindrical transonic shocks to the three-dimensional Zeldovich-von Neumann-Döring combustion equations
papers.abstract: We address the structural stability of transonic shock solutions to the Zeldovich-von Neumann-Döring (ZND) combustion equations in a cylindrical domain under three-dimensional perturbations of the incoming supersonic flow and exit pressure. The perturbed transonic shock is completely free and its strength and position are uniquely determined by the incoming flow and the exit pressure. The solution shares the same regularity for the velocity, the pressure, the entropy and the fraction of unburned gas. The main difficulties are that the shock front is a free boundary to be determined simultaneously with the subsonic flow and the equations for all states are coupled with each other due to the combustion process. One of the key ingredients of the analysis is to reformulate the three-dimensional ZND combustion equations into a deformation-curl system and four transport equations in terms of the deformation tensor and vorticity. Another one is an elaborate decomposition of the Rankine-Hugoniot conditions so that the shock front is uniquely determined by an algebraic equation and an unusual second order differential boundary condition is obtained on the shock front for the first order nonlocal deformation-curl system, from which an oblique boundary condition can be derived after homogenizing the curl system and introducing the potential function.

papers.title: Sharp Bounds for Common Spanning Forests under Color Refinement
papers.abstract: We study the common spanning structure of connected finite simple graphs that are indistinguishable by uniformly initialized color refinement. We prove that any two such graphs with common cyclomatic number $r\ge2$ contain isomorphic spanning forests with at most $r-1$ components. This bound depends only on $r$ and is sharp for every $r\ge2$, even when both graphs have maximum degree at most three. We also determine the maximum, over all such graph pairs without restricting their order, of the minimum edge symmetric difference under vertex bijections: it is exactly $4(r-1)$.

papers.title: Cayley graphs of abelian groups, circular colorings and discrete fundamental groups
papers.abstract: For each integer $k \ge 2$, we prove that an abelian group $Γ$ satisfies $\exp(Γ) \in \{1,\dots,k\} \cup \{2,4,\dots,2k\}$ if and only if it admits no non-bipartite Cayley graph whose circular chromatic number is strictly less than $2 + \frac{2}{k-1}$. This refines the algebraic characterization by Krebs and Sankar of abelian groups that admit $3$-chromatic Cayley graphs.

papers.title: Mixed moment and joint non-vanishing of $\mathrm{GL}(3)\times\mathrm{GL}(1)$ and $\mathrm{GL}(1)$ $L$-functions
papers.abstract: In this article, we study the mixed-moment problem for the product of central values of two $L$-functions twisted by a Dirichlet character of large conductor $q$. Precisely, for a fixed $\mathrm{SL}_3(\mathbb{Z})$ Hecke-Maass cusp form $π$, we asymptotically evaluate the first moment, with $\textit{power-saving}$ error term for the product of central $L$-values $L(1/2, π\timesχ)\overline{L(1/2, χ)}$ averaged over the $\textit{full family}$ $\{χ\,(\mathrm{mod}\,{q}): Q\leq q\leq 2Q\}$ of primitive Dirichlet characters modulo $q$. And as a consequence, we also established the simultaneous non-vanishing of the aforementioned central $L$-values.

papers.title: CMC foliations on Euclidean spaces are minimal foliations
papers.abstract: In this article, we provide a complete answer to one of the most classical conjectures in differential geometry (of foliations). More precisely, we present a complete positive answer to the classical conjecture, due to Meeks III, Pérez, and Ros (2008), that states that every foliation on $\mathbb{R}^{n+1}$ by (possibly varying) CMC hypersurfaces is a foliation by minimal hypersurfaces. Moreover, if $n\leq 6$, such a CMC foliation must consist of parallel hyperplanes.

papers.title: Existence and Uniqueness Proof for the Transport Equation and the Orthogonal Dynamics Equation for Zwanzig's Projection on Gaussian Spaces: A Vanishing Viscosity Method
papers.abstract: We prove the existence of unique solutions ${u\in H^1(0,T;L^2_γ(\mathbb{R}^n))\cap L^2(0,T;H^1_γ(\mathbb{R}^n))}$ of the transport equation $u_t=F\cdot\nabla u+f$ and the orthogonal dynamics equation ${u_t= Q_\text{Z} (F\cdot\nabla) Q_\text{Z} u+f}$, where $F$ is a time-independent vector field, $f$ is a forcing term, $P_\text{Z}=1-Q_\text{Z}$ is a Zwanzig projection (conditional expectation) on $L^2_γ(\mathbb{R}^n)$ defined by $P_\text{Z}h \propto \int h(\cdot ,y) ρ(\cdot,y)\rm{d}y$, and $γ$ is the standard Gaussian measure with density $ρ$. To this end, we develop a vanishing viscosity method based on the maximal regularity theory for the Ornstein-Uhlenbeck operator on $L^2_γ(\mathbb{R}^n)$. The following assumptions guarantee the existence and uniqueness of strong solutions: ${f\in H^1(0,T;L^2_γ(\mathbb{R}^n))\cap L^2(0,T;H^1_γ(\mathbb{R}^n))}$, ${g\in H^1_γ(\mathbb{R}^n)}$, $F\in W^{1,\infty}(\mathbb{R}^n,\mathbb{R}^n)$ and $\rm{ess\,sup}_{\mathbb{R}^n}\left(x\cdot F-\rm{div}F\right) < \infty$, where $g$ denotes the initial value function.

papers.title: The algebraic theory of non-archimedean intertwining periods
papers.abstract: We develop an algebraic theory of local intertwining periods for symmetric pairs $(G,H,θ)$ over non-archimedean local fields $F$ of characteristic different from $2$, and finite-length representations of Levi subgroups of $G$ with coefficients in an algebraically closed field $R$ of characteristic different from the residual characteristic of $F$. For open orbits this algebraic version is essentially contained in the work of Blanc and Delorme. The theory relies on a crucial new uniqueness result, extending a result of Blanc and Delorme for open periods, which asserts that an admissible intertwining period is the only $H$-equivariant linear form extending the corresponding integral on the space of well-supported sections. In the group case it recovers at once the results of Dat on algebraic intertwining operators. Our algebraic construction does not require the unimodularity hypothesis imposed in the work of Matringe--Offen--Yang. When $R=\mathbb{C}$, we also remove this assumption in the classical non-archimedean analytic setting, and prove convergence of intertwining periods for all symmetric spaces. At the same time we extend the context of the whole theory in the following manner: we allow $F$ to be of positive odd characteristic, we allow twisting characters in the periods, and we allow $H$ to lie between $(\mathbb{G}^θ)^\circ(F)$ and $G^θ$. Finally, in the algebraic setting, we obtain explicit polynomial bounds for the singularities of intertwining periods, and compute them in a concrete case.

papers.title: A recurrence in logarithmic Möbius sums with coprimality conditions via Euler--Maclaurin
papers.abstract: We derive a recurrence for logarithmically weighted Möbius sums by combining Möbius inversion with the Euler-Maclaurin summation formula. Consequently, starting from estimates of orders zero, one and two, we obtain polynomial approximations for these sums for every nonnegative integer exponent of $\log$. We then extend these estimates to sums with coprimality conditions via a convolution identity and to sums weighted by the reciprocal of the sum-of-divisors function. We also study the nonnegativity of the latter sums for every positive integer logarithmic order, establishing that they never change sign.

papers.title: Higher-Order Paracontrolled Calculus for Geometric Rough Paths
papers.abstract: We study the rough differential equation $$ \frac{du_t}{dt}= F(u_t) ζ_t, \ \ u(0) = u_0 \in \mathbb{R}^d, $$ where $F : \mathbb{R}^d \to L(\mathbb{R}^d, \mathbb{R}^d)$ is a sufficiently regular vector field, and the noise $ζ$ is a distribution in $\mathscr{C}^{α-1}(\mathbb{R})$ for $α\in (\frac{1}{4}, \frac{1}{3})$. We construct solutions to this equation at lower regularity than previous work of Gubinelli-Imkeller-Perkowski and Prömel-Trabs using ideas from the high-order paracontrolled viewpoint of Bailleul-Bernicot. The key tool in our work is the development of a harmonic-analytic framework for proving a set of iterated commutator estimates which are necessary for the solution theory. We also show the procedure of enhancement when the noise $ζ= dZ$, where $Z$ is a realization of fractional Brownian motion with Hurst parameter $H \in (\frac{1}{4}, \frac{1}{3})$.

papers.title: Poisson occupancy of paths on permuted regular graphs
papers.abstract: In the classical occupancy problem, $B$ balls are placed independently and uniformly into $d$ boxes. We study a graph analogue of this model. Let $G$ be a directed $r$-regular graph on $d$ vertices and fix a vertex $i$. Consider all paths of length $L$ starting from $i$, and let $N_L(i,j)$ denote the number of such paths ending at a vertex $j$. Thus the vertices play the role of boxes and the $r^L$ paths play the role of balls. In general, these occupancies depend strongly on the geometry of $G$. We show that inserting independent uniform permutations between successive layers restores the classical Poisson behavior at the empirical level. Although the path endpoints remain strongly dependent, their empirical occupancy distribution has the same limiting Poisson law as independent balls thrown into boxes. More precisely, at the critical scale $r^L/d\toλ\in(0,\infty)$, provided $rL/d \to 0$, the empirical path multiplicity distribution converges in Wasserstein distance to $\operatorname{Pois}(λ)$, independently of the geometry of the underlying graphs. We also prove a local Poisson limit theorem and a Berry-Esseen bound for the empirical distribution functions. These estimates determine the full total-variation transition of the normalized path multiplicities toward uniformity. For arbitrary doubly stochastic kernels, we further establish exact covariance and Frobenius norm identities, together with an exact contraction formula for the chi-square divergence. As applications, we study synchronous opinion averaging, obtaining an explicit cutoff profile for equal-size groups and quantitative convergence to consensus for heterogeneous group sizes.

papers.title: Dynamical Lie Algebras for Fixed-Gate Quantum Ansätze
papers.abstract: Parameterized Quantum Circuits have emerged as a central framework for variational quantum algorithms in the NISQ regime, with major applications in quantum simulation, combinatorial optimization, and, more recently, quantum machine learning (QML). By developing a new approach for computing dynamical Lie algebras associated with quantum circuits combining parametrized gates and non-parametrized entangling gates, we aim to extend the applicability of recent algebraic results to architectures that are actually used in quantum machine learning.

papers.title: Multilinear rough singular integral operators may not be of the weak type at the endpoint
papers.abstract: We show that $m$-linear homogeneous rough singular integral operators $\LL_Ω$ associated with $L^\infty$ functions $Ω$ on $\mathbb{S}^{mn-1}$ with mean value zero may not be bounded from $L^1(\mathbb R^n)\times\cdots\times L^1(\mathbb R^n)$ to $L^{\frac 1 m,\nf}(\mathbb R^n)$ except possibly for the case $n=1$ and $m=2$.

papers.title: Intersecting a curve in an abelian variety with multiples of another curve
papers.abstract: Levin asked what can be said about the locus of points lying on a given curve in $\mathbb{G}_m^n$ that have a non-zero integer power on another given curve in $\mathbb{G}_m^n$ for $n \geq 3$. We give a definite answer to the abelian analog of Levin's question, proving what is predicted by the Zilber-Pink conjecture in this case. An important ingredient in our proof is a strengthening of a height inequality by Vojta and Rémond.

papers.title: A deterministic polynomial-time algorithm for the Bilu--Linial signing problem on bipartite graphs
papers.abstract: We give a deterministic polynomial-time algorithm for the Bilu--Linial signing problem on bipartite graphs. For every finite simple bipartite graph of maximum degree at most an integer $Δ\ge3$, the algorithm assigns signs to its edges so that the signed adjacency matrix has operator norm strictly less than $2\sqrt{Δ-1}$. Our algorithm builds on the randomized recursive repair framework of Jadbabaie, Saberi, and Sra~\cite{JSS26}, with deterministic rules for sign selection and vertex deletion.

papers.title: Backward stochastic partial differential equations with unbounded random coefficients
papers.abstract: We study a linear backward stochastic partial differential equation with unbounded observation-adapted random coefficients, motivated by the duality approach to nonlinear filtering. The coefficients depend predictably on the observation history through a control with almost surely finite time-integrated squared norm. The drift, diffusion, and coefficient multiplying the martingale integrand may grow linearly in space. The diffusion matrix may grow quadratically in space and is allowed to be degenerate. Under bounded positive-order spatial derivatives and bounded smooth observation-measurable terminal data, we prove existence and uniqueness in a polynomially weighted Sobolev class up to control-energy stopping times. The proof combines conditional parameter estimates, entropy bounds for likelihoods, stability under the reference probability, and stochastic-flow reconstruction.

papers.title: Occupation counts of rarely switching Markov chains: stratified local laws, support selection and the boundary layer
papers.abstract: A Markov chain with exit rates $q_i$ runs for $N$ steps with transition matrix $I+(T/N)Q$. On each irreducible face that carries start mass, we prove a local limit theorem for the occupation counts with an explicit constant and relative error $O(1/T)$, uniformly for $1\le T\le\varepsilon N$ with $\varepsilon\max_iq_i<1$ and on compact subsets of the open face. Up to $O(1)$, minus the log-probability of counts $n$ with support $F$ is $|F|-1$ times $\log(N/\sqrt T)$ plus $N$ times the Donsker and Varadhan functional of $I+(T/N)Q$ at $n/N$. Every admissible face has an explicit power of $T$ in its largest probability for large $T\le N^{1/3}$, and a constant given by a finite-dimensional variational formula. For $T=τ\log N$ the face of the mode minimizes $τλ_F+|F|-1$ at first order, with $λ_F$ the exit rate. If an admissible face has $Δ\ge1$ more states than another and an exit rate smaller by $δ>0$, we locate every crossing of their largest probabilities for large $T\le N^{1/3}$ up to $O(1/\log N)$. For two irreducible faces the crossing is unique for large $N$ in $1\le T\le\varepsilon N$, with coefficient $1/2$ of $\log\log N$. Near a facet, the continuous-time occupation density is the facet density times an explicit kernel, with relative error $O(1/T)$ at times $x\le cT$ off the facet, $c$ small. The counts obey a lattice form with extra error $T^2/N$ for $T\le\varepsilon_1\sqrt N$. The kernel is Bessel for $x=o(T)$ at facet profiles where the removed state has equal entry and exit laws, and at a profile where the rate has a first correction, of order $m\ge3$, if and only if $x=o(T^{1-2/m})$. On the complete graph with the uniform start, each face of at least 2 states crosses a vertex exactly once.

papers.title: Normalised Hamiltonian Elliptic Systems: a Gagliardo-Nirenberg inequality for bilinear mass
papers.abstract: We study Hamiltonian elliptic systems with prescribed bilinear mass $\int_{\mathbb{R}^N}uv=a>0$. We establish a Gagliardo--Nirenberg inequality in the crossed gradient pairing and bilinear mass, on scaling-invariant component-bounded classes. It identifies the critical curve $1/p+1/q=N/(N+2)$ and the restricted energy trichotomy. For power nonlinearities, we establish uniqueness up to common translations and nondegeneracy of positive profiles throughout the Sobolev-subcritical hyperbola. Exact scaling then classifies positive normalised solutions and identifies the unique critical mass. In dimension two, we develop a bilinear exponential Gagliardo--Nirenberg estimate with a sharp gradient threshold and a truncated scalar refinement with the optimal quartic leading coefficient. Adapting variational ideas from [Cassani-Tarsi, Calc.Var.PDE (2015)] we combine a mass-normalising quotient, reduction over the full negative fibres and compactness below the concentration threshold to obtain least-energy positive radial solutions for pure exponential nonlinearities at every prescribed mass below the cubic limiting mass. Local perturbative branches and a small-frequency exponential branch yield explicit mass-response formulas.

papers.title: Hyperbolicity Beyond Convexity in the Alexandrov-Fenchel Inequality
papers.abstract: We establish an Alexandrov--Fenchel type inequality in which one of the reference bodies is replaced by a function whose Hessian satisfies a balancing condition on its eigenvalues, without being required to be positive semidefinite. The proof hinges on a new extension of Alexandrov's inequality for mixed discriminants. As applications, we derive a log-concavity principle for linear functionals of area measures, answering a question of Colesanti, Hug, and Saorín-Gómez, as well as Brunn--Minkowski type inequalities for intrinsic volumes of mean section bodies, answering a question of Schuster.

papers.title: The solvable degree of a Schur algebra
papers.abstract: The solvable degree of a Schur algebra $D$ is the greatest common divisor of all integers $n$ such that $D^{n\times n}$ is a direct summand of the rational group algebra $\Q G$ for some finite solvable group $G$. The main result of this paper gives divisibility conditions on the solvable degree depending on the center and the rational primes that divide the discriminant of $D$.

papers.title: On the structure of certain valued fields II
papers.abstract: We study the structure of finitely ramified henselian valued fields of mixed characteristic with arbitrary residue fields via their residue rings of higher length, where a residue ring of length $n$ is the quotient ring of the valuation ring by the $n$-th power of its maximal ideal. We prove an approximate lifting theorem for homomorphisms between residue rings of higher length and explicitly determine the optimal bound of error of lifting. As applications, we obtain several Ax-Kochen-Ershov principles for relative completeness, relative existential completeness, and existential closedness using the pure ring structures on the residue rings. And we show that any formula on a residue ring of length $k$ is equivalent to a normal form of sentences in pure ordered group structure and special formulas at level $n$, uniformly for all finitely ramified henselian valued fields of mixed characteristic $(0,p)$ and the same initial ramification index $e$. Here, for $n\ge k$, a special formula at level $n$ represents a definable set on a residue ring of length $k$ given by a projection image of a definable set in pure ring structure on a residue ring of length $n$. Also, such $n$ is optimally computed from the precise estimation of error of lifting and depends only on $k$, residue characteristic $p$, and initial ramification index $e$.

papers.title: Finite-time blow-up for the real-valued defocusing energy-supercritical NLW
papers.abstract: We construct real-valued solutions of the defocusing energy-supercritical nonlinear wave equation $\partial_t^2u-Δu+u^p=0$ that blow up in finite time from smooth, compactly supported initial data. We consider three cases: for $p=3$ we construct blow-up solutions in all dimensions $d\geq 9$, for $p=5$ we treat all dimensions $d\geq 7$, while for $p=7$ we treat all dimensions $d\geq 6$. The solutions we construct here appear to be the first blow-up solutions of defocusing energy-supercritical nonlinear wave equations with smooth real-valued data. The main step is the construction of nonzero \emph{discretely self-similar profiles} that are periodic in self-similar time and real-analytic across the light cone. We find approximate profiles by numerical continuation from rotating self-similar solutions of the complex-valued equation and upgrade them to exact solutions by a computer-assisted Newton--Kantorovich argument in a Banach algebra of Fourier--Chebyshev coefficients. The main analytic ingredients are an exact description of the linear mode operators and uniform bounds for their inverses. The codes for the computer-assisted parts of the proofs, together with the approximate solutions, are available on GitHub \cite{code}.

papers.title: Ideal Classes of Order $2^n$ in a Family of Totally Real Cubic Fields and Rational Points on Associated Elliptic Curves
papers.abstract: For every prime $\ell\geq5$ and integer $n\geq2$, we construct a totally real cubic field in the family studied by Ennola with a specified prime ideal above $\ell$ whose class has exact order $2^n$. For parameters satisfying two square conditions and explicit congruences, the same squareclass obstructions give four independent rational points on the associated elliptic curves. A Pell equation describes all such parameters. A genus-one base change gives five independent sections that generate a subgroup saturated at two. It also yields infinitely many elliptic curves over $\mathbb Q$, pairwise nonisomorphic over $\overline{\mathbb Q}$, with rank at least five.

papers.title: BV rigidity in the string topology of compact Lie groups
papers.abstract: Let $G$ be a connected compact Lie group and $R$ a commutative ring over which $H_*(G;R)$ is an exterior algebra on odd primitive generators. We prove a rigidity theorem: the Batalin-Vilkovisky (BV) algebra $\mathbb{H}_*(LG;R)$ of Chas and Sullivan on the homology of the free loop space is that of the product of odd spheres with the classical exponents of $G$, tensored with the group ring of the torsion of $π_1(G)$. Conversely, over an integral domain the graded algebra $\mathbb{H}_*(LG;R)$ already determines the exponents and the group ring, hence the BV algebra. The isomorphism with the product of spheres is algebraic: for $\mathrm{Sp}(n)$, $n\geq2$, and $\mathrm{SU}(n)$, $n\geq3$, no map of spaces induces it over $\mathbb{Z}$. If moreover $G$ is simply connected, then $\mathbb{H}_*(LG;R)$, as a BV algebra, is the Hochschild cohomology of $H^*(G;R)$ with the BV operator induced by Poincaré duality.

papers.title: Some arithmetical aspects of the two dimensional Jacobian Conjecture
papers.abstract: We prove that any counter-example to the two dimensional Jacobian Conjecture with integral coefficients and determinant of its Jacobian matrix equals one, has only paths of asymptotic values that can contain only finitely many points of the planar integral lattice. The second part of our paper gives some nontrivial applications of the theory of certain Theta functions to the two dimensional Jacobian Conjecture over the real field, and over the complex field.

papers.title: A Lean~4 Framework for the Radii Polynomial Method
papers.abstract: Computer-assisted proofs in dynamics establish results about nonlinear systems by rigorous numerical computation. Their correctness rests on a trusted base of interval-arithmetic libraries and analytic estimates checked by hand. We formalize in Lean~4 a framework for the radii polynomial method, which certifies an exact solution near a numerical approximation by verifying four norm bounds and the resulting polynomial inequality. Weighted coefficient algebras provide the common setting for polynomial equations and initial value problems in Taylor and Chebyshev series. Their universal properties construct the bounded operators and the evaluation maps, and the universal property of the free commutative algebra makes polynomial substitution commute with evaluation. Finite/tail reductions turn the four norm bounds into finite rational inequalities, which are checked in Lean. The radii theorem then yields an exact coefficient solution, and realization theorems carry it to a solution of the original equation. The worked examples are a square-root branch given by a convergent power series and polynomial initial value problems, among them the Lorenz system, for which the library proves existence, uniqueness within the trajectory ball, and analyticity of the function-level solution.

papers.title: Arbitrary Stage Spectra for Raikov Remainders Along Quotient Towers
papers.abstract: Let $θ$ be an ordinal and let $(N_α)_{α\leqθ}$ be a continuous increasing tower of closed normal subgroups of a Hausdorff topological group $G$, with $N_0=\{e\}$. Write $ρG$ for the Raikov completion of $G$, and put $K_α=\overline{N_α}^{ρG}$ and $H_α=GK_α$. The successive and limit differences of the groups $H_α$ mark the first stages at which points of $ρG$ become old quotient points. For every nonzero ordinal $θ$ and every set $S\subseteq(0,θ]$, there is a Hausdorff pseudocompact Boolean group with a continuous tower of closed normal subgroups such that every member of the tower is pseudocompact and the nonempty strata occur exactly at the stages in $S$. The terminal quotient can simultaneously be chosen isomorphic to $\mathbb Z/2\mathbb Z$, and for every $δ<θ$ the successive factor $N_{δ+1}/N_δ$ is compact exactly when $δ+1\notin S$. Thus a tower may have a single nonempty stratum at a limit stage even when every successive factor is compact. For a closed normal subgroup $N$ of $G$, let $\widehat q:ρG\toρ(G/N)$ extend the quotient homomorphism and put $K=\overline N^{ρG}$. Over $gN\in G/N$, the fiber in $ρG\setminus G$ is $g(K\setminus N)$, homeomorphic to $ρN\setminus N$, while for $y\in\widehat q(ρG)\setminus(G/N)$ the entire $\widehat q$-fiber lies in $ρG\setminus G$ and is homeomorphic to $ρN$. For precompact kernels this gives a canonical decomposition, and nested quotients give the two-stage identity underlying the transfinite filtration. Further results concern pseudocompact Raikov remainders and include countable Abelian examples.

papers.title: Toeplitz Infinite GMRES for Parameterized Linear Systems
papers.abstract: We develop Toeplitz infinite GMRES for solving large sparse analytic parameterized systems $A(s)x(s)=z$ at many parameter values. Our method exploits a block upper triangular Toeplitz structure in the companion Krylov sequence to construct the Arnoldi process and recover solution approximations without storing full Arnoldi vectors. We derive incremental recurrences requiring $\mathcal{O}(np^2+p^3)$ arithmetic and $\mathcal{O}(np+p^2)$ storage for $p$ Arnoldi steps, excluding factorization setup and assuming linear-cost coefficient actions and triangular solves. A dynamic generator-refreshing strategy addresses cancellation in this basic recurrence. Moreover, we show that the Arnoldi basis can be simply represented using one block row and a nilpotent matrix. For $A(s)$ admitting a split form, we further use this structure to develop an implicitly rebased method. A residual lower bound for square-summable Taylor coefficients explains the effect of scaling outside the unit disk. Theoretical analysis and numerical experiments illustrate the computational efficiency of the proposed methods.

papers.title: Discussion on "Principled type I error rate inflation in two-arm clinical trial designs with external control information borrowing" by Silvia Calderazzo, Manuel Wiesenfarth, Vivienn Weru, and Annette Kopp-Schneider
papers.abstract: Consideration of frequentist type-I error or power based on certain fixed conditions may not fully embrace the aims of a Bayesian analysis; this is particularly true in settings where informative priors are involved. Calderazzo et al. consider adaptations of a testing procedure involving Bayesian borrowing from external control data. Particular caution may be necessary here in order not to condition on parameters and data simultaneously. We consider their example case and argue that (a) the conditioning scheme may have limited practical implications, and (b) if the main concern are assumption violations, these might be better addressed by adapting the likelihood function.

papers.title: Common non-zero graphs of groups with few edges
papers.abstract: Let \( G \) be a finite group, and consider its common non-zero graph, which we denote by \( Γ_{nv}(G) \). In this graph, the vertices represent the non-linear irreducible characters of \( G \). There is an edge connecting two distinct vertices \( χ_1 \) and \( χ_2 \) if there is a vanishing element \( g \in G \) such that \( χ_1(g) χ_2(g) \neq 0 \). A finite group \( G \) is described as a strongly \( \mathcal{H}_1' \)-group if the set of vanishing elements of each of its non-linear irreducible character is equal to the set of vanishing elements of \( G \). In this paper, we prove Conjecture 1 from \cite{ourself}, which states that if \( Γ_{nv}(G) \) is null (has no edge), then \( G \) must either be a strongly \( \mathcal{H}_1' \)-group or a Frobenius group, whose Frobenius complement is isomorphic to \( Q_8 \). Additionally, we show that if there are no triangles in \( Γ_{nv}(G) \), this implies that the group is solvable. We also look at the situation where the common non-zero graph of a finite group \( G \) contains only one edge. This leads us to conclude that \( G \) is either isomorphic to \( S_4 \); or that the single edge in \( Γ_{nv}(G) \) is of the form \( \{θ, ζθ\} \) for some \( ζ\in \Irr(G/G') \) and \( θ\in \Irr(G|G') \), $G$ is a $p$-nilpotent group for some prime $p$ and for all characters \( χ\in \Irr(G|G') - \{θ, ζθ\} \), we find \( \Van(χ) = \Van(G) \). Lastly, our study also explores groups whose common non-zero graph forms a star shape, concluding that such configurations can only occur if \( G \) has exactly one non-linear irreducible character.

papers.title: $\mathcal{Z}$-stable and selfless inclusions for the infinite braid group
papers.abstract: Let $B_\infty$ be the braid group on infinitely many strands and $P_\infty$ its pure braid group. We show that $C^*_r(P_\infty)\subseteq C^*_r(B_\infty)$ and all its intermediate inclusions are $\mathcal{Z}$-stable and completely selfless. This gives natural examples of simple nonnuclear $\mathcal{Z}$-stable $C^*$-algebras. Further examples come from $\mathrm{SL}_\infty(\mathbb{Z})$ and $\mathrm{GL}_\infty(\mathbb{Z})$. We also show that $C^*_r(\mathbb{F}_\infty)\subseteq C^*_r(B_\infty)$ is completely selfless for the free group $\mathbb{F}_\infty$ of braids in which only the first strand moves. All results hold for twisted group $C^*$-algebras. In contrast, $\mathcal{Z}$-stability fails for $B_n$ with $n$ finite and for groups that are not inner amenable.

papers.title: Spectral gap, internality of relative commutants, and non-hyperlinear groups
papers.abstract: We prove that the relative commutant of a finite unitary tuple in a tracial matrix ultraproduct is internal whenever its conjugation operator has a spectral gap off the commutant. This implies the existence of a non-hyperlinear group.

papers.title: Infinite-Particle Determinantal Dynamics from Brownian Motion on $\mathrm{GL}_N(\mathbb{C})$
papers.abstract: We study the edge scaling limit of the logarithms of the squared singular values of multiplicative Brownian motion on the general linear group $\mathrm{GL}_N(\mathbb{C})$ with general initial conditions. Building on earlier work [arXiv:2605.06429], we prove that, for every initial condition in the enhanced state space, the limiting dynamics are determinantal and derive an explicit double-contour formula for their extended multitime correlation kernel. The dependence on the initial state, including information not determined by the particle coordinates, is encoded by the associated Laguerre--Pólya entire function. We further extend the construction of solutions to the corresponding infinite-dimensional system of singular stochastic differential equations to arbitrary initial configurations, including those with coinciding coordinates.

papers.title: $p$-adic spectral zeta functions via the inverse Stieltjes transform
papers.abstract: Spectral zeta functions provide a standard tool for regularizing determinants of differential operators in quantum physics. In a previous paper (J. Math. Phys. 66: 083505, 2025), we introduced a $p$-adic spectral zeta function for discrete spectra via a locally analytic interpolation function. In this paper we extend the framework to continuous spectra using the inverse Stieltjes transform. Starting from the resolvent of a bounded operator, we construct a generalized distribution, called the $p$-adic spectral distribution, and define bosonic and fermionic zeta functions and functional determinants. We establish their analytic properties, special value formulas, and Stirling expansions, and show that our previous framework is embedded into the present one in the discrete case. In this approach, the bosonic and fermionic cases exhibit an interesting symmetry. As an application, we consider the position operator in $p$-adic quantum mechanics on an arbitrary compact subset of $\mathbb{C}_{p}$.

papers.title: Proper circular arc graphs are $e$-positive
papers.abstract: We prove an $e$-positive formula for the chromatic symmetric function of proper circular arc graphs solving the $q=1$ case of a conjecture of Ellzey and of Alexandersson and Panova. In doing so, we provide a new proof of the $e$-positivity of unit interval graphs, which alongside Guay-Paquet's reduction gives a new proof of the Stanley--Stembridge conjecture. We define color matrices, which count proper colorings, and tableau matrices, whose entries are nonnegative rational numbers and ratios of elementary symmetric functions. We prove the two matrices are related by a single family of change of basis matrices, which become invertible after restricting to finitely many colors, and we show the chromatic symmetric function of proper circular arc graphs comes from taking the trace of these matrices. Using Hikita's tableaux, this gives an explicit formula for the chromatic symmetric function of a proper circular arc graph as a weighted sum over tableaux whose first and last $k$ vertices lie in the same columns.

papers.title: Critical Diameters and Vietoris-Rips Filtrations
papers.abstract: We relate critical diameters of finite configurations to the topology of Vietoris-Rips complexes. For a compact metric space and $0<r<s$, we prove that the canonical inclusion from scale $r$ to scale $s$ is a homotopy equivalence whenever $[r,s)$ contains no diameter of a finite labelled configuration at which the diameter function has zero weak slope. On Riemannian manifolds, weak-slope stationarity implies Clarke criticality. At positive diameter, when the distances realizing the diameter are smooth, both are equivalent to first-order stationarity: the absence of a direction decreasing all these distances to first order. For closed connected smooth manifolds, the Clarke critical diameter spectrum has Hausdorff dimension zero, even at the cut locus. In the real-analytic case, it is finite at each fixed number of labels and countable over all label numbers. On the unit round sphere $S^m$, $m\geq1$, positive nonantipodal weak-slope stationary configurations are characterized by nonzero nonnegative equilibrium stresses. The least positive critical diameter is $\arccos(-1/(m+1))$, and the first accumulation point is $\arccos(-1/m)$. We lift every such stress through a spherical stack construction adapted from Lovász, producing stationary diameters that approach the original value from below in the next dimension as the number of layers increases. We also give example in general metric space showing that weak-slope stationary diameters need not correspond to changes in the homotopy type of Vietoris-Rips complexes.

papers.title: Singular analysis of the principal eigenvalue for cooperative elliptic systems with drifts
papers.abstract: We determine the small-diffusion limit of the principal eigenvalue for a one-dimensional cooperative elliptic system with component-dependent drifts and Neumann boundary conditions. For scalar equations, this limit is determined by local data at the drift equilibria and boundary points. We show that such localization fails for systems: switching between components can make some intervals spectrally relevant. We first prove that the logarithmic transforms of all component eigenfunctions converge to the same function, which solves a scalar Hamilton-Jacobi equation. The associated Aubry set determines the asymptotic behavior of the principal eigenvalue. Under nondegeneracy assumptions, this set decomposes into isolated points, regular intervals, and composite intervals containing common drift zeros. We then identify the effective value of each class through local Ornstein-Uhlenbeck spectra and interval transport problems, and establish that the limit of the principal eigenvalue is the minimum of these class values. A unique minimizing class also determines the common logarithmic eigenfunction profile.

papers.title: Gromov-Hausdorff instability of the positive mass theorem for Kähler manifolds
papers.abstract: We construct a sequence of AE Kähler metrics on $\mathbb{C}^2$ with nonnegative and integrable scalar curvature whose ADM mass tends to zero but which, for a suitable choice of basepoints, fails to converge to Euclidean space in the pointed Gromov-Hausdorff sense.

papers.title: Continuous Data Assimilation for Memristive FitzHugh--Nagumo Neural Networks
papers.abstract: In this study, we investigate continuous data assimilation for a class of partly diffusive FitzHugh--Nagumo neural networks with memristive feedback and linear synaptic coupling. The nudging algorithm implemented here only adds a feedback term to the membrane-potential equations, while the recovery and memductance variables remain unobserved. We obtain weighted energy estimates that give sufficient conditions for exponential convergence of the data-assimilated solution to the reference solution under full or coarse membrane potential observations. Moreover, we prove energy-class uniqueness in dimensions one and two. In dimension three, the uniqueness criterion is an \(L^4\) membrane-potential initial data. We also establish an observational-noise estimate for locally square-integrable forcing, yielding an asymptotic error bound when the noise energy is eventually bounded.

papers.title: On the language of palindromic reduced words in a Coxeter group
papers.abstract: We prove that the language of palindromic reduced words in a Coxeter system is regular if and only if the Coxeter group is a direct product of a finite Coxeter group with finitely many copies of the infinite dihedral group.

papers.title: Robert J. Daverman (1941-2026)
papers.abstract: This is an expanded version of a memorial article that is to appear in the Notices of the American Mathematical Society.

papers.title: Open extension of a genus zero Hurwitz-Frobenius manifold
papers.abstract: Every Dubrovin--Frobenius manifold provides a solution to the WDVV equation, that was initially formulated in the study of the moduli space of curves. During the last two decades special attention was given to the "open" version of the moduli space of curves. Its genus zero intersection theory is governed by the system of equations called open WDVV equation, that extends "classical" WDVV equation. In this note we study Dubrovin--Frobenius manifold structures on the Hurwitz spaces of genus zero. We construct explicitly the solutions to open WDVV equation for these Dubrovin--Frobenius manifolds and show that these solutions appear as the restriction of the Dubrovin--Frobenius structure to its discriminant.

papers.title: Plane separating continua inscribe rectangles
papers.abstract: We prove the following: If $X$ is a plane separating continuum, then every embedding of $X$ into $\mathbb{R}^2$ contains the vertices of a Euclidean rectangle. We arrive to this result by extending a known result by H. Vaughan for Jordan curves to a wider class of topological objects via shape theory and Steenrod homology.

papers.title: Bistationary Traces, Wide Levels, and Branch-Cover Rigidity for an Unrestricted Typed Variant of the Hayut-Magidor Forcing
papers.abstract: For every uncountable regular cardinal $α$, $\mathbb S^{\ast}(α)$ is an explicitly typed four-coordinate forcing motivated by the ladder-system construction of Hayut and Magidor. The forcing is $σ$-closed and, after adjoining a formal maximum, $α$-strategically closed. For $α\geqω_2$, every nonempty countable family of designated generic branches has a stationary and costationary common trace on the generic ladder-coordinate set $L_α$, while no countable family of cofinal branches generates $L_α$. These conclusions persist under a Kurepa-style level-size bound. In the unrestricted forcing, for every infinite cardinal $μ<α$ in the ground model, some level of the generic tree contains a copy of $({}^μ2)^V$. Consequently, the endpoint-corrected restriction family indexed by $\mathcal P_{ω_2}α$ is too wide, whereas the scaled restriction system indexed by $\mathcal P_αα$ has all levels of size less than $α$ exactly when $α$ is strongly inaccessible in the ground model. When these equivalent conditions hold, the branch-covering number of $L_α$ relative to the scaled system is at least $ω_1$. The low-cofinality empty-value convention also ensures that the set of domains of $L_α$ contains no club in $\mathcal P_αα$. The unrestricted tree clause of the motivating presentation is retained, without asserting forcing equivalence.

papers.title: The Smoothability of Embedded Surfaces in 4-Manifolds Under Stabilizations
papers.abstract: We study the smooth stabilization number of a locally flat embedded surface in a smooth $4$-manifold, defined as the minimum number of connected sums with $S^2\times S^2$ needed to make the surface topologically isotopic to a smooth embedding. We prove that a nonsmoothable locally flat surface in a closed, simply connected smooth $4$-manifold becomes smoothable after a single stabilization if its homology class is primitive and noncharacteristic and its complement has abelian fundamental group. This yields infinitely many examples of nonsmoothable surfaces with smooth stabilization number one. We also exhibit examples for which a single stabilization produces infinitely many pairwise smoothly nonisotopic representatives in the same topological isotopy class. In contrast, we construct a locally flat genus-eight surface representing $6h$ in $\mathbb{CP}^2$ whose smooth stabilization number is exactly two. More generally, we show that smooth stabilization numbers of locally flat embedded surfaces in $\mathbb{CP}^2$ are unbounded.

papers.title: Biharmonic Conformal Immersions of Hypersurfaces: Dirac Rigidity and Mixed Clifford Geometry
papers.abstract: A biharmonic conformal immersion asks whether a hypersurface can become a critical point of the bienergy after a conformal change of the domain metric. We study when this flexibility can produce compact nonconstant-mean-curvature geometry in space forms. For surfaces in three-dimensional space forms, with $U=λ^2H$, Ou's system is encoded exactly by a Laplace-type operator acting on a restricted ambient Killing spinor. We classify all monic scalar--chiral factorizations of this operator. In nonzero curvature such a factorization exists locally exactly when the principal curvatures are locally constant; the normalized Euclidean branch is equally rigid, and the remaining real spherical non-CMC branch is excluded by a finite-type Frobenius obstruction. For $m>2$, this scalar rigidity does not imply geometric nonexistence. The conformal tension has independent normal and tangential components. We prove that $\mathbb Rξ\oplus TM$ is the minimal natural $O(m)$-equivariant carrier, derive the corresponding strongly elliptic Jacobi block and its two-grade Clifford realization, and identify off-diagonal hybridization as the escape mechanism. Exact cohomogeneity-one reductions, combined with validated interval and Chebyshev/radii-polynomial arguments, yield embedded proper non-CMC, nowhere-umbilical examples in round spheres, including $$ S^1\times\mathbb S^n\times\mathbb S^n\hookrightarrow\mathbb S^{2n+2} \qquad(n\ge1). $$ Thus the scalar obstruction is sharp with respect to coefficient bundle: the smallest enlargement forced by conformal tension already supports compact non-CMC solutions.

papers.title: Wehrl-type entropy problem for compact connected semisimple Lie groups
papers.abstract: Let $G$ be a compact connected semisimple Lie group, and let $π:G\to U(V_λ)$ be a finite-dimensional irreducible unitary representation associated with the highest weight $λ$. We prove that coherent projectors are the unique minimizers of the Wehrl entropy over all density matrices on $V_λ$. Similar extremal properties hold for power functions in place of the entropy function. The proof uses a second variation at the extremizer by perturbation in directions associated with Killing fields, similar to the strategy of Frank and Lieb used in \cite{FrankLieb}. Then the problem reduces to the uncertainty principle characterizing coherent states. This solves the Wehrl-type entropy problem for arbitrary compact connected semisimple Lie groups.

papers.title: Maximal Algebraic Ideals in Nonunital $C^*$-Algebras
papers.abstract: In this paper, we investigate the existence of maximal algebraic two-sided ideals in nonunital $C^*$-algebras. We formulate singular-distribution estimates in terms of lower semicontinuous $2$-quasitraces and introduce a novel criterion, which we call an admissible compact quasitracial triple set. These tools allow us to control membership in algebraic ideals and to prove the nonexistence of maximal ideals in nonunital $C^*$-algebras under a closed finite-scale face condition. This nonexistence result applies to a broad class of simple $C^*$-algebras including simple separable stable AF algebras, and nonunital, simple, separable, stably finite, $\mathcal Z$-stable $C^*$-algebras $A$ that admit an approximate identity consisting of increasing projections $(p_n)$ and for which the simplex $\operatorname{QT}_2^1(A,p_1)$ of normalized traces at $p_1$ has finitely many extreme points. Moreover, we construct a simple AF algebra whose finite-scale face is dense but not closed and which nevertheless has a maximal dense algebraic ideal. This example yields a negative resolution to a question raised by Ozawa, asking whether every maximal algebraic two-sided ideal in a $C^*$-algebra must be closed.

papers.title: Functional limit theorems for Galton--Watson processes with inhomogeneous immigration
papers.abstract: We study the asymptotic behavior of a sequence of Galton--Watson processes with inhomogeneous immigration when the limit of the means of the offspring distributions is less than $1$ or equal to $1$. Under growth conditions on the expected values of the immigration distributions and the variances of the offspring distributions, and assuming the weak convergence of properly scaled immigration processes towards a non-negative stochastic process $\mathcal Y$ with càdlàg or continuous sample paths, we establish functional limit theorems for the sequence of Galton--Watson processes with inhomogeneous immigration in question. The limit stochastic processes can be represented as a constant multiple or an integral functional of $\mathcal Y$ .

papers.title: Mixing time under monotone censoring
papers.abstract: We prove the conjecture of Ding and Mossel~\cite{DM}: the lazy random walk on the discrete cube, censored to any increasing set of fixed positive density, mixes in time $O(n\log n)$. More precisely, for every nonempty increasing set $A\subseteq\{0,1\}^n$, with $a=μ(A)$ and $μ$ uniform on the cube, we prove $$ t_{\mathrm{mix}}(P)\le C_a n\log(en), $$ where $C_a$ depends only on $a$. The proof uses hypercontractivity on the ambient cube to strengthen the Poincaré inequality on coordinate sections. An optimal stopping time occupation inequality for increasing sets converts the resulting local bound into a uniform bound on hitting times of large sets. An appendix by Y.~Peres improves the density dependence to $C_a=13a^{-1}\log(e/a)$, within a logarithmic factor of the conjectured $a^{-1}$ dependence.

papers.title: On smooth and bundle structures on topological manifolds homotopy equivalent to $S^{4k-1}$-bundles over $S^{4k}$
papers.abstract: We first verify the expected calculations of the topological structure set, in the sense of surgery theory, for the total spaces of $S^{4k-1}$-bundles over $S^{4k}$ for $k\ge3$, in which manifolds homotopy equivalent to the total spaces are organized. Next, we investigate the question of which of the elements in these structure sets can be realized as such bundles. Moreover, we study the forgetful map from the smooth version to the topological version of the structure set; we determine its image. All elements in the image turn out to have the underlying manifold such a bundle.

papers.title: Generating pairs in $\mathfrak g_2$ related by an involution
papers.abstract: Let $\mathbb O$ be the real octonion division algebra, let $\mathfrak g_2=\operatorname{Der}(\mathbb O)$, and fix a quaternionic subalgebra $H\subset\mathbb O$. We ask when an element $Z$ preserving $H$ and its conjugate $TZT^{-1}$ generate $\mathfrak g_2$, where $T$ is a prescribed involutive octonion automorphism. We prove that such a $Z$ exists if and only if $T(H)\ne H$. Moreover, a fixed set of six derivations preserving $H$ contains a generating choice for every such $T$. For an arbitrary $Z\in\mathfrak g_2$, we construct a polynomial criterion with two factors: one detects reducibility on the imaginary octonions, and the other detects generated algebras of dimension at most three. An irreducible proper generated algebra must be a principal $\mathfrak{su}(2)$. We characterize the elements admitting this case by their rotation frequencies and parametrize all corresponding involutions. For one specified involution and quaternionic subalgebra $H$, we describe the nongenerating set by four geometric families and six irredundant systems of scalar equations, and prove that it has real dimension four.

papers.title: Variational properties of Perron's extremal solutions in the Bernoulli one-phase problem
papers.abstract: We study the Perron extremal solutions of the stationary one-phase Bernoulli problem. These solutions are important in several applications, but not much is known about the regularity of their free boundaries due to their non-variational construction. We show that, in fact, Perron extremal solutions retain some variational features; specifically, they are solutions in the sense of inner variations. We establish this property by showing that extremal solutions arise as infinite-time limits of monotone solutions of the parabolic Bernoulli problem. As a consequence, we are able to describe the structure of singularities for Perron extremal solutions in two dimensions: largest subsolutions have smooth free boundaries, while smallest supersolutions have free boundary points that are either smooth, or whose blow-up limits are two-plane wedges with equal slope.

papers.title: Proximal-Linearized NEP Method for Composite Optimization with Set-Inclusion and Manifold Constraints
papers.abstract: This paper focuses on difference-of-convex (DC) composite optimization problems with set-inclusion and manifold constraints. We develop an inexact proximal-linearized nonsmooth exact penalty (NEP) method that penalizes the conic constraint while retaining the manifold constraint explicitly. At each outer iteration, the method approximately solves a strongly convex proximal-linearized subproblem over the current tangent space, using computable inexactness criteria, adaptive parameters, and a retraction-based acceptance mechanism. Under boundedness of the iterates and penalty parameters, we establish an $O(ε^{-2})$ worst-case outer iteration complexity for finding an $ε$-approximate KKT point of the original problem. We further develop a complexity-transfer framework relating uniform primal objective-gap and KKT-residual decay, or dual objective-gap decay, to total inner-iteration complexity bounds. This yields an $O(ε^{-4})$ overall oracle complexity with either accelerated semi-proximal ADMM or FISTA applied to the dual subproblem as the inner solver. Using semi-proximal ADMM as the inner solver improves the bound to $O(ε^{-2}\log(1/ε))$ under an additional uniform error-bound condition. We further establish convergence of the entire iterate sequence to a KKT point under the same boundedness assumption and the Kurdyka-Lojasiewicz property of the associated potential function. Numerical experiments demonstrate the competitive performance of the proposed method on row-sparse PCA, clustering, robust SVMs, and nonconvex SOCPs.

papers.title: Hodge-Deligne and Poincaré polynomials of $\overline{\mathcal M}_{1,n}$
papers.abstract: By studying wall crossings of Hassett moduli spaces of weighted pointed curves, we prove a recursive formula that reduces the computation of the cohomology of $\overline{\mathcal M}_{g,n}$ to that of the moduli space $\overline{\mathcal M}_{g,(0^+)^n}$ of stable pointed curves of minimal weights. For $g=1$, we further prove an explicit formula for the Hodge-Deligne and Poincaré polynomials of $\overline{\mathcal M}_{1,(0^+)^n}$. Combining these, we prove formulas that enable us to compute the cohomology of $\overline{\mathcal M}_{1,n}$ efficiently.

papers.title: Critical Schatten exponents for the Berger-Coburn endpoint problem
papers.abstract: Berger and Coburn showed that boundedness of a Toeplitz operator $T_g$ on the Fock space controls the heat transform $g^{(t)}$ for $1/4<t<1$, and conjectured that $T_g$ is bounded if and only if $g^{(1/4)}$ is bounded. Looi recently disproved the forward implication by constructing a bounded $T_g$ with unbounded $g^{(1/4)}$. We prove that the reverse implication also fails, even for a real-valued admissible symbol $g$ with $g^{(1/4)}\in C_0(\mathbb{C}^n)$, and that the forward implication fails even when $T_g\in S_p$ for every finite $p>1$. Our counterexamples come from Baire category and closed graph arguments, which yield no explicit symbols. Despite this two-sided failure, the forward implication has a sharp Schatten-class form: $\|g^{(1/4)}\|_\infty\le 2^n\|T_g\|_{S_1}$ for every admissible symbol $g$ with $T_g$ trace class. We show that the constant $2^n$ is optimal and that the same estimate holds with $S_p$ in place of $S_1$ for $T_g\in S_p$ when $0<p\le1$. For $p>1$, no corresponding uniform estimate holds, even for smooth compactly supported symbols. We also determine the optimal constants in the Berger--Coburn estimates for $1/4<t\le1$. Finally, for $1\le p<\infty$, we show that the equivalence $T_g\in S_p$ if and only if $g^{(1/4)}\in L^p$ holds exactly when $p=2$, answering a question of Bauer, Coburn, and Isralowitz.

papers.title: The maximum spectral radius of outerplanar and planar $k$-uniform hypergraphs
papers.abstract: For $k\ge3$, a $k$-angulation is a simple $2$-connected outerplane graph whose interior faces are bounded by $k$-cycles, and a closed $k$-angulation is a simple $2$-connected plane graph all of whose faces are bounded by $k$-cycles. Their face hypergraphs have the same vertices as the graphs; the hyperedges are the vertex sets of the interior faces, respectively all faces. For $k=3$, the extremal problems over these hypergraphs agree with those for the outerplanar and planar $3$-uniform hypergraphs of Ellingham, Lu and Wang, who determined the outerplanar maximizer for large $n$ and conjectured the planar one. In this paper, for each fixed $k$, we determine the hypergraphs of maximum spectral radius in both classes for all sufficiently large $n$ satisfying the corresponding face-count divisibility condition. In the outerplanar case, the unique extremal hypergraph is the face hypergraph of the fan, in which one vertex lies on every interior face. In the planar case with $k=3$, it is the face hypergraph of $K_2+P_{n-2}$, which confirms the conjecture of Ellingham, Lu and Wang. For $k\ge4$, the extremal hypergraphs are the face hypergraphs of balanced theta graphs, in which two vertices lie on every face. For $k=4$, the result holds for every $n\ge5$, with extremal hypergraph ${\mathcal H}(K_{2,n-2})$. For $k\ge6$ and an even number of faces, there are exactly $\lfloor(k-2)/2\rfloor$ extremal hypergraphs up to isomorphism.

papers.title: Matchings and shape-Wilf-Equivalence of sets of patterns of length three I: Triples
papers.abstract: Permutation pattern avoidance on Ferrers boards has become a central topic in enumerative combinatorics with important connections to matchings, set partitions, and other combinatorial structures as it allows one to build families of Wilf-equivalent patterns. While shape-Wilf-equivalence classes have been completely determined for individual patterns and pairs of patterns of length three, the corresponding classification for larger pattern sets has remained open. In this paper, we provide a complete classification of the shape-Wilf-equivalence classes of triples of patterns of length three. Our proofs use a bijective encoding of pattern avoiding transversals to establish all equivalence classes. As an application, we enumerate matchings avoiding triples of patterns of length three for all, extending previous results of Bloom and Elizalde. These enumerative results identify additional families of combinatorial objects counted by the Fuss-Catalan numbers and by other integer sequences appearing in the OEIS.

papers.title: Asymmetric Periodic Water Waves in Finite Depth
papers.abstract: We consider the full two-dimensional water-wave equations in finite depth, with and without surface tension. Water waves have been studied mathematically for more than two centuries. Reflection symmetry remains a common assumption in constructions of periodic steady waves, although asymmetric profiles have been observed in experiments and numerical computations. We construct families of periodic stationary solutions whose free surfaces have no axis of reflection, in both the pure-gravity and capillary--gravity cases. To the best of our knowledge, this provides the first rigorous construction of asymmetric periodic pure-gravity waves for the full two-dimensional water-wave problem in finite depth. The proof combines localized vorticity laws with a Lyapunov--Schmidt reduction. In the pure-gravity case, we introduce a small background shear flow to obtain an invertible boundary operator and couple the interior and free-surface approximations at leading order.

papers.title: Central non-vanishing of Dirichlet $L$-functions
papers.abstract: We prove that, for every sufficiently large modulus $q\not\equiv2\bmod4$, at least $3/8-o(1)$ of the primitive Dirichlet characters $χ$ modulo $q$ have $L(1/2,χ)\ne0$. We also establish stronger proportions for moduli $q$ satisfying certain arithmetic conditions.

papers.title: Minimum Cardinalities of Multipartite Unextendible Product Bases
papers.abstract: In quantum information theory, the state space of a multipartite quantum system is modeled by a tensor product. In the tensor-product space $\C^{d_1}\otimes\cdots\otimes\C^{d_p}$, a nonzero vector is a \emph{product state} if it can be written as $\ket{\varphi_1}\otimes\cdots\otimes\ket{\varphi_p}$ with $\ket{\varphi_j}\in\C^{d_j}\setminus\{0\}$. An \emph{unextendible product basis} (UPB) is a finite family of pairwise orthogonal product states such that no nonzero product state is orthogonal to all of them. UPBs play a key role in investigating quantum entanglement and nonlocal phenomena. Finding a smallest UPB is a natural extremal problem: it asks how few pairwise orthogonal product states suffice to prevent any further product state from being added. The general minimum-size problem for UPBs has been studied for over two decades since the seminal work of Alon and Lovász. Let $f_m(d_1,\ldots,d_p)$ be the minimum cardinality of a UPB in the space, and let \(f_{LB}(d_1,\ldots,d_p)=1+\sum_{j=1}^{p}(d_j-1)\) be the natural lower bound. Alon and Lovász determined exactly when \(f_m\) attains the lower bound \(f_{LB}\), but the obstructed multipartite cases remained open in general. We prove a stabilization theorem: for every non-all-qubit system with $p\ge3$, whenever the natural lower bound $f_{LB}$ is unattainable, the true minimum is exactly $f_{LB}+1$. Precisely, if the number of even local dimensions $d_i$ is positive and even, and at least one local dimension is greater than two, then \(f_m(d_1,\ldots,d_p)=f_{LB}(d_1,\ldots,d_p)+1\). The proof is built on a unified graph-theoretic framework. Our result, together with earlier work, settles the minimum size problem for UPBs in all finite quantum systems.

papers.title: Finite Directional Coefficient Modules over Euler Fibers of $A$-Hypergeometric Systems
papers.abstract: Let A be a d-by-n integer matrix of rank d, let beta belong to the d-dimensional complex vector space, and consider the A-hypergeometric system defined by the ideal H_A(beta), with relation lattice L equal to the integer kernel of A. No homogeneity, pointedness, or positivity assumption is imposed on A. We study directed formal logarithmic solutions simultaneously over all exponent lattices in the Euler fiber over beta, which form an uncountable family when L has positive rank. For a fixed L-generic direction, negative-support strata are described by rational sign polyhedra, and their directional boundedness is characterized by recession cones. On each exponent lattice, normalization reduces the infinitely indexed coefficient equations to a finite system of Euler, transit, and directional vanishing relations, represented by a finitely presented directional coefficient module. We prove that only finitely many exponent lattices contribute nonzero directed solution spaces and that every contributing coefficient module has finite length. Macaulay inverse-system duality then identifies the dimension of the all-lattice directed formal logarithmic solution space with the length of the all-lattice coefficient module. We also give an explicit formal-series realization and a polynomial colon-ideal criterion for all realizable lowest exponents.

papers.title: On the invariance of risk-sensitive LQR gain under input randomization
papers.abstract: This paper shows that the optimal gain of the risk-sensitive linear quadratic regulator (LQR) problem is invariant under input randomization when the cost penalizes the realized noisy input. This may appear counterintuitive at first glance because certainty equivalence does not hold for risk-sensitive LQR and input randomization inflates the effective process noise. Nonetheless, the gain is preserved because the input noise enters not only the system dynamics but also the cost functional, and its total effect eventually vanishes. Consequently, the optimal gain and the Riccati recursion need not be recomputed, and the increment in the optimal cost can be readily evaluated in closed form. This result facilitates the use of risk-sensitive LQR in applications that employ input randomization for privacy or exploration, such as dynamic watermarking for replay attack detection.

papers.title: Failure of the local decay formula for Arnold multiplicities under twisted Kähler--Ricci flow
papers.abstract: Di Nezza--Guedj--Lu asked whether local Arnold multiplicities under maximal weak twisted Kähler--Ricci flow with fixed cohomology class satisfy $λ(\varphi_t,x)=\max\{λ(\varphi_0,x)-t,0\}$. We construct counterexamples with analytic initial singularities in every dimension $n\ge2$. On the Hirzebruch surface $\mathbb F_e$, $e\ge2$, the initial current $[S]+(e+1)[F]$ yields $λ(\varphi_t,x)=1/2-t/e$ for $x\in S\setminus F$ and $0<t<e/2$, where $S$ is the negative section and $F$ a fibre. Products with smooth stationary factors give higher-dimensional examples. The Zariski negative part of $\{S\}+\{F\}$, the reduced support class, forces extra divisor mass. For pure divisorial data with simple normal crossings support, a smooth semipositive representative of the reduced support class's positive part gives exact short-time formulas. On one surface we construct flows with identical initial current germs, background data and global initial Arnold multiplicity, but different local rates.

papers.title: A note on the center of the queer super Yangian ${\rm Y}(\mathfrak{q}_1)$
papers.abstract: We investigate two families of central elements of the queer super Yangian ${\rm Y}(\mathfrak{q}_1)$, arising from the constructions of Poletaeva-Serganova and from Nazarov's quantum Berezinian. We establish an explicit relation between their generating series, thereby giving an answer to the question raised by Nazarov in \cite{Na22}.

papers.title: An Ellipse Criterion for Exact Nonuniqueness in the Planar Interior Radon Problem
papers.abstract: We characterize exact nonuniqueness in the planar interior Radon problem for arbitrary pairs of open convex sets. There exists a nonzero smooth function compactly supported in the first set whose integral over every line meeting the second set vanishes if and only if an ellipse contains the closure of the second set and is compactly contained in the first set. The same criterion holds for a nonzero $L^1$ function whose essential support is compactly contained in the first set and whose Radon transform vanishes almost everywhere on those lines. For concentric open squares, the criterion gives the sharp threshold $1/\sqrt2$ for the inner-to-outer half-side ratio. This yields counterexamples to Conjecture 1.2 of Boman (2021) and to Theorem 40.1 of Boman (2025).

papers.title: Mirror descent algorithms with logarithmic barriers
papers.abstract: We derive convergence guarantees for mirror descent and proximal mirror descent with a logarithmic barrier as the distance-generating function. When the solution lies on the boundary, the Bregman divergence blows up and classical guarantees become vacuous.
