A census of all 214,260,288 rational points of weighted moduli height at most 7 agrees with this mechanism and supports the conjecture that the proportion of fine points tends to zero like $(\log B)^{-1/2}$.

papers.title: Spectrality of convolution and product measures: a block decomposition approach
papers.abstract: We study the spectrality of convolution and product measures. Let~$μ$~be a compactly supported Borel probability measure on~$\Bbb{R}^d$~such that ~$\mathcal{Z}(\widehatμ)\cup\{0\}=T$~is an additive subgroup, and let~$ν$~be a Borel probability measure on~$\Bbb{R}^d$. We prove that~$μ*ν$~is spectral if and only if~$T$~is a spectrum of~$μ$, ~$ν$~is spectral, and~$suppν$~is contained in a translate of the annihilator of~$T$. Moreover, every spectrum of~$μ*ν$~decomposes into full cosets of~$T$, and every choice of one point from each coset is a spectrum of~$ν$. We also obtain a convolution-factor criterion which strengthens a result of Wu. As applications, we characterize the spectrality of~$L_{[0,1]}*ν$~and prove that the spectrality of~$L_{[0,1]^d}*ν$~implies that of~$ν$~without a compact support assumption. For product measures, we give necessary and sufficient conditions for an orthogonal set to be a spectrum by relating its block structure to spectra of the factors. No compact support assumptions are required.

papers.title: A note on $σ_k$ maximal conformal volume
papers.abstract: We establish a sharp spherical upper bound for the $σ_k$-maximal conformal volume $Λ_k$ introduced by Gursky and Viaclovsky. Let $(M^n,[g])$ be a smooth, closed, connected conformal manifold with $n\geq 3$ and $n/2<k\leq n$, and suppose that $[g]$ contains a $k$-admissible metric, we prove that $ Λ_k(M,[g]) \leq \operatorname{Vol}(\mathbb S^n,g_{\mathrm{rd}}), $ with equality if and only if $(M,[g])$ is conformally equivalent to the standard sphere. Combined with the existence and compactness theorem of Gursky and Viaclovsky below the spherical threshold, this completes their approach to the $σ_k$-Yamabe problem through maximal conformal volume in the range $k>n/2$.

papers.title: The Genus-One B-Model Calabi-Yau/Landau-Ginzburg Correspondence
papers.abstract: Let $f:\mathbb C^n\to\mathbb C$ be a homogeneous polynomial of degree $n$ with an isolated critical point at the origin. The Calabi--Yau/Landau--Ginzburg correspondence predicts a close relation between invariants of the Landau--Ginzburg orbifold $(\mathbb C^n/\mathbb Z_n,f)$ and those of the associated Calabi--Yau hypersurface $ X_f=\{[z_1:\cdots:z_n]\in\mathbb P^{n-1}:f(z_1,\ldots,z_n)=0\}. $ In this paper, we establish this correspondence for the genus-one B-model by constructing the Landau--Ginzburg genus-one B-model invariant intrinsically from the $f$-twisted Laplacian on $\mathbb{C}^n/\mathbb{Z}_n$ and proving that it agrees with the corresponding BCOV invariant of $X_f$ up to an additive constant depending only on the dimension.

papers.title: On 2-Arc-Transitive Cayley Graphs of Nonabelian Characteristically Simple Groups
papers.abstract: The classification of symmetric Cayley graphs has attracted considerable attention. Results have been obtained for finite abelian groups and nonabelian simple groups. However, the problem remains open for finite nonabelian characteristically simple groups, although some results on normality for small valencies are known. In this paper, we determine the possible structures of automorphism groups $X$ of connected 2-arc-transitive Cayley graphs $Γ$ of $G\cong T^k$, where $T$ is a finite nonabelian simple group and $k\geqslant2$. In the quasiprimitive case, we prove that $G\unlhd X$, $Γ$ is complete, or $X$ is of product action type with restricted parameters. For the non-quasiprimitive case, we determine the possible structures of the quasiprimitive normal quotients of $Γ$.

papers.title: Explicit weighing matrices $W(n,k)$ for all $n \equiv 0 \pmod 4$ with $4 \le n \le 108$, and all $1 \le k \le n$
papers.abstract: We present an explicit weighing matrix $W(n,k)$ for every order $n\equiv 0\pmod 4$ with $4\le n\le 108$ and every weight $1\le k\le n$: 1512 matrices in total, each checked in exact integer arithmetic. Of these, 961 come from classical constructions (identity, direct sums, Kronecker products, Paley matrices and skew-Hadamard doubling) and 551 are Goethals-Seidel matrices, found by exhaustive search (24 matrices, $n\le 24$) or by simulated annealing on the periodic autocorrelation cost (527 matrices, $n\ge 28$). The note is self-contained as far as the methods are concerned: it presents all the construction methods used and the algorithm that selects among them, explains the algorithm step by step, proves every identity on which the constructions rely, and illustrates each method with a matrix taken from the catalogue. It does not reproduce the 1512 matrices, which are available in the repository. It also gives a short parity obstruction to Goethals-Seidel matrices $W(4m,4m-1)$ with $m$ even, and lists the generating sequences of thirteen matrices whose parameters appear as unresolved in historical tables consulted by the author; their status in the current literature is still being checked, and no claim of priority is made.

papers.title: A Pythagoras Tree Grown from a Dodecahedron
papers.abstract: The Pythagoras tree of A. E. Bosman (1942) is drawn with squares in the plane and, in the three-dimensional versions we know of, with cubes. This article documents a tree built instead from regular dodecahedra: each dodecahedron carries five smaller copies, one on each edge of a single pentagonal "crown" face, scaled by $g \approx 0.4346$ and twisted by $45^\circ$ about the edge. The construction first existed only as a pair of rendered images and two undocumented C++ programs. We recover its exact parameters from the original Blender scene, reformulate it as an iterated function system with condensation, and prove with a short computer-assisted argument that it never collides with itself: two of its dodecahedra overlap only when one is the parent of the other. A Pythagorean identity for the six face axes of the dodecahedron singles out the scale $1/\sqrt{5}$ and the twist $\arccos(1/\sqrt{5})$. With these values each child rests flat against a face of its parent, the five children together have exactly the parent's surface area, and the crown of the tree is a fractal of Hausdorff dimension exactly 2. Finally we ask whether the tree can grow on all twelve faces at once. A parity argument shows that at the artwork's proportions it cannot, but smaller scale factors admit certified clash-free all-faces trees.

papers.title: Swirl ill-posedness for incompressible fluids in (sub)critical spaces
papers.abstract: For the 3D Navier-Stokes equations with sufficiently smooth initial data having zero swirl $u_{0θ}\equiv 0$, Ladyzhenskaya \cite{L1968} and Ukhovskii and Yudovich \cite{UY1968} established global regularity. It has since remained open as to whether well-posedness still holds for smooth axisymmetric initial data, with the initial swirl being smaller than an \textit{absolute} constant in a critical space. In this remark, we prove \textit{norm inflation} occurs for the Navier-Stokes scalar swirl component, with initial smallness in the critical space $\dot{H}^{\frac{1}{2}}$ or even subcritical Sobolev spaces. We also obtain norm inflation for the 3D Euler swirl \textit{vector} in the Euler subcritical space $\dot{H}^3$. Our results are achieved by introducing an anisotropic scale in Luo's supercritical norm inflation construction \cite{Luo24}, as well as performing an anisotropic bootstrap argument to get a sufficiently small swirl remainder term.

papers.title: Hodge--Deligne polynomials and $S_n$-representations on the cohomology of $\overline{\mathcal M}_{2,n}$
papers.abstract: We compute the Hodge-Deligne polynomials of the moduli spaces $\overline{\mathcal M}_{2,n}$ of stable $n$-pointed curves of genus two, together with the action of the symmetric group $S_n$ on their cohomology, for all $n$. Using Hassett's moduli spaces of weighted pointed curves, we first show that the generating function of the $S_n$-equivariant Hodge-Deligne polynomials of $\overline{\mathcal M}_{g,n}$ is obtained from that of the moduli spaces of minimally weighted pointed curves by plethysm with the explicit symmetric function $Z=h_1-\sum_{k\ge3}(x+x^2+\dots+x^{k-2})h_k$; numerically, this is an explicit change of variables. The latter spaces map to $\overline{\mathcal M}_g$, and over each boundary stratum they are built from punctured universal curves and Losev-Manin spaces. Combining the stratification by stable graphs with Burnside's formula and twisted characteristics, we obtain in genus two a closed formula whose only non-elementary input is the cohomology of symplectic local systems on $\mathcal M_{1,1}$ and $\mathscr A_2$, known by work of Eichler-Shimura and Petersen. This determines the $S_n$-representations on all $H^{p,q}(\overline{\mathcal M}_{2,n})$ for $n\le 19$ and on all even degree $H^{p,q}(\overline{\mathcal M}_{2,n})$ for every $n$. We carry out the computation in all degrees for $n\le 18$, where it agrees with an independent computation by point counts, and in even degrees for $n\le 30$. As an application, we find that the even degree cohomology of $\overline{\mathcal M}_{2,n}$ is of Hodge-Tate type if and only if $n\le 20$: the space $H^{23,1}(\overline{\mathcal M}_{2,21})$ is the multiplicity free $S_{21}$-representation with Frobenius characteristic $s_1\cdot h_2[e_{10}]$, of dimension $1939938$, so that $H^{24}(\overline{\mathcal M}_{2,21})$ is not spanned by algebraic cycle classes.

papers.title: Explicit Coleman integration over finite extensions of $\mathbb{Q}_p$
papers.abstract: Coleman integration is an important computational ingredient of the Chabauty--Coleman method and its extensions. We extend the Balakrishnan--Tuitman algorithm to general smooth projective curves with good reduction over arbitrary finite extensions of $\mathbb{Q}_p$, allowing both ramification and nontrivial residue degree. Given a suitable plane model and integral bases, we provide explicit precision bounds and an accompanying Magma implementation. As an application, a single-prime computation at $p=19$ over the unramified quadratic extension $\mathbb{Q}_{19^2}/\mathbb{Q}_{19}$ recovers all $35$ affine sporadic quadratic divisors on $X(s3,ns5)$ over $\mathbb{Q}(\sqrt5)$. Completeness is proved in an appendix using symmetric Chabauty and a Mordell--Weil sieve.

papers.title: Nilpotent Lie algebras of nilpotence class at most three via graphs
papers.abstract: In this work, we associate with each finite simple graph $G$ a nilpotent Lie algebra $\mathfrak{n}_G$ of class at most three, whose underlying vector space has a basis indexed by the vertices, edges, and paths of length two of $G$. Its nilpotency class is exactly three if and only if $G$ contains a path of length two. We compute the dimensions of its lower central series and describe its center. Over fields of characteristic different from two, we prove that two such Lie algebras are isomorphic if and only if their underlying graphs are isomorphic. We also give an algebraic description using quotients involving exterior and symmetric squares. Finally, we study balanced blow-ups and prove that $\mathfrak{n}_G$ is a retract of $\mathfrak{n}_{G^{(m)}}$.

papers.title: Global $c^{1,α}$ regularity and fine behavior at critical points for quasilinear elliptic equations with Orlicz growth and unbounded drift
papers.abstract: We investigate the global regularity up to the boundary and the fine pointwise behavior along the critical set for bounded weak solutions to general quasilinear elliptic Dirichlet problems in Orlicz-Sobolev spaces. Our structural framework encompasses operators with non-standard Lieberman-type growth alongside lower-order terms featuring natural gradient growth, an unbounded source term in $L^q$, and an unbounded spatial drift weight in $L^s$. To overcome the analytical obstructions posed by the unbounded drift across the anisotropic growth gap, we first establish global Hölder continuity up to the boundary via Moser iteration. We then construct a novel smooth regularization scheme for general homogeneous constant-coefficient operators, merging the approximation frameworks of Lieberman and Cianchi-Maz'ya, to derive global $C^{1,α}$ regularity up to the boundary through a variational perturbation approach. Building upon this global theory, we employ a geometric compactness and blow-up argument to prove that at any interior or boundary critical point where the gradient vanishes, the solution achieves an improved pointwise $C^{1,α}$ regularity. Remarkably, at boundary critical points, this quantitative improvement decouples from the lower-order terms and completely bypasses both the boundary datum regularity and the domain smoothness. Finally, we discuss the sharpness of the integrability threshold required for the unbounded drift weight in the subcritical regime.

papers.title: A Nonconvex Framework for Joint Sparse Sample Weighting and Parameter Estimation
papers.abstract: We propose a joint sparse sample weighting and parameter estimation (SWAPE) framework that jointly optimizes model parameters and sample weights to train a model while simultaneously assigning an individual weight to each training data point. Our framework accommodates several widely used loss functions for the model parameters, including convex, weakly convex, and difference-of-convex loss, and weakly convex sparsity functions to control the complexity of the sample weights. To solve the resulting bivariate problem, we propose an alternating minimization method in which the subproblems for updating the model parameters and weights are each approximated using majorize-minimize techniques. We provide several approximation methods for the loss functions considered in this paper, and show the overall algorithm's convergence. Numerical experiments on various learning tasks and data anomaly settings demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed framework in minimizing the impact of undesirable data points compared to benchmark methods.

papers.title: Semi-strict 4-categories as enriched categories
papers.abstract: We introduce several flavours of semi-strict 4-category as enriched categories. This is done using the framework of enrichment over skew monoidal categories of Gray-categories and their associated multicategories, as developed in our previous work. We give the axioms for semi-strict 4-categories in elementary terms and describe a wide range of examples. In particular, we answer the question of what exactly Gray-categories and the higher transformations between them form: namely, a left-sharp 4-category G-Cat$^4$. In addition, we describe examples arising from braided monoidal 2-categories, monoidal Gray-categories (herein defined) and Gray-categories with structure. We use the concepts introduced here and the relationships between them to unify various concepts in the literature, such as Crans' 4-teisi. In the second part of the paper, we investigate homotopical aspects. In particular, we classify the equivalence n-cells in the left-sharp 4-category G-Cat$^4$ for each n. Using this, we show that the left-sharp skew monoidal structure on the category of Gray-categories induces a symmetric monoidal closed structure on the homotopy category of Gray-categories.

papers.title: The symmetric skew monoidal structure of Gray-categories
papers.abstract: In previous work, we constructed a closed skew monoidal structure on the category of Gray-categories and Gray-functors whose internal hom Psd(A, B) captures pseudomaps and pseudo-transformations. In the present paper we give a symmetric description of the Gray-category Psd(A,B) and use this to prove that the skew monoidal structure is symmetric skew monoidal.

papers.title: Normal approximation, moderate and large deviations for the elephant random walk with stops and random step sizes
papers.abstract: We study the elephant random walk with stops and independent positive random step sizes. Building on fixed-movement estimates, we obtain quantitative normal approximations for an empirically normalized statistic by controlling its random denominator and the independent movement clock. A permutation comparison preserves the diffusive Kolmogorov rate, while variance matching permits third-order Zolotarev estimates. We also derive self-normalized Cramér-type moderate deviations. For regularly varying step-size tails, we obtain uniform precise large deviations and establish the necessity of the diffusive and critical threshold orders. Further applications of the clock representation yield large deviation principles for Weibull-type and light-tailed step sizes, and a precise light-tailed expansion in the balanced case.

papers.title: Kobayashi completeness of pseudoconvex domains: finite type and a smooth counterexample
papers.abstract: We prove that every bounded pseudoconvex domain in $\mathbb C^N$ with $C^\infty$ boundary of finite D'Angelo one-type is Kobayashi complete. As a separate consequence of our criterion of completeness and an estimate of Diederich--Fornæss, we prove that every bounded pseudoconvex domain with real-analytic boundary is Kobayashi complete. We then show that smoothness alone does not imply completeness: there exists a bounded pseudoconvex domain in $\mathbb C^3$ with $C^\infty$ boundary and a global smooth plurisubharmonic defining function whose Kobayashi and Carathéodory distances are incomplete.

papers.title: When Momentum Helps Polyak--Ruppert Averaging
papers.abstract: Polyak--Ruppert averaging gives SGD and momentum methods the same asymptotic covariance. We characterize how fast finite runs reach it and how far they can be parallelized. For strongly convex quadratics with additive noise, we prove an online--offline bridge: the empirical risk minimizer on the samples of a tail average is one Newton step from the tail-averaged query point of any online procedure. For SGD, heavy ball, and Nesterov's method with constant momentum, this step is a boundary term at the two ends of the tail and splits the gap to the offline estimator into center, covariance, and shape errors. Necessary and sufficient conditions show that, on the least curved direction, the center error sets the pace: SGD needs $m\ggκ^2$ rounds but momentum only $m\ggκ$, where $κ$ is the condition number, so at sample size $N$ the critical batch size grows from $Θ(\sqrt{N}/κ)$ to $Θ(\sqrt{N/κ})$. The covariance error separates the momentum methods: heavy ball has relative variance excess $Θ(κ^{3/2}/m)$ along the stiffest direction, whereas Nesterov has relative error $O(\sqrtκ/m)$ in every direction. The shape error is method-independent by a Berry--Esseen bound uniform in $κ$ and batch size, so confidence intervals are valid when the other two errors vanish. We further examine how the conclusions change under heavy-tailed or state-dependent noise and clipping, and establish a first-order comparison with ERM for nonlinear Nesterov averaging under explicit conditions.

papers.title: Derived equivalence classification of twisted and generalized multifold extensions of affine type
papers.abstract: Let $B$ be a piecewise hereditary algebra of affine type over an algebraically closed field. In this paper we give a derived and stable equivalence classification of twisted multifold extensions of $B$. The types $\widetilde D$ and $\widetilde E$ are already covered by the classification for tree type. We therefore consider the remaining types $\widetilde{A}_{p,q}$. We show that the $n$th power of the Nakayama functor on the full subcategory of a transjective component determines the twist, including its action on morphisms, up to conjugacy in the derived Picard group of a hereditary algebra. Together with the hereditary derived type and the folding number, this gives a complete invariant for derived equivalence, and also for stable triangle equivalence. We then compute these conjugacy classes in the unbalanced, balanced, bypass, and Kronecker cases, keeping the finite rotation data. Finally, by the normalization theorem of Asashiba--Kimura--Nakashima--Yoshiwaki, we obtain the same classification for generalized multifold extensions with nonzero integer jump.

papers.title: Inverse Zero-Sum Problems of Erdős--Ginzburg--Ziv constant: Property C and Property D conjectures
papers.abstract: Let $C_n^r$ denote the direct sum of $r$ cyclic groups of order $n$, where $n\ge2$ and $r\ge1$. Properties C and D predict a uniform multiplicity structure for extremal zero-sum problems over $C_n^r$: every sequence of maximum length avoiding nonempty zero-sum subsequences of length at most $n$, or of length exactly $n$, respectively, should have the form $T^{n-1}$. We prove that, for every $r\ge4$ and every even $n\ge2$, each of these properties holds if and only if $n$ is a power of two. This gives negative answers to the general Property C problem posed by Gao, Hou, Schmid and Thangadurai Open Problems 1.2{GHST} in 2007, and disproves the Property D conjecture proposed by Gao and Geroldinger [Conjecture 7.2]{GG} in 2006.

papers.title: A Simple Proof of I. Chowla's Theorem on Addition of Residue Classes
papers.abstract: We present a brief, elementary proof of a striking theorem by I. Chowla on the addition of residue classes (1937) which generalizes the famous result of Cauchy and Davenport to residue classes modulo a composite.

papers.title: Smoothness of Shortest Isogenies to Frobenius Conjugates
papers.abstract: Let $E$ be chosen uniformly from the geometric isomorphism classes of supersingular elliptic curves over $\overline{\mathbb{F}}_p$ and $δ_E$ be the minimum degree of isogenies from $E$ to its Frobenius conjugate $E^{(p)}$. We establish bounds for the smoothness probability of $δ_E$ and hence affirm Wesolowski's $p^{1/3+o(1)}$ attack on the supersingular endomorphism ring problem is unconditional. We also establish a uniform asymptotic formula, with a main term expressed in terms of Dirichlet $L$ values, for the probability that a connection isogeny of degree $n$ exists between $E$ and $E^{(p)}$.

papers.title: Enhanced Dissipation by Transport Noise for Stochastic $p(x)$-Laplace Equations
papers.abstract: We are concerned with dissipation enhancement by divergence-free transport noise for stochastic \(p(x)\)-Laplace equations on \(\mathbb T^d\), \(d\ge2\). Spatially variable growth removes homogeneous scaling and produces two flux growth regimes. For periodic log-Hölder continuous exponents satisfying \(2<p^-\le p^+<\infty\), we first establish global variational well-posedness and the exact energy identity in the natural dual spaces. Under the additional condition \(p^+<2d/(d-2)\) when \(d\ge3\), we then prove averaged algebraic decay with any prescribed coefficient, uniformly on bounded zero-mean \(L^2\) balls, by estimating the two flux powers separately. A deterministic lower bound yields strict averaged comparison with the unperturbed flow at prescribed positive times on shells with bounded gradient modular. We also prove optimality of the modular coercivity exponent \(p^+\) near zero. Finally, combining these estimates with intervalwise noise acceleration from the constant-exponent theory gives exponential decay in mean square and almost surely, with moments of the random prefactors bounded uniformly on the initial-data ball. For the exponential estimates, the noise depends on the prescribed rate and moment order; its intensity is fixed in time and its frequency range increases.

papers.title: Quantized slow blowup dynamics for the energy-critical Schrödinger map flow
papers.abstract: We study the Cauchy problem for the energy-critical Schrödinger map into the 2-sphere: \[ \partial_{t}u = u\timesΔu, \quad (t,x)\in\mathbb{R}^{1+2}, \quad u(t,x)\in\mathbb{S}^2 \] for equivariant initial data of homotopy degree $k=1$. Given any integer $L\in\mathbb{N}_+$, we exhibit a set of initial data arbitrarily close to the ground state harmonic map in the energy norm such that the corresponding solution blows up in finite time with a quantized rate \[ λ(t)\sim \frac{\left(T-t\right)^L}{\left|\log(T-t)\right|^{\frac{2L}{2L-1}}} \quad\mbox{as}\ \ t\uparrow T. \] Our proof is inspired by the techniques developed for the energy-critical harmonic map heat flow in a similar context by Raphaël and Schweyer [Anal. PDE 7 (2014), 1713--1805]. However, its adaptation to a Schrödinger-type equation requires the introduction of a new energy-Virial-Morawetz Lyapunov functional tailored to quantized slow blowup dynamics.

papers.title: A Half-Constant Upper Bound for Chowla's Cosine Problem
papers.abstract: Let lambda(n) denote the infimum of -min_x sum_{a in A} cos(ax) over all sets A of n positive integers. While the classical Sidon-difference construction yields lambda(n) <= (1 + o(1))sqrt(n)/2, we construct sets achieving a leading constant of 1/2: lambda(n) <= (1/2)sqrt(n) + O(n^(1/4)sqrt(log n)), establishing limsup_{n->infinity} lambda(n)/sqrt(n) <= 1/2. This construction combines a two-sided Sidon square identity, a Singer difference set, a Fejer-kernel majorant, a parity-biased deletion, and an exact-cardinality probabilistic selection. We also provide an L^4 criterion and a multiplicity bound constraining any construction with a smaller leading constant. In the opposite direction, we incorporate the L^1 norm into Bedert's boundary estimate with an explicit constant, yielding two lower bounds for f_A(x) = sum_{a in A} cos(ax): (1) -min f_A >= cn^(1/4) for every n-element set A subset of [1, Cn]; and (2) (-min f_A)^3 ||f_A||_1^2 >= cn for every n-element set A subset of N. The second bound recovers the 1/5 exponent of Bedert and Shankar and improves it whenever ||f_A||_1 is small relative to -min f_A. Numerical values of the construction are reported up to |A| = 25,440.

papers.title: Non-algebraicity of the Lawson surfaces $ξ_{k,l}$
papers.abstract: We prove that every Lawson surface $ξ_{k,l}\subset\mathbb S^3$ of genus $kl>1$ is non-algebraic: any real polynomial vanishing on $ξ_{k,l}$ vanishes identically on $\mathbb S^3$. This answers a question posed by Hsiang in 1967 and proves Lawson's 1970 conjecture for $ξ_{2,2}$. The proof uses a reflection principle for the monodromy of the associated family of flat connections.

papers.title: Pointwise improvement of the error term in the higher rank hyperbolic lattice counting problem
papers.abstract: We prove an upper bound for the error term in the higher rank hyperbolic lattice counting problem for ${\hbox{SL}(n, \mathbb{Z})}$. Blomer and Lutsko achieved recently a significant improvement of previous known results by Duke--Rudnick--Sarnak and Gorodnik--Nevo--Yehoshua. We deduce an improved upper bound for the error which holds for almost all pairs $z,w \in {\hbox{SL}(n, \mathbb{R})}$. We also derive a $Ω$-result for the error term, in the spirit of Phillips--Rudnick.

papers.title: A Half-Space Theorem for the Allen--Cahn Equation in All Dimensions
papers.abstract: We prove that, in every dimension, a bounded, non-constant entire solution of the Allen--Cahn equation whose zero set is contained in a half-space is a one-dimensional heteroclinic solution.

papers.title: Fourier quasicrystals with positive integer masses are sections of Lee-Yang cycles
papers.abstract: We prove that Fourier quasicrystal measures with positive integer masses are precisely the nonzero real sections of effective Lee-Yang cycles by matrices with positive maximal minors, with masses given by weighted local intersection degrees. For Delone support, the reduced support of the cycle can be chosen strict. For unit masses, the cycle can be chosen reduced, with local intersection degree one at every root. Every integer-mass FQ measure has support equal to the common complex zero set of finitely many real-valued trigonometric polynomials. These results answer Questions (1), (2), and (4) of Alon, Kummer, Kurasov, and Vinzant. We recover a finite-dimensional torus from the spectrum and prove that its canonical analytic set is algebraic. A support-height theorem for holonomic sequences provides a linear spectral bound, from which we reconstruct the complex branches and their integer coefficients using fiber moments. Singular sections carry their natural local intersection degrees; discarding these can destroy the Fourier quasicrystal property.

papers.title: Sharp noncommutative Hilbert and Riesz inequalities: classification and spectral corrections
papers.abstract: For every $1<p<\infty$, with $p^*=\max\{p,p/(p-1)\}$, we determine the sharp Hilbert norm $C_p=\cot(π/(2p^*))$ on $L^p(\mathbb{R};\mathcal{S}_p)$ and the sharp uniform bound $D_p=\csc(π/p)$ for retained and strict Riesz projections of maximal subdiagonal algebras in finite tracial von Neumann algebras. The Hilbert value is also the common Fourier--Schur completely bounded norm. For finite matrices, a nonnegative logarithmic determinant defect connects Heinävaara's tracial joint spectral measure to eigenvalues. The resulting transfer identity classifies finite signed real ridge inequalities on nilpotents and identifies their least additive eigenvalue corrections. A dual theorem characterizes weak-* limits of weighted angular measures of finite nilpotents. In general finite tracial algebras, separate positive-kernel and sharp determinant-covariance comparisons yield the Riesz bounds. Consequences include the sharp Volterra constant, Riesz--Titchmarsh and shifted-transform formulas, joint real-pencil norms, and exact triangular and operator-valued Fourier Riesz norms.

papers.title: Geometry-Dependent Approximation for Non-Monotone $k$-Submodular Maximization
papers.abstract: We study the maximization of a nonnegative $k$-submodular function, not assumed monotone, in which each of $n$ elements receives one of $k\ge2$ labels or stays unselected and the selected elements must satisfy a constraint. For a compact convex down-closed region $P\subseteq[0,1]^n$ of fractional selection vectors, the diagonal level $ζ(P)=\max\{t\in[0,1]:t(1,\ldots,1)\in P\}$ is the largest selection probability that can be given to all elements at once; it equals $r/n$ for a uniform matroid of rank $r$, and $ζ(P)=1$ means that the constraint is vacuous. We give approximation coefficients that increase continuously with $ζ$. They come from one inequality for the multilinear extension of the objective: the algorithm computes an action without querying the objective, and objective feedback gives a comparator-independent update direction. For $k\ge3$, feasibility of the action reduces to three polynomial inequalities in one variable; for $k=2$ the profile is closed form. At $ζ=0$ the coefficients are $0.4456\ldots$ for $k=2$ and $0.4541\ldots$ for every $k\ge3$. For every finite $k\ge3$ they reach $1/2$ above an explicit level, which is $0.4026\ldots$ for $k=3,4,5$, and at $ζ=1$ they reach $1/2$ for $k=2$, $(\sqrt{17}-3)/2$ for $k=3,4$, and $k/(2k-1)$ for $k\ge5$. Online linear optimization gives $O(\sqrt T)$ approximate regret, with gradient feedback or with value queries made after each action. The coefficients carry over to matroids, with expected and high-probability guarantees, and to any fixed number of knapsacks: the zero-level coefficients hold on every instance, and the larger ones when items are small or when prefix enumeration keeps the diagonal level on one branch. For one budget the enumeration exponent is $O(1/\varepsilon)$.

papers.title: Error Estimates in Physics-Informed Neural Networks to Heat-Wave Fluid-Structure Interactive System
papers.abstract: We study a physics-informed neural network (PINN) approximation of a coupled PDE system that models the interaction between fluid and elastic dynamics. The canonical heat-wave model considered here couples a parabolic and a hyperbolic equation through transmission conditions on a fixed boundary interface, and serves as a prototype for the Stokes-elastic systems that arises in real world applications. This coupling makes the error analysis more delicate than that for a single PDE. We bound the error between the exact and PINN solutions by the associated PINN residuals, and we moreover prove that the generalization error is controlled by the training error, the number of quadrature points, and the size of the network. {To the best of our knowledge}, these are the first error estimates for a PINN approximation of a coupled fluid-structure interaction PDE system. We also show that numerical experiments with respect to a given test problem.

papers.title: Positive sectional curvature on a family of exotic fifteen-sphere
papers.abstract: We construct metrics of strictly positive sectional curvature on at least 508 pairwise nondiffeomorphic exotic fifteen-spheres, without prescribing orientations. The construction begins with quaternionic line bundles over $\mathbb{H}P^2\times S^4$. Surgery along a Hopf fiber gives homotopy spheres with specified equivariant two-disk presentations. A calculation on the surgery filling distinguishes 1015 nonstandard oriented smooth types. We construct positively curved quotient metrics on both disks, match their boundary data under the prescribed attaching map, and smooth the seam by averaging the inverse tangential metrics. The connection estimates and the smoothing argument are proved directly for every two-plane. Thus the curvature conclusion does not require a compatible-disk theorem from the eleven-dimensional construction or an external curvature-gluing theorem. We give quantitative parameter bounds and specify the auxiliary choices for the first nontrivial member after fixing its smooth gauge family.

papers.title: Intersecting integer partitions: star bounds and counterexamples at every scale
papers.abstract: Two integer partitions $t$-intersect if they have at least $t$ common parts, counted with multiplicity. We study the largest $t$-intersecting families of integer partitions of $n$ into exactly $k$ positive parts. The canonical $t$-star consists of the partitions containing at least $t$ ones. Applying Kupavskii's weak-spread theorem, we prove that this star is largest whenever $n\ge Ak^3$, for every fixed $A>24$ and all sufficiently large $k$, uniformly over $1\le t<k$. We also give counterexamples to Borg's conjecture at every intersection scale: for all sufficiently large $k$ and for every $1\le t\le \lceil k/4\rceil$, we describe $t$-intersecting families on integer partitions of $n=\lfloor tk^2/3\rfloor$ into $k$ parts which are strictly larger than the corresponding canonical stars. Moreover we present a family of counterexamples to Borg's conjectures about largest $t$-intersecting families of integer partitions of $n$ without restricting the number of parts.

papers.title: The Work of Hong Wang
papers.abstract: Hong Wang has made several tremendous contributions to harmonic analysis and geometric measure theory. On the 23rd of July 2026, she was awarded the Fields Medal. In this short article we shall focus on her work on the Kakeya problem and other problems related to the Fourier transform. We will try to put her work in historical context and present a small selection of her contributions to harmonic analysis.

papers.title: Improving the James-Stein estimator via q-number shrinkage
papers.abstract: For estimating the mean vector of a $p$-variate normal distribution ($p \ge 3$) under quadratic loss, the positive-part James-Stein estimator dominates the original Jame-Stein estimator though it suffers from a non-smooth thresholding boundary. In this paper, we first express the shrinkage factor of the positive-part estimator using an infinite series. Truncating this series at a finite degree $m$ allows us to interpret the factor as a special case of $q$-numbers. Leveraging these $q$-numbers parameterized by a positive real index $m$, we propose a novel smooth estimator. We prove that the proposed estimator dominates the original James-Stein estimator for any dimension $p \ge 3$, provided the truncation parameter satisfies $m \ge 0.95\sqrt{p-2}$.

papers.title: Unique continuation, nonexistence and bubbling for the critical $p$-Laplace equation in the plane
papers.abstract: For $1<p<2$ we prove weak and strong unique continuation properties for the solutions to $Δ_pu+f(u)=0$ in a planar domain, with $f$ continuous and such that $|f(s)|\leq C|s|^{p-1}$: a solution vanishing on an open set vanishes identically, and so does a solution vanishing to infinite order at a single point. We can therefore make progress towards a proof of some long-standing nonexistence results available only for $p=2$, such as a celebrated one of Esteban and Lions, establishing here that for the critical $p$-Laplace equation with zero Dirichlet boundary condition on a half-plane, there are no nontrivial finite energy solutions. In the plane, unique continuation thus provides the missing ingredient for a generalisation to the $p$-Laplacian operator of a classical result of Struwe on the bubble-profile decomposition of possibly sign-changing Palais-Smale sequences associated to the Brezis-Nirenberg problem, which remains open in dimension $N\geq3$ for $p\neq2$. We obtain a characterisation of their loss of compactness in terms of the finite energy solutions of $Δ_pu+|u|^{p^*-2}u=0$ in $\mathbb R^2$.

papers.title: Lower Bounds for Localised Moments of Automorphic L-functions
papers.abstract: In this article, we describe a method to obtain lower bounds for the $2k$th moment of values of $L$-functions localised at the central point for all real $k > 0$. In particular, for the families of quadratic twists of self-dual irreducible unitary cuspidal automorphic representations of $\operatorname{GL}_2(\mathbb{A}_{\mathbb{Q}})$ and $\operatorname{GL}_3(\mathbb{A}_{\mathbb{Q}})$ our results are new in the range $0<k<\tfrac12$.

papers.title: The Critical Line Algorithm and the Constrained LASSO: One Curve, Two Literatures
papers.abstract: Many statistical procedures compute an entire solution path rather than a single estimator. For one class the path is piecewise linear, traced corner to corner by an active-set homotopy. Two of its members coincide exactly: under $Σ=X^\top X$ and $μ=X^\top y$ the gross-exposure-constrained mean--variance program and the constrained LASSO trace the same piecewise-linear curve, and they keep doing so under arbitrary linear equality and inequality constraints. Which parameter is swept, a leverage budget or a return tilt, is not a choice the curve notices: under a homogeneous mandate the two sweeps differ by a scalar. A mandate that holds the portfolio invested costs a radial rescaling instead, and the efficient frontier is that curve rescaled; its corners pass unnoticed because the frontier is continuously differentiable where they fall. We give the map between the two parametrisations and the single way it degenerates. That mean--variance selection and the LASSO instantiate one parametric quadratic program is prior art (Gärtner, Jaggi and Maria, 2012). The Critical Line Algorithm itself lies off that route, and the correspondence established here is new. The identity is one of curves, not of statistical experiments. The map between the parametrisations is computed from the data, so the geometry of the path transfers while quantities averaged over the response do not. We cross that boundary deliberately and give the degrees of freedom of the constrained fit under arbitrary linear constraints. In the long-only, fully invested case it is the expected number of holdings away from a bound, less one.

papers.title: Graded Algebras of Modular Forms and Sign Changes of Fourier Coefficients for Eta Quotients
papers.abstract: In this paper, for $N=8,12,16,20,32$, we determine the explicit structure of the graded algebra of modular forms for $\varGamma_0(N)$ of both integral and half-integral weights, with all quadratic Dirichlet characters modulo $N$. We give explicit eta quotient generators and determine the relations among them. Using these structures, for a given weight, a level among those considered above, and a quadratic character, we obtain a basis for the corresponding space of modular forms consisting of eta quotients. Using these eta quotient bases, we obtain necessary and sufficient conditions for the periodicity of the signs of the Fourier coefficients of modular forms in three specific spaces. Finally, we determine all eta quotients in these spaces whose Fourier coefficient signs are periodic.

papers.title: Hankel-Koopman Finite-Horizon Energy Decomposition of Coupled Experimental Data: A Three-Phase Data-Driven Twin Forecasting Framework
papers.abstract: Finite-horizon prediction is challenging when observations are limited and a quantity of interest depends on several coupled nonlinear measurement channels. This paper develops a three-phase data-driven twin framework that integrates finite-horizon Hankel--Koopman energy decomposition, inverse-calibrated reconstruction using nonlinear autoregressive models with exogenous inputs, and forecast composition. Channel dynamics are identified and simulated in Hankel coefficient space, with candidate models assessed after reconstruction in physical measurement space. The resulting reduced-order model of the channel dynamics drives recursive prediction of the quantity of interest. Three theorems support the framework, establishing the energy decomposition and modal orthogonality; existence, uniqueness, and inverse stability of the auxiliary continuous inverse-calibration solution; and finite-horizon stability of the composed forecast for a fixed selected model under stated assumptions. A retrospective solar-power case study yields high correlations between predicted and reference trajectories across the considered forecast horizons, demonstrating reproduction of a constructed channels-dependent quantity of interest.

papers.title: The norm of the centered Hardy--Littlewood maximal operator
papers.abstract: We determine the exact $L^p(\mathbb{R})$ norm of the centered Hardy--Littlewood maximal operator for every $1<p<\infty$, proving that it equals $p/(p-1)$. This settles the sharp strong-type problem for the centered maximal operator on the real line. For every $p$ in this range, the norm is strictly larger than the constant associated with the critical power $|x|^{-1/p}$, thereby disproving the conjecture of Dror, Ganguli, and Strichartz that this profile determines the unrestricted norm.

papers.title: Internal congruences modulo powers of 2 for $k$-colored overpartitions into odd parts
papers.abstract: Let $\overline{po}_k(n)$ denote the number of $k$-colored overpartitions of $n$ into odd parts. For every odd number of colors, we establish infinite families of internal congruences modulo high powers of $2$. The proof proceeds by expressing the relevant difference generating functions as a fixed theta quotient multiplied by polynomials in an auxiliary function. Uniform lower bounds for the $2$-adic valuations of the polynomial coefficients then yield the stated internal congruences. These results generalize an internal congruence of Saikia, Sarma and Sellers (J. Ramanujan Math. Soc.~2025) on overpartition triples into odd parts.

papers.title: Induced Size-Ramsey Numbers of Odd Cycles via Spread Measures
papers.abstract: We prove that, for every $k\ge2$ and every sufficiently large odd $n$, the induced size--Ramsey number of $C_n$ satisfies \[ \widehat R_{\mathrm{ind}}(C_n;k)=e^{Θ(k)}n. \] This improves the previous upper bound of $e^{O(k\log k)}n$ and resolves a conjecture of Bradač, Draganić and Sudakov. We obtain this result by proving a stronger form of their odd-hole gadget conjecture: we construct a graph with $e^{O(k)}$ edges whose every $k$-edge-colouring contains a monochromatic induced odd cycle of length $O(\log k)$. Our proof develops a spread-based approach to finding induced cycles. The key idea is to place spread probability weights directly on families of candidate cycles and control their possible chords through a quadratic chord score. Combining this with random sparsification and hypergraph containers yields a sparse host graph that works for every $k$-edge-colouring.

papers.title: Airy limit for the Jack process and topological expansion
papers.abstract: For every $β>0$, we establish multi-time soft-edge moment convergence for a class of Jack processes, including the Jack--Plancherel process, a discrete $β$-analogue of Dyson Brownian motion. The limiting moments admit an absolutely convergent expansion in terms of nonnegative Brownian bridges decorated by pairs of equal and opposite jumps. At equal times, we identify this limit with the joint Laplace statistics of the Airy$_β$ process for $β\geq1$. The same Brownian expansion yields an asymptotic $β$-topological expansion of the marginal $b$-conjecture and, at $β=2$, an explicit nonnegative formula for the Witten--Kontsevich intersection numbers.

papers.title: Aperiodic random walks: uniform estimates, local limits and invariance principles
papers.abstract: We prove uniform endpoint estimates, killed local limits, and conditioned-bridge invariance principles for triangular arrays of centered, aperiodic, integer-valued random walks with uniform exponential tails. The endpoint estimates cover all nonnegative heights, while the local limits treat positive diffusive and zero endpoints. The increment law may vary with the scaling parameter.

papers.title: From Truncation to Commitment: Persistent Context in Uniform Discrete Diffusion
papers.abstract: Uniform-state discrete diffusion models update all tokens in parallel while keeping every position revisable. Even when the commonly used top-$p$ rule leaves only one candidate at a position, that choice affects only the current reverse step and can be revised at the next sampling step. We ask what changes when selected hypotheses instead become persistent context for later predictions. We therefore propose committed reveal sampling (CRS), a training-free sampler that stores selected argmax tokens and inserts them into subsequent model inputs. Our analysis separates persistent context from truncation. Within one reverse step, adaptive top-$p$, randomized or not, reproduces the update induced by a visible token only when a likelihood-ratio ordering holds, while in a simple latent-mode model, keeping the selected token visible helps later parallel predictions agree on the same sequence-level choice. Empirically, paired experiments on Duo-distilled then separate this persistent effect from single-step top-$p$ restriction and scalar temperature scaling. Under the same finalization rule, CRS without top-$p$ truncation reaches lower generative perplexity (GenPPL) than fixed $p=0.95$ and $p=0.9$ baselines across budgets of 8--64 function evaluations (NFE). At 64 NFE, the comparison at matched unigram entropy also gives lower GenPPL for CRS, shifting the GenPPL--entropy tradeoff under this metric. Base Duo shows the same direction in a descriptive comparison, while other diversity and continuation metrics can rank these operating points differently. A distributional distance to held-out text (SOL) under a fixed GPT-2-Large representation also decreases with persistent context at the same late top-$p$ threshold. These results identify support restriction and persistent context as distinct controls of that tradeoff.

papers.title: The high dimensional monostable reaction-diffusion equation with free boundary and radial symmetry
papers.abstract: We consider the radially symmetric version of the reaction-diffusion equation $u_t-dΔu=f(u)$ with a monostable nonlinearity $f$, viewed as a model for the spreading of a species with population range $r<h(t)$ and density $u(t,r)$ ($r=|x|$), where the free boundary $r=h(t)$ is governed by $u(t,h(t))=δ>0$ and $h'(t)=-d u_r(t,h(t))/δ$. For the one-dimensional case ($N=1$), Du \cite{DN} proved that when $δ\in(0,1)$, spreading occurs: $u\to1$ locally uniformly in $\mathbb{R}$, $h(t)\to\infty$, and $\lim_{t\to\infty}[h(t)-c_*t]=\tilde{h}\in\mathbb{R}$ with no logarithmic shift. In the present paper we consider $N\ge2$ and establish a complete trichotomy: spreading for $δ\in(0,1)$; transition for $δ=1$, where $u\to1$ uniformly on $[0,h(t)]$ and $h(t)\to h_\infty\in(0,\infty)$; and vanishing for $δ>1$, where $h(t)\to0$ and $u\toδ$ uniformly on $[0,h(t)]$. For the spreading regime, by constructing sharp upper and lower solutions, we prove that the solution converges globally to the semi-wave profile and reveal a logarithmic shift of the form $ \lim_{t\to\infty}\big[h(t)-c_*t+c_N(δ)\log t\big]=\hat{h}\in\mathbb{R}$, with the coefficient $c_N(δ)>0$ satisfying $ \lim_{δ\to0}c_N(δ)=d(N-1)/c_0$, where $d(N-1)/c_0$ is the shift coefficient for the high-dimensional radial pushed-case Cauchy problem. These results reveal the connection to the spreading behavior modeled by the corresponding Cauchy problem.

papers.title: Tensor-Train Isogeometric Analysis for Large-Scale Three-Dimensional Linear Elasticity
papers.abstract: This work develops tensor-train (TT) formulations for solving large-scale three-dimensional linear elasticity problems discretized by isogeometric analysis. By exploiting the tensor-product structure of the basis functions and the low-rank structure of geometry-dependent coefficient fields, the stiffness operator, mass operator, force vector, and displacement solution are represented in TT format. Two solution strategies are investigated: a block-operator formulation, in which the coupled elasticity operator is stored as separated TT blocks, and a single-operator formulation, in which the full coupled system is stored as one monolithic TT operator. A matrix-free three-field TT conjugate-gradient solver is introduced for the block formulation, while AMEn is used for the single-operator formulation. Numerical examples demonstrate substantial compression of both operators and solutions compared with conventional sparse full-grid representations, showing that TT-based formulations provide an efficient and scalable approach for large-scale three-dimensional elasticity simulations.

papers.title: Internal Reasoning and Consistency in Reflective Grounded Arithmetic
papers.abstract: Reflective Grounded Arithmetic (RGA) is a paracomplete arithmetic allowing direct expression of any general-recursive computation. Every RGA term is a program and truth is grounded evaluation, with a proof certificate at each universal quantifier. This paper shows, in a machine-checked Isabelle/HOL development, that such a system is powerful enough to carry out its own metamathematics. A fuel-indexed decider of RGA's grounded semantics and checkers for RGA's proofs are compiled primitive-recursive RGA terms. RGA proves internally that its decider never affirms $0 = 1$, and that every well-formed term it affirms has an RGA proof accepted by a transparent test. RGA proves that, for each valid RGA proof, its conclusion is true. RGA proves that each grounded-true well-formed term is provable. RGA proves that no proof in either of two decided classes of RGA proofs derives $0 = 1$. Gödel's incompleteness theorems hold for RGA, but their proofs must be adapted. In RGA an implication $A \rightarrow B$ is strictly stronger than an entailment $A \vdash B$: RGA discharges a hypothesis only when it can prove the hypothesis decided, a restriction needed to defuse Curry's paradox. RGA's implication is material and RGA has the disjunction property, so RGA proves no implication between ungrounded sentences. The implications that the textbook proof of Gödel's second theorem uses are of this kind and fail, but the entailments and rules it uses hold: Gödel's proof survives as entailments. RGA does not prove its consistency sentence $\mathit{Con}$: RGA carries out Gödel's argument internally, with a decided proof predicate and explicit proof transformers, and only the last step, that RGA does not prove $0 = 1$, is left to HOL. RGA also proves its own second incompleteness theorem as an entailment from $\mathit{Con}$, and as a single sentence quantified over proofs.

papers.title: A Near-Optimal Lower Bound for $\ell_p$-Subspace Embeddings, $1\leq p<2$
papers.abstract: For $d \geq 2$, $p \geq 1$ and $ε> 0$, let $N_p(d,ε)$ be the smallest integer $N$ such that for every integer $n$ and every $A\in\mathbb{R}^{n\times d}$, there exists a matrix $Φ\in\mathbb{R}^{N\times n}$ satisfying $(1-ε)\lVert Ax\rVert_p\leq \lVertΦA x\rVert_p\leq (1+ε)\lVert Ax\rVert_p$ for all $x\in\mathbb{R}^d$. For every constant $p\geq 1$ with $p\not\in 2\mathbb{Z}$, when $d\gtrsim_p \log(1/ε)$, the bound \[ N_p(d,ε) \gtrsim_{p} \frac{d}{ε^2 \operatorname{polylog}(d/ε)} \] is established. This improves the previous lower bound $Ω(1/(ε^2\operatorname{polylog}(1/ε)))$ due to Li et al. (SICOMP 2021) and is optimal up to logarithmic factors for $1\leq p<2$. The central technical idea originated from ChatGPT 6 Pro.

papers.title: Reducibility of linear representations, free ideals, and Kippenhahn's conjecture
papers.abstract: This paper presents a comprehensive study of the characteristic polynomial of matrix tuples and finite dimensional group representations. Among other things, several key concepts are introduced, including the minimal polynomial, algebraic extension, spectral index and multiplicity, and characteristic graph. Notably, this framework leads to a complete resolution of Kippenhahn's conjecture by providing necessary and sufficient conditions for its validity.

papers.title: Ultra-high-dimensional spot support screening in continuous-time regression
papers.abstract: We study variable screening for high-frequency continuous-time regression, targeting the support of the spot regression coefficient. Under coordinatewise truncation and finite-variation jumps, uniform entrywise bounds for local correlation estimates yield the rate $\{(\log p)/n\}^{α/(2α+1)}$ under a local averaged $α$-Hölder condition, up to confidence and grid factors. These bounds imply sure screening for the marginal support. To retain the regression support under local dependence, we propose partial-residual spot iterative screening with pathwise Lepski adaptation. Under sparse eigenvalues and standardized beta-min, the procedure has the sure screening property and requires only correlation columns associated with the current active set. A list-size minimax lower bound applies to both support targets and matches the localization and multiplicity order of the marginal-screening bound when $\log(p/d)\asymp\log p$. Simulations and a high-frequency factor application illustrate the procedures.

papers.title: The Tamed Subgradient Unadjusted Langevin Algorithm beyond Convexity
papers.abstract: We study the problem of sampling from target distributions whose potentials are simultaneously non-smooth, subject to superlinear gradient growth, and non-convex. We introduce the Subgradient Tamed Unadjusted Langevin Algorithm (SG-TULA), a discretisation of the Langevin diffusion that operates directly on subgradients, without relying on computationally demanding smoothing procedures. To handle the superlinear regime, taming techniques are employed to produce a stable, explicit scheme. We derive non-asymptotic convergence bounds in Wasserstein-2 distance, with all constants tracked explicitly in terms of dimension and inverse temperature, improving upon the currently known rates for subgradient-based Langevin algorithms. We further provide excess risk estimates for the associated optimisation problem. We verify the assumptions, with explicit constants, for the regularized pretraining potential of a LLM in the GPT-2 lineage and the boosted coordinate-wise variant of SG-TULA pretrains the former competitively against finetuned AdamW and Muon, for which no comparable non-asymptotic guarantees are presently available.

papers.title: Exchangeable Testing Against an Unknown Benchmark
papers.abstract: We generate infinite binary exchangeable sequences by sequential comparison of data points against a latent benchmark. Assuming a prior distribution of the benchmark rank \(R_0\) within an unobserved group of players, we set up the Bayesian machinery which determines the posterior distribution of the running rank \(R_n\) in purely combinatorial terms, by counting insertion slots in a uniformly random ranking. This yields an explicit predictive probability of winning against the benchmark, which is a rational function of the counts. We identify some cases where the predictive probability has particularly simple form, notably a tournament related to the Topp--Leone distribution. The running benchmark rank is a Pólya urn with random initial composition, and its normalised value converges to a latent strength variable with polynomial density. In a projective time scale, the fluctuations of the normalised rank about this limit are Brownian, with the Wright--Fisher coefficient frozen at the limit, while the associated recurrent up-down Markov chain on a high level $n$ of the Pascal graph is approximated by a Wright--Fisher diffusion with a nonlinear drift expressed through the prior density.

papers.title: Bounds on Odd and Odd-Even Induced Subgraphs
papers.abstract: Let $G$ be an $n$-vertex graph and let $\ell:V(G)\to\mathbb{F}_2$ prescribe degree parities. A set $S\subseteq V(G)$ is $\ell$-admissible if every $v\in S$ has degree congruent to $\ell(v)$ modulo $2$ in $G[S]$. Let $h_\ell(G)$ be the maximum order of an $\ell$-admissible set, set $f_{\mathrm{oe}}(G):=\min_\ell h_\ell(G)$, and write $f_o(G):=h_{\mathbf{1}}(G)$, where $\mathbf{1}(v)=1$ for every $v\in V(G).$ We prove three main results for graphs without isolated vertices. First, by extending Zeng's odd-cut method to arbitrary parity prescriptions and introducing a one-sided completion lemma, we show that $h_\ell(G)\ge 2n/11$ for every $\ell$. Consequently, $f_{\mathrm{oe}}(G)\ge 2n/11$, improving the previous bound $2n/21$. Second, for bipartite graphs we derive lower bounds on $f_o(G)$ in terms of the $\mathbb{F}_2$-rank of the bipartite adjacency matrix and combine them to obtain \[ f_o(G)\ge \left(\frac14+\frac1{256}\right)n=\frac{65}{256}n. \] Thus, in the bipartite case, the factor $2$ in Scott's bound $f_o(G)\ge n/(2χ(G))$ can be replaced by $128/65<2$. Finally, a fourth-moment argument gives, for $α=α(G)\ge2$ and $δ(G)\ge 1$, \[ f_o(G)\ge \fracα{2}+\frac{\log_3α}{8} -\frac14\log_3\log_3\sqrtα. \] We also construct bipartite graphs satisfying \[ f_o(G)\le \frac{α(G)}2+\log_2\!\bigl(α(G)+1\bigr)+\frac12, \] showing that the logarithmic additive improvement over Scott's bound $f_o(G)\geα(G)/2$ has the optimal order of magnitude.

papers.title: SpectONet: A Physics-Guided Spectral Deep Operator Network for Euler-Bernoulli Beam Dynamics
papers.abstract: This paper proposes a novel physics-guided spectral deep operator network, termed SpectONet, for solving Euler-Bernoulli beam (EBB) vibration problems. The proposed framework integrates the operator-learning capability of DeepONet with physics-informed constraints and Chebyshev-Gauss-Lobatto (CGL) sensor placement. Unlike conventional DeepONet frameworks, which commonly employ uniformly distributed sensors, SpectONet uses nonuniform spectral sensor locations with a higher concentration of points near the domain boundaries. This sampling strategy improves the finite-dimensional representation of boundary-sensitive structural responses while requiring only a limited number of branch-network inputs. The governing beam equation, together with the associated initial and boundary conditions, is incorporated into the training objective to promote physically consistent and generalizable predictions. Numerical experiments on three EBB vibration problems demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed framework. Comparisons with strong baseline models such as Vanilla DeepONet, PI-DeepONet, PINN, and CNN-UNet show that SpectONet consistently achieves lower prediction errors across all considered evaluation metrics. In particular, SpectONet achieves an average reduction of approximately 79% in the mean relative $\mathcal{L}_2$ error compared with the best-performing baseline across the three benchmark problems. These results demonstrate the effectiveness of SpectONet as an accurate physics-guided operator-learning framework for structural vibration analysis.

papers.title: A case for clubs
papers.abstract: We present several remarks on cardinal coefficients associated with the generalized Baire space for an inaccessible cardinal kappa. Our inquiry originates in the work of van der Vlugt arXiv:2307.14118 . We provide evidence that the appropriate coefficients to consider are those determined by binary relations restricted to a club. In other words, we make a case for the systematic use of clubs.

papers.title: On mappings with Jacobian one
papers.abstract: We show that the set $A(n, d)$ of polynomial automorphisms $F : \Bbb C^n \to \Bbb C^n$ of degree at most $d$ and with $Jac(F ) = 1$ is Zariski closed. In particular every irreducible component of the set $A(n,d)$ of polynomial mappings with Jacobian $1$ is either composed with polynomial automorphisms or (generically) with counterexamples to the Jacobian Conjecture. Moreover every such component has dimension at least $n^2-1.$ In particular if the set $X(n,d)$ is irreducible, and $n\ge 3, d\ge 7$, then a generic element of this set is a counterexample to the Jacobian Conjecture.

papers.title: Current-Sheet Formation in Electron Magnetohydrodynamics with Split Fractional Dissipation
papers.abstract: Thin current sheets are central small-scale structures in electron magnetohydrodynamics (EMHD), closely associated with energy dissipation and fast magnetic reconnection at electron scales. We study their formation numerically in a $2\frac{1}{2}$-dimensional EMHD system on a periodic domain with split fractional dissipation, where the magnetic potential and the vertical magnetic component are damped separately. The local theory is governed by a symmetric combined damping balance, but the numerical onset of small-scale growth need not follow this symmetry. A scaling analysis identifies the out-of-plane current as the primary concentration observable, since it is regularized only through the magnetic-potential equation. Using a validated Fourier pseudospectral exponential time-differencing solver with resolution-controlled diagnostics, we find a clear decay/concentration dichotomy. The onset boundary is markedly asymmetric: current-sheet formation appears to be controlled mainly by damping of the magnetic potential, rather than by the combined damping strength. The analyticity strip collapses to the grid scale, the concentration sharpens under grid refinement, and the observed growth is consistent with an energy-critical self-similar rate, with exponent near three. These experiments indicate that magnetic-potential damping is the apparent binding constraint for current-sheet concentration, refining the symmetric sum picture.

papers.title: On dualizability and invertibility in the higher Morita category
papers.abstract: We prove a conjecture of Lurie characterizing $(n+1)$-dualizability in higher Morita categories of $\mathbb{E}_n$-algebras in terms of dualizability over certain factorization homologies. A key ingredient is a higher Morita category based on the recently developed framework of pointless factorization algebras of Karlsson and the first author. We also verify an invertibility conjecture of Brochier--Jordan--Safranov--Snyder as an immediate corollary of our main result. Moreover, we prove a relative version of the dualizability conjecture, yielding a new criterion for relative/twisted field theories. We give some examples, including Dirichlet and Neumann relative theories.

papers.title: Roots of polynomials over semirings and hyperfields
papers.abstract: We lay the groundwork for the theory of roots of polynomials over semirings and hyperfields, employing a property of a ``surpassing relation'' $\preceq$ on semirings and hyperfields that we call strong $\preceq$-reversibility. There are three kinds of roots generalizing roots in classical algebraic theory --- ``null roots,'' ``$\preceq$-roots,'' and ``factor-roots.'' The theory works best when all null roots are also factor-roots. The ensuing results include the fundamental theorem of algebra for pairs, asserting that tangible polynomials with enough roots ``$\preceq$-split,'' sometimes uniquely, into linear factors. We also examine to what extent polynomials are determined by their null roots. Next, we obtain $\preceq$-roots over extension systems, and construct integrally closed systems over various base systems, including hyperfield systems over a group. The point is that whereas hyper-polynomials behave poorly, polynomial systems remain strongly $\preceq$-reversible, so one can compose chains of $\preceq$-finitely spanned extensions. Next, we introduce real pairs, focusing on square roots and quadratic closure. In the appendix we recast the theory by considering equivalence classes of tangible polynomials which agree on almost all substitutions.

papers.title: Improved bounds on the b-chromatic number using the independence and chromatic numbers
papers.abstract: Finding a minimum proper vertex coloring is $\NP$-hard and hard to approximate. $B$-coloring is used as a heuristic approach to graph coloring. A b-coloring of a graph $G$ is a proper vertex coloring where each color class contains at least one vertex (a b-vertex) adjacent to a vertex in every other color class. The maximum number of colors in such a coloring is the b-chromatic number, ${\rm b}(G)$. A ${\rm b}^{\ast}$-coloring is a variation in which a b-vertex is adjacent to a b-vertex in every other color class. We employ the ${\rm b}^{\ast}$-coloring to prove that any $n$-vertex graph $G$ with independence number at most $t$ satisfies ${\rm b}(G) \leq [(t-1)n+tχ(G)]/(2t-1)$. This bound extends the bounds of Kouider and Zaker (2006) and Alkhateeb and Kohl (2011) and significantly improves the bound in terms of the clique partition number. We show that this bound is sharp for all $t\geq 2$ and $χ(G)\geq 3$. Furthermore, we provide a refined bound based on the maximum number of vertex-disjoint independent sets of size $t$. Finally, we prove ${\rm b}^{\ast}(G) \leq [(t-2)n+(t-1)χ(G)]/(2t-3)$ for all $K_{1,t}$-free graphs $G$, a significant improvement over the analogous bound for ${\rm b}(G)$.

papers.title: Isoperimetric and total curvature inequalities in Cartan-Hadamard manifolds with nullity
papers.abstract: Using the Chern-Gauss-Bonnet theorem, we establish a sharp inequality for the total Gauss-Kronecker curvature of convex hypersurfaces in Cartan-Hadamard manifolds $M^n$ with nullity index at least $n-3$. Consequently, the Euclidean isoperimetric inequality extends to $M^n$, which proves the Cartan-Hadamard conjecture for these spaces.

papers.title: Convergence Analysis via ODE Approach for Convex Optimization with Linear Equality Constraints
papers.abstract: This paper studies the continuous-time dynamics of primal-dual algorithms for linearly constrained convex optimization problems and provides a quantitative convergence analysis using the Lyapunov functions. With the growing prevalence of sparse and low-rank models, large-scale problems involving nonsmooth objective functions have become increasingly important. Our approach addresses nonsmooth and nonstrong convex objective functions, which is particularly effective in extending classical accelerated methods to broader large-scale optimization problems. Building upon the ordinary differential equation (ODE) approach inspired by the recent work on Nesterov's acceleration methods, we extend the analysis to an ODE associated with an optimization problem with linear equality constraints. Furthermore, to relax strong assumptions, we introduce two geometric conditions the Flatness condition and the Growth condition and derive explicit convergence rates depending on the local geometry and algorithmic parameter. When the objective function is convex and the Lagrangian satisfies the Flatness condition, an appropriate parameter choice yields a worst-case convergence rate of O(1/t^2). Furthermore, incorporating the Growth condition guarantees this worst-case rate of O(1/t^2) for any function satisfying these assumptions if and only if the parameter is chosen above a suitable threshold; under this condition, even faster convergence can be achieved. For the algorithmic construction, a numerical scheme is derived by discretizing the proposed ODE. We also investigate the influence of algorithm parameters and provide insights into their optimal selection. Finally, preliminary numerical experiments are provided to validate the consistency with the theoretical results.

papers.title: A Banach space that distinguishes two maximal operators
papers.abstract: Maz'ya and Shaposhnikova introduced a non-classical maximal operator $M^\diamond$ as the maximal convolution with the vector-valued signum kernel truncated to centered balls. We construct a translation-invariant Banach space of locally integrable functions on which $M^\diamond$ is bounded, but the sharp maximal operator $M^\sharp$ is not. This answers one of Maz'ya's questions from a collection of 75 open problems in analysis.

papers.title: On the Face Map of the Admissible Set With Parahoric Level
papers.abstract: To each face $\mathcal{F}$ of the coweight polytope $\mathcal{P}_μ$, we associate a subset $\text{Adm}(μ)_{\mathcal{F}}$ of the $μ$-admissible set $\text{Adm}(μ)$, which we refer to as a face of $\text{Adm}(μ)$. This gives rise to a face decomposition of $\text{Adm}(μ)$. As an application, we give a complete description of the fibers of the face map $|Δ|^f$ defined by Pappas-Rapoport and prove that the face map is surjective.

papers.title: Proximal Limited-Memory Quasi-Newton Methods for Nonsmooth Nonconvex Optimization
papers.abstract: We propose a regularized proximal quasi-Newton method (RPQN) for minimizing the sum of a continuously differentiable, possibly nonconvex function and a proper, lower semicontinuous, prox-bounded, possibly nonconvex regularizer. The method uses adaptive quadratic regularization and limited-memory quasi-Newton models. We establish global convergence under weak assumptions, without requiring global Lipschitz continuity of the gradient, and prove convergence of the entire sequence, with rates, under the Kurdyka-Lojasiewicz property. To solve the proximal subproblems efficiently, we exploit compact limited-memory representations and derive a compact representation of the Kleinmichel rank-one update, which preserves positive definiteness under the same condition as BFGS. Numerical experiments on logistic and Student's regression demonstrate competitive performance and the effectiveness of the proposed approach.

papers.title: Higher-order Persistence Diagrams
papers.abstract: Persistent homology tracks when topological features appear and disappear across filtered data and represents the lifetime of each feature by a persistence interval. In multiple instance learning, when the instances in a bag use filtrations over the same ordered parameter space, we can compare relationships between persistence intervals across instances. No existing method is designed to aggregate collections of persistence diagrams in multiple instance learning into a single persistence diagram of implications between intervals. We introduce higher-order persistence diagrams to represent relationships between persistence intervals and recursively construct each higher-order persistence interval from a pair of lower-order persistence intervals. We then aggregate these relationships across the persistence diagrams in a bag. Explicit construction of this aggregate is computationally expensive, so we introduce harmonic aggregation to compute coordinates of the aggregate from the lower-order persistence diagrams without explicitly constructing it. Computing a harmonic aggregation coordinate has lower asymptotic computational complexity than explicitly constructing the aggregate. We evaluate harmonic aggregation against persistence landscapes, persistence images, and PersLay on random network model and real-world graph-classification benchmarks, and find that harmonic aggregation has the highest accuracy on the random network model benchmark and on most real-world data benchmarks. Source code is available at https://github.com/cfanning8/higher-order-PDs.

papers.title: On separability of Tatra association schemes
papers.abstract: A Tatra association scheme is an association scheme arising from a symmetric bilinear form defined on the equivalence classes of nonzero $2$-dimensional vectors modulo some subgroup of the multiplicative group of a finite field. In the present paper, we prove that every such association scheme is $4$-separable, i.e., it is determined up to isomorphism by the tensor of its $4$-dimensional intersection numbers.

papers.title: Time-periodic carrying simplex for a competitive system of Carathéodory ODEs
papers.abstract: We establish the existence of a time-periodic carrying simplex for competitive systems of Kolmogorov-type ordinary differential equations of the form $\dot{x}_i = x_i g_i(t,x)$, $i=1,\dots,d$, on $\mathbb{R}^d_+$, where the vector field $g$ is $T$-periodic in time and satisfies only Carathéodory conditions rather than the classical $C^1$ regularity assumed in earlier work. We show that the time-$T$ Poincaré map $P$ generated by the flow is retrotone, and apply recent results on the carrying simplex for retrotone maps to obtain for $P$ a carrying simplex $Σ$ that is an unordered, Lipschitz, invariant manifold homeomorphic to the standard probability simplex, and that attracts all nonzero trajectories of the discrete dynamical system generated by $P$. We then extend this construction to the full nonautonomous flow by introducing an auxiliary autonomous system on the extended phase space $\mathcal{T} \times \mathbb{R}^d_+$, where $\mathcal{T}$ is the circle of length $T$, generated via a skew-product formulation. In the context of this extended phase space we then construct a compact global attractor and identify, as its relative boundary, a time-periodic family of carrying simplices $\{Σ_s\}_{s \in \mathcal{T}}$ that depend continuously on the phase $s$, each homeomorphic to the standard simplex and each attracting, uniformly in $s$, all nonzero orbits of the corresponding time-shifted flow. These results provide a rigorous foundation for the qualitative analysis of seasonally forced competitive population models in which growth rates need only be measurable and locally Lipschitz in time, broadening the applicability of carrying simplex theory to more realistic ecological settings.

papers.title: Geometry of bounded domains with piecewise smooth boundary
papers.abstract: In this paper, we study the geometry of bounded domains with piecewise smooth boundary. Specifically, we obtain the relationship between the squeezing function corresponding to polydisk and Levi flatness on bounded convex domains. As an application, we prove that a two-dimensional bounded generic convex domain with piecewise $C^2$-smooth boundary that is not smooth and admits a finite volume quotient is biholomorphic to bidisk. Moreover, we show that any Teichmüller space $\mathcal{T}_g$ with $g\geq2$ cannot be biholomorphic to a bounded domain with piecewise $C^2$-smooth boundary.

papers.title: $T$-admissible processes and noncommutative weighted ergodic theorems
papers.abstract: In this article, we study the bilaterally almost uniform (b.a.u.) convergence of weighted averages of a positive Dunford-Schwartz operator $T$ acting on the noncommutative $L_p$-spaces $L_p(\mathcal{M},τ)$ associated to a semifinite von Neumann algebra $(\mathcal{M},τ)$ for every $1\leq p<\infty$ for a variety of sequences which includes those generated by bounded i.i.d. sequences, the Möbius function, the Liouville function, and totally balanced automatic sequences. If $1<p<\infty$, then sequences generated by i.i.d. sequences with finite $q$-th moment for $q=\frac{p}{p-1}$ being the Hölder conjugate of $p$ are also shown to generate good weights for $L_p(\mathcal{M},τ)$. We also study similar problems for $T$-admissible processes on a semifinite von Neumann algebra, showing that if a Wiener-Wintner type ergodic theorem holds for a class $\mathcal{W}\subset W_q$ of weights, then it also holds for strongly $p$-bounded $T$-admissible processes assuming that the duality $\frac{1}{p}+\frac{1}{q}=1$ holds and that $T$ is a normal $τ$-preserving $*$-automorphism. A version of this result for arbitrary positive Dunford-Schwartz operators is also considered.

papers.title: On optimization on ravine functions. Minkowski-Cohn moduli surface in Cohn parameterization
papers.abstract: This paper presents a brief overview of ravine functions using the example of the Minkowski-Cohn moduli surface from the point of view of optimization on it. Elements of representation and solution of the minimization problem at a point are presented.

papers.title: WSINDy for Model Predictive Control with Applications to Fusion, Drones, and Chaos
papers.abstract: The control of complex dynamical systems remains a fundamental challenge in science and engineering, where strong nonlinearities, the presence of noise, and computational constraints often pose significant obstacles in traditional control approaches. Recent advances in data-driven methods, particularly system identification techniques, have shown a powerful alternative by providing fast, parsimonious, interpretable models that are well-suited for model predictive control (MPC). Building on these developments, the present article embeds WSINDy with actuation inputs (WSINDYc) within a MPC framework. Compared to benchmark data-driven methods, WSINDYc enables a more robust identification of the governing dynamics, particularly in the presence of high noise levels, resulting in more accurate and efficient control. The capabilities of the proposed WSINDY-MPC framework are demonstrated on a range of problems, including a tokamak plasma boundary model that includes main ion gas puff actuation, drone tracking and collision avoidance, the chaotic Lorenz system, and a simplified flight control model for an F-8 aircraft. The proposed framework achieves superior performance in the presence of noise, enabling longer prediction horizons, lower trajectory tracking error, and a more reliable obstacle clearance, while simultaneously achieving lower MPC cost values compared to the baseline methods.

papers.title: Consecutive non-square non-primitive pairs in a finite field
papers.abstract: Let $q$ be an odd prime power and write \[ θ_q := \frac{φ(q-1)}{q-1}. \] If $θ_q < \tfrac{1}{3}$, or if $θ_q = \tfrac{1}{3}$ and $q \notin \{7,13,19,25,37\}$, then the finite field $\F$ contains a pair of consecutive elements that are both non-square and non-primitive. This extends a result of Jarso and Trudgian for prime fields $\Fp$, where the same conclusion was obtained under the stronger condition $θ_p \le \tfrac{1}{4}$. More generally, let $\ell$ be the least odd prime divisor of $q-1$. If $θ_q \le \tfrac{1}{3}$, then $\F$ contains a pair of consecutive elements that are non-squares and $\ell$th powers, with the sole exceptions $q \in \{7,13,19,25,37,43\}$.

papers.title: Canonical separating coordinates in the generalized cubic Hénon-Heiles systems
papers.abstract: We study the three classical integrable generalized cubic Hénon--Heiles systems -- Kaup--Kupershmidt, KdV$_5$, and Sawada--Kotera -- from the viewpoint of bi-Hamiltonian geometry and separation of variables.
