Its discretization error decreases exponentially as the number of quadrature nodes grows, and its nested grids allow previously computed values to be reused when the mesh is refined. They also reported that their approach is more robust than Gauss--Legendre quadrature for ill-conditioned matrices. We propose two algorithms based on the DE formula. The first adaptively refines the mesh while reusing previously computed values and requires no matrix norm computations. The second uses a rigorous error bound to select the number of quadrature nodes a priori. Numerical experiments show that both methods attain lower errors than Tatsuoka et al.'s method at comparable elapsed times over the tested ranges.

papers.title: On flat metric nilpotent Lie algebras
papers.abstract: We study flat left-invariant pseudo-Riemannian metrics on nilpotent Lie groups. Associated with a flat metric Lie algebra $(\mathfrak{g},\langle\cdot,\cdot\rangle)$ there is a canonical affine action of the corresponding group on the vector space $\mathfrak{g}$, whose linear part is the Levi-Civita representation $L$. Combining this action with Scheuneman's theorem on pure translations in nilpotent affine groups, we prove that a flat metric nonabelian nilpotent Lie algebra has a nontrivial kernel of $L$, that is, $\ker L\neq 0$. As a consequence, every $n$-dimensional flat metric nonabelian nilpotent Lie algebra is a double extension of an $(n-2)$-dimensional flat metric nilpotent Lie algebra.

papers.title: Classification of vanishing fusion rings of rank four
papers.abstract: A fusion ring is said to be vanishing if one of its multiplication matrices has determinant zero. We classify all vanishing fusion rings of rank four. We then provide a more explicit classification in the integral case, which leads to new consequences: there are infinitely many nonisomorphic simple integral vanishing fusion rings of rank four and no simple integral fusion ring of rank four is 1-Frobenius. We also classify all Burnside fusion rings of rank four.

papers.title: First-order Optimization Methods with Generalized Smoothness for Low-rank Matrix Factorization
papers.abstract: This paper studies several first-order methods for low-rank matrix minimization in the Burer--Monteiro form, where the target matrix is represented as the product of a nonnegative factor matrix and its transpose. Such a factorization destroys convexity of the objective function and global Lipschitz continuity of the gradient. We prove that for a quadratic objective function that is strongly convex only on the subspace of symmetric matrices, the Burer-Monteiro factorized objective possesses generalized smoothness with a fractional exponent 2/3. For a quadratic objective, the generalized smoothness property requires positive definiteness of the operator A only on the subspace of symmetric matrices, which relaxes the assumptions of Dragomir et al. On this basis, three methods are proposed: an adaptive gradient descent method with Armijo backtracking; an unconstrained SafeAdam method combining the Adam direction with a descent-angle certificate and a fallback to the normalized gradient; and a certified projected version for the nonnegativity constraint. Global convergence and explicit convergence rates for the proposed methods have been proved. The obtained convergence rate is better than the convergence rate of ordinary unaccelerated gradient descent in the case of a sufficiently large gradient. In the small-gradient regime, the convergence guarantee is of square-root type, and the corresponding complexity scales as the inverse square of the desired accuracy. In the large-gradient regime, the convergence guarantee is of three-quarters type, and the corresponding complexity is proportional to the inverse of the accuracy raised to the power of 4/3. Experiments on SymNMF using the TDT2, Reuters and CBCL datasets, which are standard benchmarks for document and image clustering, show that the methods match or outperform Dyn-NoLips without tuning the relative-smoothness kernel parameters.

papers.title: A Spanning Subgraph of Conway's 99-graph
papers.abstract: We show that in any hypothetical $G$ = srg(99,14,1,2) a spanning subgraph with $189$ edges is forced. Moreover, the graph formed out of the remaining edges has the spectrum $(12^1,-4^{30}, 3^{40},-2^6,0^7)$ expressed in Brouwer's notation.

papers.title: Non-vanishing of primitive cubic, quartic and sextic L-functions
papers.abstract: We establish lower bounds for the non-vanishing proportions of primitive cubic, quartic and sextic Dirichlet $L$-functions over $\F_q[T]$ in the non-Kummer setting. Adapting truncated-exponential techniques for shifted moments, we improve the cubic lower bound of David, Florea and Lalín and obtain positive lower bounds for quartic and sextic families. For each family, the lower limit of the non-vanishing proportion exceeds $e^{-e^{53}}$ as the conductor degree tends to infinity with $q$ fixed. We use a common choice of truncation parameters and explicitly control the exceptional sets. The cubic argument uses the published twisted first moment. We also establish uniform twisted first moments in the quartic and sextic cases, yielding an asymptotic formula for the sextic first moment.

papers.title: Geometric operators and the third problem of Halmos
papers.abstract: In 1970, P. R. Halmos raised ten open problems on operator theory. The third problem of Halmos is the following: if an intransitive operator has an inverse, is its inverse also intransitive? This question is reduced to the case of conjugate bi-geometric operators in arXiv: 2610.11202. In the framework of conjugate bi-geometric operators, using tools from complex geometry, operator theory, and function theory, this paper gives an affirmative answer to the third problem of Halmos in the following cases: (a) bundle-preserving operator;(b) subexponential growth of operator norms. These two cases cover a large class of operators.

papers.title: A Counterexample to the Holomorphic Cancellation Problem
papers.abstract: We show that if a contractible Stein manifold $X$ with the density property admits a proper holomorphic embedding into $\mathbb{C}^k$, then $X \times \mathbb{C}^k$ is biholomorphic to $\mathbb{C}^{n+k}$ with $n=\dim X$. We also prove that McLean's exotic affine variety $K_n$, $n\ge4$, a smooth contractible affine variety which is not biholomorphic to $\mathbb{C}^n$, has the density property. Hence for $n \ge 4$ there exist an integer $m \in \{ n, \dots, 2n\}$ and an affine variety $X$ such that $X \times \mathbb{C}$ is biholomorphic to $\mathbb{C}^{m+1}$ and $X$ is not biholomorphic to $\mathbb{C}^m$. This settles the Holomorphic Cancellation Problem in the negative. We also construct holomorphic actions of $\mathbb{C}^*$ and finite cyclic groups on complex Euclidean spaces that are not topologically conjugate to linear actions.

papers.title: 0/1 integer programming over polytopes of Chvátal rank one is as hard as lattice problems
papers.abstract: A rational polyhedron has Chvátal rank at most one if a single round of Chvátal-Gomory cuts yields its integer hull. In 1973, Chvátal asked whether 0/1 integer programs over polytopes of bounded Chvátal rank can be solved in polynomial time. For polyhedra of bounded Chvátal rank, integer feasibility is in NP $\cap$ coNP, so it is unlikely to be NP-hard. We answer Chvátal's question negatively already in its most restricted form: for Chvátal rank one, for integer feasibility, and even for the SAT polytopes of formulas whose clauses have at most three literals. Our answer holds under either of two standard assumptions from lattice-based cryptography. First, a polynomial-time algorithm for integer feasibility on such SAT polytopes of Chvátal rank one would solve bounded distance decoding with polynomial factors in deterministic polynomial time, contradicting the conjectured hardness of approximating lattice problems within polynomial factors. Second, assuming the hardness of learning with errors, an average-case analog of bounded distance decoding, the problem is also hard on average, for a polynomial-time samplable distribution of formulas. This also gives negative answers to related questions of Cornuéjols, Lee, and Li. We first prove these results for parallelepipeds, where they rest on an elementary sufficient condition: a polyhedron has Chvátal rank at most one if its width is less than one along every row of some unimodular matrix. For our parallelepipeds, such a matrix exists but is hard to find. For SAT polytopes, we represent candidate lattice vectors by their residues modulo small integers, and binary arithmetic on additional 0/1 variables checks that these vectors lie in the lattice.

papers.title: Limit shapes for centrally excited walks
papers.abstract: A centrally excited random walk on $\mathbb Z^d$ moves like simple random walk, except that its first step from each site other than the origin has a drift of fixed size toward it. Kozma (2007) conjectured that after $n$ steps the visited set approximates a ball with radius of order $n^{1/(d+1)}$. We prove this in every dimension $d\geq 2$ and show that the rescaled local times converge uniformly to a cone, which is the potential generated by the drift on a ball. The same argument shows that, when the drift is opposite to a subgradient of a norm, the visited set approximates the ball of that norm. In the plane, the outer and inner radii of the visited set differ by at most $n^{1/6}$ times a power of $\log n$, and the exponent $1/6$ cannot be lowered. Earlier versions of this work appeared in three independent drafts by Nguyen (arXiv:2610.07724), Bou-Rabee and Peres (arxiv:2610.10162v1) and Singh (arxiv:2610.12138). The present paper brings together the results and ideas from these drafts.

papers.title: A curvature-ellipse-based Monge normal form of a regular surface in $\mathbb{R}^4$ and its applications
papers.abstract: We study a Monge normal form of a surface in $\mathbb{R}^4$ based on the principal axes of its curvature ellipse. The curvature-ellipse-based Monge normal form is obtained using only Euclidean motions of the ambient space and local reparameterizations of the surface, and preserves the Euclidean invariants of the curvature ellipse, including its semi-axis lengths up to their ordering. We also give applications of this normal form to the $2$-jet geometry of surfaces in $\mathbb{R}^4$ and to the geometry of their orthogonal projections.

papers.title: Two Answers on Heavy-Ball Dynamics
papers.abstract: We determine the worst-case behavior of the heavy-ball method on smooth strongly convex functions, first for Polyak's quadratic-optimal parameters and then for arbitrary constant parameters. For Polyak's tuning, the exact dimension-uniform exponential rate is the largest growth factor of an interpolable mixture of rotating geometric sequences. Four algebraic families determine this rate at every condition number. Two frequencies suffice, and one function in dimension five attains the rate at every horizon up to constant factors. We recover the sharp convergence threshold $9+4\sqrt5$ of Badithela and Seiler. For general tunings, an exact linear feasibility criterion characterizes dimension-uniform linear convergence through the angle between the characteristic polynomials of the two extreme quadratics. This gives a continuous condition-number threshold and resolves the second heavy-ball riddle of Goujaud, Taylor and Dieuleveut. The regions between consecutive cycle tongues are Farey gaps, each containing convergent and divergent tunings. Regular portions of the threshold surface are analytic plateaus with fixed periodic frequency support. Every rational rotation number in a gap anchors a single-harmonic plateau; mixed-harmonic plateaus and an exact two-lag threshold point also occur. Along tongue edges, explicit multiplier inequalities and second-order expansions of competing Farey fans bound the transition from single-harmonic to mixed-harmonic extremals. The rate bounds and the extremal constructions follow from a common interpolation and separation argument that preserves initialization with zero momentum.

papers.title: A refinement of the edge theorem for order and chain polytopes
papers.abstract: For a finite poset, we partition the edges of the order polytope and of the chain polytope into classes indexed by the connected convex subsets of the poset, and we establish that corresponding classes have the same cardinality. This yields a closed formula for the common number of edges, and it identifies the bijection of Hibi, Li, Sahara and Shikama as a disjoint union of simple bijections between corresponding classes, explaining why it is a bijection and how it acts on edge directions and lengths. As consequences, the two polytopes have equally many edge directions, with matching multiplicities, and, for every m, equally many pairs of vertices whose symmetric difference has m components; the chain polytope has at least as many edges parallel to each coordinate subspace as the order polytope; and the edge lengths of the chain polytope are dominated by those of the order polytope, with strict inequality in the last two comparisons exactly when the poset contains a three-element chain. We discuss implications for linear and convex combinatorial optimization over ideals and antichains. We also express the number of edges in terms of the comparability graph, extending to stable-set polytopes of all graphs; give a recursion for series-parallel posets and closed formulas for layered, zigzag and crown posets; and characterize the distributive lattices for which the two polytopes are unimodularly equivalent. Finally, either diameter can exceed the other arbitrarily; both are bounded by the width, and they coincide for series-parallel, zigzag and crown posets.

papers.title: Formal Matrix Rings with the Involution Property
papers.abstract: We study formal matrix rings with the involution property, that is, rings in which every element can be represented as the sum of an invertible element and an involution. After recalling the construction of formal matrix rings via Morita contexts, we describe involutions in triangular formal matrix rings and establish a criterion for upper triangular rings of order two. We then prove that a formal matrix ring of arbitrary finite order has the involution property whenever all of its diagonal rings have this property. Several examples and counterexamples are included to illustrate the obtained results.

papers.title: Beta-shifts without typical periodic optimization
papers.abstract: We show that beta-shifts whose lexicographically largest point is a Sturmian sequence do not have typical periodic optimization (TPO): on each such beta-shift there is a non-empty open set of Lipschitz functions whose unique maximizing measure is the Sturmian measure, which is not supported on a periodic orbit. These are the first known examples of beta-shifts without TPO, and, since they have the specification property, the first known examples of shift spaces with specification but without TPO. The corresponding beta-transformations do not have TPO in any space of Hölder functions on the interval. The main ingredient in the proofs is a rigidity property of Sturmian subshifts: modulo constants and Lipschitz coboundaries, the space of Lipschitz functions on such a subshift is one-dimensional. We also show that the set of $β>1$ for which the beta-shift or the beta-transformation does not have TPO is dense in $(1,\infty)$, but has zero packing dimension. The density is proved by a tuning construction, analogous to Douady--Hubbard tuning in the Mandelbrot set, which produces non-Sturmian subshifts with the same rigidity property. Finally, we show that every beta-shift has typical zero-entropy optimization: for an open dense set of Lipschitz functions, the maximizing measure is unique and its support has zero topological entropy.

papers.title: Two degenerate intersections of Clifford tori in $S^2\times S^2$ and $\mathbb{C}P^2$
papers.abstract: We construct smooth time-periodic Hamiltonians on the monotone manifolds $S^2\times S^2$ and $\mathbb{C}P^2$ for which the Clifford torus meets its Hamiltonian image in exactly two isolated degenerate points. The product example disproves the degenerate Arnol'd-Givental conjecture.

papers.title: Isolated singularities of solutions to the Yamabe equation in higher dimensions I
papers.abstract: We complete, in the general Riemannian setting, the classification of isolated singularities of positive solutions to the Yamabe equation for dimensions \(3\le n\le29\), initiated in the flat case by Caffarelli, Gidas, and Spruck in 1989. Precisely, every isolated singularity is either removable or the solution is asymptotic to a Fowler solution. The sharpness of this range is established by counterexamples for every dimension \(n\ge30\) in our companion paper.

papers.title: The Brauer $A(\infty)$ condition and Navarro's conjecture on Brauer characters under coprime actions
papers.abstract: In this paper, we prove the Brauer $A(\infty)$ condition for good non-defining primes. Consequently, we show a conjecture of Navarro on coprime actions and Brauer characters for primes larger than 3.

papers.title: Non-maximal quasi-isometric $\mathrm{PU}_{2,n+1}$-representations via alternating surfaces in complex pseudo-hyperbolic spaces
papers.abstract: For every admissible non-maximal Toledo invariant $t$, we construct a locus of irreducible representations of a closed genus-$g$ surface group into $\mathrm{PU}_{2,n+1}$ with Toledo invariant $t$ whose orbit maps are quasi-isometric embeddings. These loci have real codimension $10(g-1)$ or $10(g-1)+2(n-1)$ in the character variety depending on the Toledo value. Our construction uses $4$-cyclic Higgs bundles and their correspondence with $\partial$-alternating surfaces in complex pseudo-hyperbolic spaces. The associated equivariant minimal maps into the symmetric space are bi-Lipschitz embeddings. We further construct cocompact domains of discontinuity in the Shilov boundary. Their quotients are smooth fiber bundles over the surface with fiber homeomorphic to $S^{2n-1}\times S^{2n-1}$.

papers.title: Prime and Cohen-Macaulay ideals of 2-minors with linear resolution
papers.abstract: Prime and Cohen-Macaulay ideals of 2-minors of matrices of variables with linear resolution are classified.

papers.title: Element-wise Convergence Behavior of Subspace Iteration
papers.abstract: This paper studies the element-wise convergence behavior of subspace iteration. All results are established for both \(\mathbb{F}=\mathbb{R}\) and \(\mathbb{F}=\mathbb{C}\). For a diagonal matrix \(Λ=\mathrm{diag}(λ_1,\ldots,λ_n)\) with \(|λ_1|>\cdots>|λ_n|>0\), we analyze the modulus of each entry of the iterative matrix sequence generated by subspace iteration, both without and with the Rayleigh--Ritz procedure. Under mild assumptions on the initial matrix \(X\in\mathbb{F}^{n\times m}\), we first derive exact asymptotic expressions for \(|Q_k(i,j)|\) in the subspace iteration without the Rayleigh--Ritz procedure: entries with \(i\neq j\) decay as \(|λ_{\max\{i,j\}}/λ_{\min\{i,j\}}|^k\), and the deviation of \(|Q_k(j,j)|\) from \(1\) decays as \(\max\{|λ_j/λ_{j-1}|,|λ_{j+1}/λ_j|\}^{2k}\), with explicit coefficients determined by the LU factorization of \(X\). Similar conclusions could also be established for upper triangular matrices. For the Rayleigh--Ritz variant, we obtain element-wise bounds for the normalized Ritz vectors \(Z_k\). Specifically, for \(|Z_k(i,j)|\), off-diagonal entries with \(i\geq m+1\) decay as \((|λ_i|/|λ_j|)^k\), off-diagonal entries with \(i\leq m\) decay as \((|λ_{m+1}|^2/(|λ_i||λ_j|))^k\), and the deviation of \(|Z_k(j,j)|\) from \(1\) decays as \((|λ_{m+1}|/|λ_j|)^{2k}\). These results give an element-wise description of the convergence behavior of subspace iteration. After an orthogonal or unitary change of basis, the results could be further generalized.

papers.title: An improvement of the large sieve for square moduli under Hooley's hypothesis $R^*$ for short Salié sums
papers.abstract: Let $S(Q,M,N,(a_n))=\sum_{q\le Q}\sum_{a\bmod q^2,(a,q)=1}|\sum_{M<n\le M+N}a_ne(an/q^2)|^2$ be Zhao's large sieve sum with square moduli. Zhao conjectured that $S\ll(QN)^ε(Q^3+N)\sum|a_n|^2$. The bound of Baier and Zhao (2008) exceeds this conjecture by a factor which reaches $Q^{1/2}$ at the critical point $N=Q^3$, and there the exponent $1/2$ has not been lowered since. We prove that, under Hooley's Hypothesis $R^*$ for short Salié sums, $S\ll(QN)^ε(Q^3+N+Q^{4/3}N^{2/3})\sum|a_n|^2$. This replaces the excess over Zhao's conjecture by its $2/3$-th power throughout the range $Q^{5/2}<N<Q^4$; at $N=Q^3$ it gives $S\ll Q^{1/2-1/6+ε}N\sum|a_n|^2$. The proof is short. Following Zhao's original treatment, we approximate the point under consideration by fractions $b/r$ with denominators up to $Q^{2/3}N^{1/3}$, which for $N<Q^4$ is beyond the customary $\sqrt{N}$. If the approximation is poor, an elementary count suffices. If it is good, the analytic part of the problem disappears: after Poisson summation in both variables the count is expressed through quadratic Gauss sums, and their exact evaluation at every modulus turns the sum over the dual variable into short Kloosterman and Salié sums, to which Hypothesis $R^*$ applies and gives the square root of the elementary count. At odd moduli the hypothesis is needed only in the form of Conjecture (C*) of Friedlander and Iwaniec. The Gauss-sum evaluations, including even moduli and coefficients sharing a factor with the modulus, are proved in full. This version supersedes earlier versions, which obtained the exponent $1/2-1/28$ at $N=Q^3$ by a much longer route through sums of modular square roots. The paper was prepared in collaboration with Claude (Anthropic).

papers.title: On the arithmetic of Tate-Shafarevich groups via Kolyvagin's conjecture
papers.abstract: We investigate how Heegner points detect the finiteness of the $p$-primary part of Tate-Shafarevich groups of semi-stable elliptic curves over the rationals of \emph{arbitrary} rank with any good reduction prime $p \geq 5$ with irreducible mod $p$ representation and partially recover Çiperiani--Wiles' theorem on solvable points on genus one curves. As a key ingredient of the proof of these results, we also give a concise proof of Kolyvagin's conjecture for semi-stable elliptic curves with supersingular reduction with a relevant choice of an imaginary quadratic field. Our approach is independent of the cyclotomic Iwasawa main conjecture for elliptic curves with supersingular reduction.

papers.title: Real-rooted Eulerian polynomials from permutations, words, and paths
papers.abstract: We study seven Eulerian-type polynomial families. We prove that the descent polynomials of derangements are real-rooted, settling the derangement part of a conjecture of S.~Fu, Z.~Lin, and J.~Zeng. We also resolve the real-rootedness conjecture in OEIS A335340, strengthen the known rowwise real-rootedness of an even-top descent family to consecutive strict interlacing, and prove real-rootedness, consecutive interlacing, and real-rooted gamma-polynomials for U.~Shankar's super-Eulerian polynomials. A differential recurrence gives consecutive weak interlacing for ternary words counted by increasing runs. We prove stability of the peak-value refinement and consecutive interleaving of its positive weighted diagonals, settling a conjecture of P.~Alexandersson and O.~Nabawanda. Finally, we prove that the zig-zag Eulerian polynomials, which enumerate swaps in alternating permutations, have simple negative roots, settling the real-rootedness conjecture of T.~Kyle Petersen and Y.~Zhuang.

papers.title: A quantitative convergence rate for torsional creep to the distance function as p tends to infinity
papers.abstract: We prove that the Dirichlet $p$-torsion function $u_p$ converges to the distance to the boundary $d$ at the rate $O(1/p)$ in the uniform norm, on every bounded domain and with a constant depending only on the dimension and the diameter. The upper bound comes from a radial barrier with its pole at a boundary point, which is an admissible comparison function for $p>n$ and needs no boundary regularity; the lower bound comes from an inscribed ball. On the ball the error equals $(1+\log n)/p+O(p^{-2})$, so the order $1/p$ cannot be improved in general. Under a uniform exterior ball condition an annular barrier gives $u_p\le K_Ω^{1/(p-1)}d$ for every $p>1$, with $K_Ω$ explicit in the dimension, the diameter and the exterior radius; on convex sets the constant is the diameter, and a multiple of $d$ is a supersolution whenever $-Δd$ has a positive distributional lower bound. On $C^2$ domains, the same barrier and the classical gradient maximum principle give $\norm{\nabla u_p}_{L^\infty}^{p-1}\le K_Ω$. When $-Δd$ is a measure of finite total variation, which we prove for $C^1$ domains with a uniform exterior ball, the gradients converge in $L^q$ at the rate $O(p^{-1/2})$ for $q\le2$ and $O(p^{-1/q})$ for $q\ge2$; these exponents are not claimed to be sharp. The explicit ball profile shows that the gradients do not converge uniformly.

papers.title: An Energy-Based Conservative-Dissipative Latent Neural Evolution Operator for Magnetization Dynamics
papers.abstract: We introduce a reduced-order learning framework that couples a convolutional autoencoder to a structured latent neural ordinary differential equation. A learned scalar generates the latent dynamics through an antisymmetric operator and a positive-definite dissipative operator. The antisymmetric component permits motion along scalar level sets, while the dissipative component decreases the scalar. Adding a coercive quadratic term gives bounded continuous-time latent trajectories and approach to the scalar's critical set under the stated assumptions. The scalar provides a structural constraint rather than an approximation of physical energy. The encoder, decoder, scalar, and operators are trained jointly on short snapshot windows without time-derivative supervision, physical-energy labels, or dissipation penalties. At inference, one initial state is encoded and evolved continuously in latent space, with decoding only at requested times. We demonstrate the framework on micromagnetic magnetization trajectories from NIST $μ$MAG Standard Problem 4 and compare it with dissipative-only dynamics and an unstructured latent neural differential equation. Repeated training runs show competitive observed-horizon accuracy, while selected longer rollouts illustrate improved retention of approximately stationary states relative to the unstructured baseline. These results motivate scalar-generated latent dynamics as an inductive bias for reduced-order prediction and other learning tasks where bounded evolution and equilibrium behavior are important.

papers.title: Farey Structure in Modulo Krinkle Tilings: Mediant Splicing and Generation of Prototiles from a Single Edge
papers.abstract: The Modulo Krinkle tilings of Imura (arXiv:2506.07638) form a family of non-periodic, spiral monohedral tilings parametrized by a reduced fraction $m/k$ and an integer $t\ge 2$. We show that the Farey sum (mediant) $(m_1+m_2)/(k_1+k_2)$ of two Farey-adjacent parameters is realized by an exact geometric operation on prototiles: the lower boundary path of the $(m_1+m_2,k_1+k_2)$-prototile is obtained by concatenating the parents' lower paths after an edge-length-preserving progressive rotation (fan-twist) of their edges. Conversely, every prototile admits exactly one fan-twist splice decomposition -- no non-adjacent parameters ever splice -- the cut position being $k_1=m^{-1}\bmod k$, and the recursion descends the Stern-Brocot tree to a single unit edge. The combinatorial core of the operation is the classical standard factorization of Christoffel words; the contribution here is its exact edge-isometric realization on circular direction systems and the resulting structure theory for the Modulo Krinkle family, including the recently introduced variants: we prove a separation theorem stating that every variant prototile is the common recursively-generated core plus finitely many direction-invariant decoration edges. As a corollary of Imura's spiral-arm count formula, the two Farey parents are visible in the offset-free tiling itself: the numbers of counterclockwise and clockwise spiral arms are $tk_1$ and $tk_2$.

papers.title: Solvability of unimodular equations in groups and Lie algebras
papers.abstract: Our results imply, in particular, that a finitely generated solvable group $G$ is nilpotent if and only if it contains a solution to any unimodular equation, i.e., an equation of the form $\prod g_ix^{n_i}=1$, where $g_i\in G$ and $\sum n_i=\pm1$. A similar fact turns out to be true for Lie algebras. We also exhibit an example of a unimodular equation $w(x)=g$ over a finitely generated group $G$, which has a solution (in $G$) for any $g\in G$, but the solution is not unique for some $g\in G$. We show that, for nilpotent groups $G$, the set of unimodular mappings $G^n\to G^n$ (which are defined naturally) forms a group under the composition.

papers.title: Self-similar stationary Navier--Stokes flows in a half-space with arbitrarily large swirl forcing
papers.abstract: We study axisymmetric self-similar solutions of the stationary Navier--Stokes equations with $(-3)$-homogeneous forces and no-slip boundary conditions in a half-space. For a fixed force without swirl, we characterize the interval of amplitudes for which solutions exist and describe the velocity singularity at its finite endpoints. For each parameter in this interval, a solution exists after adding a swirl force of any size, and it is unique among solutions with bounded profiles when the swirl force is sufficiently small. The proof uses the nonnegative contribution of swirl to a Riccati equation and a comparison estimate. We also prove that, when the tangential curl of the force is sufficiently small, there exists a unique solution with small velocity profiles.

papers.title: Surjectivity of real-linear Cauchy--Riemann operators: from the minimal Harder--Narasimhan slope to automatic transversality
papers.abstract: This paper relates the minimal Harder--Narasimhan slope to the surjectivity of real-linear Cauchy--Riemann operators. We establish a conformally invariant $L^2$ criterion and an asymptotic slope criterion, which yield higher-rank automatic transversality criteria for pseudoholomorphic curves beyond the classical rank-one framework. Applications to pseudoholomorphic spheres in $S^6$ provide quantitative $L^2$ obstructions to the integrability of almost complex structures.

papers.title: Nilpotency and Engel-Type Theorems for Lie Affgebras
papers.abstract: We investigate structural properties of Lie affgebras, viewed as affine analogues of Lie algebras. We introduce the notion of an ideaf, the affine counterpart of an ideal, and establish characterizations of left and right ideafs. We further study centers, quotient structures, and product ideafs, proving, under suitable conditions, that the center of a Lie affgebra is an ideaf. We then develop the notion of affine nilpotency and establish connections between the nilpotency of Lie affgebras and that of their retracted Lie algebras. As an application, we prove an Engel-type theorem for Lie affgebras of the form $\mathfrak{a}(\mathfrak{g};κ=2λ,λ,s)$.

papers.title: Line-filtered ACM bundles and Ulrich defects on abelian varieties of Picard rank one
papers.abstract: Let $A$ be a complex abelian variety with $\NS(A)=\Z[L]$, $L$ ample. We show that a vector bundle filtered by line bundles splits uniquely into unipotent blocks, determine when it is ACM with respect to $L$, and show that it is never Ulrich. For a rank-two Ulrich bundle we bound from below the degree of the defect of every saturated line subbundle, compute the Hilbert polynomial of the defect, and show that the bound is attained exactly when an explicit cohomological support locus is nonempty. On abelian surfaces this locus is an ample curve in $\Pic^0(A)$; as a consequence, every rank-two Ulrich bundle is a Serre extension of a fixed numerical type, which we characterize and construct for every ample $L$. For $g\ge3$, we reduce the equality case to the existence of subcanonical codimension-two subschemes with prescribed cohomology.

papers.title: A note on the cohomology of pullback Lie algebroids
papers.abstract: We give a direct differential-geometric proof of a result of Crainic on the cohomology of pullbacks of Lie algebroids under surjective submersions: If the fibers are connected and have vanishing cohomology through degree $n$, pullback with coefficients in any representation is an isomorphism through degree $n$ and is injective in degree $n+1$. The proof reduces to a vanishing result for leafwise cohomology and uses an exhaustion-and-patching argument due to Buchdahl. No local triviality or finite-type assumption on the fibers is required. We also prove the analogous result for holomorphic Lie algebroids.

papers.title: Polynomiality of Stretched Schubert Structure Constants and Key Coefficients
papers.abstract: We prove that monomial coefficients in affine families of key and Schubert polynomials are eventually polynomial. These results extend to finite products. Using M.~Watanabe's Schubert duality, we deduce that stretched Schubert structure constants are eventually polynomial. This proves a conjecture stated by I.~Pak and Z.~Slonim. We also prove that the positive key expansion of every affine-code family of Schubert polynomials eventually has fixed coefficients and affine indices. The proofs combine Demazure operators and vector partition functions with P.~Magyar's orthodontic formula and the generalized Demazure character theory of V.~Lakshmibai, P.~Littelmann, and P.~Magyar.

papers.title: Functional Calculus on Noncommutative Tori, II. Complex Powers, Logarithms, and Sectorial Projections
papers.abstract: This paper develops a systematic theory of complex powers, logarithms, and sectorial projections of elliptic pseudodifferential operators on noncommutative tori, extending to this setting the classical constructions of Seeley and others. Building on the parametric pseudodifferential calculus of the prequel~\cite{LP:Part1}, we construct the complex powers associated with a given ray, show that they form a holomorphic family of pseudodifferential operators with the semigroup property, and compute their symbols. We further establish exponential growth bounds on vertical strips in the operator, Schatten, and trace-class topologies by means of a new holomorphic calculus for pseudodifferential families. The logarithm is identified as a pseudodifferential operator whose symbol is determined by the resolvent symbol, and the associated trace formula is derived. Sectorial projections are constructed as contour integrals and shown to be of order zero. This yields analogues for noncommutative tori of results of Wodzicki, Okikiolu, and Gaarde--Grubb, and provides the analytic foundations for the spectral-geometric applications developed in subsequent papers.

papers.title: Hochschild theory of multiplicative sequences of algebras and coalgebra measurings
papers.abstract: We study coalgebra measurings between multiplicative sequences of algebras and the maps induced by them on Hochschild homology. The Hochschild theory of multiplicative sequences is introduced as a functor taking values in graded algebras in the symmetric monoidal category of chain complexes, constructed with the help of the shuffle product. We develop the universal measuring coalgebra, or Sweedler Hom for multiplicative sequences, as well as study several other Sweedler operations in this context. In particular, we obtain an enrichment of multiplicative sequences over cocommutative coalgebras. Using an appropriate theory of bimodules over multiplicative sequences, we study maps induced by comodule measurings on the Hochschild theory with coefficients, as well as the corresponding enriched categories. Finally, we consider measurings and generalized Sweedler operations between multiplicative sequences induced by comultiplicative sequences of coalgebras, and also the maps in Hochschild theory obtained from them.

papers.title: SLAB: Time-Lag-Aware Deep Reinforcement Learning for Flexible Job-Shop Scheduling in PPVC Module Factories
papers.abstract: Prefabricated prefinished volumetric construction (PPVC) builds room-sized modules in factories that operate as flexible job shops. A module waits 12 to 48 h after casting, waterproofing, and painting, while its station is free for other modules. Existing learned dispatchers release the next operation before this wait ends, so their plans need repair. This paper presents SLAB (Scheduling under time-Lags with an Admissible Bound), a decision process for dispatchers trained by deep reinforcement learning. Its transition releases a module only after its wait, and its reward is the decrease of a proven lower bound that includes the waits. Training on 10-module orders with halved waits also teaches the policy the station contention of larger orders. On three existing networks, repaired plans are 42% to 133% longer than the same network's schedules inside SLAB. On orders generated from Singapore's PPVC guidebook, one trained policy gives schedules 2.2% to 8.1% shorter than the shortest-processing-time rule at 10 to 80 modules. At 50 and 80 modules, it outperforms a time-lag memetic algorithm by 6.7% and 7.4% and constraint-programming search started from that rule's schedule and given 600 s by 6.6% and 7.6%. The memetic algorithm gives shorter schedules on orders of 10 modules, and the same search given 300 s on orders of 10 and 20 modules. A module factory can therefore train one dispatcher on small orders and run it without a solver on production batches of 50 to 80 modules.

papers.title: Universal optimality of the double-centred matrix under unitarily invariant norms for dissimilarity data
papers.abstract: The classical identity relating squared distances to inner products determines every off-diagonal entry of a symmetric matrix associated with a set of pairwise dissimilarities, while leaving its diagonal free. This paper studies the resulting affine family of symmetric matrices and asks which representative is selected by minimising a matrix norm. We prove that the same representative, namely the double-centred matrix used in classical multidimensional scaling and principal coordinate analysis, minimises every unitarily invariant norm on the family. The result includes the Frobenius, spectral, nuclear, Schatten, and Ky Fan norms, and requires no assumption that the dissimilarities are Euclidean distances. The proof rests on a compression-reduction principle: the centring projection maps the entire compatible set to a single element of the family, and orthogonal compression is contractive for unitarily invariant norms; the conclusion follows without solving a separate minimisation problem for each norm. We then determine how many minimisers there are: the minimiser is unique for the Frobenius norm, for the nuclear norm and for every strictly convex unitarily invariant norm, while for the spectral norm we describe the whole minimising set, a compact convex set that reduces to a single point precisely when the double-centred matrix vanishes.
authors: M. Nuria de las Heras Santos

papers.title: Determinantal sampling on general spaces: fast approximation via diffusion geometry
papers.abstract: Determinantal point processes (DPPs) have recently emerged as a kernel-based alternative to standard independent sampling for constructing efficient minibatches, coresets, and other compact representations of large-scale datasets. One of the key strengths of DPP based samplers is that they can be deployed over very general spaces, in contrast to more classical sampling methods beyond i.i.d. which tend to be tailored to particular well-structured settings, principally Euclidean spaces. In this work, we establish explicit rate guarantees for determinantal sampling in spaces that extend far beyond known Euclidean setups, focussing on spectral kernels obtained from eigenspaces of naturally associated Markov diffusion operators, including in particular the Laplacian on manifolds and nearest-neighbour type graphs on data point clouds and the discrete Schrodinger operator on large scale networks. This covers, in particular, the settings of Riemannian manifolds and discrete networks, as well as the problem of batch sampling from discrete datasets. Overall, our approach achieves guarantees comparable to $\big(\text{sample size}\big)^{-\frac{1}{2}-\frac{1}{2d_{\text{int}}}}$ , which match with the rates for well-known determinantal samplers on Euclidean spaces of comparable dimension. In terms of techniques, we connect to the celebrated Weyl's Law for spectra on general spaces, and leverage tools from the theory of Markov diffusion operators and Dirichlet forms, which could be of independent interest in this area. Our approach is applicable to a very wide plethora of ambient spaces beyond Euclidean as soon as these ingredients are available, including e.g. fractals, leading to guarantees that will be governed by the intrinsic structural constants of such spaces.

papers.title: Sharp Asymptotic Minimaxity of the Gavrilov-Benjamini-Sarkar Step-Down Testing Procedure in Sparse Gaussian Sequence Models
papers.abstract: False discovery rate control does not by itself guarantee optimal recovery of sparse signals: a procedure may make few false discoveries while missing an unnecessarily large fraction of the alternatives. We investigate whether the classical Gavrilov--Benjamini--Sarkar (GBS) step-down procedure also achieves the sharp frequentist minimax limits for sparse recovery in independent Gaussian sequence models. Under a beta-min separation at the critical sparse detection boundary, GBS attains the exact asymptotic risk constant $\barΦ(b)$ for normalized Hamming loss and combined $\mathrm{FDP}+\mathrm{FNP}$ loss. The Hamming conclusion remains valid when the number of signals is only bounded above by the nominal sparsity $s_n$. For heterogeneous signal magnitudes, the corresponding risk under either loss equals the sharp benchmark $Λ_n(a)+o(1)$, without assuming that $Λ_n(a)$ converges; this is additive, rather than necessarily relative, sharpness. We assume $s_n\to\infty$, $n/s_n\to\infty$, and a vanishing nominal level $α_n$ satisfying $\log(1/α_n)=o(\sqrt{\log(n/s_n)})$. Unlike step-up rules, a step-down procedure must satisfy every preceding ordered $p$-value constraint before reaching a given rank. Our analysis handles this sequential obstruction directly: a finite-sample shifted order-statistic bound makes false positives negligible, while new uniform crossing arguments show that the rejection path reaches the optimal fraction of signals. The results extend the range of testing architectures known to attain the sharp minimax benchmarks, without requiring localization of a single rejection threshold.

papers.title: Asymptotic Bayes Optimality Under Sparsity of the Gavrilov-Benjamini-Sarkar Step-Down Testing Procedure
papers.abstract: In this article, we investigate the asymptotic Bayes optimality under sparsity (ABOS) of the Gavrilov-Benjamini-Sarkar (GBS) step-down multiple testing procedure (Gavrilov et al., 2009) in the sparse Gaussian sequence model. While the asymptotic optimality properties of the Benjamini-Hochberg procedure have been extensively studied, corresponding results for the GBS procedure remain unavailable despite its favorable finite-sample performance in several settings. Within the spike-and-slab Bayesian formulation and the asymptotic decision-theoretic framework of Bogdan et al. (2011), we establish that the GBS procedure is ABOS over a broad class of sparse asymptotic regimes. Existing analyses of the Benjamini-Hochberg procedure rely on approximating the random rejection threshold by a suitable deterministic surrogate. In contrast, our approach proceeds through a direct analysis of the Bayes risk by separately controlling the false discovery and false nondiscovery components. The analysis combines two key ingredients: a new finite-sample inequality for shifted order statistics associated with the GBS critical constants and a signal-crossing argument for ordered alternative $p$-values that exploits the sequential step-down structure of the procedure. For diverging expected signal counts, these tools yield ABOS without threshold localization. For bounded positive expected signal counts, a direct argument based on the first GBS critical constant establishes ABOS as well. In particular, our results cover polynomial sparsity $p_m\asymp m^{-β}$ for every fixed $0<β\le1$. To the best of our knowledge, this is the first asymptotic decision-theoretic analysis of the GBS procedure and the first proof of its asymptotic Bayes optimality under sparsity.

papers.title: Emission-aware operation of residential PV-battery systems: the role of information structure
papers.abstract: Residential batteries can reduce the carbon emissions of households with photovoltaic (PV) generation, but how much depends on how they are operated under uncertain load, PV generation, and grid carbon intensity. We cast the operation of a residential PV-battery system as a sequential decision problem and compare, under a common and explicit evaluation protocol, a family of linear policies that differ in the information available at decision time, in how they anticipate the future, and in their adaptivity: a rule-based self-consumption policy, an open-loop stochastic schedule, affine feedback policies, receding-horizon policies with deterministic, scenario-based and two-stage lookahead models, and perfect-information benchmarks. Scenarios are generated by a joint principal component model of the three uncertain quantities, which supports conditional sampling during the day. Experiments on Italian data at 15-minute resolution comprise single-day evaluations on 10000 test scenarios in three seasons and a closed-loop simulation over more than eight months of real data. When the state of charge is treated consistently across policies, the self-consumption rule is within 3.2% of the perfect-foresight emissions in closed loop, whereas open-loop schedules and receding-horizon policies that decide before measuring the current period are about 20--35% above it. With real-time measurements, scenario-based receding-horizon control consistently outperforms its deterministic counterpart and, for households that rely more on the grid, reduces emissions by about 5% with respect to the rule. The benefit of emission-aware optimization is therefore determined mainly by the information structure of the controller and by the size of the system relative to the demand.

papers.title: Local-to-Global Exactness of SDP Relaxations for Sparse QCQPs
papers.abstract: We study exact semidefinite programming (SDP) relaxation for a given sparse quadratically constrained quadratic program (QCQP). The SDP relaxation is exact if, whenever it has an optimal solution, it admits a rank-at-most-one optimal solution that corresponds to an optimal solution of the QCQP. Using the maximal cliques of a chordal extension of the aggregate sparsity pattern graph of the data matrices, we formulate the SDP relaxation in terms of clique-wise matrix variables and develop a local-to-global framework for certifying exactness. For each clique-wise matrix variable, we introduce a local sub-SDP with two parameters: a local right-hand-side vector and a consistency matrix specifying the values of entries shared by overlapping clique-wise matrix variables. In the main theorem, these parameters are determined by an optimal solution of the global clique-wise SDP. The theorem shows that if the resulting local sub-SDPs are exact, then the original SDP relaxation is exact. Under the additional assumption that any two distinct cliques intersect in at most one node, we present three classes of local QCQPs that can be incorporated into this framework: convex local QCQPs, local QCQPs characterized by sign-pattern conditions, and separable local QCQPs with a limited number of constraints. Examples illustrate how these different local QCQP classes can be combined in sparse QCQPs.

papers.title: List coloring uncrowded hypergraphs at the shattering threshold
papers.abstract: Improving an earlier bound of Frieze and Mubayi, Iliopoulos showed that any $k$-uniform uncrowded hypergraph of maximum degree $Δ$ has list chromatic number at most $(1+o(1))(k-1)\Big(\fracΔ{\logΔ}\Big)^{\frac{1}{k-1}}$. Determining the optimal leading constant in this bound remains a major open problem. A natural target for the constant, suggested by the coupon-collector heuristic, is $(k-1)^{\frac{1}{k-1}}$, which also arises independently as the shattering threshold for coloring and finding large independent sets in sparse random hypergraphs. We show that uncrowded hypergraphs attain this threshold: for $k \ge 2$, every $k$-uniform uncrowded hypergraph $\mathcal{H}$ of maximum degree at most $Δ$ satisfies $$χ_\ell(\mathcal{H})\le(1+o(1))\Big((k-1)\fracΔ{\logΔ}\Big)^{\frac{1}{k-1}}.$$ This matches the coupon-collector heuristic, and establishes a 2019 conjecture of Molloy for uncrowded hypergraphs. As a consequence, we show that every $k$-uniform linear hypergraph of maximum degree at most $Δ$ has chromatic number at most $c_k\Big(\fracΔ{\log Δ}\Big)^{\frac{1}{k-1}}$ with $c_k=1-o_k(1)$, resolving, in a stronger form, a recent conjecture of Verstraëte and Wilson on the independence number of linear hypergraphs. Our techniques yield the first palette sparsification result for hypergraph coloring using $o(Δ^{\frac{1}{k-1}})$ colors per vertex. Specifically, for an uncrowded $k$-graph $\mathcal{H}$ and $q=Θ\Big({\Big(\fracΔ{γ\logΔ}\Big)^{\frac{1}{k-1}}}\Big)$, sampling $Θ(Δ^{\fracγ{k-1}})$ colors per vertex suffices to obtain a proper $q$-coloring of $\mathcal{H}$ w.h.p. As an algorithmic consequence, we obtain a single-pass streaming algorithm using $O\big(n^{1+o(1)}\big)$ space for uncrowded $k$-graphs, and, via hypergraph partitioning, for linear hypergraphs as well.

papers.title: Long-time asymptotics of a full Camassa-Holm soliton gas
papers.abstract: We investigate the long-time asymptotics of a full soliton gas for the Camassa--Holm equation. The analysis starts from a pure-soliton Riemann--Hilbert (RH) problem with \(2N\) poles and two distinct types of residue conditions. We prove that, as \(N\to\infty\), this discrete RH problem converges to a limiting soliton gas RH problem whose jump matrix contains two nonzero reflection coefficients. In this sense, the limiting problem gives a full soliton gas model for the Camassa--Holm equation, in contrast to the previously studied half soliton gas models, whose jump matrices involve only one nonzero reflection coefficient. The limiting RH problem is analyzed by the Deift--Zhou nonlinear steepest descent method. The presence of two nonzero reflection coefficients requires two different types of triangular factorizations of the jump matrix and leads to a more delicate \(g\)-function mechanism. The main difficulty lies in the construction of suitable \(g\)-functions adapted to the Camassa--Holm phase, together with the precise control of their behavior near the distinguished point \(k=i/2\) and at infinity. Depending on the location of the spectral endpoints \(η_1\) and \(η_2\), different \(g\)-function mechanisms arise. In this paper, we focus on Case I and derive the long-time asymptotic formulas in three elliptic-wave regions of the self-similar plane. In each region, the leading term is given by a finite-gap elliptic function, while in the central region the first correction is of order \(\mathcal O(t^{-1/2})\) and involves parabolic cylinder functions.

papers.title: Quantitative Homogenization and Uniform Lipschitz Estimates for Lamé-Stokes Systems
papers.abstract: We study homogenization of Lamé-Stokes systems with fixed material parameters. Incompressible elastic inclusions are periodically distributed in a connected elastic matrix, with an elastic buffer near the outer boundary. The divergence constraint acts only in the inclusions, and the full pressure contributes to interface traction. We identify the effective elasticity system for the traction problem of period $\varepsilon$. Under the respective regularity assumptions, we obtain the optimal $O(\varepsilon)$ convergence rate for the displacement in $L^2$. For the unsmoothed first-order approximation, the displacement error in $H^1$ and the pressure error in $L^2$ over the inclusions are both $O(\varepsilon^{1/2})$. For a $C^{1,1}$ outer boundary, both errors improve to $O(\varepsilon)$ on every fixed interior subdomain. We establish local interface Schauder estimates including the full pressure and combine them with large-scale iteration to obtain Lipschitz estimates for the displacement up to the boundary and $L^\infty$ bounds for the pressure in the inclusions. These Lipschitz and pressure bounds are uniform in $\varepsilon$ for $C^{1,κ}$ interfaces and outer boundary and compatible $C^{0,τ}$ traction data, where $0<τ<κ<1$.

papers.title: Sharp minimax risks and phase transitions in sparse submatrix detection
papers.abstract: In this paper, we study the minimax risk of detecting a sparse, elevated-mean Gaussian submatrix planted in a larger noisy matrix. When the planted submatrix has size $n\times n$ and the ambient matrix has size $N\times N$ with $N=n^{1+α}$, the seminal work of Butucea and Ingster (2013) identifies the sharp detection boundary around which the risk converges to $0$ or $1$. We extend that zero-one theory by determining sharp risk asymptotics throughout a two-parameter phase diagram. Above the boundary, the risk decays stretched- or super-exponentially fast, and we determine its precise exponent. Below the boundary, where the risk tends to $1$, we obtain matching absolute-constant bounds for its polynomial rate of convergence. In both regimes, the asymptotics change across the line $α+δ=1/2$, where $δ$ parametrizes the signed distance from the detection boundary. Finally, on the boundary, we show that the minimax risk converges to the nondegenerate constant $\frac12$ in a very sparse regime where $n$ remains fixed and $N\to\infty$. Each of these rates corresponds to the risk of a suitably calibrated scan or sum test, whence follow the upper bounds. The main problem is to derive the matching regime-specific lower bounds. The mixture likelihood ratio is an average rather than a product and thus its logarithm lacks the additive structure required by standard large deviation formulations. On the other hand, classical second-moment estimates fail to be sharp due to overlap-induced correlations. To address these issues, we develop two general lower-bound principles based on truncated mixture likelihoods, tailored to the target risks on both sides of the detection boundary. The same framework yields sharp risk asymptotics for sparse subtensors with equal side lengths and also applies to more general testing problems including the detection of rectangular subtensors.

papers.title: Spectral embedding through weak* limit of finite-dimensional approximations
papers.abstract: The scope of this text is to study a process that induces another proof of the Spectral Embedding Theorem: that any densely defined symmetric operator can be extended by a multiplication operator through an embedding of the Hilbert space into an $L_2$ space. Furthermore, that process is meant to be used for specific operators, where natural spectral embeddings or equivalences may be found. That process has previously been considered in arXiv:2411.06281 and in arXiv:2511.18189, where it has been introduced through nonstandard techniques. Our contribution aims to be the reformulation of the theory through classical analysis arguments, without the use of nonstandard techniques nor ultraproducts.

papers.title: Duality theory for categorical theories
papers.abstract: We have generalised the notion of categorical theory in model theory to the context of coherent theories. We prove a duality result between the full sub-2-category of pretopoi which are categorical, and the 2-category of profinite monoids. We also study the geometry of profinite monoids via the classifying topos construction, and show it identifies them as a full sub-2-category of the 2-category of topoi.

papers.title: Block-equivalent finite Gabor frames
papers.abstract: We study finite systems of vectors whose frame operator matrices are unitarily equivalent, via explicit and computationally efficient unitary transformations, to block-diagonal matrices. We call such systems block-equivalent. We show that a Gabor system $\mathcal{G}=\mathcal{G}(g,L\times K)\subset \mathbb C^N$ is block-equivalent when either the modulation set $L$ or the translation set $K$ is a subgroup of $\mathbb Z_N$. We also characterize situations in which the frame operator matrix becomes diagonal. Finally, we show that geometric conditions on subsets of $\mathbb Z_N$ force certain diagonals of the frame operator matrix of $\mathcal{G}$ to vanish, yielding additional sparsity and block structures.

papers.title: Explicit Kodaira-Spencer maps over PEL Shimura varieties
papers.abstract: The goal of our work is to construct a class of morphisms between two canonical line bundles on integral models of PEL Shimura varieties via Kodaira--Spencer maps, and explicitly compute such morphisms and their effects on the canonical metrics of line bundles. This result provides a concrete method for comparing two canonical line bundles and the corresponding arithmetic intersection numbers. In particular, it allows us to give an explicit relationship between the height functions defined by these two line bundles.

papers.title: Transition Time for Weak Singularities of the Navier-Stokes Equations
papers.abstract: This paper constructs a rigorous mathematical framework for investigating laminar-turbulent transition induced by weak singularities of incompressible Navier-Stokes (NS) equations. By integrating the energy identity of Leray weak solutions with the singularity criterion $\left\lVert \boldsymbol{u} \right\rVert_{H_0^1(Ω)}\to0$, a closed analytical form of the laminar-turbulent transition characteristic time is derived. The theoretical scaling $t_{\text{trans}}\simν/U^2$ (equivalent to $t_{\text{trans}}\sim t_c/\text{Re}$) is verified to be consistent with classical experimental observations in shear flows. This work reveals that laminar-turbulent transition is dominated by the local regularity collapse of Leray weak solutions rather than global viscous diffusion, and provides a novel theoretical interpretation for the onset of turbulence from the perspective of NS equation weak singularities.

papers.title: A Continuous-Time Actor-Critic Framework for Jump-Diffusion Controls with Normalizing Flows
papers.abstract: Continuous-time stochastic control with time-inhomogeneous jump-diffusion dynamics is central in finance and economics, but computing optimal policies is difficult under explicit time dependence, discontinuous shocks, and high dimensionality. We propose an actor-critic framework that serves as a mesh-free solver for entropy-regularized control problems and stochastic games with jumps. The approach is built on a time-inhomogeneous little q-function and an appropriate occupation measure, yielding a policy-gradient representation that accommodates time-dependent drift, volatility, and jump terms. To represent expressive stochastic policies in continuous-action spaces, we parameterize the actor using conditional normalizing flows, enabling flexible non-Gaussian policies while retaining exact likelihood evaluation for entropy regularization and policy optimization. We validate the method on time-inhomogeneous linear-quadratic control, Merton portfolio optimization, and a multi-agent portfolio game, using explicit solutions or high-accuracy benchmarks. Numerical results demonstrate stable learning under jump discontinuities, accurate approximation of optimal stochastic policies, and favorable scaling with respect to dimension and number of agents.

papers.title: Finite-Time Weak Singularities and the Statistical Structure of Turbulence in 3D Incompressible Navier-Stokes Equations
papers.abstract: This paper provides a rigorous mathematical analysis of the global regularity problem for the 3D incompressible Navier-Stokes (NS) equations, specifically addressing the conditions under which smooth initial data may lead to a loss of regularity. By departing from traditional phenomenological turbulence models and focusing strictly on the mechanical energy transport equation, we derive a fundamental critical condition, $\boldsymbol{u}\cdot\nabla E = 0,$ where $E = \frac12|\boldsymbol{u}|^2 + p$ is the specific mechanical energy, which characterizes the transition from laminar to turbulent flow.

papers.title: Coloopless zonotopes and counterexamples to the Shifted Lonely Runner Conjecture
papers.abstract: Henze and Malikiosis (2017) have shown that the Lonely Runner Conjecture (LRC) can be restated as a convex-geometric question on the so-called LR zonotopes, lattice zonotopes with one more generator than their dimension. This relation naturally suggests a more general statement, the shifted LRC, the zonotopal version of which concerns a classical parameter, the covering radius. In this paper we do two things: 1) We show explicit counterexamples to both the shifted Lonely Runner Conjecture (starting at $n=5$) and to the Lonely Vector Property of Malikiosis-Schymura-Santos (2025). 2) We push the analogies between the two versions of LRC and their zonotopal counterparts, in particular highlighting that the proofs of the finite-checking Theorems A and B in Malikiosis-Schymura-Santos (2025) are more transparent, and the statements more general, if regarded in terms of two quite general classes of lattice zonotopes: the coloopless zonotopes that we introduce here and the cosimple ones, already defined by them.

papers.title: Weak Singularity of Navier-Stokes Equations Based on Energy Estimation in Sobolev Space
papers.abstract: Based on Dou Huashu's energy gradient theory, this paper focuses on the weak singularity of the incompressible Navier-Stokes (NS) equations in steady, fully developed flows. When the gradient of total mechanical energy is perpendicular to the streamline (i.e., $ u_j \frac{\partial E}{\partial x_j} = 0 $), substituting this critical condition into the NS equations with no-slip boundary conditions leads to the viscous term $ ν\to 0 $. To rigorously analyze the regularity of the solution, Sobolev space $ H_0^1(Ω) $ is introduced for energy estimation. The results show that the velocity field loses $ H^1 $-regularity, and the NS equations degenerate into Euler equations, which admit discontinuous weak solutions. Thus, the position where the mechanical energy gradient is perpendicular to the streamline becomes a weak singularity of the NS equations.

papers.title: Liouville phenomenon for the Klein-Gordon equation in 1+1 dimensions
papers.abstract: We study the Klein-Gordon equation in one spatial and one temporal dimension. Physically, this equation describes the wave function of a relativistic spinless boson with positive rest mass. Mathematically, this is the most elementary hyperbolic partial differential equation, after the wave equation itself. Relative to the origin, the spacetime splits according to the light cones, and we find four quarter-planes, two of which are timelike while the remaining two are spacelike. Not unexpectedly, the solutions behave quite differently in the two types of quarter-planes. It turns out that the spacelike quarter-planes exhibit a Liouville phenomenon, where insufficient growth forces the solutions to display a certain kind of symmetry, where the values on the two linear edges are in a one-to-one relation. This phenomenon shares features with the classical Liouville theorem as well as the Phragmen-Lindelof principle for harmonic functions. We obtain sharp transition from uniqueness to nonuniqueness.

papers.title: Decomposition of Spillover Effects Under Misspecification: Pseudo-true Estimands and a Local-Global Extension
papers.abstract: To measure spillovers, researchers often summarize who else was treated with a simple measure, such as the share of treated neighbors. We study what the researcher estimates when that summary is misspecified. We show that the researcher estimates the best approximation to the true policy effect among all functionals of the chosen summary, and that the usual direct and spillover estimates are exactly the components of this approximation. We then specialize this framework to a setting common in applications such as cash transfers: treatment spills over both globally, through market equilibrium, and locally, through network externalities, while the researcher models only one channel. The network estimator still recovers the network spillover, and the equilibrium estimator the equilibrium spillover, even when the other channel is ignored. We illustrate with a simulation calibrated to a large cash-transfer experiment.

papers.title: Almost Sure Convergence of Stochastic Approximation: An Interplay of Noise and Step Size
papers.abstract: We study the almost sure convergence of the Stochastic Approximation algorithm to the fixed point $x^\star$ of a nonlinear operator under a negative drift condition and a general noise sequence with finite $p$-th moment for some $p > 1$. Classical almost sure convergence results of Stochastic Approximation are mostly analyzed for the square-integrable noise setting, and it is shown that any non-summable but square-summable step size sequence is sufficient to obtain almost sure convergence. However, such a limitation prevents wider algorithmic application. In particular, many applications in Machine Learning and Operations Research admit heavy-tailed noise with infinite variance, rendering such guarantees inapplicable. On the other hand, when a stronger condition on the noise is available, such guarantees on the step size would be too conservative, as practitioners would like to pick a larger step size for a more preferable convergence behavior. To this end, we show that any non-summable but $p$-th power summable step size sequence is sufficient to guarantee almost sure convergence, covering the gap in the literature. For the regime $p \in (1, 2)$, we show that using the $\|x-x^\star\|^p$-like Lyapunov function and applying the Holder-smoothness bound suffice. For $p > 2$, such an approach is no longer applicable, and therefore, we introduce a novel iterate projection technique to control the nonlinear terms produced by high-moment bounds and multiplicative noise. We believe our proof techniques and their implications could be of independent interest and pave the way for finite-time analysis of Stochastic Approximation under a general drift condition. As a starting point, we establish almost sure convergence results for non-expansive operators under a multiplicative noise condition for $p \in (1,2]$ and an additive noise condition for $p \in (2,\infty)$.

papers.title: Stability analysis of Arbitrary-Lagrangian-Eulerian ADER-DG methods on classical and degenerate spacetime geometries
papers.abstract: In this paper, we present a thorough von Neumann stability analysis of explicit and implicit Arbitrary-Lagrangian-Eulerian (ALE) ADER discontinuous Galerkin (DG) methods on classical and degenerate spacetime geometries for hyperbolic equations. First, we rigorously study CFL stability conditions for the explicit ADER-DG method, confirming results widely used in the literature while specifying their limitations. Moreover, we discuss stability bounds for ALE methods and characterize the admissible range of grid velocities once a target CFL is fixed. Next, we extend the stability study to ADER-DG in the presence of degenerate spacetime elements, with zero size at the beginning and the end of the time step, but with a non zero spacetime volume. This kind of elements has been introduced in a series of articles on direct ALE methods by Gaburro et al. to connect via spacetime control volumes regenerated Voronoi tessellations after a topology change. Here, we imitate this behavior in a 1d surrogate setting by fictitiously inserting degenerate elements in between two cells. We show that over this simplified degenerate spacetime geometry, both for the explicit and implicit ADER-DG, the von Neumann analysis leads to the same CFL stability conditions as those for classical geometries, laying the theoretical foundations for their use in the context of ALE methods.

papers.title: Two Hornich-Hlawka-type and Gram matrix-based inequalities
papers.abstract: We establish two inequalities in real inner product spaces. The first is a multiplicative strengthening of the classical Hornich-Hlawka inequality: for all vectors $x,y,z$ in a real inner product space $H$, \[ \|x\|\,\|y\| + \|z\|\,\|x+y+z\| \;\geq\; \|x+z\|\,\|y+z\|.\] We provide a complete characterization of the equality cases. The second result is a parametric inequality derived from the positive semidefiniteness of Gram matrices: for all $x,y,z \in H$ and $α, β, γ\in \mathbb{R}$, \[ α^2\|x\|^2\langle y,z\rangle^2 + β^2\|y\|^2\langle x,z\rangle^2 + γ^2\|z\|^2\langle x,y\rangle^2 + 2(αβ+ αγ+ βγ)\langle x,y\rangle\langle x,z\rangle\langle y,z\rangle \;\geq\; 0 \], which, upon optimization over the parameters yields sharp reverse inequalities to the Gram determinant inequality $\det G \geq 0$. As a special case, this recovers and strengthens the classical Cauchy-Schwarz inequality.

papers.title: Decentralized Multi-product Pricing: Diagonal Dominance, Nash Equilibrium, and Price of Anarchy
papers.abstract: Decentralized pricing in multi-product firms and marketplaces can lose revenue because each decision maker ignores how its price affects the demand for other products. We quantify this loss through the price of anarchy of a game in which the price of each product is set to maximize that product's own revenue. Demand is linear, and cross-price effects may be substitutes or complements and need not be symmetric. Under a two-sided diagonal dominance condition with parameter $μ\in[0,1)$, which bounds the aggregate absolute cross-price effects in each row and column relative to the own-price effect, we show that the game has a unique Nash equilibrium and that equilibrium revenue is at least a fraction $4(1-μ)/(2-μ)^2$ of the centralized optimum. This bound was previously known for symmetric gross substitutes; we show that it remains valid for signed and asymmetric interactions, and that it is tight. Because asymmetry breaks the simultaneous diagonalization underlying existing analyses, we instead evaluate the revenue gap at the equilibrium itself. This yields an exact formula for the worst-case price of anarchy of each demand matrix in terms of a normalized interaction matrix, which can be much sharper than the scalar bound in heterogeneous interaction networks. The same argument extends the guarantee to jointly concave nonlinear demand under pointwise dominance of the demand Jacobian, for every pure-strategy equilibrium.

papers.title: Positive weak solutions of a double-phase variable exponent problem with a fractional-Hardy-type singular potential and superlinear nonlinearity
papers.abstract: In the present paper, we study a double-phase variable exponent problem which is set up within a variational framework including a singular potential of fractional-Hardy-type. We employ the Mountain-Pass theorem and the strong minimum principle to obtain the existence of at least one nontrivial positive weak solution.

papers.title: Random-Bridges as Stochastic Transports for Generative Models
papers.abstract: This paper motivates the use of random-bridges -- stochastic processes conditioned to take target distributions at fixed timepoints -- in the realm of generative modelling. Herein, random-bridges act as stochastic transports between two probability distributions when appropriately initialized, displaying either Markovian or non-Markovian, and continuous, discontinuous, or hybrid patterns depending on the choice of the driving process. We show how one can start from general probabilistic statements and branch out into specific representations for learning and simulation algorithms. Essentially, our framework formulates stochastic transports as noisy information processes governing the dynamic translation and propagation of information between arbitrary probability measures. Our theoretical and algorithmic presentation details training and simulation frameworks for both Gaussian and Lévy (specifically, Gamma, Poisson and Stable-$1/2$) random-bridge transports. The empirical validation focuses on the Gaussian case for demonstration and comparison purposes, where our construct delivers high-quality samples, achieving competitive Fréchet Inception Distance scores compared to widely used denoising diffusions and flow matching frameworks.

papers.title: Teleportation=Translation: Continuous recovery of black hole information
papers.abstract: The \textit{Teleportation=Translation} conjecture posits that the recovery of information from a black hole is dual to a geometric translation in the emergent spacetime. In this paper, we establish this equivalence for general local quantum field theories by constructing a continuous unitary interpolation that bridges discrete algebraic teleportation protocols and continuous modular flow. We resolve the failure of dynamic idempotency, fundamentally inherent in Type III von Neumann algebras, by employing the Haagerup-Kosaki crossed-product construction. This lift to the semifinite Type~II$_\infty$ envelope yields a canonical, dynamically consistent path. Crucially, we prove that its unique infinitesimal generator $\tilde{G}$ is exactly twice the geometric modular momentum ($\tilde{G}=2P$). We establish this identity as a closed operator equivalence using Nelson's analytic vector theorem and quantify its structural robustness via non-commutative $L^p$ theory. Ultimately, our results demonstrate that unitary information recovery fundamentally manifests as a continuous geometric translation. This provides a rigorous operator-algebraic mechanism for resolving the black hole information paradox, offering a kinematic framework naturally extendable to include gravitational back-reaction.

papers.title: Henneberg-Type Minimal Immersions in $\mathbb{R}^4$
papers.abstract: We construct a family of higher-order Henneberg-type minimal surfaces in $\mathbb{R}^4$ from explicit holomorphic data in a generalized Weierstrass--Enneper representation. The construction retains the polynomial reciprocal structure of the classical Henneberg data and yields explicit holomorphic primitives and real parametrizations for the family $\mathcal H_{(m,n)}$. We distinguish regular points from branch points, analyze the role of the complex parameter $λ$, and show that the real-$λ$ subfamily $\mathcal H_{(1,1)}$ lies in a three-dimensional linear subspace. For $\mathcal H_{(1,1)}$, we compute the induced conformal metric and Gaussian curvature, proving that the curvature is negative at every regular point. An explicit parametrization is given for $\mathcal H_{(1,1)}$, together with three-dimensional coordinate projections used solely for visualization. We also derive an integral-free formulation in terms of a single holomorphic seed function and identify the exceptional values $λ=\pm i$ for the inverse reconstruction formula.

papers.title: Fejér--Riesz factorization for positive noncommutative trigonometric polynomials
papers.abstract: We prove a Fejér-Riesz type factorization for positive matrix-valued noncommutative trigonometric polynomials on $\mathscr{W}\times\mathfrak{Y}$, where $\mathscr{W}$ is either the free semigroup $\langle x \rangle_g$ or the free product group $\mathbb{Z}_2^{g}$, and $\mathfrak{Y}$ is a discrete group. More precisely, using the shortlex order, if $A$ has degree at most $w$ in the $\mathscr{W}$ variables and is uniformly strictly positive on all unitary representations of $\mathscr{W}\times\mathfrak{Y}$, then $A=B^{*}B$ with $B$ analytic and of $\mathscr{W}$-degree at most $w$; this degree bound is optimal, and strict positivity is essential. As an application, we obtain degree-bounded sums-of-squares certificates for Bell-type inequalities in $\mathbb{C}[\mathbb{Z}_2^{*g}\times \mathbb{Z}_2^{*h}]$ from quantum information theory. In the special case $\mathscr{W}=\mathbb{Z}^h$ we recover, in the matrix-valued setting, the classical commutative multivariable Fejér-Riesz factorization. For trivial $\mathfrak{Y}$ we obtain a ``perfect'' group-algebra Positivstellensatz on $\mathbb{Z}_2^{*g}$ that does not require strict positivity; this result is sharp, as demonstrated by counterexamples in $\mathbb{Z}_2*\mathbb{Z}_3$ and $\mathbb{Z}_3^{*2}$. To establish our main results two novel ingredients of independent interest are developed: (a) a positive-semidefinite Parrott theorem with entries given by functions on a group; and (b) solutions to positive semidefinite matrix completion problems for $\langle x \rangle_g$ or the free product group $\mathbb{Z}_2^{*g}$ indexed by words in $\mathscr{W}$ of length $\le w$.

papers.title: Line-width and path-width
papers.abstract: For finite graphs, path-width is an interesting and useful concept, but if we extend it to infinite graphs in the most obvious way (by making the indexing path infinite), it does not work nicely. The simplest extension that works nicely is to allow the indexing set to be any totally-ordered set, and then the corresponding decomposition is called a ``line-decomposition'', and the maximum bag size needed is called ``line-width''. In particular, the indexing set need not be a well-order; but the corresponding decomposition would be easier to use if it was. We show that if a graph has line-width at most $k$, it admits a well-ordered line-decomposition with width at most $2k$, and this is best possible.

papers.title: Every $S^2$-Bundle over a positive genus($g>1$) Surface has Mapping Class Group of Infinite Rank
papers.abstract: In 2025, Lin, Wu, Xie and Zhang extend Dax invariant from embedded disks to embedded surfaces and show that there is surjective homomorphism from $MCG(M)$ to $\mathbb{Z}^{\infty}$ for $M= Σ\times S^2$. Let $Σ$ be a closed surface with positive$(g>1)$ genus, in the paper we show that for any nontrivial $S^2$ fiber bundles $X= Σ\ltimes S^2$, whether $X$ orientable or nonorientable, there is a surjective homomorphism from $MCG(X)$ to $\mathbb{Z}^{\infty}$. The proof is an application of generalization of Dax invariants for embedded surfaces and the restriction on pseudo-isotopy subgroup $MCG_0(X)$ also surjects on $\mathbb{Z}^{\infty}$. The property of $MCG(X)$ inherits from trivial fiber bundle $Σ\times S^2$ and main theorem shows that the algebraic size of the smooth mapping class group of $S^2$-fiber bundles does not depend on the triviality of the bundle.

papers.title: Anyonic membranes and Pontryagin statistics
papers.abstract: Anyons, unique to two spatial dimensions, underlie extraordinary phenomena such as the fractional quantum Hall effect, but their generalization to higher dimensions has remained elusive.
