The topology of Eilenberg-MacLane spaces constrains the loop statistics to be only bosonic or fermionic in any dimension. In this work, we introduce the novel anyonic statistics for membrane excitations in four dimensions. Analogous to the $\mathbb{Z}_N$-particle exhibiting $\mathbb{Z}_{N\times \gcd(2,N)}$ anyonic statistics in two dimensions, we show that the $\mathbb{Z}_N$-membrane possesses $\mathbb{Z}_{N\times \gcd(3,N)}$ anyonic statistics in four dimensions. Given unitary volume operators that create membrane excitations on the boundary, we propose an explicit 56-step unitary sequence that detects the membrane statistics. We further analyze the boundary theory of $(5{+}1)$D 1-form $\mathbb{Z}_N$ symmetry-protected topological phases and demonstrate that their domain walls realize all possible anyonic membrane statistics. We then show that the $\mathbb{Z}_3$ subgroup persists in all higher dimensions. In addition to the standard fermionic $\mathbb{Z}_2$ membrane statistics arising from Stiefel-Whitney classes, membranes also exhibit $\mathbb{Z}_3$ statistics associated with Pontryagin classes. We explicitly verify that the 56-step process detects the nontrivial $\mathbb{Z}_3$ statistics in 5, 6, and 7 spatial dimensions. Moreover, in 7 and higher dimensions, the statistics of membrane excitations stabilize to $\mathbb{Z}_{2} \times \mathbb{Z}_{3}$, with the $\mathbb{Z}_3$ sector consistently captured by this process.

papers.title: Modeling FO-limits for monadically stable sequences
papers.abstract: We show that given a monadically stable theory $T$, a sufficiently saturated $\mathbf M \models T$, and a coherent system of probability measures on the $σ$-algebras generated by parameter-definable sets of $\mathbf M$ in each dimension, we may produce a totally Borel $\mathbf B \prec \mathbf M$ realizing these measures. Our main application is to prove that every FO-convergent sequence of structures (with countable signature) from a monadically stable class admits a modeling limit. As another consequence, we prove a Borel removal lemma for monadically stable Lebesgue relational structures.

papers.title: Global well-posedness and asymptotic behavior of large strong solutions to the 3D full compressible Navier-Stokes equations with temperature-dependent coefficients
papers.abstract: It is well known that the global well-posedness of the Navier-Stokes equations with temperature-dependent coefficients is a challenging problem, especially in multi-dimensional space. In this paper, we study the 3D Navier-Stokes equations with temperature-dependent coefficients in the whole space. When the initial density and the initial temperature are linearly equivalent to some large constant states, we establish the first result on the global existence of large strong solution. Moreover, the optimal decay rates of the solution to its associated equilibrium are established when the initial data belong to $L^{p_0}(\mathbb{R}^3)$ for some $p_0\in[1,2]$.

papers.title: Diagonally-Weighted Generalized Method of Moments Estimation for Gaussian Mixture Modeling
papers.abstract: With direct computation of moments through order $L$ in $d$ dimensions, standard method of moments (MM) incurs $Ω(d^L)$ computation and storage costs, and standard generalized method of moments (GMM) additionally requires estimating and inverting an often ill-conditioned covariance matrix of size $Ω(d^L)$-by-$Ω(d^L)$ to obtain the optimal weighting matrix. Pereira, Kileel, and Kolda [arXiv:2202.06930 (2022)] avoid the tensor computation cost of MM through implicit moment computation. Despite this progress, incorporating statistically principled weighting while preserving computational efficiency remains an important challenge, particularly at low signal-to-noise ratio (SNR), where sampling variances can differ substantially across moment orders. We introduce diagonally-weighted GMM (DGMM), which assigns one adaptive weight to each moment order through a structured approximation of the optimal weighting matrix while avoiding the covariance inversion, thereby balancing statistical efficiency, computational complexity, and numerical stability. For general parametric models, we prove that DGMM is consistent, asymptotically normal, and near-efficient under explicit structural conditions. For heteroscedastic low-rank Gaussian mixtures, we design a computationally efficient and numerically stable algorithm that extends the implicit moment computation to the DGMM objective, gradients, and weights and incorporates Nyström approximations of the kernel sums. In low-SNR experiments with $d=100$ and $L=4$, where standard MM and GMM are infeasible, controlled weighting comparisons show that DGMM achieves consistently small parameter errors across tested initializations, including the challenging starts where alternative weightings struggle, with shorter median runtimes and fewer iterations. The code and data will be available upon publication at https://github.com/liu-lzhang/dgmm.

papers.title: Conformal Green functions and Yamabe metrics of Sobolev regularity
papers.abstract: We provide a full resolution of the Yamabe problem on closed 3-manifolds for Riemannian metrics of Sobolev class $W^{2,q}$ with $q > 3$. This requires developing an elliptic theory for the conformal Laplacian for rough metrics and establishing existence, regularity and a delicate blow-up analysis for its Green function. Most of the analytical work is carried out in dimensions $n \geq 3$ and for $W^{2,q}$ Riemannian metrics with $q>\tfrac{n}{2}$ and should be of independent interest.

papers.title: Differential operators on Hermitian modular forms on $\mathrm{U}(n, n)$
papers.abstract: We construct explicit differential operators on hermitian modular forms, extending methods developed for Siegel modular forms. These differential operators are closely related to the two-variable spherical pluriharmonic polynomials. We construct explicit bases for the space of such polynomials and use them to build concrete operators. As an application, we derive an exact pullback formula for hermitian Eisenstein series.

papers.title: 2-Segal sets and pseudomonoids in the bicategory of spans
papers.abstract: In this survey article, we give an introduction to the notion of a 2-Segal set and prove that 2-Segal sets are equivalent to pseudomonoids in the bicategory of spans. The proof utilizes graphical techniques for 2-Segal sets and spans that should be useful in more general settings. There are procedures for obtaining an associative algebra from a 2-Segal set (satisfying finiteness conditions). We describe these procedures and give several examples of algebras arising from 2-Segal sets. Wherever possible, we avoid higher category theory so as to make the paper accessible to a wide audience.

papers.title: Multi-cut stochastic approximation methods for solving stochastic convex composite optimization
papers.abstract: This paper considers the stochastic convex composite optimization problem and presents multi-cut stochastic approximation (SA) methods for solving it, whose models in expectation overestimate its objective function. The multi-cut model obtained by taking the maximum of a finite number of linearizations of the stochastic objective function provides a biased estimate of the objective function, with the error being uncontrollable. Instead, our proposed SA method uses models obtained by taking the maximum of a finite number of one-cut models, i.e., suitable convex combinations of linearizations of the stochastic objective function. It is shown that the proposed methods achieve nearly optimal convergence rate and have computational performance comparable, and sometimes superior, to other SA-type methods.

papers.title: Successive Convexification for Passively-Safe Spacecraft Rendezvous on Near Rectilinear Halo Orbit
papers.abstract: We present an optimization-based approach for fuel-efficient spacecraft rendezvous to Gateway, a lunar space station architecture based on a near rectilinear halo orbit (NRHO) around the Earth-Moon L2 point. Our main contribution is a method that ensures safety at all times in the presence of Gaussian uncertainty while incorporating disturbance compensation feedback through correction maneuvers. Specifically, the approach: i) ensures passive safety and satisfies path constraints at all times, ii) satisfies the specifications for critical decision points along the trajectory, and iii) accounts for common uncertainties arising from orbital insertion maneuvers, actuation, and navigation measurements. To account for these uncertainties, we use both chance constraints and disturbance compensation feedback to bound the effects of errors. We leverage sequential convex programming (SCP) together with an isoperimetric reformulation of continuous-time path constraints, including passive safety, to eliminate the risk of inter-sample constraint violations common in existing methods. This enables sparse time discretization that supports efficient offline mission design and analysis and aligns with operational preferences for less frequent control actions. We demonstrate the method on a case study representative of Gateway rendezvous operations.

papers.title: On the closure of irregular orbits of the horocyclic flow on infinite finness
papers.abstract: The topological dynamics of the horocyclic flow h_R on the unit tangent bundle of a geometrically finite hyperbolic surface is well known. In particular on such a surface the flow h_R is minimal or the minimal sets are the periodic orbits. When the surface is geometrically infinite, the situation is more complex and the presence of possible irregular orbits makes the description of minimal sets complicated. In this text, we construct a family of infinite hyperbolic surfaces for which the horocyclic flow defined on the unit tangent bundle is not minimal.

papers.title: Mathematical programs with complementarity constraints and application to hyperparameter tuning
papers.abstract: We consider the Mathematical Program with Complementarity Constraints (MPCC). One of the main challenges in solving this problem is the systematic failure of standard constraint qualifications. Carefully accounting for the combinatorial nature of the complementarity constraints, tractable versions of the Mangasarian-Fromovitz Constraint Qualification (MFCQ) have been designed and widely studied in the literature. This paper looks closely at two such MPCC-MFCQs and their influence on MPCC algorithms. As a key contribution, we introduce a third MPCC-MFCQ, lying between these two, under which we prove the convergence of the inexact sequential penalisation and Scholtes relaxation algorithms. This significantly weakens the assumptions currently used in the literature. We then form the problem of tuning hyperparameters of a nonlinear Support Vector Machine (SVM), a fundamental machine learning problem for classification, as an MPCC. For this application, we establish that the aforementioned new qualification holds under very mild restrictions. Moreover, we program robust implementations and carry out comprehensive numerical experiments on real-world data sets, where we show that the sequential penalisation method applied to the MPCC formulation for tuning SVM hyperparameters can outperform both the Scholtes relaxation technique and the derivative-free methods from the machine learning literature.

papers.title: Asymptotically accurate and geometric locking-free finite element implementation of a refined shell theory
papers.abstract: Accurate finite element analysis of refined shell theories is crucial but often hindered by membrane and shear locking effects. While various element-based locking-free techniques exist, this work addresses the problem at the theoretical level by utilizing results from asymptotic analysis. A formulation of a 2D refined shell theory incorporating transverse shear is developed using rescaled coordinates and angles of rotation, ensuring equal asymptotic orders of magnitude for extension, bending, and rotation measures and their respective stiffnesses. This novel approach, implemented via isogeometric analysis, is shown to be both asymptotically accurate relative to the underlying refined shell theory and inherently free from membrane and shear locking. Numerical simulations of semi-cylindrical shells show excellent agreement between the analytical solutions, 2D refined shell theory predictions, and 3D elasticity theory, validating the effectiveness and accuracy of the proposed formulation.

papers.title: Regularized Unbalanced Optimal Transport with Pearson Marginal Penalties
papers.abstract: We study quadratically regularized unbalanced optimal transport with Pearson marginal penalties and a lower bound $δ\ge0$ on the plan, including the sparse case $δ=0$. We organize the analysis around the active interface, where the plan switches from its lower bound to larger values. We prove a Newton remainder estimate that depends linearly on the marginal measure of the boundary layer around this interface, and a maximum-norm inverse estimate uniform over all Newton derivatives and cell volumes. Together they give local superlinear convergence of semismooth Newton iteration in function space, of q-order at least $1+α$ when the boundary-layer measure is $O(t^α)$, and a common convergence neighborhood along each refinement sequence whose data converge uniformly. Transverse interfaces give second-order supercloseness of the discrete potentials to the cell averages of the continuum potentials. A directional curvature condition on the input data verifies the interface condition before the solution is known and yields an explicit Newton convergence radius on all sufficiently fine meshes, uniformly in the lower bound. A globalized inexact semismooth Newton iteration has mesh-independent numbers of outer iterations and of full-array operations, that is, passes over the plan array. Its output satisfies an a posteriori error bound relative to the continuum optimal plan. Experiments test the rates at transverse interfaces and at interfaces with tangencies, the curvature criterion, and the algorithmic work. All estimates hold for a fixed regularization parameter and a fixed lower bound on the densities.

papers.title: Uniform bounds in excellent $\mathbf{F}_p$-algebras and applications to semi-continuity
papers.abstract: We study two important numerical invariants, Hilbert--Kunz multiplicity and $F$-signature, on the spectrum of a Noetherian $\mathbf{F}_p$-algebra $R$ that is not necessarily $F$-finite. When $R$ is excellent, we show that the limits defining the invariants are uniform. As a consequence, we show that the $F$-signature function (of the ring, pairs, and triples) is lower semi-continuous, and the Hilbert--Kunz multiplicity function is upper semi-continuous provided $R$ is locally equidimensional. Uniform convergence is achieved via a uniform version of Cohen--Gabber theorem. We prove the results under weaker conditions than excellence.

papers.title: Heavy-tailed random vectros: theory and applications
papers.abstract: In this paper we introduce and study several multivariate, heavy-tailed distribution classes, and we explore their closure properties and their applications. We consider the class of multivariate positively decreasing distributions, and its intersection with other multivariate distribution classes.

papers.title: Embeddings into the generic poset
papers.abstract: Let M be the generic poset, defined as the Fraïssé limit of the class of finite posets. We show that every countably infinite poset A can be embedded with coinfinite image into M so that each automorphism of the image of A extends uniquely to an automorphism of M.

papers.title: Convergence Analysis of Stochastic Accelerated Gradient Methods for Generalized Smooth Optimizations
papers.abstract: We investigate the Randomized Stochastic Accelerated Gradient (RSAG) method, utilizing either constant or adaptive step sizes, for stochastic optimization problems with generalized smooth objective functions. Under relaxed affine variance assumptions for the stochastic gradient noise, we establish high-probability convergence rates of order $\tilde{O}\left(\sqrt{\log(1/δ)/T}\right)$ for function value gaps in the convex setting, and for the squared gradient norms in the non-convex setting. Furthermore, when the noise parameters are sufficiently small, the convergence rate improves to $\tilde{O}\left(\log(1/δ)/T\right)$, where $T$ denotes the total number of iterations and $δ$ is the probability margin. Our analysis is also applicable to SGD with both constant and adaptive step sizes.

papers.title: A note on toric ideals of graphs and Knutson-Miller-Yong decompositions
papers.abstract: We use a Gröbner basis technique first introduced by Knutson, Miller and Yong to study the interplay between properties of a graph $G$ and algebraic properties of the toric ideal that it defines. We first recover a well-known height formula for the toric ideal of a graph $I_G$ and demonstrate an algebraic property that can detect when a graph deletion is bipartite. We also bound the chromatic number $χ(G)$ using information about an initial ideal of $I_G$.

papers.title: On the Theory of Bias Tuning in Event Cameras
papers.abstract: This paper lays the foundation of a theory for bias tuning in neuromorphic cameras, a novel sensing technology also known as "event cameras". We begin by formulating the high-level effect of the sensitivity biases on the camera's event rate in mathematical terms. We then show that, as a corollary of the Poincare-Miranda theorem, the commonly used tuning principles of rate budgeting and polarity balancing lead to a unique configuration of the sensitivity biases. As a corollary, we show how by adopting these principles, the multi-variable bias-tuning problem reduces to a two-parameter problem that can be resolved experimentally.

papers.title: Alberti representations and rectifiability of metric spaces
papers.abstract: We give a sufficient condition for a Borel subset $E\subset X$ of a complete metric space with $\mathrm{H}^n(E)<\infty$ to be $n$-rectifiable. This condition involves a decomposition of $E$ into rectifiable curves known as an \emph{Alberti representation}. Precisely, we show that if $\mathrm{H}^n|_E$ has $n$ independent Alberti representations, then $E$ is $n$-rectifiable. This is a sharp strengthening of prior results of Bate and Li. It has been known for some time that such a result answers many open questions concerning rectifiability in metric spaces, which we discuss.

papers.title: Density Hajnal--Szemerédi theorem for cliques of size four
papers.abstract: The exact minimum-degree thresholds that guarantee the existence of $k$ vertex-disjoint copies of the complete graph $K_r$ in an $n$-vertex graph were determined in the celebrated theorems of Dirac (1952) for $r=2$, Corrádi--Hajnal (1963) for $r=3$, and Hajnal--Szemerédi (1970) for general $r \ge 4$. A natural and fundamental problem is to determine the corresponding average-degree (or density) thresholds. This problem turns out to be substantially more difficult. The seminal theorem of Erdős--Gallai (1959) resolved the case $r=2$. The case $r=3$ was settled for large $n$ by Allen, Böttcher, Hladký, and Piguet~\cite{ABHP15}, who remarkably identified four distinct classes of extremal constructions arising in different ranges of $k$. They further posed the problem of establishing a density analogue of the Hajnal--Szemerédi theorem, noting that ``We are not even sure what the complete family of extremal graphs should be.'' In this paper, we establish an asymptotic density Hajnal-SzemerHedi theorem for \(K_4\) by determining \(\mathrm{ex}(n,(k+1)K_4)\) up to an additive \(O(n)\) term for all integers \(n\ge 4k\ge 0\). Five families of constructions show that this bound is sharp up to an additive \(O(n)\) term. For general \(r\ge 5\), we propose a candidate family consisting of \(r+1\) extremal construction classes.

papers.title: Historical behavior of skew products and arcsine laws
papers.abstract: We study the occurrence of historical behavior for almost every point in the setting of skew products with one-dimensional fiber dynamics. Under suitable ergodic conditions, we establish that a weak form of the arcsine law leads to the non-convergence of Birkhoff averages along almost every orbit. As an application, we show that this phenomenon occurs for one-step skew product maps over a Bernoulli shift, where the stochastic process induced by the iterates of the fiber maps is conjugate to a random walk. Furthermore, we revisit known examples of skew products that exhibit historical behavior almost everywhere, verifying that they fulfill the required ergodic and probabilistic conditions. Consequently, our results provide a unified and generalized framework that connects such behaviors to the arcsine distribution of the orbits.

papers.title: The many faces of a logarithmic scheme
papers.abstract: A standard assumption in the study of logarithmic structures is "fineness", but this assumption is not preserved by intersections, fiber products, and more general limits. We explain how a coherent logarithmic scheme $X$ has a natural decomposition into "fine faces" -- a collection of fine logarithmic subschemes. This allows for importation of the techniques of tropical geometry into the study of more general logarithmic schemes. We explain the relevance of the construction in enumerative geometry and moduli via a range of examples. Techniques developed in the study of binomial schemes lead to effective algorithms for computing the fine faces.

papers.title: Making Space for Time: The Special Galilean Group and Its Application to Some Robotics Problems
papers.abstract: The special Galilean group, usually denoted SGal(3), is a 10-dimensional Lie group whose important subgroups include the special orthogonal group, the special Euclidean group, and the group of extended poses. We briefly describe SGal(3) and its Lie algebra and show how the group structure supports a unified representation of uncertainty in space and time. Our aim is to highlight the potential usefulness of this group for several robotics problems.

papers.title: Wakamatsu tilting modules and Frobenius extensions
papers.abstract: Let $S/R$ be a Frobenius extension with $_RS_R$ centrally projective over $R$. We show that if $_Rω$ is a Wakamatsu tilting module then so is $_SS\otimes_Rω$, and the natural ring homomorphism from the endomorphism ring of $_Rω$ to the endomorphism ring of $_SS\otimes_Rω$ is a Frobenius extension provided that pd$(ω_T)$ is finite, where $T$ is the endomorphism ring of $_Rω$. We also show that the relative $n$-torsionfreeness of modules is preserved under Frobenius extensions. Furthermore, we give an application, which shows that the generalized G-dimension with respect to a Wakamatsu tilting module is invariant under Frobenius extensions.

papers.title: Les squelettes accessibles d'un espace de Berkovich
papers.abstract: We define a class of skeletons on Berkovich analytic spaces, which we call "accessible", which contains the standard skeleton of the n-dimensional torus for every n and is preserved by G-glueing, by taking the inverse image along a morphism of relative dimension zero, and by taking the direct image along a morphism whose restriction to the involved skeleton is topologically proper.

papers.title: Velocity surface disorder of large deviation rates for high-dimensional random walk in strongly mixing environment
papers.abstract: In this work, we establish the large deviation principles of random walk in strongly mixing environments. We show that the quenched and annealed rate functions share the same zero-set whose shape is either a singleton point or a line segment, with an illustrative example communicated and given by F. Rassoul-Agha. Furthermore, this paper reveals that under sufficiently low disorder, the two rate functions match on compact sets of both the interior and the boundary of the domain under finitely strongly mixing condition.

papers.title: Tropical thermodynamic formalism
papers.abstract: We investigate the zero-temperature large deviation principle for equilibrium states in the context of distance-expanding maps. The logarithmic-type zero-temperature limit in the large deviation principle induces a tropical algebra structure, which motivates our study of the tropical adjoint Bousch operator $\mathcal{L}_A^{*}$ since the Bousch operator $\mathcal{L}_A$ is tropical linear and corresponds to the Ruelle operator $\mathcal{R}_A$. We extend tropical functional analysis, define the adjoint operator $\mathcal{L}_A^{*}$ as a tropical analog of the adjoint Ruelle operator $\mathcal{R}_A^{*}$, and establish the existence and generic uniqueness of tropical eigendensities of $\mathcal{L}_A^{*}$ associated with the maximal eigenvalue. The Aubry set and the Mañé potential, both originating from weak KAM theory, serve as important tools in the representations of tropical eigendensities. With our notion of tropical completeness and our tropical Riesz representation theorem, $\mathcal{L}_A^{*}$ can also be seen as a version of the tropical Koopman operator.

papers.title: Mixed-norm Herz-type Besov spaces
papers.abstract: In this paper, we introduce mixed-norm Herz-type Besov spaces and establish their $\varphi$-transform characterization in the sense of Frazier and Jawerth. We also prove Sobolev embedding theorems for these spaces. The resulting embeddings extend and improve several known embedding results for mixed-norm Besov spaces.

papers.title: Bootstrap percolation and $P_3$-hull number in direct products of graphs
papers.abstract: The $r$-neighbor bootstrap percolation is a graph infection process based on the update rule by which a vertex with $r$ infected neighbors becomes infected. We say that an initial set of infected vertices propagates if all vertices of a graph $G$ are eventually infected, and the minimum cardinality of such a set in $G$ is called the $r$-bootstrap percolation number, $m(G,r)$, of $G$. In this paper, we study percolating sets in direct products of graphs. While in general graphs there is no non-trivial upper bound on $m(G\times H,r)$, we prove several upper bounds under the assumption $δ(G)\ge r$. We also characterize the connected graphs $G$ and $H$ with minimum degree $2$ that satisfy $m(G \times H, 2) = \frac{|V(G \times H)|}{2}$. In addition, we determine the exact values of $m(P_n \times P_m, 2)$, which are $m+n$ if $m$ and $n$ are both even, and $m+n-1$ otherwise.

papers.title: Radical subgroups of finite reductive groups
papers.abstract: Radical subgroups play an important role in both finite group theory and representation theory. This is the first of a series of papers of ours in classifying radical $p$-subgroups of finite reductive groups and in verifying the inductive blockwise Alperin weight condition for them, contributing to the program of proving the Alperin weight conjecture by verifying its inductive condition for finite simple groups. In this paper we present a uniform method for classifying radical subgroups of finite reductive groups. As applications, we investigate the inductive blockwise Alperin weight condition for classical groups, as well as groups of type $F_4$.

papers.title: The Lichtenbaum-Quillen dimension of complex varieties
papers.abstract: The Lichtenbaum-Quillen conjecture for smooth complex varieties states that algebraic and topological K-theory with finite coefficients become isomorphic in high degrees. We define the "Lichtenbaum-Quillen dimension" of a variety in terms of the point where this happens, show that it is surprisingly computable, and analyze many examples. It gives an obstruction to rationality, but one that turns out to be weaker than unramified cohomology and some related birational invariants defined by Colliot-Thélène and Voisin using Bloch-Ogus theory. Because it is compatible with semi-orthogonal decompositions, however, it allows us to prove some new cases of the integral Hodge conjecture using homological projective duality, and to compute the higher algebraic K-theory of the Kuznetsov components of the derived categories of some Fano varieties.

papers.title: An algebraic generalization of Giroux's criterion
papers.abstract: We compute the contact homology algebra of a neighborhood $(\mathbb{R}_τ \times W, ξ)$ of a convex hypersurface $W$ of any even dimension. This algebra is the derived tensor product of the augmentations of the chain-level contact homology of the dividing set, determined by the positive and negative regions of $W$. We describe methods for determining when the contact homology of $(\mathbb{R}_τ \times W, ξ)$ is non-zero in certain cases, which can be used to infer tightness of $ξ$. Full computations of contact homology are carried out in the case $\dim W = 2$.

papers.title: On the weight zero compactly supported cohomology of $\mathcal{H}_{g, n}$
papers.abstract: For $g\ge 2$ and $n\ge 0$, let $\mathcal{H}_{g,n}\subset \mathcal{M}_{g,n}$ denote the complex moduli stack of $n$-marked smooth hyperelliptic curves of genus $g$. A normal crossings compactification of this space is provided by the theory of pointed admissible $\mathbb{Z}/2\mathbb{Z}$-covers. We explicitly determine the resulting dual complex, and we use this to define a graph complex which computes the weight zero compactly supported cohomology of $\mathcal{H}_{g, n}$. Using this graph complex, we give a sum-over-graphs formula for the $S_n$-equivariant weight zero compactly supported Euler characteristic of $\mathcal{H}_{g, n}$. This formula allows for the computer-aided calculation, for each $g\le 7$, of the generating function $\mathsf{h}_g$ for these equivariant Euler characteristics for all $n$. More generally, we determine the dual complex of the boundary in any moduli space of pointed admissible $G$-covers of genus zero curves, when $G$ is a cyclic group of prime order, as a symmetric $Δ$-complex. We use these complexes to generalize our formula for $\mathsf{h}_g$ to moduli spaces of $n$-pointed smooth prime cyclic covers of genus zero curves. This version contains corrections to the published version: see the attached erratum.

papers.title: Geometric Eisenstein Series, Intertwining Operators, and Shin's Averaging Formula
papers.abstract: In the geometric Langlands program over function fields, Braverman-Gaitsgory and Laumon constructed geometric Eisenstein functors which geometrize the classical construction of Eisenstein series. Fargues and Scholze very recently constructed a general candidate for the local Langlands correspondence, via a geometric Langlands correspondence occurring over the Fargues-Fontaine curve. We carry some of the theory of geometric Eisenstein series over to the Fargues-Fontaine setting. Namely, given a quasi-split connected reductive group $G/\mathbb{Q}_{p}$ with simply connected derived group and maximal torus $T$, we construct an Eisenstein functor $\mathrm{nEis}(-)$, which takes sheaves on $Bun_{T}$ to sheaves on $Bun_{G}$. We show that, given a sufficiently nice $L$-parameter $φ_{T}: W_{\mathbb{Q}_{p}} \rightarrow \phantom{}^{L}T$, there is a Hecke eigensheaf on $Bun_{G}$ with eigenvalue $φ$, given by applying $\mathrm{nEis}(-)$ to the Hecke eigensheaf $\mathcal{S}_{φ_{T}}$ on $Bun_{T}$ attached to $φ_{T}$ by Fargues and Zou. We show that $\mathrm{nEis}(\mathcal{S}_{φ_{T}})$ interacts well with Verdier duality, and, assuming compatibility of the Fargues-Scholze correspondence with a suitably nice form of the local Langlands correspondence, provide an explicit formula for the stalks of the eigensheaf in terms of parabolic inductions of the character $χ$ attached to $φ_{T}$. This has several surprising consequences. First, it recovers special cases of an averaging formula of Shin for the cohomology of local Shimura varieties with rational coefficients, and generalizes it to the non-minuscule case. Second, it refines the averaging formula in the cases where the parameter $φ$ is sufficiently nice, giving an explicit formula for the degrees of cohomology that certain parabolic inductions sit in, and this refined formula holds even with torsion coefficients.

papers.title: A Simple Proof of the Riemann Hypothesis
papers.abstract: In this article, it is proved that the non-trivial zeros of the Riemann zeta function must lie on the critical line, known as the Riemann hypothesis.

papers.title: One-cycles on Gushel-Mukai fourfolds and the Beauville-Voisin filtration
papers.abstract: We prove that the invariant locus of the involution associated to a general double EPW sextic is a constant surface and introduce a filtration on $\CH_1$ of a Gushel-Mukai fourfold. We verify the sheaf/cycle correspondence for sheaves supported on low degree rational curves, parallel to the cubic fourfolds case.

papers.title: Difference sets in Quadratic Density Hales Jewett conjecture with 2 letters
papers.abstract: The Quadratic Density Hales Jewett conjecture with $2$ letters states that for large enough $n$, every dense subset of $\{0,1\}^{n^{2}}$ contains a combinatorial line where the wildcard set is of the form $γ\times γ$ where $γ\subset \{1,2,\dots n\}$. We show in an elementary quantitative way that every dense subset of $\{0,1\}^{n^{2}}$, for sufficiently large $n$, contains two elements such that the set of coordinate points where they differ, which we term the difference set of these two elements, is of the form $γ_{1}\times γ_{2}$ where $γ_1, γ_2$ are both nonempty subsets of $\{1,2,\dots n\}$. Further we give several non-trivial examples of dense vector subspaces of $\{0,1\}^{n^{2}}$, where in each case the wildcard set of the combinatorial line that can be obtained has restrictions on its size and shape.

papers.title: On Base Change of Local Stability in Positive Characteristics
papers.abstract: Let $X\to(C,c)$ be a flat family over a smooth curve germ over an algebraically closed field of characteristic $p>0$, with geometrically integral generic fiber. We show that the fiber pair stays log canonical after every finite dominant base change by a smooth curve if and only if it is log canonical after every finite Frobenius base change, including the original stage. More specifically, under iterated Frobenius pullback, a negative log discrepancy of a vertical divisor goes to minus infinity. For any fixed separable cover, however, log canonicity along the Frobenius tower of the original family gives a uniform lower bound instead. Putting these two bounds side by side gives the result for separable covers of arbitrary degree. We also illustrate that the single first Frobenius base change does not suffice in our criterion by an example. Finally, we include two more examples related to the main problem. Neither resolution of singularities nor inversion of adjunction is used.

papers.title: On metric space expansions
papers.abstract: When finding an original proof to a known result describing expansions on compact metric spaces as surjective isometries, we reveal that relaxing the condition of compactness to total boundedness preserves the isometry property and nearly that of surjectivity. While a counterexample is found showing that the converse to the above descriptions do not hold, we are able to characterize boundedness in terms of specific expansions we call anticontractions.

papers.title: On the non-hypercyclicity of normal operators, collections of their exponentials, and symmetric operators
papers.abstract: We give a simple, straightforward proof of the non-hypercyclicity of an arbitrary normal operator $A$ (bounded or unbounded) in a complex Hilbert space as well as of the collection $\left\{e^{tA}\right\}_{t\ge 0}$ of its exponentials, which, under a certain condition on the spectrum of $A$, is the $C_0$-semigroup generated by it. We also establish non-hypercyclicity for symmetric operators.

papers.title: On the Number of Circuits in Regular Matroids (with Connections to Lattices and Codes)
papers.abstract: We show that for any regular matroid on $m$ elements and any $α\geq 1$, the number of $α$-minimum circuits, or circuits whose size is at most an $α$-multiple of the minimum size of a circuit in the matroid is bounded by $m^{O(α^2)}$. This generalizes a result of Karger for the number of $α$-minimum cuts in a graph. As a consequence, we obtain similar bounds on the number of $α$-shortest vectors in "totally unimodular" lattices and on the number of $α$-minimum weight codewords in "regular" codes.

papers.title: Milnor fibrations and regularity conditions for real analytic mappings
papers.abstract: When f : R power n to R power p, is a surjective real analytic map with isolated critical value, we prove that the (m)-regularity condition (in a sense we define) ensures that f ||f|| is a fibration on small spheres, f induces a fibration on the tubes and both fibrations are equivalent. In particular, we make the statement of [12] more precise in the case of isolated critical point and we extend it to the case of an isolated critical value.

papers.title: Which Schubert varieties are local complete intersections?
papers.abstract: We characterize by pattern avoidance the Schubert varieties for GL_n which are local complete intersections (lci). For those Schubert varieties which are local complete intersections, we give an explicit minimal set of equations cutting out their neighborhoods at the identity. Although the statement of our characterization only requires ordinary pattern avoidance, showing that the Schubert varieties not satisfying our conditions are not lci appears to require more general notions of pattern avoidance. The Schubert varieties defined by inclusions, originally introduced by Gasharov and Reiner, turn out to be an important subclass, and we further develop some of their combinatorics. Applications include formulas for Kostant polynomials and presentations of cohomology rings for lci Schubert varieties.

papers.title: Comparing the automorphism group of the measure algebra with some groups related to the infinite permutation group of the natural numbers
papers.abstract: We prove, by a straight construction, that the automorphism group of the measure algebra and the subgroup of the measure preserving ones cannot be isomorphic to the trivial automorphisms of P(N)/fin.

papers.title: The degree distribution in bipartite planar maps: applications to the Ising model
papers.abstract: We characterize the generating function of bipartite planar maps counted according to the degree distribution of their black and white vertices. This result is applied to the solution of the hard particle and Ising models on random planar lattices. We thus recover and extend some results previously obtained by means of matrix integrals. Proofs are purely combinatorial and rely on the idea that planar maps are conjugacy classes of trees. In particular, these trees explain why the solutions of the Ising and hard particle models on maps of bounded degree are always algebraic.

papers.title: When Polynomial Multiplication Counts Geometry: Schubert Polynomials and Monk's Rule
papers.abstract: We give a geometric introduction to Schubert polynomial multiplication through point-line flags in the complex projective plane. Moving a prescribed point onto a prescribed line gives a family with local equation $au=λ$, whose limiting curve has two components. The incidence equations and their local multiplicities give a two-term divisor product, using the standard intersection product on classes of algebraic cycles. Permutation labels and Schubert polynomials express the same decomposition as an instance of Monk's rule. For three incidence conditions, each allowing either a point on a prescribed line or a line through a prescribed point, the product has degree six. Under explicit general-position assumptions, direct construction and local equations give six distinct solutions of multiplicity one.

papers.title: Combinatorial description of the mirabolic quantum Schur-Weyl duality
papers.abstract: We prove an explicit correspondence between the irreducible finite dimensional representations of the mirabolic quantum group $MU(n)$ and those of the mirabolic Hecke algebra $MH_d$ given by the mirabolic quantum Schur-Weyl duality. In particular, this resolves a generalization of a conjecture by the second author. The proof is via a careful analysis of the $MU(n)$-weight spaces and the eigenvalues of the Jucys Murphy elements of $MH_d$ on the mirabolic tensor space.

papers.title: Minimal Alt(6)-modules with additive dimension on characteristic non 3
papers.abstract: We classify the minimal faithful Alt(6)-modules with an additive dimension in characteristic not 3. We also highlight the remaining work needed to complete the classification of minimal faithful Alt(n)- and Sym(n)-modules with an additive dimension

papers.title: Rigidity and Affine Deformations of Foliations on Nilpotent and Solvable Contact Lie Algebras
papers.abstract: Let g be a Lie algebra of dimension 2n+1, let beta be a contact form, and let alpha be a nonzero integrable 1-form. We study when the affine path alpha_t = (1-t)alpha + t beta consists of contact forms with the orientation determined by beta \wedge (d beta)^n. We first establish an algebraic criterion: affine deformability is equivalent to the non-negativity of a scalar obtained from the interaction form Theta(alpha, beta) = alpha \wedge (d beta)^n + n beta \wedge d alpha \wedge (d beta)^{n-1}. For unimodular Lie algebras this scalar is (n+1)alpha(Z_beta), where Z_beta is the Reeb vector. We also derive a formula involving the modular character tau(X) = tr(ad_X) in the non-unimodular case. On nilpotent contact Lie algebras, every integrable 1-form is closed; using the standard structural properties of nilpotent contact Lie algebras, this implies that every left-invariant foliation is an affine origin for every fixed contact form. An explicit three-dimensional example illustrates that the modular term can yield affine deformability even when alpha(Z_beta) = 0. We discuss the implications for left-invariant forms on Lie groups and compact quotients. We do not claim a general obstruction example in the non-unimodular case; establishing such an example requires a separate verified construction.

papers.title: Initial Data Gluing for Asymptotically Hyperbolic Spacetimes
papers.abstract: We give a new proof of Corvino-Schoen-type gluing, also known as gluing up to linear obstructions, for asymptotically hyperbolic spacetimes satisfying appropriate smallness conditions in arbitrary dimension. The results retrieve and improve on previous known smallness requirements on initial data to conduct such gluing, including the work of Chrusciél and Delay. Our technique is highly versatile and well-suited for gluing results in highly anisotropic geometric settings.

papers.title: Automorphisms and Hodge isometries of surfaces with $K^2=p_g=1$
papers.abstract: Let $S$ be a minimal complex surface of general type with $K_S^2=p_g(S)=1$. By a theorem of Catanese, the canonical model of $S$ is a complete intersection of two sextics in $\mathbf{P}(1,2,2,3,3)$ whose equations admit a normal form, and the global Torelli theorem fails for these surfaces. We describe $\operatorname{Aut}(S)$ in terms of the coefficients of the normal form, prove that $|\operatorname{Aut}(S)|\leq 72$, and classify the surfaces attaining the bound: two surfaces with singular canonical model and a one-parameter family $X_r$ of smooth surfaces. For the surfaces $X_r$ we compute a basis of the primitive cohomology consisting of eigenvectors of a subgroup $\mathbf{Z}/6\mathbf{Z} \times \mathbf{Z}/6\mathbf{Z}$ of $\operatorname{Aut}(X_r)$, given by residues of explicit polynomials, together with the intersection form in this basis. We then show that the natural map from $\operatorname{Aut}(X_r)$ to the group of Hodge isometries of the primitive lattice modulo $\pm1$ is injective but has image of index at least $331\,776$, so that the Torelli principle for automorphisms fails for these surfaces.

papers.title: Protect the Decision, Not the Disaster: Regret-Robust Capacity Sizing and Positioning with Transportation Recourse
papers.abstract: An operator who positions mobile resources before a disruption faces two uncertainties that are usually treated as one: how the joint state of demand and travel conditions will vary, and which part of the resulting cost the positioning decision can actually change. Standard distributionally robust optimization (DRO) protects total cost, and therefore spends much of its protection on disruption costs that every feasible design would pay. This paper evaluates the worst-case regret of a design and compares it with the worst-case premium of total-cost DRO, and shows that the regret-to-premium ratio can be bounded before any robust model is solved: from marginals for the dependence question, and from single-scenario optima and one transport linear program for the regret question. The worst-case law is a relabelling of the operating record, reassigning every recorded period wholesale to another recorded period, except at most one, which is split. The comparator that exposes the largest worst-case regret is found by a single mixed-integer program. We derive an explicit radius where the sample-average design is exactly regret-robust. For finite scenario and design sets we compute a design's worst-case regret exactly, bound it from quantities a planner already has, and show on fleet and EMS data how law-relative regret changes capacity and positioning choices relative to sample-average and worst-cost planning. We apply the decision tree to several years of New York fleet data, including the year before Hurricane Sandy, and to two emergency-service events. The test flags the pre-Sandy year as exposed. The training-support regret bounds cover realized test regret in three of four fleet folds. On Ida, where the regret-robust allocation differed from the sample-average one, it moved units toward the boroughs the storm loaded and cost less than the sample-average design.

papers.title: Optimal Non-Homogeneous Improvements of the Anisotropic Hardy Inequality
papers.abstract: We consider the Hardy inequality associated with a strongly convex Finsler norm $F$ on $\mathbb{R}^n$ and we study its optimal non-homogeneous improvements in the whole range $1<p<\infty$. We show that the anisotropic Hardy difference controls a weighted critical Sobolev norm when $1<p<n$, a weighted exponential integrability of Trudinger type when $p=n$, where the Hardy term is replaced by its Leray logarithmic correction, and a weighted Hölder seminorm when $p>n$, proving in each regime that the logarithmic weights appear with the optimal exponents. In the borderline case $p=n$ this extends to general functions the optimal exponent previously known only for anisotropically radial functions. The proofs rely on a common ground-state reduction, combined with a splitting into an $F_o$-radial and a mean-free part for $1<p\le n$, and with an anisotropic Morrey representation formula for $p>n$.

papers.title: The Number of Polytope Trees and Beyond
papers.abstract: We study the symmetry-weighted enumeration of complexes formed by gluing copies of a regular polytope. For polytope trees and complexes obtained by attaching such trees to a fixed initial complex, we derive cut-and-join recurrences, differential equations for generating functions, explicit counting formulas, and asymptotic estimates. We then extend the method to complexes with cycles in their dual graphs, enumerating them by the numbers of polytopes and free facets. We derive recurrence relations and partial differential equations for the corresponding bivariate generating functions. In this setting, we obtain recurrences for connected configurations and explicit coefficient formulas for possibly disconnected configurations, both with and without a distinguished initial complex.

papers.title: Berry-Esseen bounds for products of random matrices under a $2+δ$ polynomial moment
papers.abstract: Let $(g_{k})_{k \geq 1}$ be a sequence of independent and identically distributed matrices with law $μ$ on $\mathrm{GL}(d,\mathbb{R})$, where $d\geq2$ is an integer. Suppose that the closed semigroup generated by the support of $μ$ is strongly irreducible and proximal and that the polynomial moment of order $2+δ$ is finite, where $0<δ\leq 1$. We establish a Berry-Esseen bound of order $n^{-δ/2}$ for $\log \| g_{n} \cdots g_{1} v\|$, where $v$ is a nonzero vector in $\mathbb{R}^{d}$ and $\|\cdot\|$ is an arbitrary norm on $\mathbb{R}^{d}$. As an application, we also obtain a Berry-Esseen bound of order $n^{-δ/2}$ for $\log \| g_{n} \cdots g_{1}\|$, where $\|\cdot\|$ is any matrix norm. The proof combines an $m$-dependent approximation with Stein's method. The argument uses identities for exchangeable pairs constructed by resampling individual matrices, together with a concentration inequality for sums of the approximating variables.

papers.title: When Are Nesterov Trajectories Eventually Locally Minimizing?
papers.abstract: We revisit the variational characterization of Nesterov's celebrated method and study when Nesterov trajectories are eventually locally minimizing in a variational sense, a notion that we define precisely. We show that this question is equivalent to the nonnegativity of an associated Schrödinger operator acting on variations of the trajectory. For power objectives of the form \[ f(x)=\frac{1}{p}\|x\|^p \] (where $\| \cdot\|$ denotes the Euclidean norm), we give a complete characterization: Among all exponents $p\ge 2$, the Nesterov trajectory with non-zero initial position is eventually locally minimizing if and only if $p=4$. We further interpret this exceptional exponent through the stability theory of semilinear elliptic equations.

papers.title: Joint Service Depth and Priority Design in Queueing Systems
papers.abstract: In AI-assisted service systems, the server can choose how much processing effort to spend on each job, which we call the service depth. Deeper reasoning improves output quality but occupies the server longer and increases congestion, and the realized processing time remains random because AI models are probabilistic and tasks vary in complexity. We study the joint design of service depth and priority in a single-server queue whose customers differ in delay sensitivity, with the goal of maximizing social welfare. For each customer type, the decision maker chooses a priority level and a service depth, and service times are exponential with mean equal to the chosen depth. With two customer types and linear service values, we characterize the centralized optimum. Counterintuitively, it prioritizes the patient type and gives it a smaller service depth when patient customers are sufficiently prevalent. When delay sensitivity is private, however, incentive compatibility requires the impatient type to receive a weakly shorter sojourn time, so the optimal price menu never prioritizes the patient type. Consequently, there can be a welfare gap between the centralized decision maker's optimal control policy and the optimal decentralized pricing mechanism. With a continuum of types, the centralized optimum is monotone: more delay-sensitive customers receive weakly smaller depth and higher priority, so the optimum can be implemented by a price menu with no welfare loss. Allowing randomized depths similarly closes the gap in the two-type model. Finally, we calibrate an agentic AI service system using published coding-agent trials from DeepSWE and numerically examine priority inversion, the value of joint design, and the welfare gain from personalization.

papers.title: First-order Methods for Variational Inequality Problems with Semi-Infinite Constraints
papers.abstract: This paper studies first-order methods for monotone variational inequalities with semi-infinite constraints and presents this model as a framework covering constrained saddle-point problems, robust optimization, distributionally robust function-constrained optimization, and generalized Nash equilibrium formulations. Since feasibility must hold over infinitely many indexed constraints, direct projection onto the full feasible region is generally difficult. Therefore, we propose a single-loop primal-dual constraint extrapolation method (PD-ConEx) that updates primal variables, Lagrange multipliers, and worst-case constraint indices using first-order information, linearization, extrapolation, and projections only onto simple sets. We establish convergence guarantees for smooth and nonsmooth regimes, showing how the achievable rates depend on strong monotonicity and strong concavity of the index block. For coupled convex-concave saddle-point problems, strong convexity in the minimization block can accelerate its smooth terms even without strong concavity in the maximization block. We also develop an adaptive smooth variant with $O(1/K)$ VI-gap and feasibility guarantees without an a priori bound on generated multipliers. Moment-based and Wasserstein distributionally robust models fit within the framework, and numerical experiments on robust quadratic instances and distributionally robust learning illustrate the method's optimality and feasibility behavior.

papers.title: The Intersection of nested filled-in little Julia sets have zero area
papers.abstract: It is shown that for any infinitely renormalizable quadratic polynomial $Q_c$ the intersection $K_\infty$ of all the little filled-in Julia sets (renormalization Julia sets) containing the critical value have zero area.

papers.title: Stability of certain elements in the Bernstein center
papers.abstract: Let $G$ be a split connected reductive algebraic group over a non-archimedean local field $F$ of characteristic zero. The stable center conjecture asserts that the subspace of stable elements in the Bernstein center of $G(F)$ is a sub-algebra, and this subring is conjecturally isomorphic to the regular functions on the moduli of semi-simple Langlands parameters. Bezrukavnikov-Kazhdan-Varshavsky suggested an approach towards the stable center conjecture by explicitly constructing elements and proving their stability directly without assuming LLC, and proved the stability of the depth-$r$ projectors. Following the idea, the first author and Tsao-Hsien Chen produced a family of elements in the center which are conjecturally stable using Deligne-Lusztig parameters attached to irreducible representations. This paper proves the stability of the projectors corresponding to strongly regular Deligne-Lusztig parameters in depth-zero, and for all the positive depth elements with some restrictions on the residue characteristic.

papers.title: Consistency in fractional Korn's inequalities on Lipschitz domains
papers.abstract: We investigate fractional analogs of Korn's inequality on bounded Lipschitz domains in several contexts. Constrained and unconstrained inequalities are established; constraints include quotient spaces and spaces incorporating various classes of boundary conditions or volume constraints. We also expand the parameters of integrability for which the inequalities hold. Specifically, a fractional Korn's first unconstrained inequality holds for vector fields in the fractional Sobolev space $W^{s,p}(Ω;\mathbb{R}^n)$ for all $p \in [1,\infty]$ and all $s \in (0,1)$. In the cases $p = 1$ and $p = \infty$, the inequality has no local analog. We quantify this by investigating the consistency of the inequalities as the differentiability parameter $s \to 1$; the universal constant in the inequality remains stable for $p \in (1,\infty)$ but degenerates for $p \in \{1,\infty\}$. We introduce an explicit $L^p$-bounded projection operator onto infinitesimal rigid motions as a key tool to quantitatively strengthen the inequality.

papers.title: A proof of Wang's planar D-coloring conjecture
papers.abstract: We prove Wang's planar D-coloring conjecture. A D-coloring of a graph is a proper edge coloring in which every subgraph isomorphic to $K_4$ minus an edge is rainbow. Wang conjectured that every planar graph of maximum degree $Δ$ has a D-coloring with 9 colors if $Δ=4$, 10 colors if $Δ=5$, and $2Δ-1$ colors if $Δ\ge 6$. Hu, Kong and Wang proved the cases $Δ\le 5$ and $Δ\ge 33$. We prove the sharp bound $2Δ-1$ for every $Δ\ge 6$, settling the remaining cases. The proof uses discharging; the case $Δ=6$ is computer-assisted.

papers.title: Statistical inference for boundary constrained parameters
papers.abstract: Estimation and inference under boundary constraints arises in many areas of statistics, but the available asymptotic theory remains limited and fragmented relative to the classical case, where the parameter lies in the interior of the parameter space. In this paper we derive a boundary-constrained analogue of the standard asymptotic expansion for a minimiser of a loss function, in which the deviation of the estimator from the population parameter is decomposed over lower-dimensional subspaces determined by the directional derivatives at the minimiser. Using this decomposition we show that the limiting distribution of the estimator is a mixture of point masses and truncated skew-normal distributions, with mixture probabilities determined by the directional derivative conditions. A consequence of this result is that the constrained and unconstrained coordinates do not separate: the presence of parameters on or near the boundary affects the sampling distribution of the unconstrained parameter estimators. We apply the expansion to obtain the asymptotic distribution of the quasi log-likelihood ratio statistic under a range of null hypotheses, and since the resulting mixture is not pivotal in the quasi-likelihood setting, we propose a simulation-based procedure for approximating critical values. The framework unifies and simplifies several existing results. We illustrate the methodology by testing for interactions in exponential family graphical models, where the parameters are subject to compatibility constraints that ensure a joint distribution exists.

papers.title: Intermediate subalgebras of cross-product von Neumann algebras arising from weakly compact actions
papers.abstract: In this short paper, we establish the following Galois-type property for all measure-preserving, weakly compact actions $G \curvearrowright (X,μ) $ of a non-inner amenable group $G$ on a standard probability space $X$: for any intermediate von Neumann subalgebra $\mathcal L(G)\subseteq \mathcal N \subseteq L^\infty (X)\rtimes G$, there is a factor $G\curvearrowright Y$ of $G \curvearrowright X$ such that $\mathcal N= L^\infty(Y)\rtimes G$. In particular, this holds for all pmp distal actions $G\curvearrowright X$, thereby answering positively an open problem from \cite{BCCMSW24} (which can also be traced back to \cite{CD20}). We also provide an example showing our result is optimal.

papers.title: Concurrent Space-Based Observer Placement and Scheduling for Cislunar Space Domain Awareness
papers.abstract: As interest in cislunar space grows, so does the need for space domain awareness (SDA) capabilities to safely support missions. To enhance cislunar SDA capabilities, the use of space-based observers has been proposed. Prior research has explored optimizing observer placement but has not considered scheduling limitations. We propose a mixed-integer linear programming formulation that concurrently optimizes the placement and scheduling of space-based observers for cislunar SDA. Our work considers three aspects of observer scheduling: sensor tasking, communication, and charging. We utilize a scenario-based approach that generalizes observer placement for unknown targets while applying scheduling constraints to each scenario. However, this problem quickly becomes difficult for commercial solvers to handle as the number of scenarios grows. As an alternative, a column generation approach is employed to introduce well-performing schedules into the problem for each orbital slot. A comparative analysis is performed across multiple instances to evaluate the performance of column generation against that of a commercial solver. A case study is then conducted in which the performance of the observers' placement from the concurrent formulation is tested against a set of validation target sets and compared with the performance of two baselines in which placement and scheduling are performed sequentially.

papers.title: A crystallographic quotient of the framed braid group and associated flat manifolds
papers.abstract: We study the quotient of the framed braid group $FB_n$ by the commutator subgroup of the framed pure braid group $FP_n$. We prove that $$ \frac{FB_n}{[FP_n,FP_n]}\cong\mathbb Z^n\rtimes\frac{B_n}{[P_n,P_n]}, $$ and, for $n\geq3$, that this quotient is a crystallographic group of dimension $n(n+1)/2$ with holonomy group $S_n$. We investigate its finite-order elements and conjugacy classes, prove that it has no elements of finite even order, and construct Bieberbach subgroups with prescribed finite $2$-group holonomy. Starting from suitable Bieberbach subgroups of $\frac{B_n}{[P_n,P_n]}$, we then construct Bieberbach subgroups of the framed quotient whose associated compact flat manifolds are torus bundles over the corresponding unframed flat manifolds. We describe these bundles through the generalized Calabi construction and determine their orientability, first Betti numbers, and the centers of their fundamental groups. As an application, we study a family with cyclic holonomy of odd order, obtaining a criterion for the existence of flat Kähler structures, and indicate how the same construction applies to cyclic holonomy of $2$-power order.
authors: Paulo Cesar Cerqueira dos Santos Júnior

papers.title: Congruence lattices of $2$-valued unary algebras
papers.abstract: We study congruence lattices of finite algebras whose basic operations are unary and have exactly two values. We prove that the class of finite lattices representable in this way is closed under taking filters, glued sums and ordinal sums, and direct products with finite distributive lattices, but it is not closed under taking ideals or arbitrary direct products. A classification of lattices with at most seven elements with respect to representability is also presented.

papers.title: Blind Random Search with Noisy Measurements: Almost Sure Convergence and Convergence Rates
papers.abstract: Blind random search is a simple global optimization method that only requires the value of the loss function, without needing gradient information or an explicit loss model. However, its classical formulation assumes that the loss evaluation is noise-free, which limits its direct application to practical problems with noisy measurements. We extend blind random search by combining a vanishing acceptance threshold with the running average of noisy loss measurements. Under the stated assumptions, we prove that the proposed algorithm converges almost surely to the global minimizer. We further analyze the rate at which the loss at the current estimate approaches the minimum loss. For low-dimensional cases, we obtain an almost sure asymptotic upper bound on the difference between the two, and for high-dimensional cases, we prove that this difference, suitably scaled, has an exact Weibull limiting distribution.

papers.title: On the evenness of coefficients of modular forms
papers.abstract: We study the density of primes such that $a_p$ is divisible by a prime above $2$ for modular forms $f = \sum_{n \ge 1} a_n q^n$ of small levels. First, we reduce the problem to low weight and odd level, or a mod $2$ CM type form. Then, we provide calculations for the evenness of particular newforms. In particular, we provide a list of levels where this "evenness" can be computed exactly for all the forms with trivial nebentypus.

papers.title: On the transformation of unbounded convergent sequences by linear operators on Banach lattices
papers.abstract: In this paper, we introduce a weak variant of the concept of unbounded Dunford-Pettis linear operators, which we call unbounded weak Dunford-Pettis operators. We investigate the properties of this new class, establish inclusion and coincidence results involving unbounded Dunford-Pettis operators, and examine its relationship with the class of unbounded absolutely weakly continuous operators.

papers.title: Gibbs measures on Cayley trees and homoclinic orbits
papers.abstract: We study the question of existence and multiplicity of homogeneous Markov Gibbs measures on Cayley trees with spin space $\mathbb{Z}$. We prove that, under a natural summability assumption on the interaction function, there are always at least two homogeneous Markov Gibbs measures satisfying two natural symmetry conditions. Moreover, any two homogeneous Markov Gibbs measures satisfying a suitable non-degeneracy assumption can be superimposed and produce infinitely many other homogeneous Markov Gibbs measures. When the interaction function $Q$ has bounded support in $\mathbb{Z}$, there is a one-to-one correspondence between homogeneous Markov Gibbs measures and suitable homoclinic orbits of a symplectomorphism of $\mathbb{R}^{2n}$, where $n$ is the smallest natural number such that $Q(i)=0$ for every $i>n$. For $n=1$, results from symbolic dynamics and horseshoes imply the existence of homogeneous Markov Gibbs measures whose single-site marginal is concentrated near an arbitrary finite subset of $N\mathbb{Z}$, where $N$ is a sufficiently large integer. In the case of interaction functions with infinite support, there is a one-to-one correspondence between homogeneous Markov Gibbs measures and suitable homoclinic orbits of a Lagrangian correspondence on the cotangent bundle of a Banach space.

papers.title: Weak type $(1,1)$ estimates for noncommutative maximal truncated rough singular integrals
papers.abstract: We prove a weak type $(1,1)$ estimate for maximal truncations of noncommutative rough singular integrals whose angular kernels satisfy the classical $L\log L$ integrability and cancellation conditions. The main ingredient of the proof is a new linearization method for handling the maximal truncations acting on the bad functions arising from the noncommutative Calderón--Zygmund decomposition.

papers.title: Minimum orders of clique oddomorphism counterexamples
papers.abstract: An oddomorphism to $K_n$ is a proper colouring with $n$ colours in which every vertex is designated odd or even, every vertex has in each other colour class a number of neighbours of its own parity, and every colour class contains an odd number of odd vertices. We prove that an oddomorphism witness to $K_n$ on at most $n+6$ vertices contains a $K_n$ minor with every branch meeting the witness's specified odd set. The conclusion holds inside any graph containing the witness and therefore applies to weak oddomorphisms. The bound is sharp: for every $n\ge8$ the minimum order of a graph admitting a weak oddomorphism to $K_n$ but having no $K_n$ minor is exactly $n+7$. The extremal example is a fifteen-vertex graph with an oddomorphism to $K_8$, obtained from the doubled theta graph of Kriesell and Mohr by adding one vertex adjacent to the seven roots; we give a structural proof that it has no $K_8$ minor, including their counting argument for the rooted case. A separate technical companion records further results on related root-apex graphs, an attachment theorem and a bounded nine-colour statement, together with their computational provenance; none of it is used here. The results do not resolve the unrestricted clique-target problem.

papers.title: On the Upsilon invariant and the Baldwin-Vela-Vick b-invariant of fibered knots
papers.abstract: For a null-homologous fibered knot $K$ in a rational homology sphere, Baldwin and Vela-Vick define a refinement $b(K)$ of the Ozsváth-Szabó contact invariant. We prove that if the Ozsváth-Stipsicz-Szabó concordance invariant Upsilon has slope $Υ'_K(t)=-g(K)$ for some $t\in[0,\frac{2}{n+1})$, where $g(K)$ is the genus of $K$, then $b(K)>n$. This extends a result of He, Hubbard, and the author on the Upsilon invariant and right-veering monodromies. We also prove that the knot Floer homology of a fibered knot in the $g(K)-b(K)$ Alexander grading is nonvanishing. As an application, we give many families of fibered cable knots whose $b(K)$ invariant grows arbitrarily large. Finally, we prove that if a monodromy of a fibered knot is neither right-veering nor left-veering, then the third-to-top term of knot Floer homology is nonvanishing.

papers.title: Sharp Bounds on Continuous Treatment Effects under Unobserved Confounding
papers.abstract: We study partial identification of conditional treatment effects with a continuous treatment under unobserved confounding. We target the conditional average potential outcome (CAPO) E[Y_x|z] and the conditional average treatment effect (CATE) between two treatment levels. We assume a bounded outcome and Lipschitz continuity of the response functions and of the propensity scores given the latent confounder, and show that these conditions imply the smooth treatment response and smooth treatment selection conditions of Kim et al. (2018). The combined bound of Kim et al. uses only two reference points on the identified diagonal and is generally loose. Bounding through every diagonal reference point instead gives explicit bounds whose average is the sharp identified set of the CAPO at every treatment, inside or outside the observational support. Capping the difference between the upper and lower bounds gives sharp causal bounds on the CATE. These bounds are informative without monotonicity or overlap assumptions.

papers.title: Localized Hybrid Analytical-Finite-Element Thermal Modeling for Laser Powder Bed Fusion
papers.abstract: Hybrid analytical--finite-element methods support scan-resolved, part-scale thermal simulation of laser powder bed fusion, but their analytical evaluation cost grows as scan-line contributions accumulate. This work develops a space--time localized hybrid formulation that restricts where and how long each contribution is evaluated analytically. Residual terms and boundary conditions derived from the heat equation allow the finite-element correction to account for the thermal effect of contributions removed from the analytical field. The formulation is assessed using a single-line benchmark against an independent full finite-element solution and multiline comparisons with the conventional hybrid formulation. Localization limits the number of analytical contributions retained while maintaining close agreement with the conventional solution. A comparison with uncompensated temporal truncation demonstrates the importance of the residual correction in retaining the thermal effect of removed contributions. In the 500-line case, analytical and total simulation times are reduced by factors of approximately 25.5 and 3.92, respectively, with a relative nodal 2-norm difference of 0.139%.

papers.title: Not All Mislabels Are Equal: Efficient Task-Aware Auditing with Confidence Sequences
papers.abstract: We study efficient, adaptive auditing of categorical labels in a fixed dataset, motivated by biodiversity-credit programs in which expert verification of species records is costly and downstream scores (e.g., payment) are more sensitive to errors on certain labels than on others. Our proposed ATLAS framework couples anytime-valid inference with a task-aware adaptive auditing policy. Representing label corrections through a confusion matrix, we prioritize which data points to inspect next based on both label uncertainty and the influence of potential label corrections on the downstream score function. For linear scores such as the mislabel rate, our priority-aware approach certifies the overall label error rate to $\pm 2$ percentage points with 24% and 11% fewer audits than random sampling on biodiversity data from Kenya and a widely used CIFAR-10N benchmark, respectively. For nonlinear scores such as the Hill-Shannon diversity, we exploit a linear-envelope representation that reduces inference to a family of linear-score audits; priority-aware sampling reaches the target precision with 36% fewer audits. When distribution-free guarantees are prohibitively costly, we develop a model-based Bayesian alternative that trades assumption-free validity for substantially fewer audits. Our biodiversity case study highlights a gap between statistical validity and practical feasibility: generic methods such as Serfling's bound and existing confidence-sequence procedures are rigorous but can require prohibitively many expert reviews in practice. Together, these results show task-aware auditing can significantly reduce the number of expert audits needed while providing finite-sample, anytime-valid guarantees.

papers.title: Rigidity and deformations of Besse families of minimal hypersurfaces
papers.abstract: We generalize Zoll families of hypersurfaces to Besse families of hypersurfaces, which are defined differential-topologically and may contain non-embedded and exceptional hypersurfaces. A contact-geometric discussion presents them as double Legendrian fibrations and shows that regular hypersurfaces are either spheres or real projective spaces. In analogy with the Berger conjecture on simply connected manifolds all of whose geodesics are closed, we show that every hypersurface of a Besse family on a sphere other than the 4-sphere is regular. On even-dimensional spheres other than the 4-sphere we obtain a stronger conclusion, generalizing a theorem of Gromoll and Grove about 2-spheres all of whose geodesics are closed: every hypersurface of a Besse family is regular and embedded. Moreover, building on work by Ambrozio and Guajardo, we provide metrics of non-constant curvature carrying Besse families of non-embedded minimal hypersurfaces in every odd dimension at least three, and Besse families of minimal hypersurfaces with exceptional hypersurfaces on orbifolds in every dimension at least two. We also give a short proof that manifolds admitting Zoll families of embedded hypersurfaces are homeomorphic to spheres or real projective spaces, recovering a recent result of Martins up to homeomorphism.

papers.title: Hybridizable Discontinuous Galerkin methods for the Keller-Segel model
papers.abstract: We propose a hybridizable discontinuous Galerkin (HDG) finite element method to approximate the solution of the time-dependent Keller-Segel model, a drift-diffusion system describing chemotactic cell movement. We develop and analyze the corresponding HDG scheme, and establish theoretical convergence results for the proposed discretization. Finally, we present numerical experiments that confirm the theoretical findings.

papers.title: Two parametric $q$-supercongruences from Andrews' multi-series transformation
papers.abstract: Recently, Guo and Guo (Results Math $76:37, ~2021$) obtained curious $q$-analogues of the following two supercongruences conjectured by Guo and Schlosser \cite[Conjectures $12.6$ and $12.7$]{GuoSclssr ConstApprox 21}: \begin{align*} \sum_{n=0}^{(p-1)/3} (6n+1) \frac{\left(\frac{1}{3}\right)_n^{4}(2n)!} {(n!)^{4}\left(\frac{2}{3}\right)_{2n}} \equiv p \pmod{p^{3}} \qquad \text{for primes } p\equiv 1 \pmod{3}, \end{align*} \begin{align*} \sum_{n=0}^{(p+1)/3} (6n-1) \frac{\left(-\frac{1}{3}\right)_n^{4}(2n)!} {(n!)^{4}\left(-\frac{2}{3}\right)_{2n}} \equiv p \pmod{p^{3}} \qquad \text{for primes } p\equiv 2 \pmod{3}, \end{align*} where $(z)_n=z(z+1)\cdots(z+n-1)$ denotes the shifted factorial. In this paper, we establish a one-parameter extension of them. The main ingredients of our proofs are the creative microscoping method developed by Guo and Zudilin \cite{guo2019q} and Andrews' multi-series transformation.

papers.title: Subgraph Isomorphism, Integer Linear Programming, and Lattices: A Linear Algebraic Framework
papers.abstract: The subgraph isomorphism problem (SGI) asks a deceptively simple question: is a graph B found inside a parent graph A? Famously NP-complete and the subject of volumes of study, attempts to practically solve subgraph problems typically require specialized software or the focused application of problem-specific theoretical knowledge. Here we present a straightforward linear framework that neatly joins SGI to lattice theory and constrained satisfiability and, importantly, yields an easily implemented algorithm that naturally leverages consumer-grade hardware and off-the-shelf libraries to compete with state-of-the-art specialized solvers. We additionally show practical realizations in approachable settings, along with some benchmarks that reduce 6+ hour computations to seconds. Aimed at readability, we develop a series of computable algebraic invariants and demonstrate their application to familiar problems such as the Knight's Tour, with a focus on providing an accessible entry point for researchers in graph theory, abstract algebra, and students in general.

papers.title: On the stability of rank-one factors for Anosov $\mathbb Z^k$-actions
papers.abstract: We prove $C^1$-stability of $C^\infty$ rank-one factors for a large class of higher rank Anosov $\mathbb Z^k$-actions. If the factor is a projection of a smooth fiber bundle and the action contains an element which acts as the identity on the rank-one factor and is Anosov on every fiber, then any sufficiently $C^1$-small $C^\infty$ perturbation of the action will also have a $C^\infty$ rank-one factor. In particular, we prove the $C^1$-stability of the product structure for Anosov $\mathbb Z^2$-actions which are obtained as a (diagonal) product of two $\mathbb Z$-Anosov actions.

papers.title: Some remarks on polynomial vector fields in $\RR^2$
papers.abstract: In this paper, we study planar polynomial vector fields admitting invariant circles. We characterize polynomial vector fields having $m$ concentric invariant circles, and we describe those having three invariant circles whose centers are not collinear. We also give a necessary and sufficient condition for the unit circle to be the unique limit cycle of a quadratic vector field. We prove that a cubic or quartic Kolmogorov vector field having the unit circle invariant has no circular limit cycle, and that a quartic vector field with two concentric circular limit cycles has at most three circular limit cycles, this bound being sharp.

papers.title: Ground-state spaces of generalized stabilizer codes
papers.abstract: In this paper, we determine the complete ground-state spaces for a broad class of generalized stabilizer quantum models defined over CW-decompositions of non-compact manifolds of arbitrary dimensions and topological type. We introduce a $C^*$-algebraic framework in which the quantum spin algebra $\A$ is realized as the twisted group $C^*$-algebra of an infinite discrete Pauli module $P$ endowed with a symplectic structure. We establish a correspondence between stabilizer models and isotropic subgroups of $P$: Every Lagrangian extension of such a subgroup determines a $C^*$-diagonal of $\A$, whose Weyl groupoid encodes the dynamics through a continuous 1-cocycle. This realization yields an explicit family of extremal ground-states for every admissible Lagrangian model, together with their decomposition into sectors. When the sector space is $T_0$, this gives a complete characterization of the ground-state spaces. We also prove that every Lagrangian stabilizer model admits a unique frustration-free ground state with a spectral gap.
