This new strong law arises as a combination of a strong law of large numbers for integrable random monotone vector fields on Hilbert-Hadamard spaces, that is, Hadamard spaces whose tangent cones all embed isometrically into Hilbert spaces, extending a result of Salim from Hilbert spaces, together with a new result on the interchangeability of the subdifferential and the integral, which we establish for $L^2$-Lipschitz integrands. This latter ingredient provides, to our knowledge, the first nonlinear version of (a particular case of) a previous result due variously to Ioffe and Tikhomirov, Levin, Hiriart-Urruty, Thibault as well as Rockafellar and Wets. On the way to this strong law for random monotone vector fields, we also establish a distribution-uniform generalization of Sturm's strong law of large numbers for inductive means of $L^1$-sequences of i.i.d. random variables on Hadamard spaces via a new effective non-asymptotic concentration inequality. Throughout the paper, we highlight various remaining open problems.

papers.title: The fixed-point bundle method over product-of-simplex domains arising from game equilibria
papers.abstract: Developing general-purpose algorithms with global asymptotic convergence guarantees for Nash equilibria of general-sum games remains a longstanding challenge. This paper extends the fixed-point bundle framework for finite-dimensional variational inequalities (VIs) from simplex domains to product-of-simplex domains, enabling its direct application to Nash equilibrium computation. The resulting fixed-point bundle exhibits a composite fiber bundle structure. The key innovation is to construct an equivalent VI on a simplex and establish the equivalence between the two fixed-point bundle frameworks via a fiber bundle isomorphism. Exploiting this geometric equivalence, we show that the path-following algorithm for VIs on product-of-simplex domains inherits the global linear convergence guarantees of the simplex-domain framework. In numerical experiments, the algorithm attained a precision of $10^{-5}$ on all 5600 randomly generated game instances, with dimension ranging from 2-player 128-action to 128-player 2-action. Code and data are available at https://github.com/shb20tsinghua/FiberBundle_VI.

papers.title: Boundary regularity of harmonic functions in $C^1$ slit domains
papers.abstract: We establish precise upper and lower estimates for harmonic functions vanishing on the slit of a $C^1$ slit domain, with no assumption that the slit lies in a hyperplane. The classical $\sqrt{d}$ growth near the edge, $d$ being the distance to the slit, persists in this generality, up to an explicit factor \[\exp\Big( \pm C \int_ρ^r ω(s)\, \frac{ds}{s} \Big)\] determined by the $C^1$-modulus of continuity $ω$ of the slit, where $ρ< r$ are the two scales being compared. The upper estimates allow a right-hand side and non-zero boundary data. The correction factors remain bounded above and below by positive constants as $ρ\to0$ precisely when $ω$ satisfies the Dini condition. Moduli of continuity beyond the Dini regime, as is the case for the logarithmic moduli arising at singular sets in relevant free boundary problems, were not covered by the previous $C^{1,α}$ theory. Previously, the $\sqrt{d}$ growth was known for slits contained in a hyperplane, which additionally have a $C^{1,α}$ edge (De Silva, Savin). For Lipschitz slits, there are boundary Harnack principles, but no growth rate is identified precisely. The main technical ingredient is a change of coordinates flattening a Lipschitz slit domain onto the model half-hyperplane slit, with quantitative estimates up to second order. The construction is geometric and does not use the equation, so we expect it to be useful for other boundary regularity problems.

papers.title: Optimising Selberg's method for critical zeros
papers.abstract: We revisit Zhuravlev's 1974 quantitative form of Selberg's sign-change method for the zeros of the Riemann zeta function on the critical line. Zhuravlev's work, originally in Russian and little known in the West, established an explicit positive proportion of such zeros. Using modern techniques we optimise the arithmetic mean value at the heart of the method and obtain the strongest result yet known from Selberg's method, proving that more than $6.78\%$ of the non-trivial zeros of the Riemann zeta function lie on the critical line.

papers.title: Matrix nearness problems: Do real inputs admit real solutions?
papers.abstract: Given a real square matrix $A$ and a nonempty closed target set of complex matrices $\mathcal{E}$, invariant by complex conjugation and containing real matrices, does the subset of $\mathcal{E}$ consisting of the matrices nearest to $A$ in the Frobenius distance always contain a real matrix? We give negative answers when $\mathcal{E}$ is either the set of normal matrices (solving a question posed by N. Higham) or the set of matrices whose eigenvalues lie in the closed left half-plane (solving a question posed by the first author and F. Poloni). For the latter problem, we also argue that the ratio between the real and complex distances is unbounded in every dimension $n\geq 3$, and this holds for every distance induced by a unitarily invariant norm. For both problems and $n \geq 3$, we show that a real input $A$ uniformly drawn from the unit sphere $\|A\|_F=1$ has no real minimizer over $\mathcal{E}$ with probability strictly between $0$ and $1$. Beyond these two cases, we prove for an arbitrary nonempty closed target sets $\mathcal{E}$ that, for almost every real input, either $\mathcal{E}$ contains a unique nearest matrix which is real, or every nearest matrix in $\mathcal{E}$ is nonreal.

papers.title: Averaged dynamical generalizations of Chowla's conjecture
papers.abstract: In 1965, Chowla conjectured that the signs of the Liouville function become asymptotically uncorrelated at any fixed collection of distinct shifts. In 2015, Matomäki, Radziwiłłand Tao proved an averaged form of Chowla's conjecture. In 2022, Lichtman proved a variant of this conjecture over primes on average. In the same year, Lichtman and Teräväinen proved the Hardy-Littlewood-Chowla conjecture on average. In this article, motivated by the recent work of Bergelson and Richter on the dynamical generalizations of the prime number theorem, we will first establish the analogous dynamical generalizations of these three results related to Chowla's conjecture. In the proofs, we follow an approach of Qi and Zheng who established a variant of Bergelson and Richter's theorem over irreducible binary cubic forms. In 2016, Tao proved that the two-point logarithmic Chowla's conjecture holds. Recently, Charamaras and Richter generalized Tao's theorem to bounded arithmetic functions and proposed a conjecture that generalizes Chowla's conjecture to bounded multi-variable arithmetic functions. Building on their work, we will also prove a dynamical generalization of Tao's theorem and some variants for the composition of the sum-of-digits function with the prime Omega function.

papers.title: Second-order perturbation bounds for Gibbs samplers under strong spatial mixing
papers.abstract: The basic question in perturbation analysis of Markov chains is how small changes in their transition kernels affect their stationary distributions. Classical perturbation bounds typically require the kernel error to be much smaller than $1/τ$, where $τ$ is a mixing or relaxation time. Although this scaling is sharp for Markov chains in general, we investigate a general "square-rooting" phenomenon in which one-step errors of order roughly $1/\sqrtτ$ can be sufficient for local updates. We proved a form of this phenomenon in Lin, Liu and Smith (2025) under strong assumptions. Here we substantially weaken these assumptions, and prove this phenomenon occurs using three distinct approaches. First, block factorization applies under structural assumptions on the stationary measures of both chains. Second, approximate block-update arguments extend the result to statistically relevant Markov chain Monte Carlo (MCMC) settings, where structural guarantees are available for the exact posterior and its associated sampler, but not for the perturbed posterior. Third, we use direct calculations for a class of models with hard constraints where neither general result is directly available. We illustrate these results in three MCMC settings and show how they directly inform the tuning of approximate MCMC algorithms.

papers.title: Free boundary minimal surfaces of genus zero
papers.abstract: We prove that any embedded genus zero free boundary minimal surface in the ball has first Steklov eigenvalue $1$. This implies the uniqueness of the critical catenoid.

papers.title: Exact dimensionality of stationary measures for random diffeomorphisms with all Lyapunov exponents equal and negative
papers.abstract: We prove exact dimensionality of ergodic stationary measures for random compositions of $C^1$ diffeomorphisms of a closed manifold $M$ that contract at a single Lyapunov scale. More precisely, let $ν$ be a Borel probability measure on $\mathrm{Diff}^1(M)$ such that $\log\sup_{x}\|{D_xf}\|$ and $\log\sup_{x}\|{D_xf^{-1}}\|$ are $ν$-integrable, and let $μ$ be an ergodic $ν$-stationary probability measure. If the top and bottom Lyapunov exponents of the derivative cocycle coincide and equal $λ<0$, then $μ$ is exact dimensional and $\mathrm{dim}(μ)=h_μ^{\mathrm{F}}(ν)/(-λ)$, where $h_μ^{\mathrm{F}}(ν)$ is the Furstenberg entropy.

papers.title: A Topological Figiel-Lindenstrauss-Milman Theorem and its Applications
papers.abstract: We prove a topological generalization of the Figiel--Lindenstrauss--Milman inequality, answering a recent question of Frick, Hosseini, and Vasileuski: every nonempty strongly regular CW complex with $v$ vertices, $f$ maximal cells, and a free involution that permutes its cells has $\mathbb Z/2$-index at most $4\log v\log f$. The classical inequality for centrally symmetric polytopes is the special case of polytope boundaries. As an application, we show that every finite simplicial complex homotopy equivalent to $\mathbb RP^d$ has at least $\exp(Ω(\sqrt d))$ vertices. The previous best lower bound was $Ω(d^2)$. We also construct triangulations with $\exp(O(\sqrt d))$ vertices. Using the same method, we prove a low-dimensional Postnikov factorization theorem, which gives similar vertex lower bounds for several classical families, such as complex and quaternionic projective spaces, the $d$-torus, closed symplectic and aspherical manifolds, Grassmannians, classical Lie groups, and spherical space forms. Further applications include results in learning theory, convex geometry, computational topology, and topological bounds for chromatic numbers and Vietoris--Rips complexes.

papers.title: Discrete Approximation to Time-changed Brownian Motions
papers.abstract: We develop a general discrete approximation scheme for time-changed Brownian motions on $\mathbb{R}^d$. Our approximation scheme works for any smooth measure with full quasi-support on $\mathbb{R}^d$ with suitable initial distributions. Under some mild conditions on the smooth measure, the discrete approximation scheme works for every starting point. Our results in particular give a discrete approximation scheme for Liouville Brownian motions.

papers.title: The universal measure of nonstochastic objects
papers.abstract: The usual settings for discussing the notion of stochastic objects are very different from Kolmogorov's original structure-free setting, in which there is no predefined external structure on the objects (such as the lengths of binary strings). A natural modification of stochasticity, obtained by replacing finite sets as models with probability measures, is quasi-stochasticity. The structure-free setting is common in studies of quasi-stochasticity, and known results show that the universal machine generates non-quasi-stochastic objects with exponentially small probability. This paper shows that, on the other hand, the universal machine generates nonstochastic objects surprisingly often. It also systematically explores numerous connections between stochasticity and quasi-stochasticity in the structure-free setting. In particular, the definition of quasi-stochasticity can be modified in a natural way modelled on Kolmogorov's definition so that non-quasi-stochastic objects are produced as often as nonstochastic ones; the results for this modification imply all the results of this paper showing that nonstochastic objects are frequent.

papers.title: Discrete dynamics of Eratosthenes sieve
papers.abstract: We study Eratosthenes sieve as a discrete dynamic system. At each stage of the sieve there is a cycle of gaps ${\mathcal G}(p^\#)$ of length $φ(p^\#)$ and span $p^\#$. There is a recursion ${\mathcal G}(p_k^\#)\longrightarrow {\mathcal G}(p_{k+1}^\#)$ that creates the next cycle from the current one. If we take initial conditions from the cycle ${\mathcal G}(p_0^\#)$, then for all constellations of span $|s| < 2p_1$, including gaps $g < 2p_1$, the driving terms of various lengths form Markov chains. These yield {\em exact} models for the populations $n_s(p_k^\#)$ for all further stages of the sieve. If $s$ is an admissible constellation of length $J$, then its population $n_{s,J}(p^\#)$ grows as $Θ\left( \prod (q-J-1)\right)$. So we factor out the superexponential growth to obtain the exact model for the relative population $w_s(p_k^\#)$ of the constellation $s$ across all further stages of the sieve. $$ w_{s,J}(p_k^\#) \; = \; n_{s,J}(p_k^\#) \, / \, \prod_{J+1 < p \le p_k} (p-J-1) $$ The asymptotic value of the relative population is a constant ${w_{s,J}(\infty) \ge 1}$ that depends only on the odd prime factors that divide a span in $s$. Assuming that the instances of a constellation $s$ are approximately uniformly distributed in ${\mathcal G}(p_k^\#)$, we develop initial estimates of the number of instances $s$ that would occur in the interval of survival $ΔH(p_k) = (p_k^2, p_{k+1}^2)$. We define a statistic $η_s(p_k)$, the quadratic density of the constellation $s$ over the interval $ΔH(p_k)$. We show that the initial estimates $\widehat{η_g}(p)$ for prime gaps agree with samples up to $5.677\,E14$.

papers.title: Average-Radius List-Decodability of Random Linear Codes
papers.abstract: We prove that for every prime power $q$ and every $p \in (0, 1-1/q)$, a random $\mathbb{F}_q$-linear code of rate $1 - h_q(p) - ε$ is $(p, C_{p,q}/ε)$-average-radius list-decodable with probability at least $1 - q^{-Ω(n)}$, i.e., for every center $y \in \mathbb{F}_q^n$, the $C_{p,q}/ε$ codewords closest to $y$ have average fractional Hamming distance at least $p$ from $y$. This extends a similar result for (standard) list-decoding due to Guruswami, Håstad, and Kopparty (2010) to the stronger average-radius guarantee, with the same $O(1/ε)$ list size. For average-radius list-decoding, such a result was previously known only for binary linear codes (Guruswami, Li, Mosheiff, Resch, Silas, and Wootters, 2021) and for general (non-linear) random codes over arbitrary alphabets (Elias, 1991).

papers.title: Extremal problems for suspensions of even cycles
papers.abstract: Given an integer $k\geq2$ and a graph $F$, the $k$-uniform suspension $\mathcal{S}^kF$ is obtained by adjoining a fixed set of $k-2$ new vertices to every edge of $F$. In this paper, we study two extremal problems for suspensions of even cycles. Write $K^k_t$ for the $k$-uniform clique of order $t$. Let $\mathrm{ex}(n,\mathcal{S}^kC_{2\ell})$ and $\mathrm{ex}(n,K^k_t,\mathcal{S}^kC_{2\ell})$ denote the maximum numbers of edges and copies of $K^k_t$, respectively, in an $\mathcal{S}^kC_{2\ell}$-free $k$-uniform hypergraph on $n$ vertices. We prove that, for every $k\geq2$ and infinitely many $n$, \[\mathrm{ex}(n,K^{k}_{k+1},\mathcal{S}^kC_4)=\frac{n^{k-1/2}}{(k+1)!}+O(n^{k-1}).\] This extends a folklore result for $k=2$ and, as an immediate consequence, yields the asymptotics of $\mathrm{ex}(n,\mathcal{S}^kC_4)$ for infinitely many $n$, previously established by Mubayi (for all $n$). Furthermore, for every $k\geq2$ and $\ell\in\{3,5\}$, we determine the order of magnitude \[\mathrm{ex}(n,\mathcal{S}^kC_{2\ell})=Θ(n^{k-1+1/\ell}).\] This generalizes both the classical graph case $k=2$ and a previous result of Mukherjee for $k=\ell=3$. The principal difficulty in both problems lies in constructing the lower bounds. Our construction for $\mathrm{ex}(n,K^{k}_{k+1},\mathcal{S}^kC_4)$ incorporates a novel block-packing structure, which yields substantially more copies of $K^k_{k+1}$ than previously known constructions. For $\mathrm{ex}(n,\mathcal{S}^kC_{2\ell})$ with $\ell\in\{3,5\}$, we establish a natural $k$-uniform version of Wenger graphs, addressing the subtleties involved in lifting extremal graph constructions to suspensions. We also give applications of our results to Turán problems for simplicial complexes.

papers.title: A Method of Construction of Pairwise Additive Balanced Incomplete Block Designs
papers.abstract: The existence of sets of balanced incomplete block (BIB) designs with pairwise additivity, called pairwise additive BIB designs, has been studied through direct and recursive constructions in the literature. This paper presents a new method of constructing such designs from affine resolvable semi-regular group divisible (ARSRGD) designs. Since many known ARSRGD designs are obtained from generalized Hadamard matrices, we also describe the corresponding construction of pairwise additive BIB designs from generalized Hadamard matrices. Using the construction together with known existence results for generalized Hadamard matrices, we obtain several new infinite series of pairwise additive BIB designs, including designs with parameter sets whose existence was previously unknown.

papers.title: Broadcast Domination Number is at Most Twice the Multipacking Number
papers.abstract: For a graph $ G = (V, E) $ with a vertex set $ V $ and an edge set $ E $, a function $ f : V \rightarrow \{0, 1, 2, . . . , diam(G)\} $ is called a \emph{broadcast} on $ G $. For each vertex $ u \in V $, if there exists a vertex $ v $ in $ G $ (possibly, $ u = v $) such that $ f (v) > 0 $ and $ d(u, v) \leq f (v) $, then $ f $ is called a dominating broadcast on $ G $. The cost of the dominating broadcast $f$ is the quantity $ \sum_{v\in V}f(v) $. The minimum cost of a dominating broadcast is the broadcast domination number of $G$, denoted by $ γ_{b}(G) $. A multipacking is a set $ M \subseteq V $ in a graph $ G = (V, E) $ such that for every vertex $ v \in V $ and for every integer $ r \geq 1 $, the ball of radius $ r $ around $ v $ contains at most $ r $ vertices of $ M $, that is, there are at most $ r $ vertices in $ M $ at a distance at most $ r $ from $ v $ in $ G $. The multipacking number of $ G $ is the maximum cardinality of a multipacking of $ G $ and is denoted by $ mp(G) $. It is known that $mp(G)\leqγ_b(G)$. In 2014, Hartnell and Mynhardt proved that $γ_b(G)\leq 3mp(G)-2$ whenever $mp(G)\geq2$. In 2019, Beaudou, Brewster, and Foucaud improved this bound to $γ_b(G)\leq 2 mp(G)+3$ and conjectured that $γ_b(G)\leq 2 mp(G)$. We solve their conjecture by proving that $γ_b(G)\leq 2 mp(G)$ for every graph $G$. Our proof is constructive and yields a linear-time $2$-approximation algorithm for Maximum Multipacking problem which improves the earlier approximation factor $2+o(1)$.

papers.title: Height and distance-squared functions on implicit plane curves
papers.abstract: We introduce families of Lagrange functions associated with height and distance-squared functions on implicit plane curves. We show that degeneracies of these families characterize geometric properties of the curves, such as inflections and vertices, and give geometric interpretations of the corresponding Lagrange multipliers in terms of contact with lines and circles.

papers.title: Near-optimal Turán densities of $r$-graphs on $r+1$ vertices
papers.abstract: Let $π(H)$ be the Turán density of an r-uniform hypergraph $H$ and let $H_k^r$ denote the $r$-uniform hypergraph on $r+1$ vertices with exactly $k$ edges, where $1\le k\le r+1$. Sidorenko~(JCT-B, 2024) proved that $π(H_3^r)\ge (1.7215-o(1))r^{-2}$ as $r\to\infty$ and $π(H_k^r)\ge (C_k+o(1))r^{-(1+1/(k-2))}$ for fixed $k$ as $r\to\infty$. Clemen~later improved the first bound to $π(H_3^r)\ge cr^{-2}\sqrt{\log r}$ for some constant $c>0$. In this article, we prove the following results. \begin{itemize} \item For any fixed $\varepsilon>0$, there is a constant $c_\varepsilon>0$ such that $$π(H_3^r)\ge \frac{c_\varepsilon}{r(\log r)^{2+\varepsilon}}.$$ %$π(H_3^r)\ge 1/(r(\log r)^{2+o(1)})$. Together with the known upper bound $π(H_3^r)\le1/r$, this implies $π(H_3^r)=r^{-1+o(1)}$. \item For every $3\le k\le r+1$, let $s=\min\{k-2,r-k+2\}$. Then \begin{equation*} 0\le \frac{k-2}{r}-π(H_k^r) \le \frac{128}{r}\left(\sqrt{s\log\frac{er}{s}}+\log\frac{er}{s}\right). \end{equation*} This estimate yields several asymptotically sharp results for $π(H_k^r)$. For example, $π(H_k^r)=(1+o(1))(k-2)/r$ when $\log(er/(k))=o(k)$. \end{itemize}

papers.title: Two-sided coherent algebras over any field with $\mathcal{PGF}(R)\subsetneq\mathcal{GP}(R)$
papers.abstract: For a ring $R$, let $\mathcal{GP}(R)$, $\mathcal{GF}(R)$, and $\mathcal{PGF}(R)$ denote the classes of Gorenstein projective, Gorenstein flat, and projectively coresolved Gorenstein flat left $R$-modules, respectively. We answer negatively the question whether $\mathcal{GP}(R)=\mathcal{PGF}(R)$ for every ring. More precisely, over every field $k$ we construct a left and right coherent central $k$-algebra $T$ and a strongly Gorenstein projective left $T$-module which is not Gorenstein flat; hence $\mathcal{PGF}(T)\subsetneq\mathcal{GP}(T)$.

papers.title: Commutative coherent rings with $\mathcal{GP}\not\subseteq\mathcal{GF}$
papers.abstract: For every field $k$, we construct a commutative coherent $k$-algebra admitting a Gorenstein projective module that is not Gorenstein flat.

papers.title: Two averaged dynamical generalizations of Chowla's conjecture
papers.abstract: Let $k\ge1$ be an integer and let $λ$ be the Liouville function. In 1965, Chowla gave a conjecture that the values of $λ(n+h_1),\dots, λ(n+h_k)$ are asymptotically unrelated for any distinct natural numbers $h_1, \dots, h_k$. In this article, motivated by the recent work of Bergelson and Richter on the dynamical generalizations of the prime number theorem, we will show a dynamical generalization of Chowla's conjecture on average. In the proof, we follow an approach of Qi and Zheng who established a variant of Bergelson and Richter's theorem over irreducible binary cubic forms. Moreover, we will use this approach to show an analogue of the dynamical Chowla's conjecture along the primes on average. In 2016, Tao proved that the two-point logarithmic Chowla's conjecture holds. Recently, Charamaras and Richter generalized Tao's theorem to bounded arithmetic functions and proposed a conjecture that generalizes Chowla's conjecture to bounded multi-variable arithmetic functions. Building on their work, we prove a dynamical generalization of Tao's theorem and a variant for the composition of the sum-of-digits function with the prime Omega function.

papers.title: Adaptive Schauder Stochastic Mirror Descent in Banach Spaces
papers.abstract: In this paper, we introduce an adaptive regularization strategy for stochastic mirror descent (SMD) to solve a class of risk functional minimization problems in infinite-dimensional Banach spaces. Using a Schauder basis, we construct nested finite-dimensional subspaces whose dimensions adapt to the sample size $n$ and balance approximation and optimization errors. We restrict each SMD subproblem to the corresponding subspace and project the stochastic gradient onto its dual space. This yields closed form solutions and coordinate-wise coefficient updates with low computational and storage complexity. For risk minimization in $\mathcal{L}^p$ spaces with $1<p<\infty$, we construct Bregman distances adapted to the underlying Banach space geometry using $\max\{2,p\}$-convex functionals induced by uniform convexity. At the $\mathcal{L}^1$ endpoint, we instead construct a locally strongly convex functional based on the entropy function. By developing a new analytical framework, we establish a convergence rate of $\mathcal O\left(n^{-\min\{\frac12,\frac1p\}}\right)$, up to logarithmic factors. In the misspecified setting, we prove convergence of the risk to its minimum under weaker regularity assumptions and derive explicit polynomial rates when the regularity exceeds a specified threshold. Finally, we apply the method to statistical inverse problems and illustrate its empirical performance through numerical experiments in both settings.

papers.title: On Sun's Conjectures for Truncated Jacobi-Symbol Determinants via Supersingular Elliptic Curves
papers.abstract: We study the truncated Jacobi-symbol determinants $$\{c,d\}_n=\det\!\left[\left(\frac{j^2+cjk+dk^2}{n}\right)\right]_{2\le j,k\le n-2}$$ proposed by Zhi-Wei Sun in \cite{ZWSun} and prove Conjectures 5.1(i), 5.2, 5.3, 5.4, 5.5, 5.6(i), 5.7, 5.8, a case of 5.6(ii) of \cite{ZWSun}, Conjecture 4.8(i) of \cite{Sun2019} and some strengthened forms. All results follow from a single unified approach: for a prime $p$, we diagonalize the nonzero-residue matrix indexed by $\mathbb{F}_p^\times$ and reduce the vanishing of determinants to the supersingular reduction of certain CM elliptic curves. The same framework extends naturally to further families of parameters, suggesting a general mechanism behind identities of this type.

papers.title: Turning angle analysis reveals hidden anisotropies in intracellular transport
papers.abstract: Molecular motion within living cells provides a window into the physical principles underlying intracellular organization and transport. Yet a fundamental limitation remains: measured trajectories are often short, noisy, and randomly oriented, rendering spatial anisotropies inaccessible to conventional analyses. We show that turning-angle statistics provide a robust approach for uncovering anisotropies in anomalous diffusion. Using a two-dimensional anisotropic fractional Brownian motion model with random orientations, we show theoretically and through simulations that turning-angle distributions preserve signatures of anisotropy. We apply this approach to single-particle tracking data, including quantum dots in the cytoplasm of HeLa cells and membrane proteins in hippocampal neurons. Turning angles reveal hidden anisotropies in the motion of quantum dots and Kv1.4 channels, and in specific dynamical states of glycoprotein CD4. These results establish turning-angle analysis as a powerful strategy for detecting organization in complex environments and reveal that anisotropic anomalous diffusion is an {often} overlooked feature of intracellular dynamics.

papers.title: Spherical Completeness, Coherence, and GCD Properties of Formal Power Series and Witt Vector Rings
papers.abstract: Let $K$ be a complete nonarchimedean valued field with $v(K^\times)=\mathbf R$, and let $V=\mathcal O_K$. We prove that $K$ is spherically complete if and only if $V[[T]]$ is coherent, and that this is also equivalent to $V[[T]]$ being a GCD domain. If $K$ is perfect of characteristic $p$, the same characterization holds for the Witt vector ring $W(V)$. Thus, this settles the previously unresolved full-real-value-group case in the coherence problems for both formal power series and Witt vector rings. In particular, this result also gives affirmative answers to Questions~9 and~10 of Anderson--Kang--Park. The proof combines a coherence criterion for complete rings with a spherically complete valuation quotient and a uniform construction of non-finitely generated intersections of two principal ideals from an empty ball chain.

papers.title: Discretization and Statistical Consistency of Functional Flow Matching
papers.abstract: Functional flow matching learns to generate random functions, such as velocity fields or solutions of partial differential equations, by continuously transforming a simple probability distribution into a target distribution. In practice, however, training and sampling use only finitely many grid values or coefficients. Does refining these observations recover the intended function-space model, and how do observation, learning, and numerical errors affect the generated distribution? We address these questions by first proving that the velocity targets used for training converge in mean square when the finite reconstructions converge to the underlying functions and remain uniformly bounded. The observations need not be nested: each refinement may replace earlier sensor locations. We also give quantitative bounds for orthogonal projections and extend the result to point observations under suitable regularity and reconstruction assumptions. We then bound the discrepancy between the generated and target distributions in Wasserstein distance, separating observation, learning, numerical, and endpoint errors without requiring uniqueness of the population finite-dimensional dynamics. For a normalized quadrature neural operator representing the learned velocity field, we establish stability and learning bounds with constants independent of the number of sensors. Under fixed model dimension and boundedness assumptions, the statistical excess risk decreases at an inverse-sample-size rate, up to logarithmic factors. A Gaussian example combines these estimates into an explicit sampling-error rate.

papers.title: Sharp Error Estimates for a Fully Discrete Approximation of Semilinear Stochastic Convection--Diffusion Equations with Additive Noise and Nonsmooth Initial Data
papers.abstract: We establish sharp strong error estimates for a fully discrete approximation of semilinear stochastic convection--diffusion equations driven by additive noise subject to nonsmooth initial data. The problem is discretized in space using a standard Galerkin finite element method and in time via the linearly implicit Euler scheme. By decoupling the noise regularity index $β\in (0, 2]$ from the initial data regularity index $μ\in (0, 2]$, we derive time-weighted spatial and temporal regularity bounds that isolate the initial singularity at $t = 0$ into an integrable temporal weight. By allowing the drift operator $F$ to map into negative-order fractional spaces to incorporate the convection term, we prove sharp strong convergence rates of order $O(h^β+ k^{β/2})$ for $β\in (0, 2)$ and $O\bigl(h^2 + k(1+\ln(t_n/k))^{1/2}\bigr)$ at the critical endpoint $β= 2$ for any fixed $t_n > 0$, without requiring the regularity of the initial data to match that of the noise. Furthermore, these convergence rates are achieved under a relaxed differentiability condition requiring only a Lipschitz continuous first Gâteaux derivative of $F$. Numerical experiments validate the theoretical results across both trace-class and space-time white noise regimes.

papers.title: Exact Reachability under Vertex- and Area-Centroid Control
papers.abstract: A vertex-centroid move slides one vertex of a polygon along the line through it and the centroid of all vertices; Problem 60 of The Open Problems Project asks whether such moves can make every polygon regular. We prove that two simple labeled $n$-gons, with straight angles allowed, are joined through simple polygons by finitely many positive moves exactly when they have the same orientation; a nonconstant move is positive if the vertex remains on the same side of the centroid of the other vertices. The same holds for flows toward or away from the instantaneous area centroid. Inward-only or outward-only moves reach every target of the same orientation up to translation and positive scaling. The common mechanism is a first-order criterion: a symmetric definite center response makes the one-vertex fields of a smooth affine-equivariant center bracket generating. The response is a weighted covariance for point barycenters and $(d+2)$ times the volume covariance for polyhedral centroids. Once translation and scale are factored out, the fields sum to zero, giving exact one-sided control. We resolve Problem 60 under both conventions for a vertex at the centroid. For the vertex-centroid system on $n$ affinely spanning points in $\mathbb{R}^d$, we classify positive-move reachability and prove a local $3dn$-move bound.

papers.title: Characterization of the boundedness of the segment multiplier on rearrangement-invariant spaces
papers.abstract: Given rearrangement-invariant (r.i.) spaces $X$ and $Y$, we show that the segment multiplier, the truncated Hilbert transform, and the discrete Hilbert transform (on the associated discretized space) are bounded from $X$ to $Y$ simultaneously. Moreover, when $X = Y$ this boundedness is characterized by a condition on a pair of Boyd-type indices. We also exhibit an r.i. space on which the segment multiplier is bounded while the (non-truncated) Hilbert transform fails to be bounded.

papers.title: Regularity-Aware Stochastic MGDA with Adaptive Per-Iterate Conflict-Avoidant Update
papers.abstract: Multi-objective learning (MOL) aims to optimize multiple objectives simultaneously. The multi-gradient descent algorithm (MGDA) constructs a common descent or conflict-avoidant (CA) direction by solving a gradient-aggregation subproblem. In stochastic settings, the vanilla stochastic MGDA method, SMG, replaces full-batch gradients with mini-batch estimates, causing bias in the resulting CA direction. Existing analyses control this error using continuity of the CA-direction mapping, but do not distinguish how its sensitivity varies with the geometry of the MGDA subproblem. Motivated by this limitation, we show that the MGDA direction map is Lipschitz continuous under reduced nondegeneracy, whereas its general \(1/2\)-Hölder exponent on bounded sets is sharp. This geometry motivates the Multi-objective Regularity-aware (MoRe) method, which retains adaptive MGDA aggregation in the regular regime and switches to a fixed-weight linear scalarization (LS) near degeneracy. The fallback branch skips the MGDA subproblem solve, which can reduce aggregation cost on fallback iterations while avoiding a potentially noise-sensitive update. Theoretically, we establish a per-iterate CA guarantee, and a \(\widetilde{\mathcal O}(T^{-1})\) convergence rate, improving upon the previously established \(\widetilde{\mathcal O}(T^{-1/4})\) SMG guarantee, where \(\widetilde{\mathcal O}\) hides logarithmic factors. Experiments demonstrate favorable multi-task performance and convergence behavior consistent with the theoretical rate.

papers.title: Corrigendum to "Transitive permutation groups with trivial four point stabilizers"
papers.abstract: This article revisits earlier work by the last author together with Kay Magaard. We correct mistakes in results about the Sylow 2- and 3-structure of groups that act with fixity 3 and one result about possible components, we improve some results and we add details.

papers.title: Limit theorems for supercritical branching processes in Markovian environment with linear fractional offspring distributions
papers.abstract: In this paper, we study the asymptotic behaviour for distribution of supercritical branching process in a Markovian environment with linear fractional offspring distributions. Phase transitions in the behaviour of the process is discovered, through investigating the strongly, intermediately and weakly supercritical cases.

papers.title: Classification of Smooth Minimal Kähler Fourfolds Without Effective Divisors and Surfaces
papers.abstract: We prove the following two statements: (1) If $X$ is a compact Kähler fourfold with pseudo-effective canonical bundle and no subvarieties of codimension one or two, then $K_X$ is a torsion line bundle; (2) If $X$ is a compact Kähler fourfold with no subvarieties of codimension one or two, then $X$ is not uniruled. Using the Beauville-Bogomolov decomposition and a characterization of Uniruled manifolds by Wenhao Ou, we get that if $X$ is a compact Kähler fourfold with no subvarieties of codimension one or two, then either $X$ is a torus or an irreducible holomorphic symplectic manifold.

papers.title: Weighted $H^p-L^q$ boundedness of integral operators with rough kernels
papers.abstract: In this paper, we study integral operators \begin{equation*} T_αf(x)=\int_{\mathbb{R}^{n}}K(x,y) f(y)dy, \end{equation*} with kernels $K(x,y)= k_1( x- A_1y)...k_m( x-A_my),$ where $k_i(x)=\frac{Ω_i(x)}{|x|^{n/q_i}}$ and $Ω_i: \mathbb{R}^n\to \mathbb{R}$ are homogeneous functions of degree zero, satisfying a size and a Dini condition, $A_{i}$ are certain invertible matrices, and $\frac n{q_1}+\dots+\frac n{q_m}=n-α,$ $0\leq α<n.$ We obtain the $H^{p}_{w^p}(\mathbb{R}^{n})-L^{q}_{w^q}(\mathbb{R}^{n})$ boundedness of these operators, for a class of Muckenhoupt weights $w$, satisfying the condition \begin{equation*} w(A_ix)\leq cw(x), \end{equation*} $a.e.x\in\mathbb{R} ^n $, $1\leq i\leq m$.

papers.title: Classification of skew left braces with additive group isomorphic to the infinite dihedral group
papers.abstract: We classify all skew left braces with additive group isomorphic to the infinite dihedral group. There are ten isomorphism classes.

papers.title: Pauli-Sparse regularised Counterdiabatic Shortcuts for Linear-Ramp QAOA
papers.abstract: Combinatorial optimization is a leading target for quantum algorithms, but finite-depth QAOA can suffer from strong diabatic errors when the interpolation Hamiltonian has small, or exponentially small, spectral gaps. We propose a Pauli-sparse counterdiabatic extension of linear-ramp QAOA based on the regularised adiabatic gauge potential \[ \bigl(\mathcal L_H^2+ηI\bigr)A_λ^{(η)} = -\mathrm{i}\mathcal L_H(\partial_λH), \qquad \mathcal L_H(X)=[H,X]. \] Instead of computing a dense AGP, we solve this equation approximately by an inexact conjugate-gradient method in Pauli coordinates, truncating the Pauli expansion during the iteration to obtain a gate-budget-aware set of implementable rotations. The selected support is then improved by a Galerkin refit and certified by an a posteriori residual bound. The regularization parameter \(η\) acts as an energy-resolution scale: it suppresses transitions below \(\sqrtη\) while retaining larger-gap transitions. Thus, the method can avoid resolving exponentially small splittings inside a low-energy solution manifold while reducing leakage away from it. Numerical experiments on Ferromagnetic Chain (FC) and perturbed FC--MaxCut/MarketSplit instances show that the resulting LR-CD-QAOA ansatz improves approximation ratios over the uncorrected linear ramp, especially in regimes where LR-QAOA remains far from the optimum. Overall, the proposed regularized LR-CD-QAOA framework substantially broadens the practical applicability of QAOA to QUBO optimization by improving its robustness across heterogeneous problem landscapes, including instances with near-degenerate low-energy structures and small spectral gaps.

papers.title: The contrast between real and $p$-adic integrability
papers.abstract: A fundamental question in $p$-adic symplectic geometry and $p$-adic Hamiltonian mechanics is to what extent we can learn new information about integrable systems with coefficients in the rational numbers $\mathbb{Q}$, if we view them as $p$-adic systems instead of real ones. We combine geometric analytic estimates with Galois theory in order to show that at a local level, these real and $p$-adic viewpoints give completely different information. Then we focus on understanding this local behavior for the $p$-adic case by proving effective methods to compute local normal forms. Our results are motivated by a program outlined by Pelayo-Voevodsky-Warren a decade ago, to develop a $p$-adic theory of integrable systems and symplectic geometry.

papers.title: Symmetry Breaking and Moduli for Ancient Yamabe Flows on the Sphere
papers.abstract: For every $n\ge3$, we construct compact Type II ancient Yamabe flows in the round conformal class of the unit $n$-sphere $\Ss^n$. After stereographic projection and rescaling of time and conformal factor, the solutions are asymptotic backward in time to finite superpositions of Aubin--Talenti bubbles with mutually comparable scales. For integers $h\ge1$ and $k\ge2$, the limiting centers form $h$ coaxial regular $k$-gons; when $h\ge2$, their distinct layer heights may be prescribed arbitrarily in the interval $(-1,1)$. If $hk\ge3$, the resulting flows are not geometrically equivalent to any rotationally symmetric ancient flow. For each flow, there is a fixed point of $\Ss^n$ at which the Ricci tensor has both positive and negative eigenvalues on every time slice. The corresponding volume-normalized Yamabe flows are also ancient. After rescaling each time slice to a fixed volume, the metrics converge to a wedge of $hk$ isometric round $n$-spheres in the Gromov--Hausdorff topology, as time tends to $-\infty$. For fixed $h,k\ge2$, the concentration configurations admit an explicit $(h-1)$-parameter description up to Möbius transformations. Consequently, the construction yields geometrically inequivalent flows indexed by a nonempty open subset of $\R^{h-1}$, all with the same fixed-volume backward Gromov--Hausdorff limit. The proof uses inner--outer gluing for the quasilinear parabolic equation in $n$-dimensional space that exhibits Kelvin symmetry. Weighted Euclidean and spherical Hölder estimates control the nonlinear terms and, together with parabolic regularity, yield smooth extension of the conformal metrics across the north pole of $\Ss^n$.

papers.title: Compensated Splitting For Generalized Lyapunov Equations
papers.abstract: The generalized Lyapunov equation has a natural splitting that leads to the standard fixed-point iteration (sFPI) for its numerical solution. sFPI is convergent, for an arbitrarily given initial guess, if and only if the spectral radius of the associated linear operator is smaller than $1$. This means that sFPI may diverge if the spectral radius is $1$ or bigger. In this paper, we propose a compensated splitting scheme that aims to reduce the spectral radius so that the resulting compensated fixed-point iteration (cFPI) has a better convergence property, namely, cFPI may still converge even if sFPI does not or cFPI converges faster than sFPI does when the latter is also convergent. Numerical results are presented to demonstrate the superiority of cFPI to sFPI.

papers.title: $C$-networks and the planar Ising inverse problem
papers.abstract: We solve the inverse problem for Ising models on reduced planar graphs in a disk, i.e., recovering the edge coupling constants from the boundary spin correlations. A recursive solution to this problem was provided by Galashin--Pylyavskyy. Our solution is nonrecursive. It is based on an Ising analog of the chamber ansatz which asserts that the inverse map factors through variables on the graph that transform under the Ising Y-$Δ$ move according to the discrete CKP equation.

papers.title: The Size of the Intersection of $q$-ary Hamming Balls
papers.abstract: The interest in studying the size of the intersection of multiple $q$-ary Hamming balls has grown due to the recent advances in DNA-based data storage systems. We present an exact formula for the cardinality of the intersection of $s$ Hamming balls of varying radii over a $q$-ary alphabet. It is known that the distances between the center points of the Hamming balls are not enough, in general, to determine the size of the intersection. Based on our formula, we are able to find more refined structural properties of the center points for determining the exact size of the intersection. Moreover, we also analyze the size of the intersection of Hamming balls with equal radii $t$ for sufficiently large $n$ when $t$ and $q$ are constants. When $s=3$, we give the necessary and sufficient conditions (for all $q\ge 2$, $q\neq 6$ and sufficiently large $n$) to obtain the maximum size of the intersection when the centers of the Hamming balls have a given minimum distance and demonstrate how to compute it using our general formula.

papers.title: Transient Amplification in Cascaded Gradient Methods: Exact Minimax Laws and Tracking without Resonance
papers.abstract: Leader-follower gradient iterations, including bilevel and two-time-scale methods, can exhibit large finite-time excursions despite asymptotic stability. For cascaded iterations with block matrix J = [[A,0],[C,D]], symmetric diagonal blocks of norm at most gamma < 1, and coupling norm at most c, we prove an exact, dimension-free minimax formula: at every horizon t, the worst-case amplification equals the spectral norm of [[gamma^t,0],[c t gamma^(t-1),gamma^t]], attained by an aligned two-dimensional quadratic. Consequently, the worst transient is on the order of 1 + c/(1-gamma), and eigenvalues alone cannot predict finite-time gain. Under martingale noise, the aligned system has stationary follower variance sigma^2 c^2 (1+gamma^2)/(1-gamma^2)^3, establishing cubic inverse-gap scaling. For quadratic followers, the coupling is linked to follower sensitivity R by C = (I-D)R. When the leader is isotropic and the follower map is positive semidefinite, amplification is at most 1 plus the operator norm of R, independently of the spectral gaps. A look-ahead Newton update eliminates follower memory and is minimax-optimal among linear updates that track the leader exactly. Experiments validate the bounds and show that accelerated or inexact follower solvers can exceed the sensitivity bound when their effective maps have negative eigenvalues. Code and experiment scripts: https://github.com/Axym-Labs/transient-amplification

papers.title: Bounds on the F-Pure Threshold of Isolated Hypersurface Singularities
papers.abstract: We obtain bounds for the $F$-pure threshold of isolated hypersurface singularities over an algebraically closed field of positive characteristic $p$ in terms of classical singularity invariants. For an irreducible plane curve whose value semigroup has first two generators $β_0,β_1$, we show that the $F$-pure threshold is at most $\frac{1}{β_0}+\frac{1}{β_1}$ and differs from it by less than $\frac{1}{\gcd(β_0,β_1)p}$, with equality when certain base-$p$ digits add without carrying, and we give an example showing that higher weighted-order terms can change the $F$-pure threshold. We also conjecture a lower bound in terms of the Milnor number, and prove it for semi-quasi-homogeneous singularities, for all plane curves, and whenever the number of variables exceeds $p$. In particular, it holds in characteristic $2$. As applications, we reprove Igusa's formula for the log canonical threshold of a complex plane branch (with integer coefficients), prove the conjecture of Mustaţă, Takagi and Watanabe for such branches, and bound the log canonical threshold of complex isolated hypersurface singularities.

papers.title: A path-following framework on fiber bundle for variational inequalities
papers.abstract: Developing general-purpose algorithms with global asymptotic convergence guarantees for variational inequalities (VIs) remains a longstanding challenge. This paper proposes a path-following framework for finite-dimensional VIs with arbitrary continuous mappings and polytope domains. The approach first transforms a general VI into a smooth VI on a simplex. Its key innovation is to formulate the resulting problem on a fiber bundle, called the fixed-point bundle, whose geometric structure enables the systematic integration of initialization, path-following, and singularity avoidance. Without imposing monotonicity or similar assumptions, the framework guarantees global linear convergence for nonsingular solutions and global linear convergence up to any prescribed precision for singular solutions. In numerical experiments, the algorithm attained a precision of $10^{-5}$ on all 6400 randomly generated instances, with dimensions up to 1024. Code and data are available at https://github.com/shb20tsinghua/FiberBundle_VI.

papers.title: Amply regular graphs with $μ$ close to half the valency and group divisible designs
papers.abstract: In this paper, we classify connected amply regular graphs with diameter $d \geq 4$ and parameters $(v, k, λ, μ)$ satisfying $μ= \frac{k-1}{2}$, where $k\geq 5$ is odd. We prove that such a graph must be exactly one of the following: the $5$-cube, the graph $\K_2 \square Λ$, where $Λ$ is the unique bipartite $(0,2)$-graph on $14$ vertices, or the point--block incidence graph of a group divisible design with the dual property, namely a $GDDDP\left(2, k+1;\, k;\, 0, \frac{k-1}{2}\right)$. For the last family, we give equivalent characterizations in terms of bipartite $Q$-regular graphs and relation graphs of symmetric association schemes with five classes. Furthermore, we present constructions of such amply regular graphs, yielding infinite families of examples derived from Paley graphs, Peisert graphs, and Paley digraphs.

papers.title: A unified approach to Penner, Ptolemy, and Casey's theorems in several dimensions
papers.abstract: We prove Penner's theorem on horocycles and theorems of Ptolemy and Casey, all with full converses, in hyperbolic space of several dimensions. Recently Waddle observed that the equations underpinning these three theorems are related, and it is this viewpoint that we advance, using the Lorentzian model of hyperbolic space. We show that all three theorems can be derived from a common Gram-matrix calculation applied to lightlike, timelike, and spacelike vectors. Remarkably, our approach gives a version of Casey's theorem in the plane with a full converse, involving three geometric alternatives, which to our knowledge has not previously been recorded.

papers.title: A $\mathrm{C}^*$-algebraic Hoffman-Wielandt theorem
papers.abstract: We observe that the $2$-norm distance $d_{U,2}$ between the unitary orbits of normal elements in a $\mathrm{II}_1$ factor $\mathcal{M}$ is equal to the $2$-Wasserstein distance between the spectral measures induced by the trace $τ_\mathcal{M}$. Using classification and optimal transport theory, we deduce an analogous $2$-norm equation for normal operators $x$ and $y$ in simple, separable, unital, nuclear, $\mathcal{Z}$-stable $\mathrm{C}^*$-algebras that are either monotracial, or real rank zero with finitely many extremal traces, provided that $σ(x)=σ(y)$ is convex. Consequently, $d_{U,2}$ equips the set of approximate unitary equivalence classes of contractive normal elements of $\mathcal{M}$ with the structure of a compact length space. The same is true of the set of equivalence classes of embeddings into the Jiang-Su algebra $\mathcal{Z}$ of classifiable tracial $2$-Wasserstein spaces over compact, convex planar domains.

papers.title: Stochastic Riccati equations with jumps for indefinite linear-quadratic control: A stochastic value-flow approach
papers.abstract: This paper studies the nonlinear matrix-valued stochastic Riccati equation with jumps (SRE-J) arising from indefinite stochastic linear-quadratic optimal control problems with random coefficients and Poisson jumps. We demonstrate that the presence of jumps may cause the matrix-valued optimal state process $\mathbf{X}$ to become singular, even under the standard condition. Consequently, the classical representation $P=\mathbf{Y}\mathbf{X}^{-1}$ used in the diffusion case is generally unavailable. To overcome this difficulty, we construct the Riccati process directly from the stochastic value flow under the uniform convexity condition on the cost functional, an approach that requires no invertibility condition on the jump coefficient. We then prove that the SRE-J admits a maximal strongly regular solution, which yields a closed-loop representation of the unique open-loop optimal control. Furthermore, we establish verifiable sufficient conditions for uniform convexity and provide examples of indefinite stochastic linear-quadratic problems with jumps.

papers.title: Existence of rotationally symmetric embedded f-minimal tori
papers.abstract: Let $n\geq2$, and let $f:[0,+\infty)\to\mathbb{R}$ be a smooth function satisfying $f''\geq0$ and $0<m\leq f'\leq M$ for some constants $m$ and $M$. We prove that $\mathbb{R}^{n+1}$, endowed with the conformal metric \begin{equation*} ds^2=e^{-\frac{f(|x|^2)}{2n}}\sum_{i=1}^{n+1}dx_i^2, \end{equation*} admits a compact, embedded, rotationally symmetric minimal hypersurface diffeomorphic to $S^1\times S^{n-1}$. This extends Angenent's existence theorem for self-shrinking tori, which is recovered when $f(s)=s$.

papers.title: Stack Constructions and Equality Cases for Laffey's Bound for Maximal Commutative Matrix Algebras
papers.abstract: We study equality cases in Laffey's lower bound for local maximal commutative subalgebras of matrix algebras with cube-zero radical. We introduce a stacking operation that combines algebras with common outer Loewy layers while preserving maximal commutativity. This yields standard equality bricks $B_{a,c}=(a,ac+1,c;a+c)$ for all $a,c\ge2$ and reduces further constructions to smaller building blocks. We establish the existence of all minimal equality bricks on the balanced branch and obtain sharp realizations throughout the $(4,5)$-sector. We also construct the first nontrivial nearly balanced root over arbitrary fields. We determine the balanced--nearly-balanced envelope of the numerical Laffey profile and give an arithmetic criterion for preservation of sharpness under stacking. As a consequence, the profile is attained in every matrix dimension $14\le n\le52$ and $93\le n\le114$, as well as along five infinite families over arbitrary fields. The main existence and interval results are proved in characteristic zero; the field-independent constructions are stated explicitly.

papers.title: Spanning Subdivisions in Robustly Expanding Digraphs
papers.abstract: Kühn, Osthus and Treglown [\emph{J. Combin. Theory Ser. B} \textbf{100} (2010)] proved that every sufficiently large robust outexpander with linear minimum semi-degree contains a Hamilton cycle. In this paper, we extend their result to spanning subdivisions of a digraph $F$ in a robust outexpander $D$, with prescribed branch vertices and arbitrarily specified path lengths. In particular, the digraph $F$ need not be fixed. For an $n$-vertex digraph $D$, $F$ may have as many as a constant multiple of $n/\log n$ arcs. This holds provided that $F$ has sufficiently few vertices and the prescribed lengths satisfy suitable conditions. We further establish a more general result for mixed prescribed path lengths, which allows $F$ to have linearly many arcs when the shorter replacement paths together use only a small proportion of the vertices of $D$. As applications, we obtain spanning subdivision extensions of the asymptotic Nash--Williams theorem for digraphs and an asymptotically sharp Ore-type theorem for oriented graphs.

papers.title: Wasserstein convergence rates for empirical measures of point processes
papers.abstract: In this paper, we establish upper and lower bounds on the convergence rate of empirical measures of point processes under the Wasserstein distance. To this end, we first introduce a new metric on the space of finite counting measures. Unlike many existing metrics in the literature, our proposed metric incorporates the spatial locations of unmatched points. Drawing on both this new metric and existing metrics from the literature, we identify a set of common structural properties and develop a general framework for Wasserstein distances between point-process distributions based on metrics satisfying these properties. We then use this framework to investigate the convergence rates of empirical measures, providing quantitative guarantees for approximating the distribution of the underlying point process, and further establish corresponding concentration inequalities. These theoretical results may provide ingredients for constructing oracle goodness-of-fit tests for a specified point-process distribution. We also apply our theory to the approximation of Campbell measures and discuss how the resulting bounds can help assess Wasserstein-based learning of generative point-process models.

papers.title: Correctness of Biot's model of in situ leaching for incompressible liquid and compressible solid components
papers.abstract: We study a mathematical model of in situ leaching of rare metals, in which the joint filtration of two liquids is governed by the microscopic model $\mathbb{A}^{\varepsilon}$. A key difficulty is the unknown (free) boundary $Γ(r)$ between solid and liquid components, determined by an additional condition on $Γ(r)$; no standard methods exist for this nonlinear problem. To resolve it, we apply the fixed point theorem. For a given function $r(\boldsymbol{x},t)$ from a set $\mathfrak{M}_{(0,T)}$ of sufficiently smooth functions describing the skeleton structure, we consider the auxiliary problem $\mathbb{B}^{\varepsilon}(r)$: an elliptic system for displacements of the liquid and solid components coupled with parabolic equations for the acid concentration. Selecting the weak solution of minimal smoothness, we apply the homogenization method to pass from the microscopic to the macroscopic description. The resulting macroscopic model $\mathbb{H}(r)$ contains a homogenized boundary condition that expresses the normal boundary velocity $V_{N}=\partial r/\partial t$ as a linear function of the acid concentration $c$. Since $c$ depends on $r$ via an operator $\mathbb{F}\colon\mathfrak{M}_{(0,T)}\to\mathfrak{M}_{(0,T)}$, we prove that $\mathbb{F}$ is Lipschitz continuous and, by Banach's theorem, possesses a unique fixed point $r^{*}$, which yields the unique solution $\mathbb{H}=\mathbb{H}(r^{*})$.

papers.title: Minimax Robust Designs for M-Estimated Models
papers.abstract: Experimental designs that are minimax in the presence of model misspecifications have been constructed so as to minimize the maximum, over classes of alternate response models, of the integrated mean squared error of the predicted values. The theory to date has focussed almost exclusively on Least Squares estimates. Here we extend this theory to designs tailored for M-estimation of parameters, thus obtaining additional robustness against outlying, or otherwise erroneous, responses. We show that, subject to a minor change in a tuning constant, designs optimal for Least Squares remain so asymptotically for M-estimation, under squared error loss. We argue that even this minor change should be ignored, and the tuning constant chosen in an ad hoc but sensible manner that does not depend on which M-estimate is being employed. A rather surprising additional result is that our designs and estimates, derived under an assumption of i.i.d. errors, are also robust, in a minimax sense, against broad classes of correlation structures. We also investigate designs under a more robust loss function, less influenced by outlying responses than squared error.

papers.title: Minimizers for the Cahn-Hilliard energy functional with the Flory-Huggins potential under strong anchoring conditions
papers.abstract: In this paper, we theoretically and numerically study the minimizers for the Cahn-Hilliard energy with the Flory-Huggins potential under the strong anchoring condition, i.e., the Dirichlet boundary condition. We reveal bifurcation phenomena mediated by the boundary condition, the transition layer thickness, and the temperature of the system. Numerical simulations are also presented to approximate the minimizers of this energy by solving a gradient-flow equation, namely the Allen-Cahn equation constrained with strong anchoring conditions and random initial data. The effects of varying the transition layer thickness and temperature are presented to confirm the theoretical analysis.

papers.title: Counterexamples for lacunary dilates via dyadic spike blocks
papers.abstract: We construct counterexamples, along dyadic lacunary sequences, to two problems of Erdős on the almost-everywhere behavior of sums $\sum_{j\le N}f(n_jx)$ on the circle. The main device is a dyadic spike block: rare positive spikes, each counted many times by a run of consecutive dilates, make the lacunary averages large, while a deterministic lower bound on every block prevents the rest of the series from cancelling them. We obtain a mean-zero $f\in\bigcap_{1\le q<\infty}L^q(\mathbb T)$ and a sequence $n_j=2^{m_j}$ with $n_{j+1}/n_j\ge2$ such that $\|f-S_Nf\|_2\ll(\log\log N)^{-1/2}$ and $\limsup_{N\to\infty}\frac1N\sum_{j\le N}f(n_jx)=+\infty$ for almost every $x$. This answers negatively a question of Erdős on whether the condition $\|f-S_Nf\|_2\ll(\log\log\log N)^{-C}$ suffices for almost-everywhere convergence, and shows that Matsuyama's condition $\|f-S_Nf\|_2\ll(\log\log N)^{-c}$, $c>1/2$, cannot be relaxed to $c=1/2$. A second choice of parameters gives, for every $2\le p<\infty$, functions $f\in L^p(\mathbb T)$ with $\limsup_{N\to\infty}\sum_{j\le N}f(n_jx)/(N(\log N)^{1/p-\varepsilon})=+\infty$ for every $\varepsilon>0$, almost everywhere. This is sharp up to $\varepsilon$, and the case $p=2$ answers negatively a second question of Erdős. Finally, a bounded variant in the spirit of Marstrand's disproof of Khintchine's conjecture gives sets of arbitrarily small measure whose lacunary visiting frequencies have limsup $1$ almost everywhere.

papers.title: Counterexamples to a dimension-free variant of Erdős's diameter conjecture for separated distances
papers.abstract: Erdős asked about the least possible diameter of an $n$-point set in Euclidean space when any two pairwise distances differ by at least $1$. We consider the uniform-in-dimension variant of his question, in which the dimension $d$ may grow with $n$ and the error term is independent of $d$, and answer it in the negative by an explicit construction. For every prime power $q$, we construct a set $\mathcal X_n$ of $n=q+1$ points in $\mathbb R^{q^2+q}=\mathbb R^{n^2-n}$ such that the $\binom{n}{2}$ pairwise distances are mutually at least $1$ apart, yet $$\operatorname{diam}(\mathcal X_n)\le \Bigl(1-\frac{1}{π^2}+o(1)\Bigr)n^2.$$ The construction combines a Singer cyclic difference set with a weighted product of $N=\binom n2$ regular $m$-gons, where $m=q^2+q+1$. The weights are chosen so that the resulting distances increase while the gaps between consecutive distances decrease. After normalizing the smallest gap to $1$, all distinct pairwise distances are separated by at least $1$, while the diameter has asymptotic constant $1-1/π^2<1$.

papers.title: On the existence of toric ALE and ALF gravitational instantons
papers.abstract: We establish existence and uniqueness results for asymptotically locally Euclidean (ALE) and asymptotically locally flat (ALF) gravitational instantons. In particular, we prove the existence of a unique, Ricci-flat, toric ALE and ALF gravitational instanton, for every admissible rod structure, that is smooth up to possible conical singularites. We also give an elementary proof that any toric ALE or ALF self-dual instanton is a multi-Eguchi-Hanson or multi-Taub-NUT solution.

papers.title: Local discontinuous Galerkin FEM for convex minimization
papers.abstract: The heart of the a priori and a posteriori error control in convex minimization problems is the sharp control of the differences of discrete and exact minimal energy. Conforming finite element discretizations for p-Laplace type minimization problems provide upper bounds of the energy difference with optimal convergence rates. Even for smooth solutions, known convergence rates for higher-order non-conforming finite element discretizations for the same problem class with $2 < p < \infty$, however, are exclusively suboptimal. Thus the popular a posteriori error control within the two-energy principle, that generalize hyper-circle identities, appears unbalanced. The innovative point of departure in a refined analysis of two discontinuous Galerkin (dG) schemes exploits duality relations between a discrete primal and a semi-discrete dual problem. The infinite-dimensional dual problem leads to a tiny duality gap that even vanishes for polynomial low-order terms. For a class of degenerated convex minimization problems with two-sided $p$ growth, the novel duality provides improved a priori convergence rates for the error in the minimal energies. This closes the misfit of convergence rates for the conforming and nonconforming schemes at least for the local discontinuous Galerkin schemes at hand. The motivating two-energy principle and some post-processing for a Raviart-Thomas dual variable provides an a posteriori error control, that also may drive adaptive mesh-refining. Computational benchmarks provide numerical evidence for improved convergence rates of the adaptive beyond uniform mesh-refining.

papers.title: Geometric singularities of regular surfaces with nef anti-canonical divisors over imperfect fields
papers.abstract: Let $S$ be a regular projective surface over a field $k$ of characteristic $p>0$, with $H^0(S,\mathcal{O}_S)=k$ and $-K_S$ nef. We prove that $S$ is geometrically integral over $k$ when $p\geq 7$, and we also find an example of $S$ that is not geometrically integral when $p=5$.

papers.title: On the optimal relaxation parameter of graph-based splitting methods for subspaces
papers.abstract: In this paper, we investigate the behavior of the family of graph-based splitting algorithms specialized to the problem of finding a point in the intersection of linear subspaces. The algorithms in this family, which encompasses several classical methods such as the Douglas-Rachford algorithm, are defined by a connected graph and a subgraph. Our main result establishes that when the graph and subgraph coincide, the optimal relaxation parameter is exactly $1$, thereby extending known results for the Douglas-Rachford algorithm to a much broader class of methods. Our analysis hinges on some properties of iso-averaged linear operators, which are defined as the average of an isometry and the identity, and are characterized by a specific symmetry of the norm of their relaxation.

papers.title: Neuromorphic Realization of Best Response in Finite-Action Games
papers.abstract: We develop a mechanistic dynamical-systems formulation of best response in finite-action games with relational structure on the action set. The proposed neuromorphic decision dynamics realize best response as the stable outcome of an internal state-space process, rather than as an externally imposed choice rule. This provides a deterministic account of commitment formation, symmetry resolution through basins of attraction, and hysteresis and decision persistence under perturbations. For action spaces with circulant coupling, we prove using Lyapunov-Schmidt reduction that the action-coupling operator determines which components of evidence govern decision formation. We further show that the dynamics implicitly compute a geometry-aware utility, converge exponentially to the corresponding best response, and switch only when evidence is sufficiently strong. In contrast, supplying the same geometry-aware utility directly to logit dynamics does not recover these properties, showing that relational structure must be embedded in the decision mechanism itself. We illustrate the framework in a repeated coverage game, prove that the induced game is an exact potential game, and show that its Nash equilibria are reached by the neuromorphic decision dynamics.

papers.title: Surrogate-based categorical neighborhoods for mixed-variable blackbox optimization
papers.abstract: In simulation-based engineering, design choices are often obtained following the optimization of complex blackbox models. These models frequently involve mixed-variable domains with quantitative and categorical variables. Unlike quantitative variables, categorical variables lack an inherent structure, which makes them difficult to handle, especially in the presence of constraints. This work proposes a systematic approach to structure and model categorical variables in constrained mixed-variable blackbox optimization. Surrogate models of the objective and constraint functions are used to induce problem-specific categorical pseudo-distances. From these pseudo-distances, surrogate-based neighborhoods are constructed using notions of dominance from bi-objective optimization, jointly accounting for information from both the objective and the constraint functions. This study addresses the lack of automatic and constraint-aware categorical neighborhood construction in mixed-variable blackbox optimization. As a proof of concept, these neighborhoods are employed within CatMADS, an extension of the MADS algorithm for categorical variables. The surrogate models are Gaussian processes, and the resulting method is called CatMADS-GP. The method is benchmarked on the Cat-Suite collection of 60 mixed-variable optimization problems and compared with two external mixed-variable solvers. Data profiles indicate that CatMADS-GP achieves the best performance on this collection of problems.

papers.title: Contraherent cosheaves of contramodules on Noetherian formal schemes
papers.abstract: There are two main results in this paper: the MGM equivalence between the conventional derived categories of abelian/exact categories, and the derived co-contra correspondence (i.e., an equivalence between the coderived and the contraderived category). Firstly, for any Noetherian formal scheme that is either of finite Krull dimension or semi-separated, we construct a triangulated equivalence between the conventional unbounded derived categories of the abelian category of quasi-coherent torsion sheaves and the exact category of contraherent cosheaves of contramodules. A natural dedualizing complex of quasi-coherent torsion sheaves is constructed and used for that purpose. Secondly, for any Noetherian formal scheme with a dualizing complex of quasi-coherent torsion sheaves, we construct a triangulated equivalence between the coderived category of quasi-coherent torsion sheaves and the contraderived category of contraherent cosheaves of contramodules. The exact category of contraherent cosheaves of contramodules on a locally Noetherian formal scheme, as well as the exact categories of locally contraherent cosheaves of contramodules (with respect to a given open covering) are defined and discussed in this paper. The exposition in the section of preliminaries in adic commutative algebra is worked out in the greater generality of arbitrary commutative rings with adic topologies (of finitely generated ideals).

papers.title: Hindman and Owings-like theorems without the Axiom of Choice
papers.abstract: We investigate Hindman- and Owings-type Ramsey-theoretic statements in Zermelo-Fraenkel set theory without the Axiom of Choice, with some occasional extra assumptions (such as the Axiom of Dependent Choice and/or the Axiom of Determinacy). We study several variations of Hindman's theorem on $\mathbb Q$-vector spaces; notably, we show that the uncountable analog of Hindman's theorem fails for the additive group of $\mathbb R$ (under ZF), and for $\mathbb Q$-vector spaces of uncountable dimension (under DC if such dimension is not well-orderable), among other results. In contrast, for Owings-type configurations, we obtain several positive results, especially when assuming AD. These results highlight the interaction between determinacy, algebraic structure, and dimension in the study of infinite Ramsey theory without the Axiom of Choice.

papers.title: Self-similar finite-time blowups with singular profiles of the generalized Constantin-Lax-Majda model: theoretical and numerical investigations
papers.abstract: For the generalized Constantin-Lax-Majda model with a parameter $a$, we investigate novel scenarios of self-similar finite-time blowups that arise from a new setting where the smooth initial data satisfy a certain derivative degeneracy condition. In this setting, our numerical study reveals distinct self-similar blowup behaviors depending on the sign of $a$. For $a>0$, we observe one-scale self-similar blowups with regular profiles that have not been found in previous studies. In contrast, for $a\le 0$, we discover a novel two-scale self-similar blowup scenario where the outer profile converges to a singular function at the blowup time while the inner profile remains regular on a much smaller scale. Correspondingly, an $a$-parameterized family of singular self-similar profiles with explicit expressions are constructed for $a<0$ and shown to match nicely with the limiting profiles obtained in numerical simulation. In particular, for the specific case of $a=0$, we rigorously prove the convergence of the outer profile to an explicit singular function in self-similar coordinates. Furthermore, we demonstrate the two-scale nature of the blowup in this scenario by showing that the local inner profile behavior around the singularity point of the outer profile is governed by a traveling wave on a smaller scale. To support this observation, we rigorously establish the existence of such traveling wave solutions via a fixed-point method.

papers.title: Formulation and Learning Of The Forecasting Problem
papers.abstract: Machine learning has opened new frontiers in purely data-driven forecasting of dynamical systems; the resulting methods are showing considerable promise in some application domains. However, in contrast to model-driven algorithms, analysis of these data-driven methods is poorly developed. In this paper we address this issue, developing a theory to underpin data-driven methods to solve forecasting problems. The theoretical framework comprises two key components: (i) establishing the existence of a mapping defining the forecasting problem; (ii) showing that it is possible to approximate this mapping by supervised learning techniques, to arbitrary accuracy. We work in the continuous-time and noise-free setting as this defines a simple canonical setting in which to establish an underpinning theory; the continuous-time setting leads to an operator formulation of the problem in which the underlying forecasting map is defined on pathspace. As a byproduct of our framework we show that analogous existence and approximation results may be obtained for the smoothing problem of recovering unobserved components of dynamical systems, from observed components, using supervised learning. The theoretical results, for both forecasting and smoothing, are illustrated with experiments studying the Lorenz `63, Lorenz `96 and Kuramoto-Sivashinsky dynamical systems.

papers.title: Density results for $r$-gaps between zeros of the Riemann zeta-function
papers.abstract: Let $0<γ_1\leq γ_2\leq \ldots$ denote the positive ordinates of the non-trivial zeros of the Riemann zeta-function. A result first announced by Selberg states that there exist absolute constants $Θ, \vartheta>0$ such that for each $r\in \mathbb{N}$, \[ \limsup_{n\to \infty}\frac{γ_{n+r}-γ_n}{2πr/\log γ_n}\geq 1+\fracΘ{r^α} \qquad \text{and}\qquad \liminf_{n\to \infty}\frac{γ_{n+r}-γ_n}{2πr/\log γ_n}\leq 1-\frac{\vartheta}{r^α} \] where $α$ may be taken as $2/3$, or as $1/2$ if one assumes the Riemann hypothesis. This was recently proved by Conrey and Turnage-Butterbaugh under RH and by Inoue unconditionally. We prove that in fact a positive proportion of $r$-gaps are large (and small) to the above extent, and we provide explicit estimates for the sizes and proportions of these gaps. In the case $r=1$, this quantitatively improves an unconditional result of Simonič, Trudgian and Turnage-Butterbaugh.

papers.title: Characteristic cycles of real and complex constructible sheaves, revisited
papers.abstract: For a smooth morphism $f: X \longrightarrow Σ$ of real analytic manifolds and an $\mathbb{R}$-constructible sheaf $F$ on $X$ satisfying some condition, we define a family of Lagrangian cycles parameterized by $Σ$ that we call the relative characteristic cycle of $F$ for $f$. In this way, the theory of characteristic cycles due to Kashiwara and Schapira is naturally extended to the relative setting. Based on it, we then prove a formula for the characteristic cycles of real nearby cycle sheaves. This leads us to obtain also formulas for the characteristic cycles of various constructible sheaves, such as specialization, microlocalization, and complex nearby and vanishing cycle sheaves, in a unified manner. In fact, our methods allow us to calculate not only their characteristic cycles but also their microlocal types in many situations. We will illustrate it by various examples.

papers.title: A new lower bound for the kissing number in 19 dimensions
papers.abstract: We prove that the kissing number in 19 dimensions is at least 11948, improving the bound of Cohn and Li by 256. Their odd-sign construction reduces the problem to finding a binary code of length 19 and minimum distance 5 inside a 5-punctured extended binary Golay code. In an explicit model $D$ of this ambient code, the 21 words of weights 3 and 4 are exactly the pairwise differences that such a code must avoid. They span a 10-dimensional subcode $K$. We exhibit a 6-dimensional subcode $M\le K$ for which all 21 words lie in only five cosets of $M$. After identifying $K/M$ with $\mathbb F_2^4$, these five cosets are represented by $Σ=\{e_1,e_2,e_3,e_4,e_1+e_2+e_3+e_4\}$. In the graph on $\mathbb F_2^4$ in which $u$ and $v$ are adjacent when $u+v\inΣ$, the set $Σ$ itself is independent. Lifting its five vertices gives 320 words in $K$, and translating this set through the four cosets of $K$ in $D$ gives a nonlinear code of size 1280 and minimum distance 5.

papers.title: Dunford-Pettis Multilinear Operators and Their Weak Variant on Banach Spaces
papers.abstract: In this paper, we address broader concepts of Dunford-Pettis operators, presenting new classes and results that relate this class to others already well studied in the literature, as well as an approach outside the origin. We also investigate inclusion results and conditions for the coincidence of this class with previously studied classes and with new classes that arise throughout this work.

papers.title: Optimization with Parametric Variational Inequality Constraints on a Moving Set Based on a Smoothing Method
papers.abstract: This paper focuses on optimization problems constrained by Parametric Variational Inequalities (PVI) defined on a moving set. Unlike most existing works on mathematical programs with equilibrium constraints, the equilibrium constraints have parameters not only in the function but also in the related set. We show that the solution function of the PVI is Lipschitz continuous with respect to the upper-level decision variables and the solution set of the optimization problem is nonempty and bounded. Moreover, we prove that the metric regularity of the constraints holds automatically, which allows us to characterize stationary points without any additional assumptions. A Smoothing Implicit Gradient Algorithm (SIGA) is proposed based on the smoothing approximation of the PVI with a novel scheme for updating the smoothing parameter. We prove the convergence of SIGA to a stationary point and validate the efficiency of SIGA by numerical examples from synthetic problems and portfolio management with real data.

papers.title: Online Order Fulfillment with Replenishment
papers.abstract: In modern e-commerce and service operations, firms jointly manage inventory replenishment and real-time order fulfillment under demand uncertainty.
