papers.abstract: In this paper we study the orbits of the automorphism group on a toroidal spherical variety. In the affine case, we prove that two points lie in the same orbit of the identity component if and only if the kernels of the homomorphisms from the divisor class group to their local divisor class groups coincide. These kernels are described in terms of $B$-stable prime divisors. For a smooth complete toroidal spherical variety, we obtain a similar criterion using the monoids generated by the classes of $B$-stable prime divisors that do not contain a given $G$-orbit.

papers.title: On the transcendental Yau-Tian-Donaldson Conjecture
papers.abstract: We prove the (uniform) Yau-Tian-Donaldson Conjecture for transcendental Kähler classes in the case of trivial automorphisms. Indeed, we show the existence of Special Kähler Fujita Approximations of big cohomology classes associated to big test configurations, establishing the equivalence between the uniform $K$-stability and the strengthened version for models. More generally, we show that any big cohomology class on a compact Kähler manifold admits such Special Kähler Fujita Approximations: the volume and the analogue of the Riemann-Roch coefficient of the big class are both approximated by those of Kähler classes on higher compactifications.

papers.title: Chvátal's conjecture: a proof from The Book
papers.abstract: Chvátal conjectured that every downset has a maximum-size intersecting family which is a star, that is, consists of all members of the downset containing a fixed element. Recently, Chang, Liu and Liu gave a proof of this conjecture, which follows as a corollary of more general results such as Kleitman's conjecture and a version of Kahn's conjecture (which they also prove). We give a short, direct (spectral) proof of Chvátal's conjecture, and a proof of Kleitman's conjecture along the same lines. We also prove a strengthening of Chvátal's conjecture concerning the projection packing number. Finally, we propose two spectral Chvátal conjectures which are motivated by extensive numerical experiments.

papers.title: $\mathbb{A}^1$-connectedness of moduli of vector bundles on a stacky curve
papers.abstract: Let $\mathfrak{C}$ be a projective stacky curve over an infinite field $k$ with the coarse space $C$, a geometrically connected smooth projective curve, together with a generating sheaf $\mathcal{E}$ on $\mathfrak{C}$. We consider the moduli stack of $\mathcal{E}$-semistable vector bundles of fixed determinant and multiplicities on $\mathfrak{C}$, and show that it is $\mathbb{A}^1$-connected if and only if it admits a $k$-rational point. We show that this holds whenever genus of $C$ is at least $2$ and $C(k)\neq \emptyset$. As a consequence, we conclude that, for any system of weights $\boldsymbolα$, the moduli stack of parabolic $\boldsymbolα$-semistable vector bundles of fixed determinant and quasi-parabolic data on a geometrically connected smooth projective curve is $\mathbb{A}^1$-connected.

papers.title: Abelian maximal pattern complexity and extremal words
papers.abstract: In this paper, we study the Abelian maximal pattern complexity $p_α^{\ast \mathrm{ab}}(k)$, introduced by Kamae, Widmer and Zamboni, of infinite words $α\in \mathbb{A}^{\mathbb{N}_{0}}$ over finite alphabets $\mathbb{A}$. For recurrent aperiodic words, we determine a lower bound and prove its sharpness. We further give a structural characterization of the words with minimal Abelian maximal pattern complexity. In the general case, we prove that an infinite word $α$ is aperiodic if and only if $\binom{p_{α}^{\ast \mathrm{ab}}(k)}{2}\geq k$ for every $k.$ For aperiodic words over $\ell \geq 2$ letters, each occurring infinitely often, we further prove that $p_{α}^{\ast \mathrm{ab}}(k)\geq m$ whenever $\binom{m}{2}\leq (\ell -1)(k-\ell +2)$, for all $m,k$. Together with a matching construction, this shows that the minimum Abelian maximal pattern complexity in this class is $\sqrt{2(\ell -1)k}+O_{\ell }(1)$. We call a word an Abelian pattern Sturmian word if, at every $k$, its Abelian maximal pattern complexity is the least positive integer $m$ satisfying $\binom{m}{2}\geq k$. We show that a word is Abelian pattern Sturmian if and only if, after relabeling its alphabet, it is the characteristic word of an infinite set $E\subset \mathbb{N}_{0}$ for which the bipartite graph on two disjoint copies of $\mathbb{N}_{0}$, with a left vertex $r$ adjacent to a right vertex $s$ exactly when $r+s\in E$, is a forest.

papers.title: Exact Sign Recovery for PCA Connectivity Analysis in Mixture Models
papers.abstract: We study exact sign recovery for PCA connectivity analysis in mixture models, using the projection onto the first $(K-1)$ principal components. For any fixed number of components with affinely independent means, we derive the oracle signal projection explicitly. Under anisotropic sub-Gaussian noise, with a random number of observations in each component, a rowwise eigenspace bound yields a sufficient condition, governed by the weakest signal direction, for recovering all connectivity signs without requiring a bounded condition number of the nonzero signal spectrum. Under isotropic Gaussian noise, when the configuration of the component means is fixed up to scaling and orthogonal transformations, we identify an asymptotically sharp threshold for the signal strength: exact sign recovery succeeds above the threshold and fails below the threshold, with probability tending to one when the signal strength stays a fixed relative distance from the threshold. The threshold has an explicit formula when the mixing proportions are equal and the means form a regular simplex.

papers.title: The Limits of Arithmetical Pluralism: Incompleteness, Large Cardinals, and Graded Non-Pluralism
papers.abstract: Gödelian incompleteness yields arithmetical sentences \(A\) such that \(\mathsf{PA}+A\) and \(\mathsf{PA}+\neg A\) are both consistent. Are such extensions equally legitimate? I propose graded epistemic arithmetical non-pluralism: justification for choosing between them varies with the set-theoretic strength of \(A\). I defend \(\mathsf{PA}+\mathsf{Con}(\mathsf{PA})\) and show that Friedman's concrete incompleteness results pose a serious challenge to non-pluralism about first-order arithmetic. Resolving the selection problem for such sentences turns on justifying large cardinals. Defending graded non-pluralism thus engages Gödel's programme and the justification of very large cardinals.

papers.title: Erdős-Sós via random cyclic orderings
papers.abstract: We present a simplified proof of the Erdős-Sós conjecture on trees in graphs, which is based on its recent resolution by GPT-6 Astra. At the same time, we also give another proof of the corresponding conjecture for antidirected trees in digraphs, posed by Addario-Berry, Havet, Linhares Sales, Reed, and Thomassé, and we simplify recent proofs of Kalai's conjecture for tight trees in hypergraphs. Our proof uses the language of random cyclic orderings in order to take advantage of symmetries that were obscured in the original argument, and we hope that the reader will find it intuitive. We also characterize the extremal examples for Kalai's conjecture, and we generalize it to the setting of so-called fully directed $r$-uniform hypergraphs, whose edges are ordered $r$-tuples.

papers.title: Adaptive Sparse-grid Discontinuous Galerkin Approximations to the Bhatnagar--Gross--Krook Model
papers.abstract: This work studies adaptive sparse-grid discontinuous Galerkin (DG) discretizations for the Bhatnagar--Gross--Krook (BGK) model, a kinetic equation posed in four- and six-dimensional phase-space. Standard DG methods are rendered impractical for the BGK model by the curse of dimensionality, motivating compressed representations that adapt to the solution in time. Using the adaptive sparse-grid DG method, we quantify accuracy and compression by comparing the adaptive degrees of freedom to full-grid DG methods and by assessing the resulting kinetic and fluid quantities in both fluid and rarefied regimes. Test cases include a relaxation problem, a multidimensional Sod shock tube, and shear/expansion flows used in prior low-rank BGK studies. To build an efficient Maxwellian evaluation without violating conservation, a central obstacle for structure-perserving BGK simulations, we introduce a hybrid interpolation strategy that exploits velocity separability to recover the correct discrete collision invariants and prove conservation of the resulting discrete collision operator on adaptive sparse grids. Our results show that the adaptive sparse-grid strategy can recover accurate and physically relevant solutions with sharp gradients, and the method reduces the active degrees of freedom by factors ranging from several-fold to several orders of magnitude, with the largest reductions occurring in the six-dimensional examples. All computations are performed with the open-source ASGarD adaptive sparse-grid DG library.

papers.title: Extended dynamic mode decomposition with Fourier dictionaries: Error bounds and fast implementation
papers.abstract: The Koopman operator has gained considerable attention in dynamical systems due to its capability to provide a linear viewpoint for nonlinear systems using data-driven methods such as extended dynamic mode decomposition (EDMD). In this work, we propose an EDMD-variant with a Fourier dictionary on the $d$-dimensional torus, where the data are sampled on an equispaced tensor grid. We show that the EDMD regression problem admits a unique closed-form solution and coincides with trigonometric interpolation of the Koopman image. This identification has two consequences. First, using Koopman invariance of Sobolev spaces, we transfer approximation-theoretic results for trigonometric interpolation to derive $L^p$-error bounds, $2 \le p \le \infty$, on approximations of the Koopman operator. In particular, the established bounds are of optimal order with explicit constants. Second, the EDMD matrix never has to be assembled, since its action reduces to (nonequispaced) fast Fourier transforms such that the EDMD-approximation can be evaluated matrix-free with quasi-linear cost in the dictionary size. We illustrate the results for the Kuramoto model of coupled oscillators and for the chaotic ABC flow with dictionaries of up to $10^7$ modes.

papers.title: On the Geometry of Wasserstein Barycenter II: Riemannian Rigidity, Essential Non-Branching, and Finsler Models
papers.abstract: Wasserstein barycenters provide a notion of weighted mean for probability measures on a metric space. We prove that the barycenter curvature-dimension condition ${\rm BCD}(K,N)$ is equivalent to ${\rm RCD}(K,N)$ for $K\in \mathbb R$ and $1<N<\infty$. This gives a new characterization of Riemannian curvature-dimension spaces by entropy inequalities at barycenters of finite families of measures. As a byproduct, we introduce an almost ${\rm BCD}$ condition that allows an additive error in the entropy inequality. It is stable under measured Gromov-Hausdorff convergence and implies essential non-branching when the error is sufficiently small. The resulting class contains non-Riemannian Finsler spaces. Within the ${\rm BCD}$ framework, this answers an open problem posed by Ambrosio in his 2018 ICM survey. We further bound the failure of the parallelogram identity for cotangent norms in terms of the entropy error.

papers.title: Relaxation and Steady-State Entropy Production for Langevin SPDEs: A Dirichlet-Form Approach
papers.abstract: We develop a Dirichlet-form framework for relaxation and steady-state entropy production in preconditioned Langevin stochastic partial differential equations. In infinite dimensions, the usual Fokker--Planck calculations based on ambient Lebesgue densities and the corresponding probability-current densities are generally unavailable. For the detailed-balance class, a quasi-regular symmetric Dirichlet form on the Gibbs state space yields an exact de Bruijn entropy-dissipation formula for regular densities and an integrated inequality for arbitrary finite-entropy initial laws. Self-adjointness gives detailed balance and stationary path reversal, while a coordinate-martingale criterion identifies the associated process with the prescribed SPDE. For the one-dimensional $Φ^4_1$ and convex Allen--Cahn-type Gibbs dynamics, we combine the established strong well-posedness theory with direct verification of the logarithmic derivatives, form closure, quasi-regularity and form--SPDE correspondence, and obtain relative-entropy decay bounds with exponents $2$ and $2(1-λ/m)$, respectively, with $m>λ$ in the latter case. Away from detailed balance, bounded skew-adjoint linear forcing preserves a Gaussian invariant law without requiring commutation between the forcing and covariance. We identify the antisymmetric action on cylinder observables and its Cameron--Martin current and prove that the squared current energy equals the steady-state entropy-production rate defined by forward--reverse path-space relative entropy per unit time, as well as the monotone limit of the Galerkin rates. Under commutation, we additionally obtain an explicit transient Onsager decomposition after a mass quench. Exclusion processes and Gaussian rotors provide finite-state and Gaussian benchmarks.

papers.title: Optimal Network Dependence in Distributed Stochastic Optimization via Tree Routing
papers.abstract: Communication is a central bottleneck in distributed optimization, but its effect is often summarized by the spectral gap of a chosen mixing matrix. Since this gap depends on link weights as well as topology, it can obscure the intrinsic effect of the network. We clarify this distinction by relating graph diameter to the inverse spectral gap. We establish a universal one-sided bound that is tight up to constant factors, while constructions across several graph families show that no topology-only converse or universal two-sided scaling law exists. This motivates a class-based view of network optimality: diameter-dependent guarantees can be assessed uniformly over graph classes, whereas spectral-gap optimality requires both the graph--matrix pair class and the admissible algorithm class to be specified. Based on the resulting diameter-based minimax benchmark, we introduce Tree-Routed Gradient Tracking (Tree-RGT), a distributed method for stochastic nonconvex optimization. The method pipelines model dissemination and gradient aggregation over a rooted shortest-path spanning tree. Each iteration uses one round of one-hop communication and one stochastic-gradient evaluation per agent, without inner consensus or multi-gossip. Under smoothness and unbiased bounded-variance oracles, Tree-RGT achieves uniformly optimal network dependence over connected graphs of prescribed size and diameter. It recovers centralized stochastic scaling after $\mathcal{O}(nD_{\mathcal{G}}^2)$ transient iterations, where $n$ is the number of agents and $D_{\mathcal{G}}$ is the graph diameter. This network-dependent transient-iteration bound improves upon or matches those reported for representative distributed methods. Thus, topology-aware routing attains diameter-optimal guarantees without relying on a prescribed mixing matrix.

papers.title: Optimal Deterministic First-Order Oracle Complexity for Nonconvex-Concave Minimax Optimization
papers.abstract: We study the deterministic first-order oracle complexity of smooth nonconvex-concave minimax optimization over a bounded convex dual domain under two notions of stationarity: optimization stationarity (OS) and game stationarity (GS). OS concerns stationarity of the value function, viewed as a structured nonsmooth objective obtained by maximizing over the dual variable. GS concerns the joint first-order optimality conditions for both primal minimization and dual maximization, each with the other variable held fixed. Existing upper bounds on the oracle complexity of first-order methods for finding $ε$-OS and $ε$-GS points have different dependence on $ε$, but whether this difference reflects an intrinsic separation in computational hardness remains unresolved. We resolve this question by establishing worst-case lower bounds for arbitrary deterministic first-order methods: $Ω(ε^{-3})$ oracle queries for finding an $ε$-OS point and $Ω(ε^{-5/2})$ for finding an $ε$-GS point, with the remaining problem parameters fixed. These bounds match existing upper bounds up to logarithmic factors. To close the remaining logarithmic gap, we introduce Tracked-FOAM, a new first-order algorithm whose oracle complexity matches our lower bounds for both OS and GS. Together, these results establish an intrinsic separation between OS and GS in the optimal accuracy dependence of deterministic first-order oracle complexity.

papers.title: Yang-Baxter permutation group actions on distributive Yang-Baxter algebras
papers.abstract: Let $(X,r)$ be a finite square-free distributive set-theoretic solution of the Yang-Baxter equation, and let $\mathcal{A}(X,r)$ be its associated Yang-Baxter algebra. We prove that $\mathcal{A}(X,r)$ is isomorphic to a skew polynomial algebra and explicitly compute its Nakayama automorphism. We study the natural faithful action of the permutation group $\mathcal{G}(X,r)$ on $\mathcal{A}(X,r)$ by graded algebra automorphisms. We characterize when $\mathcal{G}(X,r)$ is a reflection group and, in that case, describe the invariant subalgebra $\mathcal{A}(X,r)^{\mathcal{G}(X,r)}$ together with its Jacobian, reflection arrangement, and discriminant. We further establish a necessary and sufficient condition for the noncommutative Auslander theorem to hold for the permutation group action on a distributive Yang-Baxter algebra. Finally, for a class of non-trivial distributive Yang-Baxter algebras, we obtain a lower bound for the pertinency of the permutation group action.

papers.title: Jacobian estimates and geometric inequalities under intermediate Ricci curvature
papers.abstract: We prove a Jacobian estimate underlying both the Heintze--Karcher comparison and the Alexandrov--Bakelman--Pucci method for submanifolds of arbitrary codimension. The estimate retains the contributions of ambient curvature along geodesics emanating from the submanifold and requires no curvature sign assumption. As applications, we obtain a quantitative Fenchel--Willmore inequality with explicit curvature remainders under nonnegative $n$-intermediate Ricci curvature, Michael--Simon Sobolev and isoperimetric inequalities under nonnegative $(n-1)$-intermediate Ricci curvature, and corresponding extensions under quadratic curvature decay. In each result, the required intermediate Ricci curvature condition depends only on the dimension of the submanifold and is independent of its codimension.

papers.title: Moments Comparison Inequalities for Critical 2d Stochastic Heat Flow, Polymers and GMC
papers.abstract: We employ a Gaussian convex inequality developed in [AC15], [Che26], [Gue22], and [FUMPC26] to establish (one sided) moment comparison inequalities for Gaussian multiplicative chaos, directed polymers in Gaussian environment and, in particular, the Critical 2d Stochastic Heat Flow (SHF), including upper bounds on negative moments, as well as similar lower bounds for $p$-th moments with $p\in (0,1)$. For the Critical 2d SHF, averaged over small balls, we also obtain the matching (up to multiplicative constants) complementary bounds. We establish the complementary bounds using a bootstrap argument inspired by [DS10] and a geometric decomposition introduced in [GT26]. Specifically, we prove that for locally averaged SHF, for every $p\in\mathbb R$, the $p$-th moment is, up to multiplicative constants, bounded in both sides by the $\frac{p(p-1)}{2}$-th power of its second moment.

papers.title: Connected irregular cospectral graphs with distinct Lovász numbers
papers.abstract: For every integer $n \geq 11$, we construct connected, irregular, nonisomorphic graphs on $n$ vertices with equal adjacency, Laplacian, signless Laplacian, normalized Laplacian, and Seidel spectra and equal independence, clique, chromatic, complement chromatic, and maximum-cut numbers, but distinct Lovász $\vartheta$-numbers. We join each graph in a fixed cospectral, nonisomorphic regular pair on ten vertices, due to van Dam and Haemers (2003), with $K_{n-10}$. We prove that these joins preserve equality of the five spectra and stated integer-valued invariants, and leave the respective Lovász numbers unchanged. We derive exact expressions for these numbers and prove that they are distinct. We also determine the cardinality-constrained maximum-cut profiles of both base graphs and their complements, yielding exact formulas and equality of maximum-cut numbers for the joins of either the base graphs or their complements with $K_{n-10}$. For $n=10$, we present a regular pair satisfying all stated properties except irregularity, followed by a connected, irregular, nonisomorphic pair satisfying all properties. An exhaustive computer search finds no connected, irregular, nonisomorphic pair on at most nine vertices sharing the first four spectra and all stated integer-valued invariants. Thus, ten is the smallest possible order, and such pairs exist for every $n \geq 10$. This extends and strengthens Sason's (2024) result for \emph{even} $n \geq 14$, which used the neighbors splitting join operation and did not address Seidel matrices, complement chromatic numbers, or maximum-cut numbers of the graphs or joins of their complements. Thus, the Lovász number efficiently certifies nonisomorphism even when all five spectra and stated integer-valued invariants coincide.

papers.title: Classification of finite-dimensional Nichols algebras of rank two in twisted Yetter--Drinfeld categories
papers.abstract: Let \(G\) be a finite non-abelian group, let \(Φ\in Z^3(G,\mathbb C^\times)\) be normalized, and let \(V,W\) be finite-dimensional simple objects of \({}_G^G\mathcal{YD}^Φ\). We classify, up to interchange, the braided-indecomposable pairs \((V,W)\) whose supports generate \(G\) and for which \(\mathcal B(V\oplus W)\) is finite-dimensional. The classification consists of eight cases with five possible support quandles. In every case the Cartan graph is standard of type \(A_2\), \(B_2\), or \(G_2\), and the dimension is determined explicitly. A new phenomenon occurs {in the \(Γ_2\) case}: the twisted setting admits a family of type \(G_2\) absent from the ordinary \(Γ_2\) classification and we construct an explicit example over a non-abelian group of order \(16\).

papers.title: Primes are Complete for a Class of Cantor Spectral Pair
papers.abstract: We study the complete number problem for a class of self-similar spectral measures on the real line. We say that a real number $t$ is complete for a spectral pair $(μ,Λ)$ if $(μ,tΛ)$ is also a spectral pair. In this paper we consider the partial homogeneous Cantor measure $μ_{N^r,\mathcal D}$ and its canonical spectrum. Our main result fully characterizes all prime powers $p^n$ that are complete for $p>N$. In particular, we obtain a necessary and sufficient condition for an arbitrary prime $p$ to be complete. {We further establish a connection between the problem and certain Diophantine equations}, including the Nagell--Ljunggren equation, and obtain complete number results for a class of related models. As applications, known solutions of the Nagell--Ljunggren equation provide complete and incomplete prime-power examples.

papers.title: On The Rational Realization of Even-dimensional Spheres and Products of Eilenberg--MacLane Spaces as Classifying Spaces
papers.abstract: In this paper, we study the rational realization problem for the classifying space $B\mathrm{aut}_1(X)$. We prove that if $S^{2n}$ is realized as $B\mathrm{aut}_1(X)_{\mathbb{Q}}$ for a simply-connected space $X$, then $X$ is $π$-infinite and has vanishing rational Gottlieb elements above degree $2n-1$. In particular, even-dimensional spheres cannot be realized as $B\mathrm{aut}_1(X)_{\mathbb{Q}}$ for any simply-connected $π$-finite space $X$. We also prove that, for all $n\geq 2$ and $s,t\geq 1$, the product of Eilenberg--MacLane spaces $K(\mathbb{Q}^s,n)\times K(\mathbb{Q}^t,n+1)$ cannot be realized as $B\mathrm{aut}_1(X)_{\mathbb{Q}}$ for any simply-connected $π$-finite space $X$. Moreover, we prove that if $r\geq 2$, $n\geq 3$ and $K(\mathbb{Q}^r,n)$ is realized as $B\mathrm{aut}_1(X)_{\mathbb{Q}}$ for a simply-connected $π$-finite space $X$, then $X$ has the rational homotopy type of $K(\mathbb{Q}^r,n-1)$. The proofs are based on two structural results for Gottlieb elements in the derivation Lie algebra of a Sullivan minimal model, which provide a uniform method for these realization problems.

papers.title: Kronecker Products, Polarity Quotients and Large Graph Constructions
papers.abstract: In this paper, we establish a structural compatibility between the Kronecker product of bipartite graphs that admit polarity and their polarity quotients, and provide a sharp upper bound on the diameter of these graphs. We use these properties to construct new families of graphs, all of which have orders that asymptotically approach the Moore bound. We show that the bipartite compatibility graphs have a natural polarity, and that the corresponding polarity quotients comprise a new family of graphs of any even diameter $2k$ with degree $(q+1)^k$ for any prime power $q$, much smaller than those of other known families of that diameter and field order $q$. These families generalize the Erdős-Rényi-Brown polarity graphs. Kronecker products of these polarity quotients give another new family of graphs of any even diameter for every pair of prime powers $q,r$. Certain generalized polygons are known to admit polarity with polarity quotients approaching the Moore bound asymptotically. Kronecker products of these polarity quotients give another new family of graphs of diameters $2$, $3$ and $5$, including a diameter-$3$ degree-$18$ graph of order larger than any previously known for that degree and diameter.

papers.title: Information Percolation and cutoff for Potts Glauber Dynamics
papers.abstract: We prove cutoff with an $O(1)$ window for the continuous-time heat-bath Glauber dynamics of the ferromagnetic $q$-state Potts model on the discrete torus $Λ_n=(\mathbb Z/n\mathbb Z)^d$ at sufficiently high temperature. More precisely, for every fixed $d\ge2$ and $q\ge3$, there exists $β_0=β_0(d,q)>0$ such that, for $0<β<β_0$, the cutoff occurs in an optimal $O(1)$ window centered at \[ t_\star=t_\star^{(n)}:=\frac{1}{2\mathfrak{r}}\log |Λ_n|, \] where $\mathfrak{r}\in(0,1)$ is the exact exponential decay rate of the one-site color bias. Thus, the mixing time is determined up to an additive \(O(1)\). It is characterized by the time at which the macroscopic color-density bias from the monochromatic initial condition enters the scale of equilibrium fluctuations. Moreover, our proof shows that the monochromatic initial condition uniquely maximizes the color bias. This is the first implementation of information percolation to prove cutoff for a non-monotone spin system. On a transitive graph, information percolation naturally gives an upper bound on the mixing time of one half of the grand coupling time which is sharp for the Ising model. However, for many non-monotone systems including the Potts model, this misses additional averaging over the update histories giving an upper bound that is off by a constant multiplicate factor. We develop a new framework that treats the information percolation histories as random polymers and show how to average over them to give the effective bias from the initial condition. This accounts for all the additional mixing, recovering a sharp upper bound and cutoff. We believe this approach will be applicable in a much wider range of settings.

papers.title: A proof of the 3-Decomposition Conjecture
papers.abstract: We prove the 3-Decomposition Conjecture: every finite connected cubic loopless multigraph decomposes into a spanning tree, a 2-regular subgraph, and a matching. The proof rests on a new theorem on matching complements in subcubic graphs. Let H be a finite connected bridgeless simple graph of maximum degree three, and let S be its set of degree-two vertices, with |S| = k >= 2. We show that H has a matching of size equal to its cyclomatic number, |E(H)| - |V(H)| + 1, whose deletion leaves a single tree containing all of S, together with cycles disjoint from S. The proof is by induction on k.

papers.title: Measure rigidity for regular polynomial endomorphisms and applications
papers.abstract: We classify regular polynomial endomorphisms of $\mathbb C^k$ with the same equilibrium measure under some mild condition on the dynamics at infinity. In particular, for $f$ in a Zariski dense open subset of the parameter space and any $g$ of the same degree, $μ_g=μ_f$ if and only if $f=g$. We also establish finiteness results for maps with a prescribed equilibrium measure. Our approach rests on the stable manifold structure near the hyperplane at infinity. Applications include a Tits-type alternative, results on iterated centralizers, and an arithmetic non-density theorem.

papers.title: When Is Two-Stage Sample Robust Optimization Asymptotically Optimal? A Simple Perspective
papers.abstract: Two-stage sample robust optimization with linear decision rules is a standard data-driven approach to two-stage stochastic linear programs with unknown distributions. \cite{bertsimas2022two} established that this approach is asymptotically optimal under several conditions. Most conditions are mild, but one imposes a technical requirement on the recourse system. Whether this condition is implied by the others was left as an open question. We resolve this open question through a geometric feature of the support set: simpleness, the property that every vertex is incident to exactly as many edges as the dimension of the support. For simple support sets, the technical condition is automatic, and asymptotic optimality holds under the remaining standard assumptions. For every non-simple support, we construct a recourse system that is feasible everywhere in the support but violates the technical condition, and this construction resolves the open question. We further characterize the simpleness of one-sided and two-sided budgeted uncertainty sets and identify when budget perturbations can restore simpleness. We also develop a polynomial-time algorithm that certifies the technical condition at a given vertex using its incident edge directions. Numerical experiments on newsvendor and network lot-sizing problems illustrate the characterization and the effectiveness of the verification algorithm.

papers.title: Integral representations of quantum Rényi divergences on von Neumann algebras
papers.abstract: We prove an integral representation of the $α$-$z$ Rényi divergences for normal states on arbitrary von Neumann algebras. Along each ray $z=cα$, the divergence is a positive average of relative entropies evaluated in a canonical family of escort states. For orders $α$ above one, we require the divergence to be finite, whereas for orders below one support inclusion suffices. An explicit boundary correction removes the lower-order support assumption. The proof uses a compatible weighted Haagerup $L^p$ scale and applies outside the data-processing region. For faithful density matrices, we express the derivative of the escort relative entropy with respect to the Rényi order in terms of a nonnegative fluctuation quantity. Differences of order-one derivatives of the divergence give quantum Fisher information and Wigner-Yanase skew information. For faithful bipartite density matrices, we also express optimized conditional $α$-$z$ entropies at orders above one as averages of ordinary conditional entropies. Further applications concern coherent-state divergences in quantum field theory and the optimizing order for the strong converse exponent in hypothesis-testing.

papers.title: Central limit theorem in Rényi divergence for lattice random variables
papers.abstract: Let $\{X_i\}_{i=1}^n$ be independent, identically distributed lattice random variables with zero mean, unit variance, and maximal span $h>0$. Let $S_n=(X_1+\cdots+X_n)/\sqrt n$. Let $Z_n$ denote the quantization of a standard Gaussian random variable on the support lattice of $S_n$. We show that the Rényi divergence $D_α(S_n\|Z_n)$ of order $1<α<\infty$ tends to 0 as $n\to\infty$ if and only if $D_α(S_{n_0}\| Z_{n_0})<\infty$ for some integer $n_0$ and a sub-Gaussian condition holds. Furthermore, we derive an Edgeworth-type asymptotic expansion of the divergence to arbitrary order. We also show that the Rényi divergence $D_\infty(S_n\|Z_n)$ of infinite order tends to 0 as $n\to\infty$ if and only if a sub-Gaussian condition, a curvature condition, and a uniform separation condition hold. These results constitute lattice counterparts of Rényi entropic central limit theorems for continuous random variables obtained by Bobkov, Chistyakov and Götze (\emph{Ann. Probab.} \textbf{47} (2019), 270--323) and Bobkov and Götze (\emph{Ann. Probab.} \textbf{53} (2025), 453--477). Uniform separation is an additional assumption beyond the sub-Gaussian and curvature conditions used in the continuous setting. The failure of uniform separation may cause an exponentially tilted version of $X_1$ to concentrate on a sublattice of max span $kh$ for some integer $k>1$, which yields the lower bound $D_\infty(S_n\|Z_n)\ge\log k$, and hence a failure of the entropic central limit theorem.

papers.title: Optimizing bounds for energy-constrained optimal cooling problems in two dimensions
papers.abstract: We study optimal control problems for incompressible fluids in two-dimensional domains with a cold boundary and internal heat sources and sinks. Given a kinetic energy budget, measured by the square of a nondimensional Péclet number $\mathrm{Pe}$, the goal is to maximize a cooling efficiency inversely proportional to the mean square gradient of the fluid's temperature. Using Lagrange duality, we formulate a well-posed dual problem whose solution yields an upper bound on the maximum cooling efficiency $\mathcal{E}(\mathrm{Pe})$. We then numerically approximate the dual problem using a convergent hierarchy of semidefinite programs obtained via discretization. We illustrate this computational approach on optimal cooling problems in a square and in an annulus, explaining also how problem symmetries can be exploited to reduce computational complexity. Finally, we construct admissible points for the dual problem to obtain new analytical upper bounds on the optimal cooling efficiency $\mathcal{E}(\mathrm{Pe})$. Specifically, we prove that $\mathcal{E}(\mathrm{Pe}) \lesssim \mathrm{Pe}^{2}$ for arbitrary domains and heat distributions, and that $\mathcal{E}(\mathrm{Pe}) \lesssim \mathrm{Pe}^{2}/ \ln^2\mathrm{Pe}$ for cooling flows in disks and annuli with heat source/sink distributions with a uniformly positive azimuthal average. These results generalize and improve known efficiency bounds for energy-constrained cooling flows in a disk.

papers.title: Risk-Aware Unit Commitment in District Heating Networks: Chance-Constrained and CVaR Optimization Under Demand Uncertainty
papers.abstract: While district heating networks are a key component of the energy transition, their operational planning is challenging due to substantial uncertainty in heat demand. We study how unit-commitment schedules can account for this uncertainty and what reliability costs. By adapting chance-constrained programming (CC) and conditional value-at-risk (CVaR) optimization to the mixed-integer unit-commitment problem for district-heating networks, we can compute optimal unit-commitment schedules under demand uncertainty. We generate heat demand scenarios using a Bayesian model, which explicitly quantifies forecasting uncertainty and yields predictive distributions as input to the network optimization. To handle the inherent uncertainty in heat demand, we apply two stochastic optimization approaches that exploit this distribution: chance-constrained programming limits the probability of unmet demand, and in our scenario-based setting reduces to a deterministic MIP in which demand is replaced by an empirical quantile, while CVaR optimization penalizes severe shortfalls in the tail of the distribution. We evaluate the approaches both on real-world data from the Berlin district heating network and on a benchmark set of synthetic, realistically parameterized instances of varying sizes. The results show that the two methods are complementary: CC cheaply traces the high-reliability end of the cost--reliability trade-off and reveals the physical reliability limit of the network, whereas CVaR covers the low-cost, risk-tolerant regime at considerably higher computational effort.

papers.title: Eventual polynomiality and dualities of relative Ehrhart functions
papers.abstract: Classical Ehrhart theory measures the discrete capacity of a convex rational (or integral) polytope $P$ by counting the number of lattice points in the $t$-th dilate $tP$ of $P$. In this paper, we extend this paradigm by replacing a lattice point with a geometric object $Q$ of dimension at most $\dim P$. We show that the counting function $\mathrm{ehr}(P,Q;t)$ of such valid translations of $Q$ into $tP$ inherits eventual quasi-polynomiality (or eventual polynomiality) with leading term $\mathrm{vol}(P)t^d$, where $d = \dim P$. This result is naturally derived by induction on the dimension, based on the classical quasi-polynomiality (or polynomiality) of Ehrhart functions. Similarly, replacing $P$ with its relative interior $P^\circ$ defines $\mathrm{ehr}^\circ(P,Q;t)$, which is also shown to be an eventual quasi-polynomial (or eventual polynomial). Furthermore, we prove several formulas for relative Ehrhart functions under the condition that $P = kP_0$ and $Q = lQ_0$ for some integers $k$, $l > 0$, and polytopes $P_0$ and $Q_0$ with $\dim Q_0 > 0$ such that $Q_0$ is inscribed in $P_0$. In particular, we prove that under this condition, $\mathrm{ehr}(P,Q;-t) = (-1)^{d}\mathrm{ehr}^\circ (P,Q;t+ρ)$ $(t \gg 0)$ holds for some integer $ρ> 0$ if and only if $k \mid 2l$ via the classical Ehrhart--Macdonald reciprocity law. We also prove that under the same condition, $\mathrm{ehr}(P,Q;t) = \mathrm{ehr}^\circ (P,Q;t+σ)$ $(t \gg 0)$ holds for some integer $σ> 0$ if and only if $\mathrm{ehr}^\circ (P_0;\mathrm{codeg}\,P_0) = 1$ and $k \mid \mathrm{codeg}\,P_0$.

papers.title: A general paracontrolled ansatz for singular SPDEs
papers.abstract: We provide a general ansatz for the paracontrolled approach introduced by Gubinelli, Imkeller, Perkowski for treating singular SPDEs. The ansatz proposed covers a large class of equations. It is described via decorated trees that encode its coefficients and its stochastic data. The main novelty is the recursive definition of the paracontrolled stochastic iterated integrals that involve a well-chosen combinatorial set of words. The paralinearisation is performed via a lift of iterated paraproducts to modelled distributions. The main idea is to integrate localised iterated paraproducts in order to get a global object with a good regularity. We also provide a fixed point argument and the renormalised equation with this ansatz when one uses the preparation map formalism that encompasses the BPHZ renormalisation. The last main result is the convergence of the renormalised stochastic data via the BPHZ renormalisation using an adaptation of the spectral gap approach. One obtains in the end a general solution theory for parabolic singular SPDEs via the paracontrolled approach.

papers.title: Geometry of Unimodular Random Hyperbolic Polyhedra
papers.abstract: We develop a geometric and probabilistic theory of unimodular random infinite trivalent hyperbolic polyhedra in $\mathbb{H}^3$, allowing ordinary, ideal, and hyperideal vertices. Our results relate local dihedral geometry to global conformal type and random-walk behavior. A central role is played by a geometric characteristic $L_f(P)$, determined by the dihedral angles incident to a face $f$. We establish the unimodular Gauss-Bonnet identity $$ \mathbb E[L_f(P)]=2π-\fracπ{3}\mathbb E[deg(f)]. $$ Together with circle-pattern uniformization, this yields a sharp parabolic-hyperbolic dichotomy governed by the expected geometric characteristic. We also introduce polyhedral soficity and prove that admissible Benjamini-Schramm limits of finite trivalent hyperbolic polyhedra are parabolic. We further establish a quantitative Ring Lemma for regular circle patterns, providing degree-sensitive geometric control without assuming bounded degrees. Combined with unimodular probability methods, this estimate enables us to identify the Poisson boundary of the face random walk and establish positive linear hyperbolic speed. Our results extend the geometric-characteristic theory beyond ideal polyhedra, connecting three-dimensional geometry, unimodular Gauss-Bonnet theory, and stochastic boundary behavior.

papers.title: Geometric Properties of Higher Dimensional Solenoidal Attractors
papers.abstract: We study the skew product systems $T: \mathbb{S}^1\times\mathbb{R}^d \to \mathbb{S}^1 \times\mathbb{R}^d$, \begin{equation*} T(x,y)=(\ell x, A y+φ(x)), \end{equation*} where $\ell\geq 2,$ $A \in GL_d(\mathbb{R})$ with $ρ(A)<1$, and $φ\in C^r(\mathbb{S}^1, \mathbb{R}^d)$, with $r>(d+3)/2. We allow the fibers to have any dimension and $A$ to be non-conformal. We show that: when $|\det(A)|\ell<1$, for almost every $φ$, the Hausdorff dimension of the solenoid attractor and the SRB measure equal 1+ the affinity dimension; when $|\det(A)|\ell>1$, for almost every $φ$, the SRB measure is absolutely continuous. In the latter case we investigate the Sobolev regularity of the density of the SRB measure. We introduce a derivative dispersion condition, replacing the usual transversality condition.

papers.title: On the Realizability of Edge-Girth Sequences
papers.abstract: The edge-girth of an edge $e$ in a simple connected graph is the length of a shortest cycle containing $e$, with $g_e = \infty$ if no such cycle exists, and the edge-girth sequence of a graph is the nondecreasing sequence of the edge-girths of its edges. We characterize the sequences that are realizable as the edge-girth sequence of a simple connected graph. A constant sequence $(g^{(m)})$ with $g$ finite and $m \geq 1$ is realizable if and only if $m = g$ or $m \geq \lceil 3g/2 \rceil$. Otherwise, writing $S = S_0 \uplus (g^{(m)})$, where $g$ is the maximum value of $S$ and $m$ its multiplicity, we prove that $S$ is realizable if and only if $S_0$ is realizable and $m$ lies in an explicit set determined by $g$ and by the maximum diameters of the graphs realizing $S_0$, alone or extended by fewer than $g$ edges of edge-girth $g$. The proof rests on a chaining lemma, which turns a shortest cycle of a realization into a lower bound on the maximum diameter of the realizations of a shorter sequence.

papers.title: The stability landscape in wave-packet scattering: geometric rigidity and sharp Sobolev thresholds
papers.abstract: A central problem in harmonic analysis is to understand how frequency resolution constrains stability under nonlinear changes of coordinates. Motivated by Mallat's wavelet scattering theory, we establish a sharp resolution--robustness principle for nonlinear representations built from two-dimensional wave-packet systems, showing that the transverse geometry of the frequency channels determines the critical Sobolev regularity. Whenever the channels are thinner than in the wavelet regime, arbitrarily small smooth deformations can move high-frequency mass between adjacent channels, producing instability already at the level of the linear filter bank and the first scattering layer. We match this obstruction with scale-sharp commutator estimates propagated through the full scattering cascade, obtaining Lipschitz stability at the critical regularity threshold. Together, the results provide the first intrinsic deformation-stability theory for non-wavelet Euclidean scattering transforms and identify a microlocal transport mechanism governing robustness across nonlinear multiscale representations.

papers.title: The shifted symplectic geometry of derived higher groupoids
papers.abstract: The main goal of this work is to introduce derived Lie n-groupoids and their shifted symplectic structures. We further define shifted lagrangian structures and prove that their composition is well defined under suitable conditions. As an application, we show that our framework incorporates several reduction procedures at critical values, including: classical Hamiltonian reduction, group valued moment maps, Poisson Lie group valued moment maps and Mikami-Weinstein for proper symplectic groupoids.

papers.title: Stochastic stability of master--slave synchronization for a class of PDEs with Burgers-type nonlinearity
papers.abstract: Master--slave synchronization reconstructs the evolving state of a reference (or master) system by continuously correcting a second system, the slave, using observations of the master. In applications, the observations are often contaminated by noise, so the corrections injected into the slave are themselves uncertain. In this paper we aim at quantifying the effect of noisy observations on master--slave synchronization for a family of evolution equations that combine a quadratic transport term with a polynomial linear differential operator. The family includes the Burgers, Kuramoto--Sivashinsky, Kawahara, Benney--Lin and Nikolaevskiy equations, among others. Under periodic boundary conditions, a Fourier--Galerkin approximation of order $K$ yields a finite-dimensional master--slave system in which white observation noise of intensity $σ$ is modeled through an Itô stochastic differential equation. In this framework, we first establish local exponential stability of noiseless synchronization for sufficiently strong scalar coupling. Then we compare the stochastic synchronization error with its noiseless counterpart resulting from the same initial slave state, isolating in this way the effect of noise. Assuming bounded reference paths, the mean-square deviation between the noiseless and noisy synchronization errors is $\mathcal O(σ^2)$ on finite time intervals. Under additional regularity assumptions, we also bound the error between the finite-resolution stochastic slave model and the infinite-dimensional deterministic master field, explicitly separating spectral approximation error, deterministic synchronization error and observation noise. Numerical experiments for the Kawahara and Nikolaevskiy equations confirm the predicted noise scaling.

papers.title: Some homotopy coherent finite group actions on spheres
papers.abstract: We provide some examples of homotopy coherent smooth finite group actions on spheres which do not arise from strict actions.

papers.title: Quartic Fourier-Laplace limits for $(p,q)$-Rogers-Szegő polynomials
papers.abstract: We prove asymptotic formulae for $(p,q)$-Rogers--Szegő polynomials with positive real parameters when the leading quadratic term in the logarithmic expansion about the middle coefficient vanishes. For coefficient indices whose distance from $n/2$ is of order $n^{3/4}$, the coefficient ratios have a quadratic--quartic exponential limit. A uniform bound valid for all indices allows the ratios to be summed and gives locally uniform convergence of the centred and normalised generating polynomials to a Fourier--Laplace integral. We also obtain an asymptotic formula for the sum of the coefficients, convergence of all rescaled moments, weak convergence of the normalised coefficient measures, and convergence with multiplicity of the zeros near $w=1$ for which $n^{3/4}\log w$ remains bounded.

papers.title: On $(p,q)$-binomial coefficient ratios for complex parameters
papers.abstract: We prove local asymptotics for near-central complex $(p,q)$-binomial coefficient modulus ratios allowing an imaginary parameter perturbation of order $n^{-3/4}$ at a $\sqrt{n}$ length scale from the centre. Moreover, we obtain ratio asymptotics for a smaller imaginary perturbation of order $n^{-5/4}$ at the length scale $n^{3/4}$. These results were obtained by reducing the two-parameter coefficients to just one parameter, giving a branch-free logarithmic representation of the second-order ratio and, hence, uniform complex curvature asymptotics for near-central ratios.

papers.title: Robustness Verification of an Autonomous Underwater Vehicle-based Plankton Classifier
papers.abstract: The assessment of planktonic standing stocks and microorganism structures is critical for understanding upper ocean biological processes. Currently, autonomous underwater vehicles (AUVs) equipped with in-situ optical imaging and artificial intelligence (AI) methods offer a promising solution for persistent surveillance, mapping and monitoring of planktonic life. However, current AI methods often lack robustness in dynamic, unstructured environments, where environmental noise and non-biological artifacts lead to frequent misclassifications. Standard convolutional neural network (CNN) classifiers often struggle with such conditions, leading to misclassifications that require time-consuming manual validation by marine biologists. To address this issue, we propose a novel robustness verification framework for in-situ plankton classifiers based on reachability analysis. We also introduce a continuous-time neural ordinary differential equation (neural ODE) classification model leveraging the high-resolution imaging capabilities of the SilCam particle imager. In this paper, we demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed framework by formally verifying the robustness of the neural ODE model against environmental perturbations. We demonstrate that our verification framework acts as an automated filter providing formal guarantees of model stability against ambiguous data, thereby improving the reliability of autonomous sampling and reducing the post-processing workload.

papers.title: Dissipativity properties of a class of nonlinear time-delay systems via Bessel-Legendre inequalities
papers.abstract: Time delays are inherent in many physical and engineered systems and can significantly affect their stability and performance. In this work, we investigate the dissipativity of a class of nonlinear time-delay systems with multiple discrete delays and derive sufficient conditions for both delay-dependent and delay-independent dissipativity using Bessel-Legendre inequalities. For linear systems, the resulting dissipativity conditions are expressed in terms of linear matrix inequalities (LMIs) which can be solved numerically to obtain Lyapunov-Krasovskii-type storage functions.

papers.title: LLM-Guided Transportation Hub Capacity Planning with Textual Business Inputs
papers.abstract: While traditional hub capacity planning models optimize effectively for quantitative inputs, they often fail to digest qualitative business context. We propose a novel framework where a large language model (LLM) agent iteratively proposes hub capacity decisions guided by natural-language business context descriptions. The key mechanism is a chain-of-thought reasoning protocol: the LLM constructs a structured decision table that maps each contextual item to specific capacity adjustments based on the implied direction and magnitude of changes. The new capacity decision is then validated through a feedback loop with an optimization model, which provides routing-based performance metrics to guide the agent's selection. On a real-world 13-hub freight network in the southeastern US, our framework achieves a 2.8% optimality gap relative to the hidden ground-truth, a significant improvement over the 11.0% gap produced by the traditional optimization model without textual business inputs. This demonstrates that LLMs can serve as a contextual bridge, integrating qualitative business insights into Operations Research workflows.

papers.title: Hilbert transforms on graph products of finite von Neumann algebras
papers.abstract: We study Hilbert transforms on graph products of finite von Neumann algebras, with particular interest in their boundedness on the associated noncommutative $L_p$-spaces for $1<p<\infty$. We establish a generalized Cotlar identity for Hilbert transforms, valid on operators whose lengths exceed a constant depending only on the underlying graph. We further prove that graph products of finite von Neumann algebras satisfying a Haagerup-type inequality admit $L_p$-bounded Hilbert transforms, therefore extending the corresponding result of Mei and Ricard for free products of finite von Neumann algebras. In addition, we obtain several equivalent characterizations of this Haagerup-type inequality. Our results apply, in particular, to graph products of finite groups, right-angled Hecke von Neumann algebras, and graph products of finite quantum groups. As an application, we provide a complete characterization of a compactness problem posed by Ozawa for graph products of finite groups and right-angled Hecke von Neumann algebras.

papers.title: Convergence of Large-Stepsize SGD for the Cross-entropy Loss via Stochastic Lyapunov Stability
papers.abstract: Modern deep learning has been shown to operate using learning rates far larger than those justified by classical optimization theory. Most prior analyses of this phenomenon focus on deterministic gradient descent, leaving the stochastic setting largely unexplored. In this work, we provide sharp convergence guarantees for Stochastic Gradient Descent (SGD) applied to the multiclass cross-entropy loss, for both linear classifiers and two-layer neural networks. We show that the stochasticity of SGD may cause the dynamics to alternate between an edge-of-stability regime that is dominated by curvature-driven oscillations, and a stable regime in which the expected loss decreases at a controlled rate. Despite that, we prove that SGD stabilizes the dynamics, ensuring that the iterates return to stability in a fixed number of iterations and allowing convergence in the best-iterate sense even with large learning rates. Experiments validate our theoretical findings and illustrate the benefits of SGD in the large-stepsize regime.

papers.title: An infinity-categorical TQFT from instantons
papers.abstract: In this paper, we lift the instanton TQFT from ordinary categories to the $\infty$-categorical setting by constructing a functor $CI:\mathrm{BI}^{\partial}\longrightarrow\mathsf{D}$ from an $\infty$-cobordism category $\mathrm{BI}^{\partial}$ for instantons to an $\infty$-derived category $\mathsf{D}$ of $2$-periodic chain complexes. The construction of $\mathrm{BI}^{\partial}$ is a modification of the $\infty$-cobordism category $\mathrm{Bord}_4$ introduced by Lurie and by Calaque--Scheimbauer using complete Segal spaces. The target $\infty$-category $\mathsf{D}$ is obtained via the dg nerve of the dg category of $2$-periodic chain complexes of finitely presented projective $\mathbb{Z}$-modules. The information encoded by the functor $CI$ was already developed by Kronheimer--Mrowka using families of metrics on cobordisms. Our reinterpretation in terms of $\infty$-categories conceptually simplifies the construction of the hypercube complexes underlying the link spectral sequence. This viewpoint also clarifies hyperbox complexes and compression in Manolescu--Ozsváth's work, and possible $A_\infty$-structures, especially their signs and higher coherence. In addition, we lift the generalized cap product $μ$-operators in instanton Floer homology to the chain level and construct explicit homotopies and higher homotopies establishing the commutativity of multiple $μ$-operators in even degrees.

papers.title: Spectral deferred corrections parallelized across the method for differential-algebraic equations
papers.abstract: In this work, the performance of different spectral deferred corrections (SDC) methods applied to initial value problems for differential-algebraic equations (DAEs) of index one is analyzed. The SDC method solves a series of correction equations, and after each iteration, the numerical solution is corrected by adding the obtained approximation of the error. The formulation of the SDC method allows for a parallelization across the method to obtain small-scale parallelism, for which a number of processes equal to the number of collocation nodes can be used. Recently, an analytical approach to finding optimal diagonal coefficients for parallel SDC was proposed. So far, no analysis with the new coefficients for parallel SDC applied to DAEs was done. We demonstrate that parallel SDC methods solve DAE problems with high accuracy faster than the associated sequential SDC schemes, obtaining speedup in a small-scale parallel regime.

papers.title: On Automorphism Groups of (1,2)-Surfaces
papers.abstract: Let $S$ be a minimal surface of general type with $K_S^2=1$ and $p_g(S)=2$, called a $(1,2)$-surface. We give a geometric recovery and refinement of D. Wen's bound $|\mathrm{Aut}(S)|\leq 200$ using the canonical genus-two fibration and the double-cover model over the Hirzebruch surface $Σ_2$. Computing $\mathrm{Aut}(Σ_2)$ from its Cox ring separates the action on the base $\mathbb{P}^1$ from the vertical kernel. If $\overline K_0$ denotes the vertical image on $Σ_2$, then $\overline K_0$ is cyclic of order $5$, $4$, $2$, or $1$, and we prove the respective sharp bounds $|\mathrm{Aut}(S)|\leq 200, 192, 48, 80$. The proof combines singularity indices of genus-two fibrations with invariant divisors arising from the branch equation. We also construct admissible branch divisors attaining all four bounds and show that their full automorphism groups are, respectively, $(C_{10}\times C_{10})\rtimes C_2$, $(BO_{48}\times C_8)/\langle(-I,J^4)\rangle$, $(BT_{24}\times C_4)/\langle(-I,J^2)\rangle$, and $C_{40}\times C_2$. Here $BO_{48}$ and $BT_{24}$ denote the binary octahedral and binary tetrahedral groups, respectively, and $J$ denotes a generator of the corresponding cyclic factor.

papers.title: Matrix-analytic methods for $M/M_D/c$ queues with Marshall--Olkin dependent servers
papers.abstract: We study multiserver queues with Marshall--Olkin dependent service mechanisms, heterogeneous servers, and fixed idle-set assignment. An explicit matrix-analytic solution links the stationary queue distribution to departure and customer-delay laws. Waiting time conditional on delay is exactly exponential, and the stationary \chg{sojourn law has a phase-type representation with at most one more phase than the number of servers.} A consistency condition characterizes when Markovian completions admit a Poisson shock representation. For two three-server families with identical bivariate residual-service laws, we prove a conditional waiting-time ordering and identify when their unconditional waiting tails cross. The results show how higher-order dependence affects performance beyond marginal rates and pairwise service dependence.

papers.title: Sharp coefficient, logarithmic and Schwarzian estimates for $α$-convex functions on the real line
papers.abstract: The class $M_α$ of $α$-convex functions, introduced by Mocanu in 1969, interpolates between starlike ($α=0$) and convex ($α=1$) mappings and has traditionally been studied only for $α\geq0$. We show that several of its sharp invariant estimates in fact extend to the entire real line. Our main result characterizes $M_α$ for every real $α\neq0$ through an explicit pointwise inequality, generalizing a theorem of Chuaqui, Duren and Osgood from the convex case, and we determine the sharp value of $β$ for which $M_α\subset C_β$ when $α\geq1$; we also show that the reciprocal inclusion $C_β\subset M_α$ fails for every $α>1$. Building on this, we obtain a sharp Fekete--Szegő inequality, valid for every $α\notin\{0,-1,-1/2\}$, and sharp bounds for the first two logarithmic coefficients of $M_α$, which recover the classical values for starlike and convex functions as special cases. We also determine the order of $M_α$, establish a piecewise sharp bound for its Schwarzian norm together with an explicit quasiconformal extension criterion via the Ahlfors--Weill theorem, and compute the Schwarzian norm of the $α$-Koebe function explicitly for $α=1/n$, $n\in\mathbb N$, verified for $n\leq9$ and numerically supported for $n<50$, leading to a conjecture for the general case. Finally, we propose a conjectural sharp bound for the second Hankel determinant of $M_α$, consistent with the known values $1$ and $1/8$ for the starlike and convex subclasses.

papers.title: Online Feedback Optimization for Constrained Stochastic Problems with Decision-Dependent Distributions
papers.abstract: Online feedback optimization (OFO) leverages real-time output measurements to optimize the operation of networked systems without requiring full knowledge of system dynamics or disturbances. We develop an OFO approach for constrained stochastic optimization problems in which the distribution of the system's random parameters shifts in response to the control actions. We propose a projected primal-dual algorithm where the true dual constraint sets are replaced by surrogate sets. Our main result is an upper bound on the mean-square tracking error, which decomposes into four interpretable terms reflecting: (i) the stochasticity of the problem, (ii) output measurement errors, (iii) time-variability of the problem, and (iv) the mismatch between surrogate and true dual constraint sets. The theory is illustrated in a numerical experiment for power grids with price-responsive assets.

papers.title: PDECheck: A Diagnostic Software Suite for Auditing Learned PDE Simulators
papers.abstract: PDECheck audits learned PDE simulators through callable propagators or saved predictions. It evaluates relative $L^2$ error, temporal composition, finite-difference generators, and equation-specific physical residuals, retaining horizons and missing prerequisites. Analytic and manufactured defects verify the kernels. A heat-equation sweep quantifies generator sensitivity to timestep, frequency, grid, and precision. A three-equation, five-seed FNO study compares supervised, PINO-style, and composition-regularized training. An accuracy-matched advection comparison has state errors below 0.3% and a semigroup-error ratio of 1.48 (95% interval 1.34-1.62). The composition penalty lowers semigroup error but increases composed-state and longer-rollout prediction error. A time-reparameterization check produces identical low-error endpoints with different compositions. Applications to five external equation families exercise the readers and physical contracts on coarse grids. The release includes reproducibility artifacts and measured CPU/CUDA costs.

papers.title: The Weyl-orbit embedding and a representation-theoretic characterization of the Clifford hierarchy
papers.abstract: Bu, Gu, and Jaffe introduced the quantum uniformity measures to analytically characterize the Clifford hierarchy. We prove that the quantum uniformity measures are the pullbacks of the matrix-valued uniformity functionals of Gowers and Hatami under the map $U\mapsto(a\mapsto W_aUW_a^*)$, which we call the Weyl-orbit embedding. We study the structure of the Weyl-orbit embedding, and among other results, establish a canonical decomposition of the ambient matrix-valued uniformity space into uniformity preserving twisted copies of the quantum uniformity space. The Weyl-orbit embedding identifies the Clifford hierarchy with Leibman polynomial maps. This identification yields a representation theoretic characterization of the Clifford hierarchy in terms of unitary representations of the universal polynomial groups introduced by the first author and Thom.

papers.title: A coupled finite element formulation for chemo-mechano-thermodynamical contact and its application to bonding and debonding
papers.abstract: This work presents a finite element formulation for coupled chemo-mechano-thermodynamical large deformation contact. The formulation is based on the contact theory of Sauer et al. (2022) that contains six coupled (but separate) fields: the deformation and temperature of the two contacting bodies, as well as an interfacial bonding field and interfacial temperature. The latter is governed by the chemical and mechanical energy dissipation at the interface. Here the focus is placed on the evolution of bonding and debonding, and how it is coupled to the mechanical and thermal contact state. Several elementary models are proposed for this based on a quadratic contact potential. The resulting contact formulation becomes very general and versatile, which is illustrated by several challenging examples. They include pressure- and gap- dependent bonding, exothermic bonding reactions, thermal hardening and thermal expansion, as well as simultaneous bonding and debonding. They are based on a monolithic finite element implementation using classical and isogeometric shape functions together with implicit time integration. Its full linearization, required for the Newton-Raphson solution method, is also provided for the six-field problem, as well as for several of its simplifications. If bonding sites are material points, the bonding variable can be condensed-out locally.

papers.title: Homogeneous spaces with transcendental Brauer--Manin obstruction to the Hasse principle
papers.abstract: Over any number field with sufficiently many roots of unity, we construct homogeneous spaces of $\mathbf{SL}_n$ with finite geometric stabilizers of nilpotency class $2$, whose unramified algebraic Brauer group consists only of constant classes, and which has no rational point but has local points in every completion of the ground field. This provides the first known examples of failures of the Hasse principle for homogeneous spaces of connected linear algebraic groups that are detected only by transcendental Brauer classes. The construction builds on the failure of a global--local principle for cup-product decomposition, based on a previous idea of Borovoi and Kunyavskii.

papers.title: The computable functional calculus
papers.abstract: We show that the continuous functional calculus is computable. As consequences we obtain the computable compactness of the spectrum of any computable normal element of a computably presented $\mathrm{C}^*$-algebra, the existence of effective approximate units for computably presented $\mathrm{C}^*$-algebras, and an effective version of the Spectral Theorem for compact operators on separable Hilbert spaces.

papers.title: Weak rank rigidity for groups with a navigable path system
papers.abstract: We show that groups with a mild form of non-positive curvature (a navigable path system) satisfy the weak rank rigidity conjecture: they either have linear divergence or a Morse element. This class includes discrete groups of projective automorphisms of open convex cones, Helly groups (answering a question of Genevois), Coxeter groups, weak Garside groups (in particular Deligne's groups and fundamental groups of Salvetti complexes of oriented matroids), hierarchically hyperbolic groups, and other examples. Along the way, we show that those groups satisfy the Morse local-to-global property, providing a unified proof for the whole class. In the metric setting, the same condition of non-positive curvature allows to provide a local definition (that is, in a sense, optimal) of rank one/Morse geodesics, mirroring the one using parallel Jacobi fields from Riemannian geometry; to deduce linearity of divergence from linearity on a sequence; to obtain new cases in which Morse geodesics are strongly contracting. The main new tool introduced is the generalised contraction space, a hyperbolic space that encodes the negative curvature of a given space.

papers.title: Solutions for Hecke Sum Questions of Banerjee and Bringmann
papers.abstract: We previously conjectured a Hecke-type identity for a series arising from two-color partitions. Banerjee and Bringmann proved the conjecture using modular methods and asked for a direct proof using Bailey pairs. They also suggested investigating the odd part of the series. We answer both questions by applying Bailey's transform to a Bailey pair of Andrews and a conjugate Bailey pair of Lovejoy. Our main theorem gives formulas for the even and odd parts of a series $P_a(q)$ depending on a parameter $a$. The specialization $a=1$ gives the conjectured formula and a companion formula for the odd part.

papers.title: Classification of Double Saddle-Point Systems
papers.abstract: We offer a classification of a broad and practically relevant class of symmetric double saddle-point system. At the core of the paper is the division of the associated matrices into ``block-arrow'' and ``block-tridiagonal'' forms. We describe relevant applications, invertibility conditions, spectral properties, and block preconditioners. Our discussion is kept within a general framework rather than tailored to specific applications.

papers.title: A min-max gap characterization of minimal foliations on the torus
papers.abstract: We extend an energy introduced by Mather to the setting of Almgren-Pitts min-max theory and obtain a parametric, higher-dimensional analogue of Mather's variational barrier theory for twist maps and geodesics on tori. We use this energy to establish several criteria for the existence of foliations of the $n$-torus by minimal hypersurfaces. We show that for a generic metric, whenever a lamination by area-minimizing hypersurfaces of the $n$-torus contains a gap, there exists a minimal hypersurface inside the gap that is not area-minimizing. This hypersurface is a higher-dimensional analogue of the secondary minimax orbit appearing in Aubry-Mather theory.

papers.title: On $4$-perfect-matching covers of cubic graphs with two adjacent odd circuits in a $2$-factor
papers.abstract: Let $G$ be a cubic graph admitting a $2$-factor consisting of exactly two odd circuits, and let the complementary $1$-factor contain precisely three spokes (along with an arbitrary number of chords). We show that four perfect matchings can cover $G$. As a consequence, $G$ fulfils the $7/5$-Conjecture of Alon and Tarsi.

papers.title: On weighted extremal Kähler metrics
papers.abstract: The notion of weighted extremal Kähler metrics extends the classical notion of Calabi's extremal Kähler metrics, but includes many well-studied objects in Kähler geometry such as Kähler-Ricci solitons and Sasaki-Einstein metrics. In this paper, after explaining how this notion grew out, we will try to survey recent works concerning the YTD conjecture on weighted extremal Kähler metrics.

papers.title: Non-abelian extensions of Hom-Jacobi-Jordan algebras
papers.abstract: This paper develops a cohomology theory for Hom-Jacobi-Jordan algebras using and applies it to classify non-abelian extensions. The main result establishes that equivalence classes of split extensions of a Hom-Jacobi-Jordan algebra $J$ by $V$ are in bijection with the second cohomology group $H^2(J,V)$, generalizing classical results from Lie and Leibniz algebra theory. We characterize extensions explicitly through 2-cocycles $(ρ, θ)$ satisfying compatibility conditions, and provide complete classifications of low-dimensional cases.

papers.title: Fixed-point-free automorphisms of solvable Lie algebras
papers.abstract: In this paper, we investigate the existence of fixed-point-free automorphisms for finite-dimensional Lie algebras. By a result of Jacobson, a Lie algebra admitting a fixed-point-free automorphism is solvable. We prove that such a Lie algebra must be even strongly unimodular. We find a necessary and sufficient criterion such that a complex almost abelian Lie algebra admits a fixed-point-free automorphism. For complex filiform Lie algebras we show that the existence of a fixed-point-free automorphism is equivalent to not being characteristically nilpotent.

papers.title: Thermodynamic formalism for singular flows
papers.abstract: We prove that $C^\infty$ smooth three-dimensional flows with positive topological entropy admit only finitely many ergodic measures of maximal entropy, even in the presence of singularities (zero-velocity points). Furthermore, for flows in a $C^\infty$-open and dense subset of the space of such three-dimensional flows, every ergodic measure of maximal entropy is rapidly mixing. To prove this result, we construct a novel symbolic coding framework for singular flows, which serves as the fundamental technical tool. We then introduce the property of strong positive recurrence (SPR) for singular flows, and prove that SPR flows can be coded by suspension flows over SPR countable discrete symbolic systems. Under appropriate conditions, we further establish that such suspension flows are rapidly mixing. These frameworks can be further generalized to a broad class of flows, including star flows, and the results naturally extend to general equilibrium states.

papers.title: Semi-discrete approximation of Mañé, Aubry and Mather sets
papers.abstract: We study a variational discretization in time of Aubry--Mather theory for Tonelli Lagrangians on the flat torus. We define discrete Mañé, Aubry and Mather sets, establish their compactness and inclusion properties, and investigate their convergence as the time step tends to zero. We prove upper-limit results for the Mañé sets and, when the continuous Aubry set has finitely many static classes, for the Aubry sets. We obtain full Kuratowski and Hausdorff convergence of the Aubry sets when this set is a single equilibrium or periodic orbit, and, under additional assumptions, a finite union of equilibria. Every weak limit of discrete Mather measures is a continuous Mather measure. For equilibrium Aubry sets, we give sufficient conditions for exact preservation of Mather sets and measure families at small time steps. A mechanical example illustrates these results and exhibits exact preservation of the Aubry set as well.

papers.title: On nonnegative solutions of the differential inequality $Δ_pu+ Δ_q u+V(x)u^s\leq 0$ on Riemannian manifolds
papers.abstract: In this paper, we are concerned with differential inequalities with $(p,q)$-Laplacian operator on Riemannian manifolds. Using a test function argument, we establish Liouville-type theorems under the manifold's geometry and the potential's behavior at infinity. Finally, we give an example showing the sharpness when $V(x)$ is a positive constant.

papers.title: Signless Laplacian spectral radius of simplicial complexes without $r$-dimensional wheels
papers.abstract: An $r$-dimensional wheel is defined as the join of an $(r-2)$-simplex and a cycle. In this paper, we study the maximum signless Laplacian spectral radius of $n$-vertex $r$-dimensional pure simplicial complexes that contain no $r$-dimensional wheels. For sufficiently large $n$, we determine the extremal complexes that attain this maximum. Our result generalizes the corresponding extremal results of signless Laplacian on graphs and provides a spectral anlogue of a theorem of Brown, Erdős and Sós on the maximum number of facets of simplicial complexes in the case $r=2$.

papers.title: Approximation of structures:local and global
papers.abstract: We provide a mathematically rigorous definition of local approximation and demonstrate its applicability to some interesting classes of structures. In particular, we prove that any compact simple Lie group is locally approximated by finite groups. The definition and main examples are motivated by physics but the techniques are of model theory. Namely, we introduce the ultraproduct of emerging metric structures, which generalises the ultraproduct in metric model theory.

papers.title: Prime Density, Kolmogorov Quotients and Homeomorphisms between Macías Spaces of Integral Domains
papers.abstract: For an integral domain $R$ that is not a field, the Macías space $M(R)$ is the set $R^0=R\setminus\{0\}$ endowed with the topology generated by the subsets $σ_k^0=\{x\in R^0:\langle x\rangle+\langle k\rangle=R\}$ for $k\in R^0$. We show that the unit group is open in $M(R)$ precisely when $R$ is not semiprimitive, and characterize semiprimitive Dedekind domains and unique factorization domains (UFDs) by means of the density of their irreducible and prime elements, respectively. We describe the Kolmogorov quotient of $M(R)$ in terms of the maximal ideals of $R$, and reduce the homeomorphism problem to these quotients and the cardinalities of the fibers of the quotient maps. Consequently, two local domains have homeomorphic Macías spaces if and only if they have the same cardinality. We characterize the pairs of Dedekind domains with homeomorphic Macías spaces in terms of the cardinalities of their unit groups and the relations among the ideal classes of their maximal ideals; in particular, two Dedekind domains with torsion class groups, such as principal ideal domains (PIDs), have homeomorphic Macías spaces if and only if their unit groups have the same cardinality and so do their sets of maximal ideals. This characterization addresses, for countably infinite semiprimitive PIDs, the homeomorphism problem raised by Macías in 2024. Under an additional hypothesis, UFDs admit an analogous characterization in terms of comaximality with prime elements. Finally, for a class of domains of characteristic zero, we characterize additive homeomorphisms between Macías spaces in terms of isomorphisms of the underlying rings, partially answering a problem raised by Macías and Ortiz in 2024.

papers.title: Capillary John ellipsoid theorem with applications to capillary curvature problems
papers.abstract: In this paper, we apply a capillary John ellipsoid theorem for capillary convex bodies in the Euclidean half-space $\overline{\mathbb{R}^{n+1}_{+}}$. This theorem yields a non-collapsing estimate for capillary hypersurfaces, which provides a new approach to obtaining $C^{0}$ estimates for solutions to some capillary curvature problems (including the capillary $L_{p}$ Christoffel-Minkowski problem and the capillary $L_{p}$ curvature problem), based on the corresponding gradient estimates. As an application, we study the capillary $L_{p}$ dual Minkowski problem. A gradient estimate, together with the non-collapsing estimate and a $C^2$ estimate, yields existence for every $1<p<q<\infty$ with positive smooth even data and an acute contact angle. The same estimates also yield the eigenvalue problem for $p=q>1$, with uniqueness up to dilation. We further obtain existence and uniqueness for $p>q$ without an upper restriction on $q$.

papers.title: On Stanley-Reisner Rings with Minimal Betti Numbers
papers.abstract: We study simplicial complexes with a given number of vertices whose Stanley-Reisner ring has the minimal sum of Betti numbers. We prove that every full subcomplex of them is homotopy equivalent either to a point or to a sphere. Moreover, we prove that such kind of simplicial complexes coincide with those having minimal Taylor resolutions.

papers.title: Poly-Bernoulli numbers from shifted log-sine integrals
papers.abstract: In 1999, Arakawa and Kaneko introduced a zeta function connecting multiple zeta values with poly-Bernoulli numbers through its special values. Log-sine integrals are also known to be related to zeta values at positive integers. In this article, we study the values of a shifted log-sine integral at negative integers and establish a connection with anti-diagonal sums of poly-Bernoulli numbers.
