We show that, for every $\varepsilon>0$, every sufficiently large prime $p$, and every $A\subseteq\mathbb{F}_p^D$ of density $α$, there exists a nonzero $d\in\mathbb{F}_p$ such that \[ \mathbb{E}_{\underline{x}\in\mathbb{F}_p^D} \mathbf{1}_A(\underline{x}) \prod_{\substack{1\leq i\leq k\\ ω_i=1}} \mathbf{1}_A\bigl(\underline{x}+P_i(d)v_i\bigr) \geq α^{\,1+\sum_{i=1}^kω_i}-\varepsilon \] simultaneously for every $ω\in\{0,1\}^k$. The main new ingredient is a directional arithmetic regularity decomposition adapted to mixed directional box norms.

papers.title: Finite time implosions of the multidimensional compressible Euler equations with a finite far-field cutoff
papers.abstract: We study the problem of finite time singularities in the isentropic compressible Euler equations in multiple dimensions with radial symmetry. Our initial data consists of the radially symmetric Kidder self-similar implosion with a continuous constant density cutoff. Motivated by our recent work on the one-dimensional problem, we present high-resolution radially symmetric adaptive mesh refinement simulations that when combined with asymptotic similarity solution analysis present a full picture of the ensuing dynamics of the implosion. From the cutoff point in the initial data, an expanding wave emerges. The endpoints of the wave follow the "imploding" and "exploding" characteristic speeds associated with the system of hyperbolic conservation laws. This wave has much more complex structure than the exact non-centered rarefaction wave that emerges in the one-dimensional problem. As in the one-dimensional case, the inner Kidder solution is swallowed up by the expanding wave as time approaches the singularity time. However, unlike the one-dimensional case, a blowup occurs along the point where the `imploding' side of the expanding wave attaches to the Kidder solution. This composite blowup has an asymptotic self-similar form that has an interpretation in terms of the Gurderley-type self-similarity structure. The numerical method for the PDE necessitates a Lagrangian scheme to avoid the numerical diffusion inherent in Eulerian methods. We use a leapfrog method coupled to recursive refinement of the mesh near the blowup, which allows for very high resolution simulations, resolving many orders of magnitude of the self-similar blowup. Consistent with prior rigorous results for these equations, the blowup does not involve mass concentration and exhibits a critical $L^p$ space for the concentration of the density, depending on the dimension of space.

papers.title: Scattering of plane waves and a modified Pompeiu criterion
papers.abstract: In this paper we prove that plane waves always scatter from bounded, strictly convex planar inhomogeneities with constant material parameters. Our approach involves the introduction of a modified Pompeiu property, whose failure corresponds to the vanishing of the Fourier transform of the indicator function of the inhomogeneity on a complexified circle not centered at the origin. We then show that such vanishing is impossible for bounded, strictly convex planar sets.

papers.title: Covering lemmas associated to maximal operators of weak type
papers.abstract: Building on the work of A. Córdoba and R. Fefferman, we provide a necessary and sufficient covering condition on a basis $\mathcal{B}$ on a separable metric space $X$ with a Borel measure $μ$ so that the associated \mbox{geometric} maximal operator $M_\mathcal{B}$ satisfies for all $α> 0$ the weak type estimate $$μ\left(\left\{x \in X : M_\mathcal{B}f(x) > α\right\}\right) \leq \int_{X}Φ\left( γ_\mathcal{B} \left|\frac{f}α\right|\right)\,dμ\;,$$ where $Φ: [0, \infty) \rightarrow [0, \infty)$ is an everywhere finite Young's function.

papers.title: Dynamic Active Fleet Sizing of Heterogeneous UAV Relays for Post-Disaster Communication Networks
papers.abstract: Uncrewed aerial vehicle (UAV) communication systems are increasingly used to provide temporary connectivity when ground communication infrastructure is damaged by disasters such as hurricanes and wildfires. However, the amount of aerial support required changes as ground networks recover and communication demand evolves. We focus on dynamically adjusting the number and allocation of actively deployed UAVs within a fixed available fleet. We develop a model predictive control (MPC) framework for dynamic fleet sizing of heterogeneous UAV relays during post-disaster communication recovery. The framework accounts for communication demand, ground network recovery, heterogeneous UAV operation, UAV energy availability, and backhaul capacity, which limits how much relayed traffic can be transmitted to the external communication network. The resulting formulation is a convex quadratic program that supports efficient online fleet sizing and deployment decisions. We evaluate the framework using seven historical disaster recovery case studies based on Federal Communications Commission reports, together with four backhaul scenarios and sensitivity analyses. Results show that required active UAV fleet size varies considerably throughout recovery, while backhaul capacity and fleet composition affect communication performance, highlighting the value of adapting active fleet size over time.

papers.title: Rational limit of Rains integrals of type $A_n$
papers.abstract: We deduce the rational analogue of the elliptic Rains identity of type $A_n$ arXiv:0309252. We also derive reductions of the rational analogue and present the connection of them with well-known integrals in literature.

papers.title: Automorphisms of Twisted Chevalley Groups over Commutative Rings
papers.abstract: We classify all abstract automorphisms of the elementary and full twisted Chevalley groups of types ${}^2A_\ell$ ($\ell\geq3$), ${}^2D_\ell$ ($\ell\geq4$), ${}^2E_6$, and ${}^3D_4$ over arbitrary commutative rings, for every invariant isogeny type. The coefficient automorphism $θ$ has order dividing that of the diagram automorphism. We assume that $2$ is invertible and, for triality, that $3$ is invertible as well. Three features distinguish the answer from the usual inner--diagonal and coefficient decomposition. The elementary groups of types ${}^2A_3$ and ${}^2A_4$ admit an additive family of exceptional automorphisms supported at $θ$-fixed maximal ideals with residue field $\mathbb F_3$. In type ${}^2D_4$, diagram automorphisms may vary on idempotent components, subject to compatibility with the involution and the isogeny lattice. In triality, the coefficient automorphisms preserve the trace operator $r\mapsto r+θ(r)+θ^2(r)$ but need not commute with $θ$. We determine which elementary automorphisms extend to the full groups and describe the remaining central factors. A nonzero exceptional unitary factor extends precisely in the simply connected type ${}^2A_3$, giving a classification for the hyperbolic group $\operatorname{SU}_4(R,θ;Q_4)$. The proof glues uniquely determined normalization data for a finite root frame and then recovers the coefficient action from root-subgroup relations.

papers.title: Matrix-Free Local Multigrid for $C^1$ Hermite Discretizations on GPUs
papers.abstract: I present a matrix-free local multigrid method for $C^1$ tensor-product Hermite discretizations on adaptively refined Cartesian meshes, using the clamped biharmonic problem as the model problem. Extending a cell-wise primal-dual formulation to Hermite elements, I enforce continuity through a constraint operator that is never formed. At refinement edges, geometric prolongation supplies both the trace and its normal derivative, so the local V-cycle needs no edge operator and no hanging-node machinery. For the cubic element, an even-odd decomposition based on the signed reflection symmetry of the Hermite basis, applied along two axes, splits the element matrix into four dense $16\times16$ blocks and reaches 85% of peak memory bandwidth. Chebyshev-Jacobi and vertex-patch smoothers both preserve conformity by construction. In three dimensions on one NVIDIA A100 in double precision, conjugate gradients preconditioned by the Chebyshev-Jacobi V-cycle need five or six iterations on uniform meshes and solve at up to 4.23 million cells per second. On locally refined meshes the count rises to at most sixteen, ordered by the fraction of cells on a refinement edge and nearly equal for both smoothers.

papers.title: Structure-Preserving Dimension Reduction and Surrogates for Partially Linear Bayesian Inverse Problems
papers.abstract: Many Bayesian inverse problems are characterized by two parameter vectors with distinct roles. A medium property, operator coefficient, or geometry block enters the forward model nonlinearly, whereas a volumetric, initial condition, or boundary condition source enters linearly. General-purpose nonlinear surrogates must relearn this known source dependence from data and may not preserve the correct source scaling outside the training regime. We introduce a structure-preserving partially linear (SPPL) framework that constructs separate reduced spaces for outputs, (linearly appearing) sources, and (nonlinearly appearing) medium variables and represents the reduced forward map as an affine function of the retained source coordinates, with coefficients that depend on the medium variables. Here, "affine" refers to the retained, mean-centered source coordinates: the physical forward map remains linear in the source, while the affine offset is induced by the source-prior mean and vanishes when that mean is zero. The analysis first identifies the optimal blockwise ridge approximation and then derives the optimal affine-in-source approximation under independent medium and source priors. A direct decomposition of the forward error into output, source, medium, and surrogate contributions yields blockwise spectral criteria and prior-predictive expected-KL control. For a Gaussian source prior, the optimal affine-in-source approximation coincides with the optimal blockwise ridge approximation. In a coseismic numerical example, a three-model controlled ablation on common block-reduced coordinates separates the effects of coefficient-matrix supervision and structure-preserving affine-in-source parameterization. Reduced-space surrogate MCMC provides orders-of-magnitude online acceleration relative to high-fidelity posterior sampling.

papers.title: On Borodin-Gorin presentation of Heckman-Opdam $\mathfrak{gl}_n$ hypergeometric function
papers.abstract: We prove that Borodin-Gorin presentation for Heckman-Opdam $\mathfrak{gl}_n$ hypergeometric function by interlacing integrals is equivalent to two other integral presentations studied in arXiv:2508.18864. We also consider related Baxter operators and the corresponding limiting procedure from the Ruijsenaars hyperbolic model.

papers.title: Continuous-time analysis and algorithms for linear and convex quadratic programs via exactly solvable differential inclusions
papers.abstract: Linear and convex quadratic programs are fundamental problems in optimization. While many methods have been developed for solving these programs in large-scale applications, to our knowledge none have attempted to solve their continuous-time gradient flow, a differential inclusion, in full generality without assumptions beyond feasibility. Recent work solved the gradient flows in two special cases, basis pursuit and the lasso, and obtained competitive algorithms. Motivated by these results, we solve the general case exactly. Using the minimal selection principle for monotone differential inclusions, we show that the trajectory of the gradient flow consists of finitely many pieces, each obtained from one nonnegative least-squares problem. Its final piece yields an optimal solution or a certificate of unboundedness. This analysis leads to two algorithms. The first algorithm is exact, terminates after finitely many steps, and applies to linear programs and projections onto polyhedra. The second algorithm, which we call minimal selection descent, discretizes the gradient flow for general convex quadratic programs. Its iterates converge to an optimal solution when one exists and otherwise certify unboundedness. We apply both algorithms to a positivity-preserving limiter for a discontinuous Galerkin scheme and to optimal control problems for the Poisson and heat equations. In the limiter, the first algorithm conserves the total mass more accurately than the state-of-the-art Douglas--Rachford splitting method. On the control problems, minimal selection descent reaches the optimal value to machine precision and is competitive in time with commercial and open-source solvers.

papers.title: Cographs in chordal graphs
papers.abstract: For a graph $G$, let $\text{cg}(G)$ be the maximum $k\in \mathbb N$ for which $G$ contains a $k$-vertex cograph as an induced subgraph. The Erdős-Hajnal conjecture asserts that for every proper hereditary graph class $\mathcal{G}$, there exists $γ\in(0,1]$ such that every $n$-vertex graph $G\in\mathcal{G}$ satisfies $\text{cg}(G)\geq n^γ$. This is still open; however, for some hereditary classes, one may guarantee much stronger bounds. For instance, every chordal graph $G$ on $n\geq 2$ vertices satisfies $\text{cg}(G)\geq n/(2\log n)$. Paul Seymour asked whether this bound is optimal up to a constant factor. We answer this affirmatively, even for interval graphs: For every integer $n\geq 2$, we construct an $n$-vertex interval graph $G$ with $\text{cg}(G)<64n/\log n$.

papers.title: Generalized Images for Brownian First Passage to Monomial Boundaries
papers.abstract: We study the first passage of Brownian motion to a monomial moving boundary. For every integer degree at least two, we construct a time-independent signed image measure whose heat potential is the killed Brownian transition density on a nonzero interval of the natural Brownian time scale. The image density is determined by a second-kind Volterra equation in the image coordinate, not by the classical Volterra equations in time for the hitting density. Its kernel is an explicit Wright function, and the first-passage density is recovered afterwards from the boundary flux. Exponential bounds establish convergence, while a beta-moment transform connects the Wright kernel with the finite-order differential hierarchy previously obtained from transported moving zeros. A cubic numerical experiment independently checks the resulting density against simulated Brownian paths.

papers.title: Quantum field theory and four-manifolds: Perspectives from physics and geometry
papers.abstract: These lecture notes are based on lecture series by the authors for the Summer School 2025 on ``Physical mathematics of quantum field theory" at the University of Massachusetts Amherst organized by Owen Gwilliam, Chris Elliott, and Matteo Lotito. The lectures centred around algebraic structures arising from twists of supersymmetric quantum field theories, correlation functions of topologically twisted supersymmetric gauge theories, and their mathematical counterparts as intersection-theoretic invariants associated to moduli spaces of instantons, semistable sheaves, or Higgs sheaves on four-manifolds or complex projective surfaces.

papers.title: Syzygy and Adjoint Matroids
papers.abstract: We give a matroid-theoretic analogue of Gaussian elimination and use it to construct, for every matroid M, the syzygy matroid Syz(M) on the collection of circuits of M. Dualizing the construction yields the combinatorial adjoint Adj(M) on the collection of maximal proper flats of M, and the two are related by Adj(M) \simeq Syz(M*). Neither construction depends on a realization. We determine Syz(M) when M is U_{k,k+3} or the Vamos matroid V_{8}. We also show that Adj(M) is an adjoint of M when M has rank 3. When M has rank 4 and V_{8} is a restriction of M, Adj(M) has rank 3 and is not an adjoint of M.

papers.title: Global well-posedness for the modified dispersion-generalized Benjamin-Ono equations
papers.abstract: In this short note, we prove the global well-posedness of the modified dispersion-generalized Benjamin-Ono equation with dispersion $1<α<2$, $$\partial_t u + D^α\partial_x u + u^2\partial_x u=0,$$ over the Sobolev space $H^s(\mathbb{R})$, for any regularity $s$ greater or equal than the sharp analytic well-posedness regularity. As a byproduct, we also derive nonlinear smoothing estimates and give a simple proof of local well-posedness.

papers.title: Denominators of Hodge integrals and Minkowski numbers
papers.abstract: We prove that the least common denominator of all genus $g$ Hodge integrals is the Minkowski number $T_{2g}$ or, equivalently, the Bhargava factorial $(2g+1)!_{\mathbb{P}}$ associated to the set of primes $\mathbb{P}\subset\mathbb{N}$. As a corollary, we prove a conjecture of Liu-Xu on the multiplicity of $3$ in the least common denominators of certain descendant integrals, and generalise their result on a conjecture of Itzykson-Zuber to Hodge integrals with $λ$ classes. Namely, the order of the automorphism group of any pointed stable curve of genus $g'\le g$ divides the least common denominator of all genus $g$ Hodge integrals. We also comment on the use of generative AI via IMProofBench, which played a fruitful part in the development of this (entirely human-written) paper.

papers.title: Summation-by-parts operators for general function spaces: Flux differencing, entropy stability, and accuracy
papers.abstract: Summation-by-parts (SBP) operators are a cornerstone of provably stable high-order methods for hyperbolic conservation laws. For nonlinear problems, the flux-differencing framework of Fisher and Carpenter combines such SBP operators with entropy-conservative two-point fluxes to obtain semi-discretizations that are conservative in the sense of Lax--Wendroff and discretely entropy-conservative or stable. So far, this framework has been developed exclusively for operators that are exact for polynomials. Function-space SBP (FSBP) operators lift this restriction by being exact on a general finite-dimensional function space that can be tailored to the problem at hand. In this work, we extend flux differencing to FSBP operators for general (potentially non-polynomial) function spaces. We prove that, whenever the operator has a diagonal norm and its function space contains the constants, the resulting semi-discretization is conservative in the sense of Lax--Wendroff, semi-discretely entropy-conservative within a single element, and entropy-stable across element interfaces. We also provide the first theoretical accuracy analysis of FSBP operators: We characterize their design order through an algebraic criterion on the underlying function space, prove that suitable non-polynomial spaces achieve the same design order as polynomial spaces of equal dimension, and show that the flux-differencing semi-discretization retains this order. Notably, the entropy-conservative two-point flux is reused unchanged; only the underlying function space differs from the polynomial case. Numerical experiments for the Burgers' equation and the compressible Euler equations in one and two dimensions confirm these properties.

papers.title: DBDSVDMR3: An MRRR-Based Bidiagonal SVD Solver Built from DSTEGR
papers.abstract: The optimal algorithm for the symmetric tridiagonal eigenvalue problem is Multiple Relatively Robust Representations (MRRR or MR$^3$), which is capable of computing $k$ eigenvalue/eigenvector pairs in only $O(kn)$ floating-point operations. While MRRR is nearly 30 years old, it has never successfully been adapted to the bidiagonal SVD. This is not for lack of trying; two previous attempts produced implementations that were considered for LAPACK but eventually abandoned, a result of the fact that neither was reliable enough when run on test problems. The question therefore remained: is there a problem with the theory of MRRR for the bidiagonal SVD or were there simply bugs in the previous implementations that went undetected? This paper resolves this question by presenting DBDSVDMR3 -- a new implementation of the MRRR-based algorithm for the bidiagonal SVD originally proposed by Willems and Lang [ETNA 2012], which, for the first time, performs well on a variety of test problems while achieving significant speedups over both LAPACK's bisection-based solver and, in certain cases, divide-and-conquer for the bidiagonal SVD (thereby indicating that the theory is sound). DBDSVDMR3 will be available in the next release of LAPACK. In this paper, we discuss the design of our implementation, which was obtained with the help of Claude Code, and exhibit its performance on a diverse set of test problems.

papers.title: Ergodic Linear-Quadratic Optimal Control with Stochastic Coefficients
papers.abstract: We investigate ergodic linear-quadratic optimal control problems with stochastic coefficients and introduce the associated stochastic ergodic Hamilton-Jacobi-Bellman (HJB) equation, in which the classical ergodic constant is replaced by a random process $λ$. We establish well-posedness of the equation and show that $λ$ characterizes the optimal ergodic costs for a general class of averaging kernels, including those corresponding to normalized finite-horizon and discounted costs. For random-periodic coefficients, we construct a random-periodic solution and show that the optimal ergodic costs associated with all admissible averaging kernels coincide. We also establish stability of the optimal ergodic costs under perturbations of the coefficients.

papers.title: Relaxation and $Γ$-Convergence of Stretch Energy on Surface Homeomorphisms
papers.abstract: Area-preserving parameterization of triangular meshes is an essential task in geometry processing, yet an exactly area-preserving simplicial mapping may not exist in general. In this paper, we study area preservation of simplicial mappings in the limit of mesh refinement by establishing the $Γ$-convergence of the discrete stretch energy, a functional that measures their area distortion. We first introduce its limit functional, the relaxed stretch energy on surface homeomorphisms, defined through the pushforward of the area measure, and show that it is the relaxation of the stretch energy of diffeomorphisms with respect to uniform convergence. Then, to compare simplicial mappings with homeomorphisms, we construct a geometric lift that requires no shape-regularity assumption on the image mesh. Finally, we establish the $Γ$-convergence and show that the minimal discrete energies converge to the continuum minimum. Moreover, any homeomorphism arising as a limit of lifted discrete local minimizers in fixed-radius balls is area-preserving.

papers.title: Bridge change-of-measure for propagator estimation of diffusions
papers.abstract: The propagator of one-dimensional diffusions has relevant applications in statistical inference and across many disciplines. Yet it is obtained in closed form only for very few simple models. Here we analyze an importance sampling strategy based on a bridge change of measure to estimate propagators: paths are generated under an auxiliary diffusion whose bridge between the two fixed boundary points is easy to generate, and the target propagator is recovered through a Radon-Nikodym derivative or likelihood ratio correction derived from Girsanov's theorem. This method overcomes the main limitations of the crude Monte Carlo estimator, which relies on binning in state space, introducing bias and becoming inefficient with rare transitions. We apply the method to a range of benchmark processes and show that the bridge-based estimator matches the accuracy of crude Monte Carlo with orders of magnitude fewer sample paths. Finally, we elaborate on discretization schemes for the Radon-Nikodym derivative and on approximations to the best-in-class change of measure, both of which increase the efficiency of the method.

papers.title: Finite zero products of Toeplitz operators with harmonic symbols
papers.abstract: We study finite products of Toeplitz operators with harmonic symbols on the Fock space over the complex plane. If every symbol has the form $f+\overline g$, where $f$ and $g$ are entire functions of exponential type, we prove that a finite product vanishes if and only if one symbol vanishes identically. It suffices to test the product on reproducing kernels. The proof represents the product by a two-variable entire function and transforms the equation for a left factor by $\exp(-\partial_z\partial_w)$. A Fock norm identity then permits cancellation of each nonzero factor.

papers.title: Higher-order tangent and secant numbers, special-value integrals, and a common zero attractor
papers.abstract: We study two families of coefficients associated with powers of the tangent function and with products of the secant and tangent functions, and develop a unified treatment of the corresponding higher-order tangent and secant numbers. The first part establishes a common identity for even derivatives of $\tanh x$ and odd derivatives of $\operatorname{sech}x$. Combined with integral formulae for these derivatives, this yields finite power-integral representations for the normalized values $ζ(2n+1)$ and $β(2n)$ and naturally introduces two polynomial families $P_n$ and $Q_n$. We determine several arithmetic and structural properties of these polynomials. In particular, we identify the exact content of $P_n$, prove that $Q_n$ is primitive, establish strict log-concavity and unimodality of their coefficient sequences, and describe their real zeros. For even indices each family has a unique negative real zero, and the two sequences of real zeros have the same limit. We also derive differential recurrences and generating functions for $P_n$ and $Q_n$. The generating functions lead to a global complex-singularity analysis. We construct a compact Jordan curve $Γ$ and prove that the complex zero sets of both $P_n$ and $Q_n$ converge to $Γ$ in Hausdorff distance. The normalized zero-counting measures converge weakly to the same equilibrium measure on $Γ$. We determine the logarithmic capacity of the enclosed compact set, give an explicit arclength density for the limiting measure, and compute its first moments. Numerical plots for $P_{20}$, $P_{50}$, $P_{100}$ and $P_{150}$ illustrate the zero-attractor theorem.

papers.title: Triple Products of Correlated Multivariate Hermite Polynomials
papers.abstract: Stochastic Galerkin schemes (SGS) are used to approximate solutions to differential equations with stochastic parameters. In particular, they express the solution with an infinite orthogonal functional basis of the parameter space and derive a deterministic system of PDEs; the solution of this deterministic system can be used to produce a {surrogate} approximation of the original stochastic equations. When the parameters are correlated, the infinite series representation of the solution does not provably converge for all joint distributions; further, classic decorrelating transformations (e.g., Roseblatt) often introduce known numerical instabilities. Rahman (2017) established convergence in probability and distribution for correlated {Gaussian} parameters when the basis functionals are {multivariate Hermite polynomials} (MHPs), where these polynomials are only {weakly orthogonal} with respect to the underlying joint density. Due to weak orthogonality, the $N$th moments of MHPs introduced during Galerkin projection do not trivially decompose into products of one-dimensional expectations and have no closed-form expression for $N > 2$; consequently, these moments are typically estimated via brute-force sampling and quickly become prohibitively expensive to compute. In this paper, we introduce and prove several foundational results for MHPs. These results culminate in an equation that can be used to calculate the $N = 3$ moments (triple products) exactly, whose implementation dramatically reduces the computational bottleneck otherwise inherent to SGS with correlated Gaussian parameters.

papers.title: Commutators in selfless C$^\ast$-algebras
papers.abstract: We show that if \((A, τ)\) is a selfless C\(^\ast\)-probability space with \(τ\) being a faithful trace, then commutators are dense in \(\ker τ\).

papers.title: Alexander Torsion and Floer Comparisons in the BV-BFV Formalism
papers.abstract: We compare relative Abelian BF torsion with the Alexander-graded Euler characteristic of knot Floer homology. A meridional annulus boundary condition identifies the normalized relative torsion with the Alexander polynomial. One exact prime-cyclotomic torsion value recovers all its coefficients under a sharp genus bound, compatibly with connected-sum gluing and branched-cover formulas. We compute interface contractions and obstructions to scalar comparisons, including the pairing defect of two-sector reduction for the degree-zero torus algebra. A six-generator dg resolution yields an equivalence of perfect-module categories preserving derived pairings and admits a classical one-dimensional BV-BFV realization. In the fixed nonresonant polynomial quantum BFV sector, over characteristic zero with $\hbar$ inverted, both states and Weyl observables reduce to a vacuum field; a Hochschild invariant obstructs a Morita equivalence with the degree-zero torus algebra. These results do not establish a full geometric BV-BFV/Floer equivalence.

papers.title: Scaling H2 Factorization to Billion-Unknown Three-Dimensional Problems
papers.abstract: Strong recursive skeletonization provides approximate direct solvers for dense matrices from integral equations and kernel methods, but distributed implementations face substantial communication costs and limited parallelism, especially in three dimensions. We present a distributed-memory $\mathcal{H}^2$ factorization solver for symmetric matrices that combines spatial box coloring, delayed Schur complement updates, streamed sketching-based interpolative decomposition, and BLAS-3 and shared-memory kernels. Spatial coloring enables every process to participate in each boundary stage, while delayed updates and streamed sketching reduce dense storage and communication. To our knowledge, this is the first distributed-memory strong recursive skeletonization factorization demonstrated for three-dimensional volume integral equations at billion-unknown scale. Experiments on up to 512 compute nodes demonstrate factorization of a three-dimensional Laplace system with 3.62 billion unknowns, alongside three-dimensional Helmholtz tests and a two-dimensional Matérn system with 268 million unknowns. Combining streamed sketching and fully delayed updates reduces factorization time by $6.9\times$ for Laplace and $8.5\times$ for Helmholtz relative to the unsketched, eager configuration, while reducing maximum per-process resident memory by 57\% and 54\%, respectively.

papers.title: Generalized Kahler BHE threefolds
papers.abstract: We study the notion of generalized Kahler Bismut--Hermitian--Einstein (GKBHE) manifolds, namely generalized Kähler manifolds for which both Bismut Ricci forms vanish, and we develop a theory for such structures on compact threefolds. We organize the analysis according to the horizontal rank, an invariant taking values in $\{0,1,2\}$ that measures the relative position of the canonical foliations associated with the two Hermitian structures. We characterize the case of horizontal rank $0$ (which corresponds to Kähler Ricci flat geometry) and describe the case of horizontal rank $1$, revealing its close interplay with the steady $ν$-soliton equation in Kähler geometry. This description also provides a tool for constructing new compact GKBHE threefolds.

papers.title: Temporal Exploration and Rendezvous via Weisfeiler-Leman Colorings
papers.abstract: Temporal graphs are graphs whose edge relation changes in discrete time steps. The Temporal Exploration Problem (TEXP) asks for a temporal walk that visits all vertices. We show that every connected temporal graph with $n$ vertices can be explored in $O(qn\log^3(n))$ time steps, where $q$ is the number of vertex color classes induced by the 2-dimensional Weisfeiler-Leman (2-WL) coloring. For small $q$, our bound substantially improves on the known worst-case bound of $Θ(n^2)$ in general connected temporal graphs. A corresponding walk can be constructed in deterministic polynomial time. The upper bound is complemented by lower bounds of $Ω(n\log(n))$ when $q$ is constant and $Ω(qn)$ when $1 \leq q \leq n$. We also apply our techniques to the Temporal Rendezvous Problem (TRP), in which two agents that do not communicate have to meet on a vertex of the temporal graph. Our exploration algorithm yields that, with only polynomial-time computational power, the agents can meet in $O(n\log^3(n))$ time steps, leaving a gap of only $\log^2(n)$ to the known lower bound. Dogeas, Erlebach, Kammer, Meintrup, and Moses Jr. [ICALP'24] have shown an $O(rn^{1+ε})$ bound for TEXP, for every fixed $ε> 0$, where $r$ is the number of orbits, and an $O(n^{1+ε})$ bound for TRP. Both results require superpolynomial computation time. Our contribution improves upon these results in several ways. First, the dependence on $n$ in the upper bounds on the number of time steps is decreased from $n^{1+ε}$ to $n\log^3(n)$ for both TEXP and TRP. Second, for TEXP, we bound the number of time steps linearly by the parameter q, which is efficiently computable and upper bounded by $r$. Third, we provide novel deterministic polynomial-time algorithms for both TEXP and TRP.

papers.title: A Quasipolynomial Algorithm for $\ell_\infty$ Contractions
papers.abstract: We give an algorithm for computing an $\eps$-approximate fixed point of any $d$-dimensional nonexpansion with respect to the $\ell_\infty$ norm in time $\log(1/\eps)^{O(\log^2 d)}$. At its core, our method uses a boosting argument to geometrically shrink a search region. Among other consequences, our algorithm implies that simple stochastic games can be solved in quasipolynomial time.

papers.title: Self-normalized Bernstein Inequalities for Regenerative Processes and Applications to Learning Without Independence
papers.abstract: We prove a self-normalized Bernstein inequality for bounded functions of a regenerative process with independent, identically distributed marked cycles of finite mean length. The bound uses observed cycle lengths and retains explicit terms for truncation and the cycle ending after the observation horizon. Selecting a tuning parameter from a finite deterministic collection gives a version of Bernstein inequality where all terms are empirical but one, related to the tails of the regeneration times. We then study this term in many regimes: it turns out that it is of second-order in many cases of interest. This is important for applications in machine learning: we prove generalization error bounds for classification with non-i.i.d., regenerative data. These bounds can be used to define learning objectives: by minimizing the first-order term only in the bound, we define agnostic classifiers that still satisfy oracle inequalities. We also show that the bound on the average deviation provided by our results is minimax-optimal in the sample size and in the expected regeneration time. Finally, we combine the Bernstein inequality with a regenerative strong approximation to obtain a Gaussian approximation using an observable block variance estimator.

papers.title: On ABP Estimates for a Class of Fully Nonlinear Singular-Degenerate Elliptic Equations and Applications
papers.abstract: We establish an Alexandrov-Bakelman-Pucci type estimate for a class of fully nonlinear elliptic equations with singular or degenerate coefficients and nonlinear dependence on the gradient. The estimate bounds sub-solutions in terms of their boundary values and weighted integrals of the data. It holds for classical sub-solutions and for viscosity sub-solutions with locally Lipschitz gradients. The assumptions allow general rates of growth in the gradient, with a smallness condition on the data when the associated gradient weight has finite integral. The proof uses the classical weighted contact-set argument. As applications, we obtain sup-norm estimates for viscosity sub-solutions to a class of generalized Monge-Ampère equations, Hessian equations, Hessian quotients under an additional condition on the contact Hessian, and anisotropic mean-curvature-type equations.

papers.title: Boundary-Driven Nonequilibrium for the Coulomb Landau Equation
papers.abstract: We establish a nonlinear theory of the Coulomb Landau equation in smooth bounded domains with non-isothermal diffuse reflection. We construct a stationary state, prove its perturbative uniqueness and global nonlinear stability, and establish exponential convergence when the wall temperature approaches its stationary profile exponentially. We also establish stationary and global nonlinear well-posedness for prescribed inflow, together with asymptotic stability. The analysis combines a critical kinetic integrability gain with finite-exponent velocity-gradient estimates near grazing, allowing the nonlinear Coulomb estimates to close without $L_x^\infty$ control of velocity gradients.

papers.title: Minimax Optimality of the NPMLE for Gaussian Mixtures in Hellinger Distance
papers.abstract: We analyze the problem of estimating univariate Gaussian mixture densities using the nonparametric maximum likelihood estimator (NPMLE) based on $n$ independent and identically distributed samples. We show that the unconstrained NPMLE achieves the minimax optimal rate $\log(n)/n$ in squared Hellinger distance, when the true mixing measure is sub-Gaussian. In addition, we show that when the true mixing measure has compact support, the NMPLE constrained to a compact interval also achieves the minimax optimal rate, which is slightly faster and of order $\log(n)/(n \log \log n)$. Our proof consists of sharply characterizing the local Hellinger bracketing entropy of the class of finite Gaussian mixtures. One of our key technical innovations is to sharply bound the $L^2$ bracketing entropy of balls of bounded-degree polynomials, which may be of independent interest. As an application, we establish the regret-optimality of $g$-modeling procedures based on the NPMLE in the Gaussian Empirical Bayes problem with bounded priors.

papers.title: A well-posedness theory for the 2D inhomogeneous incompressible Euler equations and a class of global-in-time solutions
papers.abstract: We consider the Cauchy problem for the 2D inhomogeneous incompressible Euler equations. We show that the Cauchy problem is locally well-posed in a class of $m$-fold symmetric functions at critical regularity and allowing the velocity field to grow linearly at spatial infinity. This was a problem posed by P.L. Lions in the homogeneous, not necessarily symmetric case. A key ingredient is a variable-coefficient elliptic theory developed using quasiconformal mappings and Schauder estimates in certain scale-invariant Hölder spaces. Local well-posedness allows us to derive the one-dimensional system on $\mathbb{S}^1$ satisfied by solutions with $0$-homogeneous vorticity and density. For this system, we can obtain global well-posedness for a class of initial data away from equilibrium. We are unaware of any previous nonperturbative class of time-dependent solutions to the two-dimensional inhomogeneous Euler equations for which global well-posedness has been established. Finally, for some signed global solutions, we show a dichotomy between density homogenization and averaged relaxation in infinite time.

papers.title: Joint Uniform Continuity of Reduced Free Products for strong convergence
papers.abstract: We investigate a generalization of Skoufranis' theorem on joint continuity of free products of laws in the strong topology. Namely, we show that this operation is moreover \emph{uniformly continuous}. Our methods follows those of Piser and go through the estimates of Ricard-Xu.

papers.title: When Standardization Spreads Factor Variation Across the Spectrum
papers.abstract: Standardizing variables by their sample standard deviations is routine in multivariate analysis and removes marginal scale differences before dependence is assessed. The resulting correlation matrix captures both dominant common components and dependence beyond them. A central inferential difficulty arises because the same random sample variances normalize the entire spectrum. In spiked covariance models, the sampling errors of leading and residual eigenvalues can become asymptotically independent. Sample standardization fundamentally changes this behavior and can preserve their dependence, allowing strong factors to remain a major source of uncertainty even after the leading eigenvalues are excluded. To obtain valid inference for both residual and full spectrum statistics, we establish their joint sampling law for sample correlation matrices with diverging spikes. The theory reveals exact trace compensation and statistic dependent transitions between asymptotic independence and dependence as the spikes grow. It leads to tests of an identity correlation matrix under strong factors and a feasible two sample comparison of residual spectral concentration. A sex balanced HapMap analysis illustrates the substantial effect of factor variation on residual spectrum inference.

papers.title: AnyonWiki.org
papers.abstract: The AnyonWiki is an open-source project that provides full algebraic and numerical data of fusion and unitary modular fusion categories as a resource for the scientific community. It comes with a database, the AnyonWikiDatabase, that currently includes the classification of multiplicity-free pivotal (braided) fusion categories through rank 7 and more than 25000 fusion rings including the classification of multiplicity-free fusion rings through rank 10, with work in progress to expand. This data is available through AnyonWiki.org, a website that provides robust search and download functionality and presents each fusion ring and category via a dedicated webpage. In this short article we discuss the data available at AnyonWiki.org as well as the scientific and communal motivations for the design of its underlying AnyonWikiDatabase, which are centered around making the data accessible, independently verifiable, granularly citable, useful, and easy to work with.

papers.title: The Dynamics of RMSProp Beyond the Stability Threshold
papers.abstract: We study what happens to RMSProp when the learning rate is too large for convergence to the minimizer. For positive-definite quadratic loss functions, we show that the minimizer is Lyapunov un- stable above an explicit critical learning rate. Nevertheless, every trajectory eventually enters a compact trapping region. We obtain explicit bounds proportional to h in the spatial variables and to h2 in the memory variables, where h is the learning rate. We also prove that nontrivial period-two orbits exist precisely above the critical learning rate, and under additional spectral assumptions, an attracting branch of these orbits emerges from the minimizer. For sufficiently large learning rates, we construct branches near admissible corners of a cube. We then explore the dynamics inside the trapping region using the parameterization method and numerical continuation, exploring invariant circles and tori, coexistence of attracting sets, circle-doubling sequences, and chaotic motions. We examine how the dynamics depend on the loss Hessian, memory decay, and dimension. Finally, we test a learning-rate reduction schedule and continue selected invariant circles into an autonomous variant of the Adam optimizer.

papers.title: A linear, second-order, unconditionally energy-stable scalar-auxiliary-variable scheme for the CHQ viscoelastic phase-separation model
papers.abstract: The CHQ model describes viscoelastic phase separation in a polymer--solvent mixture: a Cahn--Hilliard equation for the polymer volume fraction $φ$ is two-way coupled, through a phase-dependent cross-diffusion flux, to a damped relaxation equation for a scalar bulk elastic stress $q$. We propose a scalar-auxiliary-variable (SAV) time discretisation of this system, combining the SAV reformulation of the double-well potential with a second-order backward differentiation formula (BDF2) and a second-order extrapolation of all phase-dependent mobilities: a linear, computationally cheaper complement to the reference scheme's fully nonlinear Newton solve. The resulting method is (i) linear at every time step, with a coupling structure we prove has exactly one solution at every step, for every choice of time-step size; (ii) mass conserving, exactly, as an algebraic identity of the discrete equations themselves (the only drift ever seen numerically traces to the finite tolerance of the iterative linear solver, not a failure of the conservation property); and (iii) unconditionally stable for a modified discrete energy, via an exact one-step energy--dissipation identity. We show the energy identity extends to this filtered variant as well, with two explicit extra non-negative terms. Hence, the scheme actually producing the physics results is itself provably stable for the same energy. A Fourier--Galerkin implementation verifies that the energy identity holds at every time step to within floating-point round-off. It also confirms second-order temporal accuracy, including in the steep-interface regime, and agreement with an independently implemented nonlinear Newton--BDF2 solver. Compared with that independent nonlinear Newton--BDF2 solver, at equal grid resolution, the SAV method uses $2.5$--$3.0\times$ fewer linear-solver iterations and $1.7$--$2.0\times$ less wall-clock time.

papers.title: Parallel AI Agent Collaboration as Graph-Structured Distributed Block Optimization
papers.abstract: Parallel AI agents can produce useful local edits yet degrade a shared solution when their edits are combined. We model this coordination problem as discrete block optimization with an exactly evaluable objective and a known dependency graph. Independent sets certify compatible edits whose verified gains, measured against the same current solution, add exactly. A coordinator constructs a safe compatible candidate and can also evaluate interacting edits to capture favorable interactions. We prove that an optimal fractional coloring yields a merger that preserves a $1/χ_f(G)$ fraction of the total verified local improvement, where $χ_f(G)$ is the graph's fractional chromatic number. This guarantee is tight among mergers that select a subset of the same proposals. Under conditional local-improvement guarantees and a block error-bound condition, repeated collaboration converges geometrically in the objective gap. The rate separates task structure, agent allocation, and computation cost, yielding a linear program for agent assignment and an explicit time-cost trade-off. Code-repair experiments show that verified merging resolves conflicts between individually useful edits that cause naive merging to fail. On larger conflict-free tasks, parallel agents reduce modeled completion time at higher input-token-equivalent cost. On three public road networks, fractional integration retains 922 units of verified graph-cut improvement across 90 paired runs. For route-search agents sharing exclusive access to vehicle routes, fractional scheduling reduces measured wall time by a median of 15% across twelve paired runs, with route-cost changes varying across runs.

papers.title: When Windowed Anderson Acceleration Converges Faster
papers.abstract: Windowed Anderson acceleration AA($m$) combines at most $m+1$ recent iterates by least squares. For a real affine contraction $x\mapsto Wx+b$ with $q=\|W\| \in(0,1)$, we determine exactly when AA($m$) converges from every starting point with an asymptotic factor below $q$. We give a polynomial criterion for this improvement and an equivalent spectral condition: there is no probability distribution on the phases of the eigenvalues of modulus $q$ whose first $m$ cosine moments are $q,q^2,\ldots,q^m$. If such a distribution exists, we construct a starting point from which AA($m$) reproduces fixed-point iteration at every step. Otherwise, over a fixed number of consecutive steps, every run contracts the residual norm by a common factor strictly smaller than the corresponding power of $q$. The polynomial criterion also gives explicit convergence-rate bounds with constants independent of the dimension. When $q$ equals the spectral radius, this characterizes improvement over the asymptotic convergence factor of fixed-point iteration. For general affine contractions, the asymptotic factor never exceeds the numerical radius of $W$, and a related moment condition gives a uniform upper bound strictly below that radius.

papers.title: Alternative moduli of twisted curves
papers.abstract: We define new Artin stack compactifications of the moduli of smooth curves, which parameterize "relatively polarized curves" consisting of stacky semistable curves equipped with line bundles that are trivialized away from the rational bridges. Using techniques from birational geometry, we prove that stacks of relatively polarized curves admit the classical coarse space $\overline{M}_g$ of stable curves as a good moduli space. One of our main motivations is a companion paper where we construct a proper moduli space of $\mathrm{SL}_N$-bundles on relatively polarized curves. This suggests the hypothesis that relatively polarized curves are suitable sources for defining Gromov-Witten theory for Artin stack targets.

papers.title: Reflection functors for non-simply-laced quiver varieties
papers.abstract: We prove the braid relations between reflection functors on non-simply-laced analogues of Nakajima quiver varieties, which are defined as critical loci of certain quivers with potential. We extend this framework to categories of matrix factorizations and critical $K$-theory.

papers.title: On the proof of the Kozma-Nitzan conjecture
papers.abstract: In this short note, we give an exposition of the recent proof of the Kozma-Nitzan conjecture provided by OpenAI.

papers.title: Unitary similarity for dual complex matrices and dual quaternion matrices
papers.abstract: We study unitary similarity of dual complex matrices and dual quaternion matrices. First, we characterize unitary similarity in terms of the existence of a skew-Hermitian solution to a Sylvester-type matrix equation. For $2\times2$ dual complex matrices, we obtain a complete three-trace criterion when the standard part is nonnormal and analyze the limitations of trace-word criteria when the standard part is normal. We then prove, for every $n\geq1$, that two $n\times n$ dual quaternion matrices are unitarily similar if and only if their dual complex adjoint matrices are unitarily similar, and we extend this result to finite families. As a scalar consequence, we derive a finite Trace-word criterion when the standard part is nonreal and exhibit its failure when the standard part is real.

papers.title: Facets of the X-ray polytope of doubly stochastic matrices
papers.abstract: We study the polytope of anti-diagonal X-rays of k x k doubly stochastic matrices, the image of the Birkhoff polytope under the map that sums the entries along each anti-diagonal. Its facets other than the coordinate facets are the minimal joint tail bounds for lattice laws of a sum of two dependent uniform random variables. We give an exact facet criterion in terms of the allowed edges of a tight graph. For rays of the underlying tropical fan, total support of the tight graph suffices for a facet but is not necessary, as an example with k=19 shows. Up to affine functions and positive scaling, the potentials that define a facet form a polytope whose vertices are its rays. Facets propagate by padding and by grid refinement under explicit hypotheses. We give infinite families of facets from no step potential, facets of quadratic height, superpolynomially many facets, and a classification of three-step potentials. Total support of a step potential is characterized by a Hall-type condition on block starts; with computer assistance, total support decides facets of step potentials for k<=26. The facet counts up to k=12 are found directly for k<=3 and, for k>=4, come from an enumeration by a provably complete algorithm; an independent exact recomputation reproduces its ray lists for 5<=k<=12.

papers.title: Differential powers of monomial ideals in affine semigroup rings
papers.abstract: This article gives explicit descriptions for differential powers of monomial ideals in certain (possibly non-normal) affine semigroup rings. We use these descriptions to show that the topologies defined by the ordinary, symbolic, and differential powers of any monomial ideal are all linearly equivalent. We then prove the existence of differential signature in our settings, relating it to the volume of some convex polytope. Finally, we apply our results to pinched Veronese rings.

papers.title: Multiplying matrices via polynomials: exposition and barriers
papers.abstract: We give an exposition of OpenAI's recent proof that the exponent $ω_\mathbb{C}$ of matrix multiplication over the complex numbers satisfies $ω_\mathbb{C}\leq9/4$. Our version of the proof gives $ω_\mathbb{F}\leq9/4$ over every field $\mathbb{F}$. We also treat the rectangular matrix multiplication exponent $ω_\mathbb{F}(a,b,c)$. Here we have $ω_\mathbb{F}(1,k,1)=2$ for $0\leq k\leq1/2$ and $ω_\mathbb{F}(1,k,1)\leq1+k+1/(4k)$ for $k\geq1/2$, and, for real numbers $a\geq b\geq c\geq0$, $ω_\mathbb{F}(a,b,c)=a+b$ if $c(a+b)\leq ab$ and $ω_\mathbb{F}(a,b,c)\leq(a+b+c)/2+(ab/c+ac/b+bc/a)/4$ otherwise. Our exposition is in the language of degeneration inequalities among polynomial multiplication tensors and Strassen's asymptotic spectrum duality. We moreover prove an operational barrier (which can be thought of as coming from an operational asymptotic spectrum) showing that the current analysis of all these upper bounds on $ω_\mathbb{F}$ and $ω_\mathbb{F}(a,b,c)$ is optimal and that in fact the current degeneration ingredients cannot improve the bounds.

papers.title: On OpenAI's proof of the Nagata conjecture
papers.abstract: These notes are an expanded account of my talk at UMass Amherst on OpenAI's remarkably simple proof of the Nagata conjecture. I hope they will be useful, especially to non-experts. The standard reduction to the normal cone and the collision of fat points into one monomial scheme reduce the problem to interpolation of monomial schemes on the normal ruled surface of a smooth plane cubic. The novelty is that the study of the asymptotics of theta functions as the cubic develops a node, together with interpolation duality, reduces the problem further to interpolation on a triangle of lattice points, which is straightforward. The same calculation determines the nef and pseudoeffective cones of a weighted blow-up of ${\Bbb P}^2$ at one point for very general local parameters when the ratio of weights is greater than nine.

papers.title: Long-time dynamics of viscous Gröbli triangles
papers.abstract: In 1877 Gröbli discovered that three point vortices in the plane can move self-similarly, forming a triangle that rotates while either expanding indefinitely or collapsing in finite time. We study the viscous counterpart of these configurations, namely the two-dimensional Navier--Stokes evolution starting from three point vortices arranged in a Gröbli triangle. In the expanding case, viscosity spreads the vortex cores at the same rate as the triangle grows, so the vortices remain well separated relative to their size. Building on this observation, we show that at high Reynolds number the solution stays close to three Lamb--Oseen vortices centered near the vertices of the inviscid triangle for times that grow exponentially with a power of the Reynolds number. In the collapsing case, the same description holds up to times close to the inviscid collision. As an application of the long-time result in the expanding case, we obtain a vanishing viscosity realization of the vortex burst, a nonuniqueness mechanism for point vortices in which a single vortex splits into an expanding Gröbli triangle.

papers.title: Irregular Gabor Frames for the Poisson Kernel
papers.abstract: Consider the semi-regular system of time-frequency shifts of the Poisson kernel $g(t) = {{1} \over {t^2+w^2}}$ $$\G(g, M \times α\Z) = \left\{ e^{2πi λt } g(t-n) \colon (λ, n) \in M \times α\Z \right\}$$ where $M \subset \R$. We obtain {\it a criterion} for $\G(g, M \times α\Z)$ to form a frame in $L^2(\R)$ for an {\it arbitrary} set $M$ of finite upper density. It turned out that the lower density alone does not determine the frame property, even when $M$ is uniformly discrete.

papers.title: Dual Effect and Certainty Equivalence Revisited for a Linear-Gaussian Dual Control Problem
papers.abstract: This paper revisits the relation between dual effect and certainty equivalence (CE) through a scalar linear-Gaussian model. In dual control, the current input affects not only the immediate cost but also the information available for future decisions, and hence the future cost. Dynamic programming (DP) provides a natural framework for formulating dual control problems. At each step of the Bellman recursion, an optimal input minimizes the sum of the stage cost and the expected cost-to-go. We restrict attention to stage costs minimized by the CE input. However, CE may not minimize the Bellman objective because of the input-dependent expected cost-to-go. Classical no-dualeffect (NDE) conditions guarantee CE optimality in certain problem classes by requiring the conditional distribution of the estimation error to be independent of past controls. In the present model, we observe that CE can remain optimal at the level of a single Bellman recursion even when the classical NDE conditions fail, provided that the expected cost-to-go is independent of the current input. Motivated by this observation, we introduce a notion of NDE formulated directly at the level of the Bellman objective, which we call Bellman-side NDE. Under some mild regularity conditions, we show that Bellman-side NDE can be characterized by a heat equation. This characterization identifies the class of Bellman-side NDE functions, and further yields a decomposition of a generic cost-to-go function into a Bellman-side NDE component and a dual-effect component.

papers.title: The recent counterexamples to the Eisenbud-Schreyer-Weyman Ulrich problem (2003) and to Hochster's small Cohen-Macaulay conjecture (1973): a survey, with a generalization to arbitrary dimension
papers.abstract: In September 2026 four preprints and an AI-generated manuscript moved one numerical obstruction from projective geometry to local algebra. For a smooth complex projective surface $Y$ with an ample, globally generated divisor $H$ such that $H^2<σ(Y)$, the signature, one obtains in turn: no Ulrich bundles when $H$ is very ample (Anghel, arXiv:2609.02718; extended to every dimension by Lopez, arXiv:2609.06678), answering negatively the Eisenbud-Schreyer-Weyman question of 2003 for sheaves supported on the whole variety; no arithmetically Cohen-Macaulay bundles, i.e. section rings without graded maximal Cohen-Macaulay modules in characteristic zero (Anghel, arXiv:2609.15589); and complete local domains without small Cohen-Macaulay modules, counterexamples to Hochster's 1973 conjecture, if $K_Y\equiv4H$ (Chen, arXiv:2609.24142, proposed) or $σ>2H^2$ (OpenAI, released 6 October). We recall the definitions and main statements, and add two things. First, through a finite projection to $\mathbb P^2$ and an identity already present in the OpenAI manuscript, the three obstructions become one variance identity; for surfaces this explains the factor $2$ between the graded bound $σ\le H^2$ and the local $σ\le2H^2$. Second, we generalize the argument of the OpenAI manuscript to every dimension $m\ge2$, with complete proofs: if $X$ is a smooth complex projective variety of dimension $m$ and $H$ an ample, globally generated divisor, a small Cohen-Macaulay module over the completed section ring of $(X,H)$ forces $(K_X^2-2c_2(X))\cdot H^{m-2}\le(m+4)H^m$. Consequently the completed section rings of all Hesse pairs, including the ball quotient of the first preprint, have no small Cohen-Macaulay module, and products of Hesse surfaces with projective spaces give complete local domains with an isolated singularity, of every dimension $\ge3$, without small Cohen-Macaulay modules.

papers.title: Zeros of $E_2$, quasi-periods, and Schwarz maps
papers.abstract: We study the zeros of the Eisenstein series $E_2$, their distribution near rational cusps, and the values of modular functions at these zeros. Using Watson's inversion formula, we prove that the number of zeros in $0\leq\operatorname{Re}τ<1$ with imaginary part at least $Y$ satisfies \[ N(Y)=\frac{1}{2πY} +O\!\left(Y^{-1/2}\log\frac1Y\right) \qquad(Y\to0^+). \] We also determine the limiting distribution of the scaled displacements from the cusps and prove that two zeros whose difference is rational differ by an integer. At every zero $ρ$, classical transcendence theorems imply that both $j(ρ)$ and $λ(ρ)$ are transcendental. We use this fact to obtain an exact multiplicity formula for arithmetic quasimodular forms at arbitrary congruence level and to show that all ordinary derivatives of arithmetic modular functions on congruence subgroups, evaluated at $ρ$, are algebraic over $\overline{\mathbb Q}(j(ρ),j'(ρ))$. We then relate Watson's formula to the Schwarz map of a rational transform of the Legendre hypergeometric equation. Finally, we give conditional results on the transcendence of $ρ$ under modular Schanuel and period conjectures, and determine why the associated analytic subgroup fails the rank condition in Waldschmidt's theorem.

papers.title: Tempered Langevin diffusions with polynomial-tailed targets: explosions, moment thresholds and ergodicity
papers.abstract: For tempered Langevin diffusions (TLDs) targeting polynomially tailed measures, the convergence rate is known to change from polynomial to exponential to uniform as the temperature rises through a critical value. We explain this transition by the tails of the marginal laws of the norm of the TLD, up to a second, larger critical temperature beyond which the TLD explodes. As the temperature increases, these tails change from stretched-exponential, through super-polynomial at the first critical temperature, to polynomial, mirroring the transition in the convergence rate. Moreover, this tail analysis gives a complete quantification of the convergence rates throughout the non-explosive regime, in both $f$-variation and Wasserstein distances.

papers.title: On the gap of thresholds
papers.abstract: We propose an algorithm to compute the gap numbers of log canonical thresholds, anticanonical thresholds, and $\mathbb{R}$-complementary thresholds for surface pairs with a given rational hyperstandard coefficient set. As an example, we compute these gap numbers for a special hyperstandard set that appears in the effective boundedness of $n$-complements for surface pairs.

papers.title: On optimal (v,5,3,1) optical orthogonal codes
papers.abstract: In this paper, we establish a tight upper bound for the size of a $(v,5,3,1)$ optical orthogonal code (OOC) and call such a code optimal when it achieves this upper bound. In addition, if an optimal OOC has the property that all non-identity elements of $\mathbb{Z}_v$ are covered by the list of differences of its codeword-sets then it is called perfect. In this paper, we present direct and recursive constructions for infinite classes of optimal and perfect $(v,5,3,1)$-OOCs.

papers.title: Almost Every Pair of Interval Exchange Transformations Does Not Generate a Free Group
papers.abstract: We show that the Lebesgue measure of the set of pairs of interval exchange transformations that generate a free group of rank $2$ is zero.

papers.title: On the strict approximation of currents and space-time trajectories
papers.abstract: This work establishes a wide variety of strict approximation results for space-time trajectories, a class of space-time currents that are used to model the evolution of dislocations in crystalline materials. In particular, we introduce a strict-type notion of convergence which respects quantities associated with geometric transport phenomena and prove approximation results in this topology. These results build on the classical strict approximation results for normal and integral currents developed by Federer and Fleming, which we also review and refine.

papers.title: On $k$-connected Sets in Matroids
papers.abstract: In 1966, Tutte defined $k$-connected matroids for each $k \ge 2$. Robertson and Seymour built on Tutte's idea to define tangles as a way to identify highly connected parts of a matroid. Motivated by tangles, a set $Z$ in a matroid $M$ has been defined to be $3$-connected if, for each $j$ in $\{1,2\}$, there is no $j$-separation $(X,Y)$ of $M$ such that each of $|Z \cap X|$ and $|Z \cap Y|$ is at least $j$. This paper solves a problem of Whittle for $k= 3$ by proving that a minor-minimal matroid having $Z$ as a $3$-connected set has at most $3|Z| - 4$ elements. We also identify the matroids for which this bound is attained.

papers.title: Lax descent and foliated Verdier duality
papers.abstract: Higher categorical methods allow us to view recollements as lax descent data and build a corresponding descent theory governed by an $\infty$-bicategorical theory of limits. We demonstrate some concrete innovations brought along by these new techniques in the classical context of constructible and perverse sheaves on stratified spaces. Our first application uses partially (op)lax descent to recover the famous result of Beilinson telling us how to glue perverse sheaves in terms of vanishing and nearby cycles. The remainder of the article is concerened with establishing a uniform view on a series of classification results for perverse sheaves culminating in recent work of Kapranov-Schechtman. Namely, we use lax descent to establish a ``foliated'' variant of Verdier duality which, informally speaking, identifies the derived constructible category of a suitably foliated space with sections of a categorical cosheaf on the leaf space whose stalks are the categories of sheaves along the leaves. Again, this is obtained as an application of lax descent, and seems to provide a reasonable framework to formalize the idea of ``mixed sheaf-cosheaf objects'' promoted by Kapranov and Schechtman.

papers.title: Characters and Polynomiality for Maximal Parabolic Unipotent Radicals in Finite Classical Groups
papers.abstract: Characters and Polynomiality for Maximal Parabolic Unipotent Radicals in Finite Classical GroupsLet $q$ be a power of an odd prime. For the unipotent radicals of maximal rational parabolic subgroups of the finite symplectic, orthogonal and unitary groups, we determine all complex irreducible characters, their values, and the number of characters of each degree. Each of these numbers is a polynomial in $q-1$ with nonnegative integer coefficients, in analogy with a conjecture of Isaacs for unitriangular groups. For the orthogonal radicals, the character table and the power maps do not depend on the Witt type of the residual form, whereas the isomorphism type of the radical does when the isotropic dimension is at least three and the residual dimension is positive and even. Consequently, for $3\le a\le n-1$ the radicals of the stabilizers of totally isotropic $a$-spaces in $\SO^+_{2n}(q)$ and $\SO^-_{2n}(q)$ form Brauer pairs; for $a\le n-2$ both stabilizers are maximal parabolic subgroups. Finally, we express the multiplicities through $R$-polynomials, with the unequal parameters $q^2,\dots,q^2,q$ in the unitary case.

papers.title: Nonlinear Inviscid Damping of Couette Flow with Vorticity Perturbations Supported up to the Boundary
papers.abstract: We establish nonlinear inviscid damping of the near-Couette flows in a finite channel, with vorticity perturbations vanishing to infinite order at the boundary. To study the boundary effect, we decompose the vorticity into dyadic layers whose supports expand toward the boundary, and use an inductive Newton scheme to track nonlinear interactions across layers. Finally, precise elliptic estimates are established to quantify the velocity generated by different layers.

papers.title: On Divisibility Properties of Zipf Law and Relatives
papers.abstract: We describe recursive chance mechanisms and processes involving Zipf's law and relatives, all showing up mixing properties, both geometric and Poisson. Relations to Markov processes are explored.

papers.title: Mackey formulas for smooth stacks
papers.abstract: We study parabolic induction and restriction functors on derived categories of constructible sheaves, D-modules, and other sheaf theories on smooth stacks with good or adequate moduli spaces. We prove a commutation rule between them in the form of a Mackey filtration, indexed by the set of relative positions of two elements in the component lattice, a combinatorial structure that characterizes inductions and restrictions on a given stack. This generalizes similar results for adjoint quotient stacks studied in generalized Springer theory and the theory of character sheaves, and for stacks of quiver representations appearing in Lusztig's categorification of quantum groups. We also apply our result to the stack of semistable principal bundles on a curve, as a first step towards Mackey formulas in geometric Langlands correspondences.

papers.title: Differentiability of Shape Function for Piecewise Smooth Lagrangians in Poissonian Random Environments
papers.abstract: We consider a family of models of directed first passage percolation type in continuous multi-dimensional Euclidean space and discrete time with admissible paths constrained to visiting a Poissonian point at each step. We show that even if the Lagrangian defining the cost or energy of a step is allowed to have gradient discontinuities, the resulting shape function, or effective Lagrangian, belongs to the class C1 and provide a formula for its gradient. We also study the limit shapes for the associated growth model. We show that the part of the boundary of the limit shape that can be called the effective front is also C1, and we describe the complementary part, the footprint. We include a study of several concrete examples and several simulations.

papers.title: A Sharp Bound for Additive Complements
papers.abstract: Let $A$ and $B$ be infinite sets of nonnegative integers whose sum contains all sufficiently large integers, and let $A(x)$ and $B(x)$ be their counting functions. We give a discrete proof of the sharp implication \[ \limsup_{x\to\infty}\frac{A(x)B(x)}{x}<\frac32 \quad\Longrightarrow\quad A(x)B(x)-x\longrightarrow+\infty. \] The constant $3/2$ is best possible. Using finite convolution sums, we show that a long gap in one set forces a gap in the other. We then compare the counting functions before and after the gap to obtain the sharp bound.

papers.title: Rigidity of the ball for Hartree-type energies and second shape derivative via a continuity argument
papers.abstract: We study the second shape derivative of an optimal design functional involving a nonlocal term in order to prove rigidity of the ball. Our approach relies on a continuity argument that relates the second variation to that of the corresponding local problem. The model serves as a prototype for a broader class of shape optimization problems to which the same strategy may be adapted.

papers.title: Saturating spaces for the squared-gradient nonlinearity on compact Riemannian manifolds via Nash embeddings
papers.abstract: We study the saturation property on smooth compact Riemannian manifolds without boundary. Starting from a finite-dimensional space of smooth functions, one considers successive iterations of the nonlinear map $f\mapsto|\nabla_g f|_g^2$ and convex combinations. We extend to the general setting of compact manifolds existing results on particular geometries, namely the torus, spheres and Lie groups. Our approach relies on the existence of an isometric embedding of the manifold into $\mathbb{R}^n$ due to Nash. As an application, we obtain global approximate controllability in arbitrarily small time for the bilinear Schrödinger equation on any connected compact Riemannian manifold, with finitely many potentials.

papers.title: Compression Formula for Nonattacking Fillings of Non-symmetric Macdonald Polynomials
papers.abstract: Macdonald polynomials are an important family of orthogonal polynomials that have applications to statistical physics. Corteel, Mandelshtam, and Williams proved a combinatorial model involving multiline queues for partitions; however, their work does not apply to weak compositions in general. We conjecture a first step towards this direction via a variant of the nonattacking filling model for nonsymmetric Macdonald Polynomials $E_μ$. This new model compresses the classical nonattacking filling model of Haglund, Haiman, and Loehr and mirrors the concept of trivial pairs in the multiline queue model. We prove it for a large family of weak compositions and explain the difficulty of extending this proof to the general case.

papers.title: Existence of Minimizers for the Gaussian Mumford-Shah Model via Covariance Floors on the Value Distribution
papers.abstract: The Gaussian Mumford-Shah model segments an image into regions by minimizing a continuous multivariate Gaussian negative log-likelihood term plus a perimeter penalty. It is used for scalar- and vector-valued images, in particular hyperspectral images, but the existence of a minimizer in general is not guaranteed. The energy is unbounded below whenever the covariance of a single region degenerates, regardless of the perimeter of the regions. A quantitative covariance floor on the covariances of all regions, or equivalently uniform Hölder continuity with exponent at most one of all one-dimensional marginals of the histogram, guarantees a lower bound on the energy and the existence of a minimizer. Our approach therefore shows that existence follows from a property of the histogram of the image, and we furthermore argue that scale-independent covariance floors cannot exist. Admitting a quantitative covariance floor is generic: it holds almost surely for all images with suitable noise. As applications of our theory, we show the convergence of regularized models used in practice and of numerical methods.

papers.title: Twisting of affine algebraic groups, III
papers.abstract: Let $G$ be an affine algebraic group over $\C$ and let $J$ be a Hopf $2$-cocycle for $\Os(G)$. We prove that one-sided cocycle twisting preserves Gelfand--Kirillov dimension and that $\Os(G)_J$ is simple if and only if $J$ is minimal. If $H$ is the support of $J$, we identify the primitive and maximal spectra of $\Os(G)_J$ with the closed points of $G/H$ and show that all primitive quotients are isomorphic to the minimal support algebra $\Os(H)_J$. In particular, the prime and Jacobson radicals vanish, and finite-dimensional irreducible modules exist exactly when $H$ is finite. For connected solvable $G$, we construct an iterated differential Ore presentation over an algebraic quantum torus and deduce that $\Os(G)_J$ is an affine Noetherian domain. We describe the torus-trivial Hopf $2$-cocycles on $\Os(G)$ using nilpotent solutions of the classical Yang--Baxter equation and identify their supports with the algebraic hulls of their carriers. We also separate the centrally supported toral sector and formulate a relative Hopf $2$-cocycle problem for the remaining classes. Finally, we compute multi-extended Jordanian examples, study a McConnell-type family of quantum differential algebras, and establish a conditional birational deletion criterion and a normal form when the unipotent radical has dimension at most one.

papers.title: Painlevé representations for joint moments of characteristic polynomials from the orthogonal and unitary symplectic groups
papers.abstract: We study joint moments of characteristic polynomials and their second derivatives for Haar-distributed matrices from the unitary symplectic and orthogonal groups. We establish their large-$N$ asymptotics throughout the full admissible range of the moment parameters and identify the limiting coefficients probabilistically in terms of the first inverse power sum of the Bessel point process. This extends the corresponding results of Assiotis, Gunes, Keating, and Wei [Proc. Lond. Math. Soc., 132 (2026), e70136] to the full admissible parameter range. Throughout this full range, we also express these limits in terms of a distinguished solution of the $σ$-Painlevé III' equation. Our approach reduces the problem to singular inverse-power statistics of the Jacobi unitary ensemble and combines their finite-$N$ $σ$-Painlevé V representation with a refined Riemann-Hilbert analysis yielding precise small-$x$ asymptotics and uniform derivative estimates for the finite-$N$ correction term. A key ingredient in the probabilistic identification is a kernel-based proof that the rescaled first inverse power sum of the Jacobi ensemble converges in distribution to its Bessel point process counterpart.

papers.title: Rudin's Problem on Uniformly Bounded Homogeneous Orthonormal Bases
papers.abstract: Rudin's problem asks whether, in the unit ball of $\mathbb C^d$ with $d\ge2$ fixed, the Hardy space $H^2(\partial\mathbb B_d)$ admits a uniformly bounded orthonormal basis consisting of homogeneous holomorphic polynomials. For $d=2$ and $d=3$ the answer is due to Bourgain, but the general-dimensional case has remained open. This paper gives an affirmative answer to Rudin's problem in every fixed dimension. More precisely, we prove that there is an orthonormal basis consisting of homogeneous polynomials $\{p_j\}_{j=1}^\infty$ of $H^2(\partial\mathbb B_d)$ such that $$\|p_j\|_{L^\infty(\partial\mathbb B_d)}\leq \exp\left(\frac12d\log d+O(d)\right).$$ Here the implicit constant in $O(d)$ is independent of $d$ and $j$.

papers.title: Germwise singular Fourier--Mukai partnerships
papers.abstract: We study how local behavior on the base controls whether integral transforms induce fully faithful functors or equivalences between singularity categories of proper flat families. By working with étale germs, we show (under mild hypotheses) that the loci where this happens are open and are compatible with étale base change. Moreover, we give examples, exhibit an autoequivalence of the singularity category which detects regularity of the base, and compute these loci for arithmetic families.

papers.title: Small-time approximate controllability of bilinear Schrödinger equations on compact normal homogeneous spaces
papers.abstract: We prove small-time global approximate controllability in $L^2$ for bilinear Schrödinger equations on compact connected normal homogeneous spaces. The controls act through finitely many smooth real-valued potentials. We first construct finite saturating families on compact connected Lie groups endowed with bi-invariant metrics, using Peter-Weyl theory and the Casimir operator. Their phase saturation contains the representative algebra and is therefore dense in $L^2$. We extend this construction to normal homogeneous quotients using finite generation of the algebra of highest-weight functions.
