papers.title: An exact formula for optimal axis-parallel packing of eight squares
papers.abstract: We determine the smallest square container for eight axis-parallel squares of prescribed side lengths. The optimal side length is the minimum of the costs of 23 explicit packing strategies, and each cost is a maximum of sums of side lengths. No minimum of fewer convex functions represents it. Three strategies suffice for seven squares; the jump to 23 for eight squares witnesses the beginning of a combinatorial explosion. We prove the formula by combining the constructions with geometric lower bounds derived from disjoint coordinate projections, cornering arguments, and a weighted area comparison.

papers.title: Extremals for Sharp Trace Gagliardo--Nirenberg--Sobolev Inequalities on Convex Cones
papers.abstract: Zugmeyer~\cite{Zug} established sharp trace Gagliardo--Nirenberg--Sobolev inequalities on convex cones for $a\geq n>p>1$. We classify all nonzero real-valued extremals of these inequalities. Let the cone be the epigraph of a finite convex function that is positively homogeneous of degree one, and let $H$ be any norm. We prove that equality holds precisely for functions of the form $A H(x+te+\ell)^{-(a-p)/(p-1)}$, where $A\in\mathbb{R}\backslash\{0\}$, $t>0$, $e=(0,\ldots,0,1)$, and $\ell$ belongs to the largest vector subspace contained in the cone. The result includes the critical Sobolev trace inequality at $a=n$, as well as nonsmooth norms and cones, half-spaces, and cones containing lines.

papers.title: Quadratic hulls of osculating varieties of rational normal curves
papers.abstract: Let $T^p c_r$ be the $p$-osculating variety of the rational normal curve $c_r\subset\mathbb{P}S^r(\mathbb{C}^2)$. We study its quadratic hull, the scheme defined by the quadratic equations vanishing on $T^p c_r$. For $r\ge2p+3$, we prove that this scheme is a complete intersection of $\binom{r-2p}{2}$ quadrics whenever \[ p\ge\binom{r-2p-1}{2}. \] When the inequality is strict, the hull is integral and strictly contains $T^p c_r$. On the boundary its support is reducible, except for $(p,r)=(1,5)$, where the hull equals the osculating variety. The proof is local at the highest weight point. Koornwinder's relation between Clebsch--Gordan coefficients and Hahn polynomials leads to a description of the tangent-cone equations in which each antidiagonal becomes an ordinary polynomial space of bounded degree. An incidence estimate then gives a normal integral tangent cone in the strict range, and the $SL_2$-action turns this local statement into global integrality.

papers.title: Photonic band structure by direct second-kind free-space boundary integral equations
papers.abstract: We present a direct boundary integral equation (BIE) formulation of the Bloch eigenvalue problem for two-dimensional photonic crystals that uses only the free-space Helmholtz Green function. The unknowns are the Cauchy data of the Bloch mode on the inclusion boundary and on two cell walls. On the inclusion boundary, the transmission conditions are imposed via Müller's formulation. The wall equations, in turn, come from a stack formulation, in which Green's formula is applied on stacks of three cells, so that the wall self-interactions and the interactions between arcs sharing endpoints cancel exactly. The resulting system is of the second kind, Fredholm of index zero, and free of corner singularities, and the walls may be curved to keep the cell boundary away from the inclusions. Its operators are assembled once per frequency and reused for all Bloch vectors. We prove that every Bloch mode yields a nonzero null vector, and that a null vector comes from a Bloch mode exactly when its cell representation vanishes outside the cell, which gives an inexpensive test for spurious null vectors. The band frequencies are computed with a high-order Nyström discretization and the search of Bruno, Santana and Trefethen, which locates them as poles of adaptive Antoulas--Anderson (AAA) rational approximants to a randomly scalarized resolvent sampled on the real frequency axis. Numerical examples validate the method against exact and published band structures and include a challenging triangular lattice of air pores in a dielectric, whose cell requires curved walls.

papers.title: Discrete Exterior Calculus-based Whittle-Matérn Fields on Meshes
papers.abstract: This work presents a sparse precision formulation for Whittle-Matérn fields based on Discrete Exterior Calculus. By treating the $k$-cochain as the latent object to be modeled, we show that a single formulation can produce Whittle-Matérn fields for all $k$ and integer $α$ values. By utilising Whitney maps we can enable a push-forward of the prior on 1-cochains, enabling inference for discrete vector fields. We demonstrate this model on interpolation of vector fields on a sphere.

papers.title: Liouville Theorems for Semilinear Parabolic Equations Involving the Nonlinear Gradient Term
papers.abstract: In this paper, we prove the Liouville-type theorem for equation $u_t-Δu=u^p+M|\nabla u|^q$ via the integral Bernstein method, where $q=2p/(p+1)$ is critical and $M<0$. As an application, we can establish a universal priori estimate for this equation by using the doubling lemma. These results generalize the previous work of Liang and Zhang. We can also prove the Liouville-type theorem for equation $u_t-Δu=u^p+M|\nabla u|^2$, which corresponds to the supercritical case.

papers.title: A single generation theorem for simple unital $C^*$-algebras with CPoU and comparison
papers.abstract: In this note, assuming the finite factor generation theorem obtained by OpenAI, we demonstrate that if a separable simple unital $C^*$-algebra $A$ with nonempty trace space, has the strict comparison for positive elements, and its uniform tracial completion has complemented partitions of unity (CPoU), then $A$ is singly generated.

papers.title: Counting Bessel zeros and applications
papers.abstract: We establish o-minimal definability results and develop point-counting machinery applicable to the zeros of a Bessel function of fixed non-negative real parameter. We also give an Ax-Schanuel theorem for Bessel functions of fixed (complex) parameters and exponential functions. We combine these to prove a sparsity result (weak Manin-Mumford) for points on an algebraic variety whose coordinates are zeros of a Bessel function of fixed (non-negative real) parameter. We apply this result to improve density results on spectral sets for the unit ball motivated by Fuglede's conjecture.

papers.title: On the Geometry of Low Rank Correlation Matrices
papers.abstract: Correlation matrices of bounded rank form a stratified space whose factor representations lie in a product of spheres. Using the orbit-type description of the rank stratification, we prove that padding factors preserves the Riemannian geometry of each fixed-rank stratum and the intrinsic length metric of every rank-bounded subset. In the reduced model, a Sylvester equation describes the mechanical connection and its horizontal lifts. We derive sectional-curvature formulas and bounds, characterize zero-curvature directions, and determine the connection's holonomy groups. In particular, a flat rank-two connection can have nontrivial dihedral holonomy. For geodesics subject to a rank bound, rank cannot decrease in the interior of a minimizing segment with maximal-rank endpoints; the local excess over the unconstrained quotient distance is controlled by a dimension-independent cubic estimate. Finally, we compute the exact change of measure between quotient Riemannian volume and Euclidean surface volume in the off-diagonal entries. Coarea yields explicit factor densities for both normalized uniform laws.

papers.title: C*-selflessness and $\mathcal{Z}$-stability for Thompson's group $F$
papers.abstract: We prove that the reduced C*-algebra of Thompson's group $F$ is $\mathcal{Z}$-stable and selfless.

papers.title: On the stability of displacement energy in toric manifolds
papers.abstract: We present a quantitative exploration of the behaviour of displacement energy of Lagrangians under stabilization. In particular, we completely characterize the displacement behaviour of toric fibres in Fano 4-manifolds. Our approach relates the geometry of the moment polytope's caustic to the structure of the (bulk-deformed) superpotential and to the presence of symmetric probes.

papers.title: Independent transversals in hypergraphs with low codegrees
papers.abstract: We prove that for every fixed $r\geq3$, $k>0$ and $\varepsilon\in(0,1)$, there is $γ>0$ such that the following holds for all sufficiently large $b$. An $r$-uniform hypergraph $\mathcal H$ whose vertex set is partitioned into parts of size at least $b$ contains at least $\lceil(1-\varepsilon)b\rceil$ pairwise vertex-disjoint independent transversals, provided that the average degree in each part is at most $kb^{r-1}$ and maximum $j$-codegree $Δ_j(\mathcal H)\leqγb^{r-j}$ for $2\leq j<r$. Under the same average degree, if $q$ is the minimum part size and $Δ_j(\mathcal H)=o(q^{r-j})$ for $2\leq j<r$, the maximum number of pairwise vertex-disjoint independent transversals is $(1-o(1))q$ as $q\to\infty$. We develop an iterative halving reduction for partitioned hypergraphs to apply the theorem of Delcourt and Postle on matchings avoiding forbidden submatchings.

papers.title: ACM, almost Ulrich, and Ulrich vector bundles arising from Frobenius
papers.abstract: Let $X$ be a smooth projective variety of dimension $n$ over an algebraically closed field of positive characteristic. We investigate ACM, almost Ulrich (both ACM and weakly Ulrich), and Ulrich properties of the sheaves of locally exact and closed $i$-forms $B_X^i$, $Z_X^i$. These cohomological properties are closely related to the fundamental concepts of Frobenius splitting and ordinarity. Joshi studied the sheaf $B^1_X$ in this context in \cite{MR3920911, MR4206787}, including ACM and almost Ulrich twists of $B^1_X$. However, varieties with Ulrich twisted $B_X^1$ have not been classified for $n\ge2$. We classify subcanonical polarized varieties with initialized ACM $B^i_X(aH)$ for $i=1, n$ and prove that, for $n \ge 2$, varieties with ACM $B^i_X$ for all $i \le \left\lceil\frac{n}{2}\right\rceil$ are ordinary. When $X$ is ordinary with trivial $Ω^1_X$, almost Ulrich twists of $B^i_X$ and $F_*^e(Z_X^i(aH))$ are determined. We classify polarized varieties $(X,H)$ with $B_X^i(aH)$ Ulrich when $n=1, 2$, and establish strong necessary criteria for $n \geq 3$, together with an example. We also prove that $Z_X^i(aH)$ is never Ulrich. Finally, we classify polarized abelian varieties with Ulrich $B^1_X \otimes L$ allowing twists by arbitrary line bundles.

papers.title: Backward Homogeneous Heat Equation with $Ψ$-Caputo Time Derivative and Spectral Fractional Laplacian
papers.abstract: In this work, we study a fractional diffusion model in time and space, formulated in an open and bounded domain, involving a Caputo fractional derivative of order $μ\in(0,1)$ with respect to a time scale function $Ψ$, together with a spectral fractional Laplacian operator of order $s\in(0,1)$. The associated direct problem is analyzed, as well as the inverse problem of temporal reconstruction from final data, which is inherently ill-posed. Through a spectral representation, the instability of the problem and the effect of the choice of the function $Ψ$ on the amplification of spectral modes are examined.

papers.title: Linear Axiomatization of Linear Differential Equations
papers.abstract: This article presents an axiomatization of linear differential equations that is complete for topologically open properties with compact initial conditions and time horizons by proving them deductively via a sound reduction to formulas of linear real arithmetic. Indeed, linearity is preserved: linear differential invariants are complete for open properties of linear differential equations and reduce with a linear number of Lie derivatives (per atom) to linear real arithmetic. In particular, this article shows that the linear fragment of differential dynamic logic (dL), a modal extension of standard first-order logic over the reals satisfies these completeness properties. By establishing completeness within decidable linear real arithmetic, the need for proving sophisticated nonlinear formulas of real arithmetic is circumvented. Furthermore, this article establishes generalizations to the nonlinear fragment of dL that enable the practical certification of reachability computations, validating the output of external computations in dL with machine-checkable proofs.

papers.title: Hyperbolic comparison and rigidity for the hyperspherical radius
papers.abstract: We prove Gromov's hyperbolic hyperspherical radius comparison and rigidity conjectures in all dimensions $n\ge3$, without the spin assumption. Let $(X^n, g)$ be a smooth, oriented, connected, compact Riemannian manifold with nonempty smooth connected boundary $S$. If ${\rm Sc}_g\ge -n(n-1)$ and $H_S\ge (n-1)\coth R$ for some $R>0$, then ${\rm Rad}(S,g_S)\le\sinh R$, with equality if and only if $(X^n,g)$ is isometric to the closed hyperbolic geodesic ball of radius $R$. Under the same curvature bounds, every smooth $1$-Lipschitz map of nonzero degree from $S$ to the boundary of the hyperbolic geodesic ball of radius $R$ extends to an isometry of the fillings. Here, $g_S$ is the induced boundary metric, $H_S$ is the mean curvature of $S$ with respect to the outward unit normal, and ${\rm Rad}(S,g_S)$ denotes the hyperspherical radius.

papers.title: Real-analytic standard families and rotational invariant curves
papers.abstract: In this paper we study one-parameter families of exact standard maps of the form $$\widehat{f}_{k,g}(\widehat{x},\widehat{y}) =\bigl(\widehat{x}+\widehat{y}+kg(\widehat{x}) \bmod 1,\widehat{y}+kg(\widehat{x})\bigr),$$ where $k$ is a real parameter and $g:\mathbb{T} \rightarrow \mathbb{R}$ is real-analytic, 1-periodic and has zero mean. The most famous example is when $g(\widehat{x})=\frac{\sin(2π\widehat{x})}{2π}$. In this case, the closed subset $A_{\sin(2π\cdot)/(2π)}\subset \mathbb{R}$ of values of $k$ for which $\widehat{f}_{k,\sin(2π\cdot)/(2π)}$ has rotational invariant curves is conjectured to be a closed interval. Much has been done towards this conjecture, both numerically and analytically. But a complete proof has not yet been achieved. Our approach here goes in the opposite direction: we construct a function $θ:\mathbb{T} \rightarrow \mathbb{R}$ satisfying the above conditions, such that $A_θ$ is not an interval: It contains at least 2 different connected components, which are non-degenerate closed intervals.

papers.title: Geometric chains of orbifolds with corners and singular homology
papers.abstract: We study a geometric homology theory (GHT for short). Its chains are generated by smooth maps from compact oriented orbifolds with corners to a smooth space, and two kinds of chains are set to zero: those admitting an orientation reversing automorphism, and degenerate ones, which, together with their boundaries, factor through smooth maps to orbifolds of lower dimension. Bisecting the source of a geometric chain along a hypersurface transverse to its corners changes the chain only by the boundary of an explicit prism and by prisms over its faces; cutting a geometric cycle along a regular level set of a smooth function on the target does not change its homology class. Geometric chains also behave well under products and pullbacks along fibre bundles, which overcomes some of the combinatorial rigidity of singular chains. We prove that geometric homology is naturally isomorphic to singular homology with rational coefficients for every smooth space admitting a good cover, such as smooth manifolds, orbifolds and locally finite polyhedra, and also for orbifolds with corners. The proof uses cutting operators along level sets of functions on the target, realized by explicit prisms, instead of triangulations. For continuous maps into arbitrary spaces we conjecture the same statement, and prove it for Euclidean neighbourhood retracts in degrees at most one, with surjectivity in degree two. Without the relation killing degenerate chains the comparison fails for orbifold chains: the weighted projective plane $\mathbb{P}(1,1,p)$, $p\ge5$ prime, mapped to a point is a cycle that does not bound. Applications on Morse theory and the BV structure on geometric chains of moduli spaces of bordered Riemann surfaces, following Costello and Harrelson--Voronov--Zúñiga, are given.

papers.title: Scaling limits for peeling explorations of the Brownian half-plane
papers.abstract: We construct and study peeling explorations of the Brownian half-plane by successively revealing hulls of fixed radius. We prove that for any peeling process, as the radius of the hulls tends to zero, the sequence of discovered hulls converges to an explicit family of Brownian disks. We also consider the particular case of what we call nearest-neighbour peeling explorations, where the center of each new hull is chosen on the outer boundary of the previously discovered hull, naturally giving rise to an exploration curve. We provide scaling limits results for these curves, jointly with the convergence of the associated boundary-length and volume processes.

papers.title: Do Neural Models Prefer Their Submodels?
papers.abstract: A neural model is the set of functions that can be expressed by a given neural network architecture. Neural models contain natural submodels, such as those obtained by setting some neurons to be inactive. We study the geometry of neural models and ask whether they prefer their submodels. By this we mean whether local minimizers of the loss function lie in a given submodel. We introduce a geometric framework to determine if this occurs. For shallow multilayer perceptrons, we show that subnetworks with inactive hidden neurons are never preferred. For deep multilayer perceptrons, we give conditions under which subnetworks with inactive hidden neurons are not preferred. For lightning self-attention, lower-rank submodels are usually not preferred, but we identify examples where they are because they lie on a boundary of the model. Our results show that, aside from a few exceptions, preference for submodels cannot be explained by the geometry of the neural model, and must instead come from other sources such as training dynamics.

papers.title: Transversality at Virtual Centers
papers.abstract: We consider the family of transcendental meromorphic functions with finitely many singular values, none of whose asymptotic values is infinity. We prove that transversality holds at any boundary point of a shell component in a dynamically natural slice of the parameter space at which an asymptotic value is a prepole.

papers.title: Brunn-Minkowski inequality for p-capacity of compact sets
papers.abstract: We prove the capacitary Brunn-Minkowski inequality for arbitrary nonempty compact sets in $\mathbb R^n$, $n\geq2$, and every $1<p<\infty$, with no assumption of convexity, connectedness, interior, or boundary regularity. For $1<p<n$ the inequality is for the variational $p$-capacity. For $p>n$ it is for the capacity determined by the constant term at infinity of the normalized $p$-harmonic Green's function with pole at infinity, and for $p=n$ for an outer regularization of this quantity, which agrees with it for $n$-regular sets and in the plane is a constant multiple of logarithmic capacity. In particular, it holds for Newtonian capacity of all compact sets in $\mathbb R^n$, $n\geq3$, and for logarithmic capacity of all planar compact sets. Previously these inequalities were known for convex sets and, for logarithmic capacity, for planar continua. When both capacities are positive, equality holds for $0<λ<1$ if and only if the filled sets, obtained by adjoining the bounded components of the complement, are convex and equal up to translation and dilation. This characterization is new for nonconvex sets, even for Newtonian and logarithmic capacity.

papers.title: Determinant characters and multiplicative solubility of finite skew braces
papers.abstract: Let $B$ be a finite skew brace. We prove that if the additive derived subgroup $(B,+)'$ is nilpotent, then the multiplicative group $(B,\cdot)$ is soluble. In particular, this holds for finite skew braces with supersoluble or metabelian additive group.

papers.title: Convergence and semisimplicity of big quantum cohomology of flag varieties
papers.abstract: We prove the folklore conjecture that the big quantum cohomology of a flag variety $G/P$ of general Lie type is convergent near the large-radius limit and is generically semisimple. The convergence relies on a slightly modified version of Iritani's reconstruction theorem, together with Cauchy's formula that avoids directly taking the non-equivariant limit at the origin. Generic semisimplicity follows from a surprising application of the big quantum $D$-module mirror symmetry for $G/P$ established by the first, third and fourth authors jointly with Hinault and Zhang. Moreover, we prove the regularity conjecture on the big quantum cohomology of $G/P$ formulated by Perrin and Smirnov, which implies generic semisimplicity.

papers.title: Bounded Symbols and One-Component Inner Functions
papers.abstract: Let $θ$ be a nonconstant inner function, we prove that every bounded truncated Toeplitz operator on the model space $K_θ=H^2\ominusθH^2$ admits a bounded symbol if and only if $θ$ is one-component, that is, if $\{z\in\mathbb D:|θ(z)|<r\}$ is nonempty and connected for some $r\in(0,1)$. This establishes the previously open necessary direction and resolves a conjecture of Baranov, Chalendar, Fricain, Mashreghi, and Timotin. For every non-one-component inner function, we construct a sequence of norm-one rank-one truncated Toeplitz operators whose infimal $L^\infty$-norms over all representing symbols tend to infinity. The quantitative lower bound is obtained by forming two inner divisors from angularly separated parts of the zero set and singular measure. The argument applies without restrictions on the Blaschke or singular parts of $θ$. The order of this lower bound is sharp, already for a family of degree-two Blaschke products. A continuation argument for local inverse branches produces the required sequence of points. Consequently, every non-one-component model space supports a trace-class truncated Toeplitz operator without a bounded symbol. Combined with known equivalences, the characterization also yields geometric criteria for weak factorization and for continuous-symbol representations of compact truncated Hankel operators.

papers.title: A Convex Feasibility Problem for Which Douglas-Rachford Converges Only Weakly
papers.abstract: We provide two closed, convex sets with nonempty intersection and an initial point for which the Douglas-Rachford algorithm converges weakly but not strongly. This resolves an open question as noted earlier by Aragón Artacho, Borwein and Tam (2014, Remark 2.2). Our construction is a simple lift of a recent construction by Bauschke and Tung concerning firmly nonexpansive operators.

papers.title: Forbidden graded posets in middle levels: supersaturation, enumeration and randomness
papers.abstract: Let $P$ be a fixed finite poset whose maximal chains all have $h$ elements, and let $\mathcal W_{n,h}$ be the union of $h$ consecutive middle levels of $2^{[n]}$. We prove that the maximum size of a $P$-free subfamily of $\mathcal W_{n,h}$ is $(π(P)+o(1))M_n$ for a constant $π(P)$, where $M_n=\binom n{\lfloor n/2\rfloor}$, and that the number of $P$-free subfamilies is $2^{(π(P)+o(1))M_n}$. For connected $P$ we prove supersaturation above $(π(P)+ε)M_n$ and determine, in terms of the coordinate patterns of the copies of $P$ in the window, a range of $p$ in which the largest $P$-free subfamily of the random family $\mathcal W_{n,h}(p)$ has size $(π(P)+o(1))pM_n$ and a range in which it has size $(h+o(1))pM_n$; the two ranges meet whenever all copies have the same pattern. For the Boolean poset $Q_d$, which has height $d+1$, the threshold order in the corresponding window $\mathcal W_{n,d+1}$ is $n^{-d/(2^d-1)}$, and $π_d=π(Q_d)$ satisfies $(d+1)λ_d\leπ_d\le d+1-\binom d{\lfloor d/2\rfloor}^{-1}$, where $λ_d$ is the vertex Turán density of $d$-dimensional subcubes in the hypercube. Together with a construction of Ellis, Ivan and Leader this gives $d+1-π_d=\exp(-Θ(d))$. For the diamond, known bounds give $2.1479\leπ_2\le2.15121$.

papers.title: Near-blowup asymptotic analysis and analytical extension for the inviscid primitive equations
papers.abstract: The primitive equations widely approximate the Navier--Stokes equations in large-scale geophysical fluid dynamics. Their finite-time singularity formation-which occurs exclusively in the inviscid case-sheds light on the mechanisms driving small-scale creation. Building on \cite{Collot2023}, which constructed 2D horizontally odd solutions where the on-axis derivative $\partial_X u(t,0,Z)$ blows up at rate $(T-t)^{-1}$ with boundary concentration scale $|\ln (T-t)|^{-1}$, this paper characterizes this blow-up as forming between hyperbolic stagnation points. We derive precise asymptotic expansions for on-axis derivatives beyond leading order, identifying a horizontal concentration scale of $(T-t)^{3/2}$ characteristic of generic Burgers' singularities. Furthermore, we justify the 2D solution's expansion near the symmetry axis by proving $(T-t)^{3/2}$ is a universal lower bound on the radius of analyticity.

papers.title: Sprinkling for random regular graphs and Kim-Vu's sandwich conjecture
papers.abstract: We show that the uniform random $d$-regular graph model on $n$ vertices is, in total variation distance, asymptotically close to the union of $d$ uniformly random edge-disjoint perfect matchings, provided that $n$ is even and $ω(1) = d \leq n^{1/10}$. This confirms a conjecture by Hollom, Lichev, Mond, Portier, and Wang for this range of parameters. This result has a couple of interesting consequences. First, this shows that random $d$-regular graphs on $n$ vertices exhibit sprinkling properties for some range of parameters, thereby confirming a conjecture by Isaev, McKay, Southwell and Zhukovskii in that range. Second, we give a short alternative proof of the upper side of Kim-Vu's sandwich conjecture in the sparse regime.

papers.title: On complete morphisms of Butson Hadamard matrices
papers.abstract: A complete morphism of Butson classes replaces each entry of a matrix in $\mathrm{BH}(n,k)$ by an $m \times m$ block, uniformly, to produce a matrix in $\mathrm{BH}(mn,t)$. We show that every complete morphism is described by a pair $(U,Z)$, where $Z \in \mathrm{BH}(m,t)$ and $U$ is a unitary matrix annihilated by the $k^{\textrm{th}}$ cyclotomic polynomial. We deduce from a theorem of Lam and Leung that complete morphisms onto real Hadamard matrices exist precisely when $k$ is a power of $2$. The exponent-reducing morphisms of Östergård--Paavola and Ó Catháin--Swartz achieve the smallest block size the degree bound allows, and we show that there are no other complete morphisms for which $U$ is monomial. We construct new complete morphisms where $U$ is not monomial: a complete morphism $\mathrm{BH}(n,7) \rightarrow \mathrm{BH}(6n,6)$ is given, the first to eliminate a prime from the alphabet.

papers.title: Budgeted Admission from Timestamped Capacity Records in Shared Clusters
papers.abstract: A cluster admission gate can receive a capacity record that no longer matches current schedulability. We study one exogenous binary schedulability unit under a bound on the joint probability of admission and unavailability. For a symmetric Markov state, we derive the stationary admission frontier for a fixed observation delay and apply finite likelihood allocation to a delay-tagged delivered record. A one-sided exact binomial endpoint calibrates each fitted policy, and exact enumeration confirms the per-policy confidence target in every tested parameter cell. A separate deterministic guard charges every unresolved admission against the realized allowance and bounds unavailable-state admissions at every prefix under truthful outcome feedback. An executable admission procedure composes the allocation and guard. The controlled system binds source sampling, NATS delivery, randomized admission, Kubernetes objects, and API-derived outcomes in one append-only record. Independent audit finds no missing event, identity mismatch, or state mismatch in the completed functional block. A separate CPU request-accounting check preserves Job and Pod identity across an unschedulable-to-complete transition.

papers.title: Sharp Bounds for Nodal Sets of Steklov Eigenfunctions on Smooth Surfaces
papers.abstract: We prove a sharp linear upper bound for the interior nodal length of Steklov eigenfunctions on smooth compact Riemannian surfaces with boundary, establishing the upper bound predicted by the Steklov analogue of Yau's conjecture in dimension two. On each fixed surface, we also show that the nodal length divided by the logarithm of the eigenvalue tends to infinity, uniformly over the eigenfunctions. We construct examples to show this divergence can be arbitrarily slow. These examples rule out every general lower bound by a positive power of the eigenvalue, in contrast with the linear lower bound on analytic surfaces by Polterovich-Sher-Toth. Moreover, boundary zero counts and both interior and boundary nodal domain counts satisfy sharp linear bounds for large eigenvalues. We also prove density estimates for boundary zeros on at least one boundary component and construct a fixed analytic cylinder on which another component remains free of boundary zeros along an unbounded sequence of eigenvalues.

papers.title: A note on the cube inequality
papers.abstract: In this note, we adapt ideas from No. 336 of OpenAI's October 6, 2026 mathematics release to prove the weighted cube inequality in all dimensions.

papers.title: Szarek and Ball made simple
papers.abstract: We present proofs of Szarek's moment comparison and Ball's cube slicing inequalities based on elementary convexity and majorisation. The key ingredient is a moment-lifting argument which allows us to use Schur monotonicity, avoiding the integral inequalities used in the original Fourier-analytic approaches.

papers.title: Near Optimal Finite Model POMDP Approximation of Controlled Diffusion with Partial Information
papers.abstract: We study continuous-time stochastic control problems under partial information. Our main contributions are the following: (i) We show near optimality, under finite horizon as well as discounted infinite horizon cost criteria, of piece-wise constant control policies obtained via solutions to discrete-time partially observable Markov decision process (POMDP) approximations, constructed via Euler-Maruyama approximations of both state and observation processes; (ii) we obtain several regularity properties of such POMDP approximate models; and (iii) using these regularity properties, we arrive at near optimal finite model approximations. (iv) These culminate into our main result which is that an optimal solution for the approximate finite POMDP model is near optimal for the original diffusion with partial information.

papers.title: Avoiding abelian squares with three colours in the continuous setting
papers.abstract: An $n$-colouring of the real line is a Lebesgue measurable function $f \colon \mathbb{R} \to A$, where $A$ is a set of $n$ colours. An abelian square for $f$ is a finite interval $U\subseteq \mathbb{R}$ where every colour shows up in the left and in the right half of $U$ with exactly the same Lebesgue measure. It is known that every $2$-colouring contains an abelian square. On the other hand, Alon, Grytczuk, Laso{ń}, and Michałek (2009) proved that there exist $4$-colourings that avoid abelian squares, while the question for $3$-colourings remained open. We construct a $3$-colouring that avoids abelian squares, disproving a conjecture of Laso{ń} (2015). However, in contrast to the case of 4-colourings, the set of 3-colourings that avoid abelian squares is meagre. We show this using an argument based on the KKM lemma.

papers.title: Interior $C^2$ Estimates and a Liouville Theorem for the Complex Monge--Ampère Equation
papers.abstract: We establish an interior $C^2$ estimate for locally bounded plurisubharmonic Bedford-Taylor solutions of the complex Monge--Ampère equation $\det(u_{i\bar j})=f$ under weak quadratic growth bounds on sufficiently large balls, where $f$ is positive and Dini-continuous. We assume a distributional lower bound for the Laplacian of $f^{1/n}$. The main ingredient is a pseudo-$C^2$ estimate using the Green-function averaging error, valid also when $f$ is nonnegative. As an application, we prove that every entire Bedford-Taylor solution of $\det(u_{i\bar j})=1$ with weak quadratic growth is a real quadratic polynomial, resolving a conjecture of Gábor Székelyhidi.

papers.title: Fast and scalable multi-GPU sliced FFT solvers for asymptotically compatible discretizations of 3D nonlocal diffusion problems
papers.abstract: Large-scale 3D peridynamic transient diffusion simulations are constrained by the computational cost and memory requirements of nonlocal interactions. We propose a fast and scalable multi-GPU sliced FFT algorithm based on the recently developed asymptotically compatible finite difference (ACFD) scheme. By exploiting the discrete operator's structure and finite interaction range, the algorithm combines FFT acceleration with local inter-GPU communication. It preserves the ACFD scheme while avoiding the global data redistribution required by full 3D FFTs. We build a matrix-free GPU conjugate gradient (CG) solver, use multigrid preconditioning to reduce iteration counts, and introduce a human-audited configuration agent for efficient cross-level configuration. Strong-scaling tests show that sliced FFT-CG achieves 93.2% parallel efficiency on eight GPUs, compared with 28.2% for full FFT-CG on the same problem and hardware. The framework supports approximately 10.29 billion degrees of freedom on eight RTX 4090 GPUs with 24 GB of memory each. The insulated penny-shaped cutout benchmark demonstrates transient simulation with approximately 8.58 billion degrees of freedom. Three-dimensional star-shaped interface evolution further demonstrates convergence toward the local solution in a nonlinear phase-field problem. These results demonstrate that sliced FFT provides a scalable multi-GPU approach for fast computation of 3D peridynamic diffusion.

papers.title: Thin-Layer Dichotomy in Three-Phase Mullins-Sekerka Flow: Gap Dynamics and Composite Interfaces
papers.abstract: We study the thin-layer limit of the Mullins-Sekerka flow in concentric circular geometries at fixed wave number $k$, contrasting a two-phase annulus with a genuine three-phase layer. A dichotomy emerges: for $k\ge2$ the rates blow up like the inverse thickness when the same phase lies on both sides of the layer, whereas between two different phases the matrix governing the linearized Fourier mode extends analytically to zero thickness. Both cases share the singular Dirichlet-to-Neumann factor of the thin annulus and differ only in whether the Gibbs-Thomson law forces an order-one potential difference across it. In the three-phase case the pure thickness-modulation rate stays below the logarithmic growth rate of the mean thickness, for every $k\ge1$ and all positive tensions, and, after projection onto the mean displacement and the outer interface, the collapsed pair moves as one interface carrying the sum of the two tensions. All statements concern the instantaneous fixed-mode linearization. The singularity is a property of the phase coupling, not of the thin geometry.

papers.title: A General Construction of Strict Models in HoTT
papers.abstract: Homotopy type theory (HoTT) provides a natural setting for studying the metatheory of type theory, as it comes with additional extensionality principles compared to ordinary Martin-Löf type theory. In particular, it is especially suitable for developing semantics of type theory, where one distinguishes two kinds of models: strict models, which give us sound interpretations, and pseudomodels. Pseudomodels are useful as they occur prevalently and can be turned into strict models by constructions called strictifications. However, the commonly used strictifications do not translate well to HoTT, as they require assumptions that are generally not satisfied by concrete examples of models. We show how to carry out the universe model construction, due to Voevodsky, in HoTT. Under this construction, every pseudomodel together with a universe type closed under enough type formers gives rise to a strict model. We also show how to interpret type formers in the resulting model assuming that the universe is closed under them. Finally, we demonstrate that this construction generalises existing instances of strict set models in the literature, and we apply it to more examples, yielding presheaf models and assembly models of type theory in HoTT. Our results are formalised in Rocq using the UniMath library.

papers.title: Confessions of a Masked MDP
papers.abstract: In reinforcement learning, one presumes the action set to be known ahead of time, and, thus, one must know if any state-action pairs are not permissible ahead of computations. In some applications, determining this action mask is the main computational bottleneck. Isolating this problem to highlight its core properties, we study how to combine the search for an optimal policy with the learning of the mask itself, under a linear MDP model in which each attempted action reveals the exact value of a linear score determining its validity. In this framework, we first construct an algorithm based on deterministic optimistic optimization and show that it is minimax optimal, which we show is also computationally efficient. However, it is sub-optimal on non-degenerate instances, as we show. We propose an alternative, which is also computationally efficient, which plans its exploration strategy. This algorithm admits a formal interpretation as an analogue of information-directed-sampling for deterministic feedback, which may be of independent interest. Finally, we study an application of this framework to transfer learning, where the invalid action set changes over time.

papers.title: Economic resources, sporting efficiency and uncertainty: a global test on the 2026 FIFA world cup
papers.abstract: A related paper (arXiv:2610.06967) developed a stochastic optimization framework in which football performance combines GDP/population-based potential with a latent mean-reverting efficiency process. The framework was applied to a cross-section of the 24 national teams participating in AFCON 2025. This paper applies the same methodology to the full 48-team 2026 FIFA World Cup, extending the analysis beyond Africa without modifying the underlying model. Using GDP, population, FIFA ranking data, and complete tournament outcomes, it evaluates the framework against a global sample spanning all six confederations. Two findings emerge. First, GDP and population explain only 9 percent of single-tournament performance variance, compared with 33 percent for FIFA points. This gap is consistent with the model's distinction between systematic performance and match-specific idiosyncratic shocks. Second, using the less noisy FIFA-points measure, the African pattern persists globally: Morocco, Senegal, Argentina, Croatia, Portugal, and Uruguay emerge as leading GDP-relative over-performers. Conversely, several major economies, including the United States, Germany, Japan, and South Korea, underperform their GDP-implied potential. As in the related paper, we interpret the residual as a symmetric, non-structurally identified conditional performance residual, rather than an SFA-consistent efficiency estimate. We also quantify the extent to which its cross-country variance mechanically reflects the underlying performance measure. The GDP-rank/simulated-performance-rank correlation is robust to the choice of the model's unidentified dynamic parameters across a wide grid.

papers.title: Attracting Rotations Obstruct Almost-Global Consensus on Spheres over Strongly Connected Graphs
papers.abstract: We study discrete-time consensus on the Euclidean unit sphere, where weighted combinations of neighboring states are normalized to unit length. For symmetric weights on connected undirected graphs and ambient dimension $d\ge3$, earlier results establish instability of non-consensus fixed points under suitable weight conditions. For directed graphs on the unit circle, earlier results show that fixed points other than consensus and antipodal configurations occur only for a measure-zero set of weights. We show that these conclusions do not extend directly to general strongly connected directed graphs in higher dimensions. First, we construct full-rank non-consensus fixed points whose tangent eigenvalues all equal one, showing that strict linear instability need not hold. In a separate construction, for every $d\ge3$, we present a sparse strongly connected graph admitting full-rank fixed points on an open set of its permitted weights. Our main result establishes robust counterexamples to almost-global consensus: attracting rotating motions exist for $d=2$ with every $n\ge3$ and for $d=3$ with every $n\ge6$. These motions are locally asymptotically stable modulo common rotations and have asymptotic phase. They persist on open sets of strictly positive weight matrices. For each such matrix, an open set of initial configurations approaches neither consensus nor any fixed configuration. Thus the absence of full-rank non-consensus fixed points does not ensure almost-global convergence to consensus.

papers.title: First-Order Mean Field Games with Time-Measurable and $C ^{1,1}$ Hamiltonians: Analysis and Approximation
papers.abstract: We introduce and analyze a numerical framework for a class of first-order, non-local Mean Field Game (MFG) systems with two sources of low regularity: the time-dependent data are merely measurable, and the Hamiltonian is only of class $C^{1,1}$ with respect to the momentum variable. The proposed method combines a semi-Lagrangian approximation of the Hamilton--Jacobi--Bellman equation with a Lagrange--Galerkin discretization of the continuity equation. Temporal measurability is handled by averaging the data over the time-grid intervals and using the stability theory of $L^1$-viscosity solutions. The limited regularity of the Hamiltonian is addressed through arguments from nonsmooth analysis, based in particular on Clarke's generalized differential calculus. We prove that the discrete solutions converge, up to some subsequence, to a solution of the MFG system. As a consequence, the numerical approximation also provides a constructive existence result. Under a monotonicity assumption on the coupling terms, we show that the solution to the MFG system is unique, implying the convergence of the whole sequence of discrete solutions. Finally, numerical experiments in one and two spatial dimensions illustrate the robustness of the method, including a linear--quadratic example with a running cost that is discontinuous in time and for which we compute an exact solution.

papers.title: A Joint Local Limit Theorem for Prime Divisor Counting Functions
papers.abstract: We establish a uniform two-dimensional local limit theorem for the joint distribution of $Ω(n)$ and $Ω(n+1)$. More precisely, along a set of scales of logarithmic density one, the normalized joint counts are uniformly approximated by the density of two independent Gaussian random variables, each with mean and variance $\log\log x$, up to a power-saving error. The proof builds upon a recent circle-method framework of Tao and Teräväinen. Our results equally hold for the additive function $ω$. Additionally, we explore applications of our local limit theorem in the setting of uniquely ergodic systems.

papers.title: Optimal power concavity of the variational mean curvature via singular $1$-Laplace problems
papers.abstract: Let $Ω\subset \mathbb{R}^N$ be a bounded convex domain and let $H_Ω\leq 0$ denote its variational mean curvature, in the sense of Barozzi, Gonzalez and Tamanini [PAMS, 1987]. We prove that $-H_Ω$ is harmonic convex, that is $1/H_Ω$ is a convex function in $Ω$, and that the exponent $-1$ is optimal in the class of convex domains. This strictly improves the concavity of $H_Ω$ obtained by Alter and Caselles [Nonlinear Anal., 2009], who also proved, by geometric methods, a closely related property for the classical mean curvature under Minkowski interpolation of convex bodies. Our approach is analytic: the result is deduced from a concavity property of the solution of the singular $1$-Laplace Dirichlet problem $$\begin{cases} -Δ_1 u = {u^{-γ}} & \quad \hbox{in $Ω$}, \\ u = 0 &\quad \hbox{on $\partial Ω$}, \end{cases}$$ for $γ\in (0,1]$, whose unique positive solution is $u=(-H_Ω)^{-1/γ}$. We show that $u^γ$ is concave, and we obtain this by proving that the solutions $u_p$ of the approximating problems $-Δ_p u_p = u_p^{-γ}$ are $\frac{p-1+γ}{p}$-concave on every bounded convex domain, without any boundary regularity, and then letting $p\to 1^+$. Explicit examples show that no Hölder continuity of $H_Ω$ up to $\partialΩ$ holds uniformly in the class of convex domains with $C^{1,1}$ boundary.

papers.title: Spherical harmonics and infinitesimal projective transformations
papers.abstract: Consider the space of $C^\infty$-functions on the two-dimensional sphere $S^2$ and its decomposition $\oplus\mathcal H_m$ into a direct sum of minimal rotation-invariant spaces. We consider elements of $\oplus\mathcal H_m$ as functions of two variables, a nonnegative integer variable $m$ and a complex variable $u$ (a restriction of such function to a set $m=k$ is a polynomial in $u$ of degree $\le 2k$). The group $\mathrm{GL}\,(3,{\mathbb R})$ of all matrices of order 3 acts on $S^2$, so its Lie algebra acts in $C^\infty(S^2)$ by differentiations along vector fields. We construct operators in $\mathcal W^\infty$ corresponding such differentiations and obtain a collection of differential-difference operators in $\mathcal W^\infty$. The expressions include shifts $m\mapsto m\pm 2$ and derivatives of order 4 in $u$.

papers.title: Area gaps for minimal surfaces in spheres
papers.abstract: In this paper, we prove that a linearly full minimal $2$-torus in $\mathbb{S}^N$ with $N\geq 5$ must have area $>2π^2$, and that a linearly full closed minimal surface in $\mathbb{S}^N$ with $N\geq 9$ must have area $>8π$. These results verify the Willmore conjecture and the generalized Willmore conjecture in higher codimension for minimal surfaces. The area gaps are obtained by applying the Cheng--Li--Yau comparison theorem and deriving a lower bound of the heat trace, where the monotonicity of the shifted normalized Riesz mean is used. We also establish a volume gap above the balanced Clifford product for linearly full closed minimal $n$-submanifolds in $\mathbb{S}^N$ when $n=3$, $N\geq 9$, or $n\geq 4$, $N\geq 3n-1$.

papers.title: Stability of 2D MHD with Only Horizontal Dissipation near a Background Magnetic Field on $\mathbb{R}^2$
papers.abstract: Whether the two-dimensional Navier--Stokes equations with dissipation in only one direction are stable in $H^2$ on the whole plane is a well-known open problem: without transverse dissipation, a cubic interaction fails to be time-integrable. We show that a magnetic field removes this obstruction. For the 2D incompressible MHD equations on $\mathbb R^2$ in which both the viscosity $ν$ and the magnetic diffusivity $μ$ act only in the horizontal direction, we prove the global nonlinear $H^2$ stability of every background field $γe_2$ aligned with the non-dissipative direction, with a stability threshold that is explicit in $ν$, $μ$ and $γ$. The stabilizing mechanism is genuinely nonlinear: at the linear level the background field produces no damping at all in the vertical direction. Instead, in Elsässer variables the obstruction becomes an interaction between Alfvén waves travelling in opposite directions, and we identify nonlinear dissipative quantities that measure the overlap of these waves and are time-integrable although neither wave decays. We then sharpen the threshold by a space--time div--curl estimate for balance laws in the $(t,x_2)$-plane. For $ν=μ\leq1\leqγ$, the admissible perturbations are of size $ν^{2/3}γ^{1/3}$, improving the direct scale $ν$ and growing without bound as the background field strengthens.

papers.title: Space-time large deviations for continuum birth-and-death processes
papers.abstract: We establish a space-time large deviation principle for the empirical process of spatial birth-and-death dynamics in the continuum with area interaction at arbitrary inverse temperature, including the free evolution. The good rate function is the dynamical specific relative entropy with respect to the dynamics, and the result holds on the space of space-time stationary laws on the Skorokhod path space, equipped with the topology of weak convergence. For the time marginals of the empirical process, we identify the rate function in terms of the Hellinger distance between the birth and the death measure of the observed point process, which vanishes exactly at the translation-invariant Gibbs point processes. This proves a continuum version of conjectures of Dai Pra and Handa, and connects space-time large deviations with entropy production.

papers.title: An Erdős-Szekeres-Type Result on Permutation Patterns
papers.abstract: We construct an infinite set of patterns $(p,q)$ where $p$ is an almost increasing permutation and $q$ is an almost decreasing permutation, such that the exponential growth rate of permutations avoiding $(p,q)$ is 2. This extends a classical result of Erdős and Szekeres.

papers.title: Learning Normal Coordinates on Riemannian Manifolds with Flow Charts
papers.abstract: Riemannian manifolds are powerful models for problems with non-Euclidean structure. Recent work in geometric machine learning has focused on training deep neural networks to learn Riemannian metrics from high-dimensional data. However, many geometric algorithms require repeated evaluations of the exponential and logarithmic maps, whose high computational cost restricts the utility of learned Riemannian manifolds in practice. We propose to address this cost by training a conditional invertible neural network, called a flow chart, to approximate normal coordinates around points on a given Riemannian manifold. With this approach, the exponential and logarithmic maps can be approximated by fast Euclidean operations in the model's learned coordinate space. Our main contribution is an efficient loss function for training flow charts that is nonnegative and, under suitable domain assumptions, is zero precisely when the chart is normal. Across sixteen synthetic and data-derived geometries, flow charts are competitive with a specialized neural geodesic interpolator for logarithmic map estimation, while also being able to estimate the exponential map. When pretrained, flow charts provide a median speedup of 60-70x over numerical baselines at comparable logarithmic map estimation error, and their learned coordinates improve the accuracy of a numerical geodesic solver.

papers.title: Gaussian Fluctuations of the Gradient of the Fréchet Function and Nonstandard Asymptotics of Sample Fréchet Means
papers.abstract: We establish a central limit theorem for the gradient of the population Fréchet function in local Euclidean coordinates on a metric space. Assuming a unique population mean, a consistent measurable sequence of sample means, semiconcavity and moment bounds for the squared distance functions, and local $C^{1,α}$ regularity of the population Fréchet function, we prove an asymptotic linear representation for the gradient of the population Fréchet function evaluated at the sample mean. The leading term is the negative empirical average of the gradients of the squared distance functions at the population mean; these gradients exist almost surely under our assumptions. On connected complete Riemannian manifolds, uniqueness of the population mean, existence of a $(2+η)$-moment, and local $C^{1,α}$ regularity suffice, and the leading term is expressed through the logarithm map. To control the empirical process uniformly over a neighborhood where squared distance functions may be nonsmooth, we use one-sided partial derivatives of the squared distance functions. The key estimate is a polynomial bound on the $L^2$ bracketing numbers of the resulting function classes. We also give a sufficient condition for the regularity of the population Fréchet function through probability bounds for neighborhoods of cut loci. We then show how the local behavior of the population Fréchet function transforms these Gaussian fluctuations into limit distributions for suitably rescaled sample Fréchet means, allowing for anisotropic scaling and non-Gaussian limits. Polynomial, logarithmic, and oscillatory examples illustrate the applicability and limitations of this approach.

papers.title: Primal-Dual Adaptive Subgradient Methods
papers.abstract: We propose adaptive primal-dual subgradient methods for constrained convex optimization. Our first method applies an AdaGrad-style step-sizes to the dual problem and recovers primal solutions by averaging the associated Fenchel-type oracle outputs. It achieves $\widetilde{\mathcal{O}}(T^{-1/2})$ convergence for the dual objective residual, primal objective residual, and feasibility gap in the nonsmooth regime, while automatically improving to $\mathcal{O}(T^{-1})$ when the dual objective is smooth. We further develop an accelerated variant, which retains the $\widetilde{\mathcal{O}}(T^{-1/2})$ nonsmooth rate while achieving $\mathcal{O}(T^{-2})$ convergence in the smooth regime under mild assumptions. These guarantees require no prior knowledge of the underlying regularity. We demonstrate the empirical performance of the proposed methods on optimal transport and semidefinite relaxation of the Max-Cut problem.

papers.title: Ordered Trees with Linear Off-Diagonal Ramsey Numbers
papers.abstract: We characterize the following three classes of ordered trees: $\qquad$ (1) trees $T$ satisfying $R_<(T,K_n)=O(n)$; $\qquad$ (2) $χ$-bounding trees; $\qquad$ (3) Ramsey-good trees. In particular, we show that the first two classes coincide. The second characterization answers a question of Axenovich, Rollin and Ueckerdt, and the third resolves a problem of Balko and Poljak. In our proof, we also introduce several novel constructions of ordered graphs with sublinear independence number, giving lower bounds on $R_<(F,K_n)$ for various ordered forests $F$.

papers.title: Random $C^*$-subalgebras
papers.abstract: Given a discrete countable group $Γ$, we introduce the concept of random subalgebras of the reduced group $C^*$-algebra $C_r^*(Γ)$. This extends the existing theory of invariant random subgroups and the one of invariant random subalgebras of the group von Neumann algebra ${\rm L}(Γ)$. As applications, we provide a characterisation of $C^*$-simplicity, a condition for amenability of the group and show the existence and uniqueness of a maximal nuclear $Γ$-invariant unital $C^*$-subalgebra of $C^*_r(Γ)$. Moreover, we give a topological characterisation of exactness of any separable unital $C^*$-algebra. Finally, we study exotic random subalgebras of $C^*_r(Γ)$ and super-exotic random subalgebras of ${\rm L}(Γ)$, that is, random subalgebras which do not arise purely from random subgroups of $Γ$ and not from random subalgebras of $C^*_r(Γ)$, respectively.

papers.title: Local Work, Global Progress: A Convergence Theory of AI Agent Collaboration
papers.abstract: Teams of large language model (LLM) agents are increasingly applied to complex tasks, but their collaboration protocols are mostly designed empirically, without convergence guarantees. We formalize collaborative problem solving as block optimization: each agent improves one part of a shared solution, guided by its local objective plus a correction for how its changes affect the other parts. A coordinator checks every proposal against the global objective and merges proposals that do not interfere with each other. We prove linear convergence up to an error floor that vanishes when the corrections are exact. Interfering proposals can also be merged once their combination has been checked; the rate then depends on how well the proposals actually combine, not on worst-case interactions. With GPT-OSS-120B agents on robot routing, a three-agent team finds collision-free plans in every run, better than those of a single agent that controls all robots. On a larger routing task, a six-agent team completes its search about twice as fast as the single agent (in median). Merging the best checked combination of proposals, rather than only proposals that do not interfere, cuts the team's search time by about 30%. With constants measured on the runs, our convergence bound holds in every round and follows the observed progress. We also test the theory on query planning in SQLite and on a synthetic task.

papers.title: Gaussian Integral Operator between Fock Spaces
papers.abstract: We study Gaussian integral operators \[(Tf)(z)=\frac1π\int_{\mathbb C} e^{αz^2+β\overline w^{\,2}+γz\overline w+ηz+δ\overline w} f(w)e^{-|w|^2}\,dA(w)\] acting between Fock spaces $\mathcal F^p$ and $\mathcal F^q$, where $0<p,q\leq\infty$. We give complete characterizations of their boundedness and compactness in terms of explicit conditions on the parameters of the Gaussian kernel. The proofs are based on a unified approach combining reproducing-kernel estimates, atomic decompositions, and sampling sequences, together with a reduction to diagonal operators on sequence spaces. We also study Schatten-class membership on $\mathcal F^2$ and compute the Hilbert--Schmidt norm explicitly.

papers.title: Closed maximal eventually different families for $\boldsymbolΣ^0_3$ and weakly Farah ideals
papers.abstract: Motivated by the existence of closed maximal $\mathcal{I}$-eventually different ($\mathcal{I}$-MED) families, we study uniform combinatorial properties of ideals. For a fixed ideal, a property is uniform if its witnesses can be chosen by a single Borel map. We prove that every $\boldsymbolΣ^0_3$ ideal is uniformly weakly $P^+$. We also prove that the classes of Farah and weakly Farah ideals coincide, answering a question of Hrušák and Meza-Alcántara. We then show that every weakly Farah ideal is uniformly weakly Ramsey. As an application, we obtain closed $\mathcal{I}$-MED families for $\boldsymbolΣ^0_3$ ideals and weakly Farah ideals.

papers.title: Global $L^2$ Approximation in the Bergman Spaces with Values in Holomorphic Vector Bundles
papers.abstract: In this paper, we get global $L^2$ approximation theorems in Bergman spaces with values in singular holomorphic vector bundles over Stein manifolds generalizing results of Li and Zhou. The main results combine strong openness property of multiplier submodule sheaf and twisted $L^2$ estimates of $\bar\partial$-equations.

papers.title: A Complete Dichotomy for $L_\infty$ Permutation Removal
papers.abstract: We study the removal problem for permutation patterns under the normalized $L_\infty$ earth mover's distance. We prove a complete dichotomy. Let \[ \mathcal E =\{(12),(21),(132),(213),(231),(312)\}. \] If $σ\in\mathcal E$, then every permutation of length $n$ that is $\varepsilon$-far from being $σ$-free contains at least $\varepsilon(n-1)$ copies of $σ$; for $0<\varepsilon\le 1/16$, this is sharp up to a constant factor for all sufficiently large $n$. If $σ\in S_k\setminus\mathcal E$, then for every sufficiently large $n$ there is a permutation of length $n$ that is $1/(8k)$-far from being $σ$-free and contains exactly one copy of $σ$. Thus the usual positive-density removal conclusion fails for every nontrivial permutation pattern, but the sparse behavior is completely characterized: the minimum number of copies is linear for exactly six patterns and is one for all others. Consequently, no canonical one-sided tester that rejects only after finding a forbidden copy can have query complexity independent of the permutation length.

papers.title: There can be equitable social welfare orders but no fair voting system
papers.abstract: In the context of intergenerational equity it is natural to ask that social welfare orders have th properties of finite anonymity and strong Pareto efficiency. Such social welfare orders can be constructed from nonprincipal ultrafilters over the set of natural numbers, and the existence of ultrafilters of this kind is known to be equivalent to the existence of a fair voting system for a countably infinite population in the sense of Arrow's theorem. Unfortunately, the existence of this variety of social welfare order, which we call anonymous Pareto, implies the existence of nonmeasurable sets of real numbers. For some, such as Litak, this entails that such social welfare orders are inadmissible for use in theoretical economics because they are non-constructive in nature. The authors seek to give nuance to this view, proving that anonymous Pareto and other social welfare orders can exist in the absence of nonprincipal ultrafilters over the set of natural numbers.

papers.title: Nonlocal geometric rigidity inequalities and the justification of linearized peridynamics
papers.abstract: We prove geometric rigidity inequalities for vector fields using double-integral Gagliardo-type quantities. We show that the nonlocal-norm distance of the difference quotient of a vector field from the difference quotient of a single rigid motion is controlled by the same nonlocal norm of a difference characterizing the distance to the manifold of all rigid motions. The inequality is then used to show the variational convergence of a sequence of rescaled nonlocal fully nonconvex integral functionals to a linearized energy functional. Related functionals arise in peridynamic formulations of continuum mechanics via the total strain energy; this variational convergence provides a rigorous justification of linearized peridynamics with volume constraint via the convergence of rescaled displacements. We additionally establish analogous rigidity inequalities in the linearized setting, which can be thought of as nonlocal analogues of Korn's inequality for displacements.

papers.title: Foliations and Laminar Currents for $C^2$ Maximal Plurisubharmonic Functions
papers.abstract: Let $u\in C^2(Ω)\cap\mathrm{PSH}(Ω)$ satisfy $(dd^c u)^2=0$ on a domain $Ω\subset\mathbb{C}^2$. We prove that the positive-rank locus of its Levi form carries a foliation by holomorphic curves tangent to the Levi-null directions, along which $u$ is harmonic. The flow boxes are locally bi-Lipschitz; in particular, the Levi-null slope is locally Lipschitz in the transverse variable. The Levi current is uniformly laminar on the positive-rank locus, with an explicit transverse measure, and laminar on $Ω$. A smooth example also shows that the Levi current can be laminar without being uniformly laminar on the whole domain. The analytic construction combines a local partial Legendre transform with a Hardy-space boundary equation.

papers.title: Small Viscosity Limit of Navier-Stokes Equations in A Quarter Plane with Navier Slip Conditions
papers.abstract: We study the vanishing-viscosity limit of Leray solutions to the two-dimensional incompressible Navier--Stokes equations in a quarter plane with Navier slip boundary conditions on both edges for a class of compatible well-prepared initial data. By multi-scale analysis, we deduce that a boundary layer of order $O(\sqrtε)$ arises near each edge of the corner and is described by a linearized Prandtl equation, and near the corner, their overlap and nonlinear interaction are captured by a two-dimensional corner profile. Although this profile occurs at order $O(\sqrtε)$, it is governed, in the fast variables, by a nonlinear initial-boundary value problem of Navier--Stokes type. The well-posedness and Sobolev regularity of the outer flow problems, together with the well-posedness and weighted estimates of the boundary-layer and corner-layer problems are obtained on a common time interval $[0,T]$ independent of $ε$. To ensure the required regularity of the outer Euler flow in the critical right-angle domain, it is assumed that the initial vorticity of the outer leading order flow vanishes in a neighborhood of the corner. We then rigorously justify the resulting composite expansion in the small viscosity limit. More precisely, after retaining the leading outer flow, the two weak boundary layers, the nonlinear corner layer, and the order-$ε$ outer correction, the error between the exact solution and this truncated expansion is $O(ε^{5/4})$ in $L^\infty(0,T;L^2(\Q))$ and $O(ε^{3/4})$ in $L^2(0,T;H^1(\Q))$.

papers.title: Proliferation Transitions for Quantum Doubles of Groups
papers.abstract: Proliferation transitions are phase transitions between a 2+1d topological order $\mathcal{T}$ and another $\mathcal{T}/\mathcal{A}$, obtained by condensing anyons in an algebra $\mathcal{A}\subset \mathcal{T}$. We consider such transitions in quantum doubles of groups, $\mathcal{T}=D(G, ω)$, for finite groups $G$ possibly with three-cocycle $ω$, for which condensable algebras are fully classified. Given a condensable algebra $\mathcal{A}$, we represent $\mathcal{T}$ in terms of a Symmetry Topological Field Theory (SymTFT), that is tailored to the $\mathcal{A}$ proliferation transition. The SymTFT bulk is constructed from the Müger center of the subcategory generated by the algebra, i.e. the category of transparent lines, which can be bosons or fermions. Properties of the transition can then be inferred directly from the algebra classification data. For gauged Landau-Ginzburg (LG*) type transitions, we show that they do not only depend on the anyons in $\mathcal{A}$ through their field content, but the cubic interactions are fixed in terms of the multiplication structure of $\mathcal{A}$. Applied to twin algebras, which have the same anyon content but different multiplication structures, we show that twins result in distinct proliferation transitions.

papers.title: Oscillator representations of quantum affine orthosymplectic superalgebras II
papers.abstract: As a continuation of our study on quantum affine spin-oscillator correspondence, we introduce a category of $q$-oscillator representations of quantum affine superalgebras of type $XB$ ($X=B,D$) and construct irreducible objects in a uniform way. Under the truncation functor inspired by the theory of super duality, they are related to finite-dimensional irreducible representations of $U_q(D^{(2)}_{n+1})$ ($X=B$) or $U_q(B^{(1)}_{n})$ ($X=D$). We also considerably streamline our previous arguments, which clarifies how our construction can be understood as a quantum affinization of classical super duality.

papers.title: Strictly convex ergodic billiards
papers.abstract: We produce the first known strictly convex ergodic billiards: sufficiently asymmetric lemon billiards. These billiard tables are the intersection of two circles of which one contains the centers of both. We previously proved that they have \emph{uniformly} hyperbolic returns to a suitable section, and we here control singularity curves, with an approach that seems new. This implies ergodicity and indeed the Bernoulli property.

papers.title: Density Evolution for Stochastic Dynamical Systems Driven by α-Stable Processes: An Equation-Free Numerical Approach
papers.abstract: While well-established approaches exist for computing probability densities of stochastic differential equations driven by Brownian motion, computing probability densities for general stochastic differential equations driven by α-stable processes remains challenging, and few general-purpose methods are available. A major difficulty is that the corresponding Fokker--Planck equations governing the density are generally unavailable in explicit form. In this paper, we develop an efficient approach to compute probability densities for stochastic differential equations driven by α-stable processes without relying on Fokker--Planck equations or any other governing equations. The proposed approach is easy to implement and computationally efficient. Numerical examples demonstrate its effectiveness and indicate an approximately first-order convergence rate with respect to the time step.

papers.title: Kähler-Ricci Shrinkers with Nonnegative Ricci Curvature
papers.abstract: We prove that every complete Kähler--Ricci shrinker with nonnegative Ricci curvature is holomorphically isometric to $\mathbb{C}^k\times N^{n-k}$ for some $0\le k\le n$, where $\mathbb{C}^k$ is the Gaussian shrinker and $N$ is a compact Kähler--Ricci shrinker with nonnegative Ricci curvature. As a corollary, every complete Kähler--Ricci shrinker with quasi-positive Ricci curvature is compact.

papers.title: A necessary condition for a Romanoff type theorem
papers.abstract: Let $\{a_k\}_{k\ge1}$ be an infinite strictly increasing sequence of positive integers with $a_k\mid a_{k+1}$ for every integer $k\ge1$. Dai and Pan proved that the set of integers of the form $p^2+q^2+a_k+a_l$, where $p,q$ are primes and $k,l\ge1$, has positive lower asymptotic density if $\limsup_{k\to\infty}\frac{\log a_k}{k}<\infty$ and $\sup_{k\ge1}\sum_{d\mid a_k}\frac1d<\infty$. They also asked whether the latter condition is necessary. In this paper, we show that this condition is necessary by proving that if $\sup_{k\ge1}\sum_{d\mid a_k}\frac1d=\infty$, then this set has asymptotic density zero.

papers.title: From the Optimal $L^2$-Estimates \((p,n)\) and \((n,p)\)-Forms to Uniform Griffiths \(p\)-Positivity via Convolution and Restriction
papers.abstract: We prove that the optimal \(L^2\)-estimate property for \((p,n)\)-forms is preserved under standard convolution regularization. As an application, we show that a singular Hermitian metric satisfying the optimal \(L^2\)-estimate property for \((p,n)\)-forms is uniform Griffiths \(p\)-positive. By establishing the restriction property, we prove that a singular Hermitian metric satisfying the optimal \(L^2\)-estimate property for \((n,p)\)-forms is also uniform Griffiths \(p\)-positive.

papers.title: Likelihood-Based Confidence Curves for Bounded Parameters
papers.abstract: When a parameter is bounded, the likelihood ratio statistic does not generally follow the chi-square limit distribution of Wilks' theorem. In fact, its asymptotic null distribution depends on the distance from the null value to the boundary, interpolating between the chi-bar-square law on the boundary and the chi-square law in the deep interior of the parameter space. We derive this distribution and use it to construct confidence curves, which are nested collections of two-sided confidence intervals or regions, for bounded parameters. We extend the existing result for the scalar parameter to a two-dimensional parameter with one or both components bounded. As the bivariate distributions are integrals of normal distributions, which are not reducible to standard statistical functions, we also give a simpler approximated distribution obtained by moment-matching. We illustrate the methods on a canonical analysis from high-energy physics, namely the Poisson signal-plus-background experiment.

papers.title: Boundedness of radial solutions to the parabolic-parabolic Keller--Segel system on the plane with subcritical mass
papers.abstract: We establish uniform-in-time boundedness of radially symmetric global solutions to the two-dimensional parabolic-parabolic Keller--Segel system on the whole space with mass below $8π$. While global existence is known throughout this subcritical mass range, uniform-in-time boundedness has remained open. On bounded domains, the free energy method of Nagai, Senba and Yoshida (1997) yields both global existence and boundedness under the optimal mass condition. On the whole space, however, the corresponding estimates do not rule out growth as time tends to infinity, preventing a direct application of this approach to establish boundedness. The key ingredients are new interior estimates controlling the localized free energy in terms of its dissipation, together with uniform-in-time exterior estimates exploiting radial symmetry.

papers.title: Hausdorff dimension of the singular set in optimal transport
papers.abstract: We study optimal transport between bounded smooth domains in $\mathbb{R}^n$, with smooth positive densities bounded above and below. Without convexity assumptions on the domains, we prove that the optimal map is smooth outside a relatively closed set of Hausdorff dimension at most $n-1$.

papers.title: Simultaneous popular differences for polynomial and linear progressions in finite fields
papers.abstract: We study simultaneous popular differences for polynomial progressions and linear progressions over finite fields $\mathbb F_p$. For certain families of polynomial progressions of algebraic complexity $1$, such as $(x, x+y, x+2y)$ and $(x, x+y^3, x+2y^3)$, we prove the existence of $y \neq 0$ which is popular simultaneously for both progressions. This extends previous results by Conlon, Dong and Hong who considered complexity $0$ progressions. On the other hand, we construct counterexamples showing that simultaneous popular differences are not guaranteed to exist for $(x, x+y, x+2y)$ and $(x, x+y^2, x+2y^2)$, or for $(x, x+y, x+2y)$ and $(x, x+y, x+3y)$, or for $(x, x+y, x+2y)$ and $(x,x+y,x+2y,x+3y)$, answering questions posed by Conlon, Dong and Hong.

papers.title: Extremal graphs without cycles of length 0 modulo 4
papers.abstract: In a remarkable recent result, Győri, Li, Salia, Tompkins, Varga and Zhu determined the maximum size in a graph of given order and containing no cycle of length divisible by 4. In this paper, we give a complete characterization of all graphs attaining this maximum. This answers a question posed by Li, Pan and Shi. Very recently, Chu, Park and Ryu established a sharp upper bound on the number of edges in a 2-connected graph containing no cycle of length divisible by 4. We also give a complete characterization of all such graphs attaining this bound.

papers.title: Norm-optimal model order reduction in reproducing kernel Hilbert spaces
papers.abstract: We consider the problem of model order reduction (MOR) in reproducing kernel Hilbert spaces (RKHSs). We prove generalizations of well-known necessary interpolatory conditions for norm-optimal reduced-order models, originally stated for rational functions in $H_2$ Hardy-Hilbert spaces. We construct an alternative to the iterative rational Krylov (IRKA) algorithm for RKHSs with differentiable kernels to obtain norm-optimal reduced-order models. Then, we introduce generalized Malmquist-Takenaka (GMT) functions that can be used to define orthonormal bases in an arbitrary RKHS. Using GMT functions, we propose unitary transformations between separable RKHSs. This allows us to extend our optimality conditions and subsequent algorithms to MOR problems posed in RKHSs with non-differentiable kernels. The potential and versatility of the proposed MOR framework is demonstrated in several numerical experiments. We perform norm-optimal MOR on various machine learning models such as support vector machines and deep ReLU networks. In addition, we show how the proposed MOR framework can be used to solve seemingly unrelated problems. In particular, we provide an example for fitting high degree polynomials to data and also obtain a FEM-like method for solving partial differential equations (PDEs) with an optimal kernel basis.

papers.title: Secure Domination in Odd-order Sierpinski Graphs
papers.abstract: A nonempty vertex set D of a graph is secure if and only if, for every nonempty subset X of D, the closed neighborhood of X contains at least as many vertices of D as vertices outside D. A secure dominating set is a set that is both secure and dominating, and the secure domination number is the minimum cardinality of such a set. Previous work determined the secure domination number of Sierpinski graphs S_n k for even k and for odd k when n = 2. The exact values for odd k and n\geq3 remained open. In this paper, we determine these remaining values.

papers.title: The Gagliardo-Nirenberg equation on Riemannian manifolds
papers.abstract: We establish geometric and analytic rigidity results for the Gagliardo-Nirenberg equation. On a complete noncompact Riemannian manifold with nonnegative Ricci curvature, the existence of a positive critical point of the Gagliardo-Nirenberg quotient forces the manifold to be Euclidean and the solution to be extremal. No minimizing assumption or volume growth hypothesis is required, thereby strengthening earlier rigidity results. In Euclidean space, we prove that all positive solutions of the normalized equation whose nonlinear mass on expanding annuli has sublinear growth are extremals. The linear threshold is optimal, as shown by explicit profiles that are constant in one direction. We also prove a sharp pointwise estimate involving the solution and its gradient, valid without assumptions at infinity, with equality at one point characterizing the extremals. The proofs use weighted divergence identities and a reflection argument controlled by annular mass. Explicit constructions reveal the geometric and variational limits of rigidity: nonflat quotient critical points exist beyond the curvature hypothesis, while the normalized equation admits positive solutions even under strictly positive sectional curvature and maximal volume growth.

papers.title: On the MDS conjecture in even characteristic
papers.abstract: We prove that every nontrivial linear $[n,k]$ maximum distance separable (MDS) code over a finite field $\F_q$ of characteristic two satisfies $n\le q+1$, except in dimensions $k=3$ and $k=q-1$, where $n\le q+2$. This resolves the linear MDS conjecture in even characteristic.

papers.title: Kadison duality for biaffinely convex sets
papers.abstract: Classical Kadison duality establishes a categorical equivalence between compact convex sets and Archimedean order unit spaces of affine functions. This paper develops a Kadison-type duality for sets with coordinate-wise convex structure in product domains $\mathbb{R}^n \times \mathbb{R}^m$. While slice-wise convex (biconvex) sets appear to be the natural geometric domain, separate convexity along coordinates is insufficient to ensure separation by biaffine polynomials. In classical convexity, every closed convex set is determined by affine functionals because any exterior point can be separated by a hyperplane. In contrast, biaffine polynomials can only probe a biconvex set $K$ up to its biaffine hull biconv$(K)$, the envelope formed by the intersection of all regions cut out by valid biaffine inequalities on $K$. To resolve this obstruction, the geometric setting is restricted to biaffinely convex sets, those that coincide with their biaffine hull ($K =$ biconv$(K)$) and therefore admit strict biaffine separation. On the algebraic side, we introduce the dual objects, which we call biaffine order unit spaces.
